Moreover, we should also keep in view that just as this religion was revealed by Allah through the Messenger, Allah likewise established its method of work through the Sunnah of the Messenger. This prescribed method (manhaj) is the one that accords with the nature of this religion, and this religion and its natural method cannot be separated.

At the same time, it should also remain before us that just as Islam seeks to reform human character through ideological reform, in exactly the same way it seeks to change the method by which intellectual and ideological reform is brought about. For instance, it does not want mere intellectual construction in a philosophical manner; rather, alongside intellectual reform and guidance, it wants to set in motion a movement as well, so that a nation (GreAt NAtion) may be built in which doctrinal concepts and the existence of a living and dynamic society are present side by side in its outlook. In short, according to the Islamic worldview, there is no dividing line between its way of thinking, the foundational concepts arising from that thinking, and the society that comes into being in accordance with those concepts, such that when one is being worked upon, the others may not be touched. According to the Islamic method of reviving the religion, all of them will be worked upon simultaneously.

The importance of this method:
Having understood this method of reviving the religion, we should keep in mind that this method is extremely important and extremely fundamental. It is not specific to a particular stage, a particular family, or a particular society, nor was this method specific to the circumstances of the first Islamic movement. It is a method without adopting which the work of reviving the religion cannot take place in any place or at any time.

Islam did not intend merely to change some beliefs of people and make some reforms in social conditions and then sit back. It wanted a comprehensive transformation in the thinking and outlook of people, and this was the mission it undertook. It gave them a theory and also gave them reality, and it gave them a specific method for this; and since this is the method determined by Allah, by its very nature it is entirely different from the flawed methods devised by humans.

The attainment of the Islamic conception of life and the Islamic system of life is impossible until we develop within ourselves an Islamic way of thinking (IslAmic WAy of Thinking). Allah shaped the beliefs and concepts of people upon this way of thinking, and as a result all their beliefs became correct and the formation and construction of their practical lives also took place along correct lines. If, influenced by modern ideas, we reduce the Islamic worldview to a merely academic and pedagogical theory, it will lose its distinctive character, and we will fall victim to that mental defeat whereby it appears that the Islamic method and the divine standpoint are inferior to human theories and systems, or that they are deficient compared to them, and we wish to make changes to remove that deficiency so that it conforms to human methods and standards... This will be a great defeat and also a destructive one.

The distinctive feature of the Islamic system of life is that it should grant the workers of the Islamic movement a particular way of thinking and liberate them from the bonds of the jahili way of thinking that now overshadows everywhere and by which our organizations and our entire culture are affected. If we view the Islamic system of life from the same standpoint from which a worldly jahili system is viewed, this will be entirely contrary to the nature of the Islamic system of life, and in this way that very real purpose of this religion, which it keeps before it in relation to the welfare of humanity, will be lost. After adopting this standpoint, it will be extremely difficult for us to free ourselves from the jahili system of life, while this system is now prevailing everywhere. Thus we will lose a golden opportunity, our collective life will be buried under jahili ideas and non-Islamic thoughts, and its consequences will be far-reaching and destructive.

The balance of viewpoint:
In the movement for the revival of Islam, there is no difference in importance between the way of thinking and the method of work on the one hand, and the conception of life and the system of life on the other. The way of thinking and the method of work can never be separated at any time from the detailed system of life and conception of life, and if an attempt is made to present this conception of life and system of life merely in the form of exposition, then as a result no movement at all will come into being, and the Islamic worldview will become merely a mental theory. Alongside this, it is also an undeniable reality that even if we adopt merely the expository method to present the Islamic conception of life, then too only those people will be able to benefit from it who have in practice adopted this movement, and that too only to the extent that, at the stage where these workers stand, they act fully upon the commands of the Islamic system of life. That is, benefit from this worldview is obtained according to the measure of action, not according to the measure of knowledge. In short, the summary of my remarks is that the Islamic conception of life must immediately appear in the form of a movement, and this movement must be a correct representation and translation of that conception of life. This is the natural method for establishing the Islamic system of life, and it is also loftier, more elevated and more solid than all other methods. It also accords more with human nature, and there is more dynamism and activity in it. Merely presenting a static, complete and self-contained theory of life in a rigid form, this method is more beneficial, because in it a plan of action is presented before active and dynamic people, and one does not deal with inactive people; rather, people become living embodiments of mental concepts and the theory of life.

Islamic movement and scholarly research:
If this opinion regarding the genuine Islamic worldview is correct, then it should also be correct regarding the foundational concepts of the Islamic worldview. Likewise, in the matter of presenting the detailed laws of the Islamic system of life, this same method, that is, the unity of codification and implementation, should be the correct one.

At present the situation is that around us there is the thick darkness of jahiliyyah. It is affecting the workers of the Islamic movement. As they advance step by step, in accordance with the prescribed method of the Islamic system of life for the revival of the religion, it asks them, in a very innocent tone, what the details of the system of life to which they are calling people are, what scholarly research they have done for its implementation, how far its intellectual and theoretical foundations have been prepared, and how far the codification of Islamic jurisprudence along modern lines has progressed. On hearing these "innocent" questions, one feels as though the only obstacles now standing in the way of implementing the Islamic system of life are the need to complete the codification of jurisprudential rulings and research on certain jurisprudential topics. As for jahiliyyah, it has already bowed before the sovereignty of Allah, and all people have become prepared for the implementation of Islamic laws; the only difficulty encountered is that no jurist, mujtahid, or legislator can be found who could codify Islamic Shariah along modern legal lines. This is in fact a deep conspiracy and an open mockery being carried out against the Islamic Shariah, and every sensitive heart should give it due attention.

The followers of jahiliyyah, by raising such questions, actually want to evade the implementation of the Shariah. One of their aims is that Muslims should remain subject to non-Islamic and man-made laws; the second aim is that the Islamic movement should be diverted from the Islamic method of establishing the religion, the necessary stage of building thought and reviving the movement should be ignored, and the codification of law should begin before that, whereas the correct method of establishing the religion is that first the Islamic worldview should emerge in the active form of an Islamic movement, and that detailed laws should be brought forward only in accordance with the real need of the stage of establishing the religion that is faced, and that codification of law should take place only when its need arises.

It is the foremost duty of the workers of the Islamic movement to keep this very method before them. They should refrain from the methods of conspiracies and military coups, and they should not dictate on their own any method in opposition to this Islamic method. Those who do not believe in Allah and His Messenger at all should not be paid attention to in their talk. These people actually want to mislead the workers of the Islamic movement and make them hasty. Toward them we must be extremely serious.

The spread of narrow-mindedness among Islamist elements through various means must be firmly countered. We should work to foil this conspiracy as well, and ignore the base mentality being spread in the name of "the accumulation of Islamic jurisprudence" in a country that does not at all accept the obedience to and implementation of the Shariah. We should ignore this useless mockery and turn toward our real objective in accordance with the correct Islamic method. We should understand that sowing seeds in the air will be of no benefit at all. This happy spectacle of Islamic investigations and jurisprudential development is in fact a deep conspiracy, and our duty is to remain firmly on the correct and natural method of reviving the religion against it. The secret of this religion's strength lies in it, and it is the source of our workers' spiritual strength.

(At present in Egypt, several institutions modelled on Pakistan's Islamic Culture Institute and the central Islamic Research Institute are conducting research on Islam. This research is like that of a skilled craftsman engaged in archaeological discoveries in deserts. Sayyid Qutb's aim is that such people have no concern with the revival of Islam, nor do the people who work in these institutions act upon Islamic teachings, nor is it the aim of their governments that this research be implemented; rather, the work is carried out merely as an intellectual and technical indulgence, and it is clear that no such measure is desired by Islam.

Nevertheless, it is an undeniable reality in its own right that there is a pressing need for research in light of modern questions and modern circumstances raised on every topic of Islam, especially defensive research. It should also be kept in view that the Islamic system was presented for the first time to the Arabs and was gradually implemented alongside that, so naturally the building of thought, its method, the Islamic movement and the formation of the system of life all proceeded side by side. But the situation we now face has two aspects. On one side are the common people, who are ready for the implementation of the Islamic system or at least are not opposed to its being implemented upon them; and on the other side is a limited minority that does not accept the possibility of implementing the Islamic system and is blocking the path of the Islamic system of life merely through force and power. Therefore, keeping this situation in view, the very method adopted in which all people are assumed to be non-Muslims cannot be followed. A further difference is that in the first era the details of Islamic laws were hidden in the unseen, and those of jahiliyyah could object only to those laws and commands that had already been revealed. But at present the Islamic system of life is set out in detail in the Qur'an and Sunnah, Islamic history has been codified, and jahiliyyah has been given the opportunity to raise all kinds of objections regarding Islamic culture.

Therefore, at every stage of the initial method of reviving the Islamic system of life, it will be necessary to answer the objections of jahiliyyah and to clarify various aspects of Islamic laws. Moreover, the whole world at present faces the fundamental problems of life, and in the clash of different systems of life, only that system can succeed which offers the best solution to global problems. Therefore it is necessary that the Islamic movement also impress upon minds, in this field, the superiority of the Islamic system of life. Thus correct Islamic research along proper lines also becomes absolutely necessary. In view of these realities, Sayyid Qutb's dictum that the details of Islamic law should not be touched at all is not free from exaggeration.)

The Islamic method of reviving the religion and the Islamic system of life itself are identical to each other. There is no difference or separation between them. No method other than this method can give birth to the Islamic system of life. Only some human and jahili system of life can be born as a result of any other method. The revival of the Islamic system of life cannot in any way take place in accordance with it. In short, the essence of this entire discussion is that in every movement and every effort for the revival of the religion, adherence to the Islamic method of reviving the religion is necessary.

This is my final word, and I am confident that through this lengthy note I have fully clarified the Meccan surahs and the method established within them. Now all these leaders should understand well the nature of the Islamic method for their movements, and those who wish to do the work of Islam should then be satisfied and hope that the method they have attained is goodness and benefit, that they are the highest people, and that the path the noble Qur'an shows is more upright. (Verse) "Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright" (Qur'an 17:9).

Now let us say something about this surah. In Zilal al-Quran, this is the first Meccan surah on which we have the opportunity to comment, and it is a complete picture of the Meccan Qur'an, its Meccan style of speech, and its themes. Its characteristics, its temperament, and its themes were described in the earlier pages. This surah contains an exemplary discussion of the Qur'an's distinctive features, its method of address, its fundamental theme, and its manner of expression. While adopting this general style, the surah also maintains its own temperament. As with all the surahs of the Qur'an, each one preserves, alongside the Qur'an's general style and approach, a particular character and style of its own. The specific atmosphere of each surah is not found in the others. Every surah of the Qur'an has its own individual personality, its own axis, its own distinct features, and a central theme around which all its discussions revolve. Then there are the relevance of that theme and other factors that make the expression of its meaning extremely effective: a particular depiction of scenes, particular shadows, and a particular atmosphere, which stand out and are distinct in each surah.

In each surah, phrases of a particular style recur repeatedly. The themes are sometimes similar, but the identity of a surah is not determined by its theme. Rather, it is determined by other features which serve as the setting for that surah's personality, which are peculiar to that surah and are not found in other surahs.

As for the surah under discussion, it has a central theme, and this theme is presented at every moment, in every scene, with remarkable beauty. It is a beauty such that the eyes are dazzled by it, a person is left speechless, and his breath is held, when someone reflects on its scenes, observes its ups and downs, and feels its effects.

Yes, this is a very important reality. I find it within myself whenever I move along with the discourse of this surah, tour its scenes, and feel its effects. I believe that anyone who has a sensitive heart will surely find some of the feelings that I experience. It is a fact that the beauty of this surah overwhelms a person, and the mind and heart, enthralled, move along with it.

As a whole, this surah deals with the sovereignty of God, both within the sphere of this entire universe and within the sphere of human life, within the sphere of the human self and conscience, within the sphere of the unknown secrets of the visible universe, and also within the sphere of the unknown secrets of the realm of the unseen. This surah presents the concept of divine sovereignty in relation to the creation of this universe, the creation of life on this earth, and then the creation of human beings among the animals. Then, from a historical perspective, this surah also shows some aspects of divine sovereignty in the mutual conflicts of those who passed away and in the succession of those who took their place. In short, while looking at this universe, the sovereignty of God over the phenomena of nature, His sovereignty over the great events that occur in the world, and His sovereignty over prosperity and adversity in the world, is the theme of this surah. God's sovereignty in the various manifestations and observations of divine power, God's sovereignty in His outward and inward grip over human life, God's sovereignty over the events and occurrences that take place on this earth, and, last of all, God's sovereignty in the witnessing of the Resurrection and in people standing before the divine court.

The theme that runs from beginning to end in this surah is the theme of ideology. All its constituent elements are ideological, and all its hidden meanings are ideological too. This surah takes hold of human societies and leads them through the whole universe. It takes them on a tour of the ideological sources of this universe and its outward and hidden signs. Taking the human self along, it moves through the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, where this self tours the realm of darkness and the realm of light, and sees the sun, the moon, and clusters of stars. It takes a tour through the gardens of this earth, which contain every kind of fruit, on which rains are falling, and beneath which rivers flow. Then this surah places the human self in a field of battle in which past nations are seen perishing and fading away, and their ancient remains are visible. Then one is taken on a tour through the darknesses of land and sea. Some unseen secrets are revealed, and the secrets of human psychology are made manifest. Then we see the living emerging from the dead and the dead emerging from the living, a seed which is hidden in the darkness within the earth's womb, and a drop of semen being nourished in the darkness of the womb. Then on this surah's screen appear the jinn and humankind, and then flocks of birds and other beasts. Then the first and the last appear. The living and the dead are also seen, and at night and in the day the guardians of God are visible too.

These countless cosmic witnesses and scenes assault human senses and the human self from every direction. A person feels an entirely new touch. A very vivid feeling arises within the self, and these scenes and meanings are seen racing alive across the screen of thought. The condition becomes such that scenes and feelings that are repeated and already familiar also appear entirely new and unique, completely modern, completely dynamic, and alive. A person feels that this awareness and this consciousness are being experienced for the first time, as though no human conscience or consciousness had ever encountered these feelings before.

This surah, with its witnesses and situations, its signs and effects, and its images and shades, flows on in the way a river flows with its waves. One wave does not strike the shore before another rises. Amid these rises and falls of waves, the river of this surah keeps moving constantly forward.

With this continuous turbulence of its waves, and with the collision of its waves against one another, this surah appears so beautiful that a person is enthralled. Along with this beauty, its themes and meanings are also expressed with great harmony and graceful skill, and the themes are presented in such an impactful way that human feelings are left astonished. There are words that are extremely vivid, dynamic, harmonious, and have effective sound, which affect the human self from every direction and every side, and enchant it. Phrases full of life, effective sounds, and a pictorial manner of expression leave their impact on every aspect of the human self.

We are certain that we cannot express in our own words the effects that this surah has on the heart and mind. It is best that the reader read it himself and directly feel its effects and wonders.

We cannot describe the literary and allusive qualities of this surah in our human words and phrases. However, through our broken words, we show a path to those who have abandoned the Qur'an. A chasm has come between their lives and the Qur'an, and they live in atmospheres that are contrary to the atmosphere of the Qur'an.

To live in the Qur'anic atmosphere does not mean that we acquire knowledge of the Qur'an, recite it with proper recitation, know its sciences and arts, and are aware of its literary excellences. That is not the Qur'anic atmosphere. In our view, to live in the atmosphere of the Qur'an means that a person lives in circumstances, in an atmosphere, in a struggle, in difficulties, and with values such as those that existed at the time the Qur'an was revealed in the first age, as if the Qur'an were being revealed right now. A person should live in opposition to the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) that currently prevails over the whole earth. A person should be confronting jahiliyyah in his heart, in his intentions, and in his movements, creating Islam anew within his own self and the selves of others, in his own life and the lives of others, confronting jahiliyyah and bringing Islam into being again. He should confront afresh all the concepts of jahiliyyah, all the preferences of jahiliyyah, all the customs of jahiliyyah, and the entire practical reality of jahiliyyah. He should stand in battle array against all the pressures of jahiliyyah, every kind of conflict of jahiliyyah, every kind of contest, and every kind of attack upon the Islamic ideology of life and the Islamic system of life. He should fulfil all the requirements of the Islamic system and the Islamic ideology of life, strive in the way of Islam, and remain steadfast in it. This is the meaning of the Qur'anic atmosphere.

This is the Qur'anic atmosphere in which the Qur'an demands that one live. Only in this condition can a person of discerning taste attain the Qur'an. This is because the Qur'an was revealed in precisely such circumstances, and the Qur'an did its work in precisely such a sea of difficulties. Those Muslims who are unfamiliar with such atmospheres are deprived of the Qur'an, even if they study in Islamic seminaries, are reciters, and are experts in the sciences and arts of the Qur'an.

The benefit of the bridge of understanding of the Qur'an that we are building, for the use of the sincere, to enter the world of the Qur'an, will accrue to these sincere people only if they cross this bridge and enter the world of the Qur'an. They must leave this realm and this zone and enter another territory, and through their action and their struggle they must enter the atmosphere of the Qur'an, and they themselves must create this atmosphere. Only then will they perceive the taste of the Qur'an, and only then will they realise that God has favoured them with a blessing.

This surah deals with the Islamic ideology of life. Its theme is the divinity of God and the servitude of the servant. This surah presents before the servants of God an introduction to God: what God is? What is the reality of this universe? What hidden secrets lie behind it? Who are these human beings? Who brought them into existence? Who created them? Who provides them with sustenance? Who sustains them? Who manages their affairs? Who effects change in their hearts and in their outlook? What is the purpose of their creation? Why has their life been limited here? What will be their end? What is this life and what are its varied colours? Who spread it over this earth? What is water? What are these springs and these fruits, one above another? What are these meteors? What is this emergence of dawn? What is this darkness of night? What is this revolution of the heavens? Who is behind them? And what secrets lie behind them? What information is there? Why do these nations, these centuries, and these peoples suffer destruction? And then, what is the end of the new people who are brought forward and placed in the trial? How do trial, reward, and punishment take place? What is this cycle of action and recompense?

In this way, this surah takes the human heart along to all these dimensions and horizons, and takes it on a tour through all these ups and downs. Yet throughout the surah the Meccan style of the Qur'an remains, whose style we explained in the earlier pages. Along with the Meccan style, the manner of speech of the whole Qur'an is also in this surah at its highest standard. The manner of argument is not merely ideological, nor is it composed of theological dialectics that keep readers' thoughts and minds occupied. Rather, in a simple and straightforward manner, this surah introduces the Lord of the worlds to people, so that they may adopt the worship and servitude of their true Lord. Their conscience and their soul should become subservient to God. Their struggle and all their efforts should be in obedience to God. Their customs and traditions should be in submission to God, and the whole practical reality of their lives should be under the sovereignty of God alone, besides whom there is no sovereignty within the heavens and the earth.

It appears that this surah, from beginning to end, is moving toward a defined goal: that God alone is the Creator, He alone is the Owner, He alone possesses power, and He alone is the King and the Subduer. He alone knows the hidden things and the unseen. Just as He turns the night and the day, so too He turns hearts and minds. Therefore He alone should have authority over the lives of all people, and the authority to command and forbid in people's lives should belong to Him alone. No command or law should exist other than His. The authority to determine what is lawful and unlawful also belongs to Him alone, because all these matters are the constituent elements of God's divinity. Therefore, only God can exercise control over these matters in people's lives. There is no creator other than Him, no provider other than Him, no giver of life, no giver of death, no bestower of benefit, no inflicter of harm, no giver, and no preventer. In short, no one other than God can be the owner of benefit or harm for anyone, or for himself, either in this world or in the Hereafter. Throughout this surah, from beginning to end, arguments and evidence are presented for this purpose, and these arguments are presented through the observations, the influences, and the natural situations that exist in this universe and that enchant the thought and the vision. From the study of these natural phenomena, the heart receives impressions and influences from every direction, through every door and every aspect.

The most important issue that this surah emphasizes is the matter of the divinity and sovereignty of Allah within the heavens and the earth: the concept of God's sovereign authority across the vast expanse of the heavens and the earth and throughout this immense universe. This surah presents this very issue, but in a moral manner and in a way suited to the subject matter. The people of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance), in the matter of certain slaughtered animals and certain foods, gave the authority to declare what is lawful and unlawful to others besides Allah. Likewise, in the matter of vows concerning certain offerings, certain fruits and certain children, the worshippers of jahiliyyah gave authority to other gods besides Allah. Because of this connection, Allah has explained here in detail the doctrine of divine sovereignty over this entire universe, and indications of this connection have been given in the final verses of the surah.

(So if you truly believe in Allah's signs, eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned. Why should you not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, when He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except in cases of necessity? Indeed, many people lead others astray with their desires, without knowledge. Your Lord knows best the transgressors. Abstain from open sin and from secret sin. Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they have earned. And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned at its slaughter, for that is indeed deviance. Indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you; and if you obey them, you will indeed be polytheists. (6:118–121)

And they assign to Allah a portion of the crops and cattle that He has created, and they say, "This is for Allah," according to their claim, and "this is for our partners." But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah reaches their partners. Evil is their judgement. And likewise, to many of the polytheists their partners have made the killing of their children appear attractive, in order to ruin them and to confuse them regarding their religion. Had Allah willed, they would not have done so; so leave them to their fabrications. They say, "These cattle and this crop are forbidden; none may eat of them except whom we wish," by their own invention; and there are cattle whose backs are forbidden, and cattle over which they do not mention the name of Allah, all of this as a fabrication against Him. He will soon recompense them for their fabrications. And they say, "What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females; but if it is stillborn, then both may share in it." He will indeed recompense them for their description. Indeed He is All-Wise, All-Knowing. Certainly those have lost who killed their children foolishly, without knowledge, and forbade what Allah had provided for them, fabricating against Allah. They have indeed gone astray and were not among the rightly guided. (6:136–140)

This was a practical aspect of the life of the Muslim community, and in view of it this great issue was taken up in this surah. In that period, the environment of the Muslim community was also overshadowed by jahiliyyah, in which these polytheistic beliefs existed regarding legislation and the determination of what is lawful and unlawful. For their reform, the issues of Allah's divinity, Allah's sovereignty, and the worship and servitude of all human beings are addressed here. Just as this issue is addressed throughout the Meccan Qur'an, so too is it addressed in great detail in this surah. In the Madani verses, wherever the explanation of lawful and unlawful and the right of legislation comes, the issue of divine sovereignty is likewise addressed.

In this context, a flood of effective guidance, decisions and resolutions is rushing forward, and in this light the polytheists' refutation regarding these animals, vows and slaughterings is being presented. Here, in this same connection, the issue of Allah's divinity and Allah's right of legislation is also being explained. It is shown that this legislation of lawful and unlawful is connected with Islamic beliefs and Islamic doctrines. That doctrine of Islam is the doctrine of divine sovereignty and of human servitude and subjugation, and this is not a trivial matter; it is the issue of Islam and disbelief, and of Islam and jahiliyyah. From this flood of guidance, we shall present here only a few examples in the introduction to this surah, but their complete details will come when we discuss the verses of this surah in detail. Yet in its effects, this flood implants in the human soul the true nature of this religion's temperament: that whether a human matter is small or great, ... must be resolved under the sovereignty of Allah's right, and Allah's sovereignty is recorded in the form of the Islamic Shariah. If this is not so, then it will be considered that such people or such a society has left the religion. A person has departed from religion to the extent of a partial or minor matter.

This large collection of guidance also shows that this religion removes human sovereignty from every aspect of human life and from all affairs of life. Whether these matters are important or unimportant, great or small, it brings them within the scope of this great principle. That is, the meaning of Allah's divinity is that Allah, the Exalted, is the absolute ruler over this entire earth, and He alone, without partner, exercises authority over this universe. This principle is fully manifest and embodied within the religion of Islam.

In this surah, after the mention of the customs and rituals of the age of jahiliyyah concerning cattle, fruits, vows and offerings, and children, various commentaries have also been made, through which the purpose is to show that these customs and rituals are extremely foolish and extremely contradictory. In some places it is said that it is not human beings' right to determine lawful and unlawful by themselves; rather this is a great doctrinal matter, and obedience to Allah's commands in determining lawful and unlawful is the only correct path and proper conduct. If anyone does not obey Allah's commands in determining lawful and unlawful, he has left the religion. Observe, after the preceding verses, the manner of expression and then the commentary:

"It is He who produced gardens, trellised and untrellised, and date palms and crops of varying produce, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of their fruit when they bear fruit, and render its due on the day of its harvest, and do not be excessive; indeed He does not love the excessive. And it is He who produced among the cattle those for carrying and for flesh. Eat of what Allah has provided you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan; indeed he is to you a clear enemy. Eight pairs: two of the sheep and two of the goats. Say, O Muhammad (ﷺ): has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females carry? Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful. And of the camels two, and of the cattle two. Say: has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females carry? Were you present when Allah commanded you this? Then who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah to mislead people without knowledge? Indeed Allah does not guide the unjust people." Say, O Muhammad (ﷺ): I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, unless it be carrion, or flowing blood, or swine flesh, for it is impure, or a transgression, that which has been slaughtered for other than Allah. But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor exceeding the limit, indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. And for those who adopted Judaism We made forbidden every animal with undivided hooves, and of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what is on their backs or entrails, or what is mixed with bone. That was Our recompense for their rebellion; and indeed We are truthful. So if they deny you, say: your Lord has vast mercy, and His punishment cannot be averted from the criminal people. The polytheists will certainly say: "If Allah had willed, neither we nor our fathers would have associated anything with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything." Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our punishment. Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can bring forth to us? You follow only conjecture and mere speculation." Say: "To Allah belongs the conclusive argument; had He willed, He would have guided you all." Say: "Bring your witnesses who will testify that Allah has forbidden these things." Then if they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs, and who disbelieve in the Hereafter, and who make equals to their Lord. Say, O Muhammad (ﷺ): come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you:
(1) That you associate nothing with Him.
(2) And that you be good to your parents.
(3) And do not kill your children out of fear of poverty; We provide for you and for them. And do not approach indecencies, whether apparent or hidden.
(4) And do not kill the soul which Allah has made sacred, except by right ... These are what He has enjoined upon you, that perhaps you will understand.
(5) And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner, until he reaches maturity.
(6) And give full measure and weight in justice; We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity.
(7) And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative.
(8) And fulfill the covenant of Allah ... These He has enjoined upon you, that perhaps you will remember.
(9) And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other paths, lest they separate you from His way. This is what He has enjoined upon you, that perhaps you will be mindful."

Here it is evident that a very particular matter, the permissibility or impermissibility of the customary vows and offerings of cattle, animals, fruits and children that were current in jahiliyyah, has been linked with great doctrinal and intellectual issues. This permissibility and impermissibility has been linked with guidance and misguidance, adherence to the Islamic system and adherence to the satanic system, and with the issues of Allah's mercy and Allah's seizure, which are among the most important matters of life. It has been declared that these matters express the doctrine of tawhid and the equating of another with Allah. It has been declared that those who offer vows to other than Allah have departed from Allah's straight path. Therefore, in view of the importance of these matters, the same expressions have been adopted that were adopted to express these lofty doctrinal issues.

This is why the same style of indications and proofs has been adopted here that the Qur'an adopts for these exalted matters. The issue of creation and the various kinds of living things, gardens and vineyards, date groves and fields, various colors and flavors, olives, pomegranates, similar and dissimilar flavors, and so on. Truths which are brought for the doctrine of tawhid have also been brought, and here the punishment and seizure of Allah for the polytheists has also been brought.

All these scenes and sights were presented earlier in this surah as well, when the subject was the doctrine of tawhid. At that time the issue of vows and offerings was not under discussion. This shows that where the matter is the doctrine of tawhid and the issue of Allah's sovereignty is under discussion, the Qur'an's manner is exactly like this, even if the matter is a partial one.

(Due to its great length, the complete commentary on this verse could not be included. We apologize for this. Kindly read the remainder of the commentary on this verse in Fi Zilal al-Quran.)

The surah opens with the theme that the position of those who set up associates with Allah is extremely weak, even though the proofs of tawhid (the oneness of Allah) are before them. They are surrounded by these proofs on every side, and they can see them within their own souls and in the horizons. This surah greets us with a clear reality of divinity, and through a few glimpses it unfolds the pages of this entire universe. In just three glimpses we descend to the depths of this whole universe and take its vastness within our grasp.

These three glimpses are as follows. In one glimpse the creation of this entire universe is shown. In the second, the creation of all humanity is shown. In the third, the Divine Being encompasses these two existences. What a miracle this is! Look at the force and power of the speech, how comprehensive and conclusive a statement it is!

In the presence of this universe, which points to the oneness of the Creator, and in the presence of human existence, which bears just witness to a single Governing Being, and in the presence of this earth and the celestial spheres, and the continuing and pervasive sovereignty of Allah within them, there should be no room, by the standard of reason, for the shirk of the polytheists or for the doubt of those who doubt. If anyone does so, his attitude is astonishing in the light of the order of the universe, the human soul and its nature, and the heart and intellect of a sound person.

At this point, another wave emerges in the river of this surah. In it, the position of those who deny is presented, and it is explained that these people reject the signs and proofs that lie scattered within this entire universe and within the human soul itself. By presenting the strange and bizarre position of these deniers, they are also given a severe warning. Before them are set the pictures of those deniers whose remains are scattered across the screen of human history, and from which it becomes evident that before the overwhelming power of Allah they have no standing at all. It is astonishing that they are not at all afraid of a seizure of this kind from Allah. Even while seeing the manifest truth, they remain firm in their rebellion. This wave shows that the deniers do not reject out of a lack of proofs; rather, their intention is not sound, and their hearts are not yet open to accepting the truth. The doors of their hearts are closed. Look at the words of the Qur'an:

"The state of the people is that there has not come to them any sign from among the signs of their Lord without their turning away from it. So now, when the truth has come to them, they have also denied it. Very well, soon there will reach them news of that which they have been mocking. Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, generations which had dominance in their own time? We established them on the earth in a way We have not established you, We sent down abundant rain upon them from the sky, and We made rivers flow beneath them, yet (they were ungrateful for the blessings). So We destroyed them for their sins and raised up after them other generations. O Prophet (ﷺ), even if We had sent down to you a book written on paper, and the people had touched it with their own hands, those who disbelieved would still say, 'This is nothing but clear magic.' They say, 'Why has no angel been sent down upon this prophet?' If We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided long ago, and then they would not have been given any respite. And if We had sent down an angel, We would have sent him in human form, and thus We would have caused them to be confused in the same doubt in which they are now confused."

O Muhammad (ﷺ), before you too, many messengers were mocked, but upon those who mocked them there ultimately came down the very reality at which they used to scoff. Say to them: Go about the earth and see what the end of those who denied was.

At this point a third wave rises. In this wave there is a true introduction to the majesty of divinity, expressed in this way: the Divine Being is the owner of the heavens and the earth and whatever is within them. Whatever remains settled in the darkness of the night and the brightness of the day belongs to Him. He is the Provider who feeds all, and He has no need of being fed in return from any quarter. For this reason, He alone is the Protector, and there is no other protector, and His servants ought to surrender themselves to Him alone. It is He who will punish the disobedient in the Hereafter. He is the one who holds the power over the well-being and the affliction of His servants, and He is capable of everything. He has complete control over His servants. He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.

After this whole preface, the wave now reaches its heights. After proof and argument between the Messenger and his people, a complete decision is pronounced. The people are warned to keep away from shirk, and it is declared that the Messenger is not responsible for their shirk. This proclamation is made in a voice of great strength and in a manner that is most decisive. Look at the words of the Qur'an:

"Ask them: To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: To Allah. He has prescribed mercy upon Himself. He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, there is no doubt about it. But those who have destroyed themselves are the ones who do not believe. To Him belongs whatever remains settled in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Say: Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds and is not fed? Say: I have been commanded that I should be the first to submit to Him, and, 'Do not be among the polytheists.' Say: If I disobey my Lord, I fear the punishment of a great day. Whoever is spared on that day, Allah has shown him great mercy, and that is the clear success. If Allah should afflict you with any harm, there is none who can remove it except Him, and if He should touch you with good, then He is capable of everything. He has complete control over His servants, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware. Ask them: What testimony is greatest? Say: Allah is witness between me and you. This Qur'an has been revealed to me by inspiration so that I may warn you and whoever it reaches. Do you indeed bear witness that there are other gods along with Allah? Say: I do not bear such witness. Say: He is only one God, and I am truly free of that shirk in which you are involved."

Now a fourth wave rises. In it, there is mention of the attitude of the People of the Book toward this new scripture, which the polytheists have denied. In this wave it is explained that shirk is a great injustice, and it is worse than all other injustices. In this wave, before the polytheists, the scene of the events that will befall them on the Day of Resurrection is presented. In this scene, the people of shirk question those whom they used to make partners with Allah, and those beings clearly deny their shirk. Therefore, the fabrications of this false invention are torn apart at their very roots. In this wave, the condition of the people of shirk is depicted. It becomes apparent that their natural faculties for accepting the truth are inactive. They are unable to benefit from the indications of faith, and therefore they do not believe. They do not find the proofs, because veils lie over their hearts, since their claim is that the Qur'an is merely a collection of ancient stories. In this wave they are told that they prevent others from accepting guidance and also flee from the Qur'an themselves, and in this way they cast themselves into destruction. Their state is depicted in this manner:

"The scene of that time, when they will stand upon the fire. At that time, their thought will be that they wish they could be returned to the world, and that they would not deny the signs of their Lord, and would be among the believers. But even if they are returned, they would again deny the Hereafter and the Return. Another aspect of the scene: when they are presented before their Lord, they will be questioned about their denial and rejection. Their condition will be that they bear their sins upon their shoulders individually. At the end of this wave, mention is made of their regret and remorse. In that meeting they gain nothing, and they reach the conclusion that the life of this world was mere play and amusement, and that the Hereafter alone is the everlasting life. Look at the words of the Qur'an:

'Those to whom We have given the Book recognize this as they recognize their own sons, without any doubt. But those who have ruined themselves do not believe. And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah, or denies His signs? Surely the wrongdoers will never prosper. On the day We gather them all and say to the polytheists, "Where are your partners whom you used to claim?", they will have no excuse except to say, "By our Lord, we were never polytheists." Look how they lie against themselves, and how all their fabricated gods will vanish from them. Among them are some who listen to you, but We have placed veils upon their hearts so that they do not comprehend it, and heaviness in their ears. Even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. To the point that when they come to you and dispute with you, those among them who have decided to deny say, "This is nothing but ancient tales." They prevent others from accepting this truth and themselves keep far from it, yet in reality they are preparing their own destruction, though they are unaware of it. If only you could see their condition when they are made to stand at the edge of the Fire. Then they will say, "Would that we could be sent back to the world, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers!" In truth, they will say this only because the reality which they had covered up will then be exposed before them. Otherwise, if they were returned to their former life, they would again do all that they were forbidden.'

They are indeed liars. Today they say that life is only this worldly life, and that we will never be raised again after death. If only you could see the scene when they are made to stand before their Lord. Then their Lord will ask them, "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, our Lord, this is indeed the truth." He will say, "Then taste the punishment for your denial." ... Lost are those who denied the meeting with Allah. When the Hour suddenly comes upon them, they will say, "Alas! How much we have neglected in this matter!" They will be carrying their burdens upon their backs. Behold how wretched is the burden they bear. The life of this world is only play and amusement; in truth, the abode of the Hereafter is better for those who wish to avoid loss. Will you not then use your reason?"

Now in this surah's river a fifth wave rises. In it the address turns to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He is consoled, and his grief and sorrow are removed. His worry was that people were denying him and the speech revealed to him. He is instructed to take as his model the conduct of the earlier prophets, who were denied, rejected, and tormented, until the help of Allah reached them. It is explained that this is the sunnah of Allah, and it does not change; yet the sunnah of Allah does not come before its appointed time. If you do not show patience in the face of their denial and rejection, then you may bring some miracle of your own, and consider this: if Allah's will had been so, He would have gathered them all upon guidance. Allah alone is the possessor of command and disposal, and His will required that those people accept the call to truth whose natural faculties had not yet become incapable of accepting the truth. As for those who are spiritually dead, with no spark of life remaining within them, they do not turn toward the signs of guidance and do not accept the truth. A day is certainly coming, and all of them will rise and be presented before it.

"O Muhammad, We know that the words these people fabricate cause you grief. Yet they do not deny you; rather, these wrongdoers are in fact denying the signs of Allah. Many messengers were denied before you, but they were patient over that denial and those torments inflicted upon them, until Our help reached them. No one has the power to alter the words of Allah, and you have already received news of what befell the earlier messengers. Nevertheless, if you find it unbearable to see these people's indifference, then if you have any strength, seek a tunnel in the earth or set a ladder to the sky and try to bring them some sign. If Allah had willed, He could have gathered them all upon guidance, so do not be among the ignorant. Only those who hear will respond to the call to truth; as for the dead, Allah will raise them from their graves, and then they will be returned."

In this surah the flow of speech moves in waves, in the manner of the examples we have placed before the reader. From those examples the temperament of this surah should be clear, and light is also thrown on its theme. Some of its waves are higher than those we have cited as examples, and in certain places their flow and clash are more fervent and intense. It is not possible for us to present a critical survey and introduction of this entire surah in these brief words. Nevertheless, its other aspect will be seen in the next paragraph.

Earlier we stated that this surah presents its central theme in a remarkably distinctive manner, because at every moment, in every stance and in every scene, it bears a beauty that dazzles the eyes. When a person observes its scenes, its effects and its allusions one after another, the human self makes them its own, binds all their effects to itself, and receives the light of guidance.

Now we place before the reader some verses in which these realities appear directly in the Qur'anic style, because however much we praise them through commentary, that is generally less beneficial than the direct study of the Qur'anic verses. The direct impact of the verses is of a different kind.

The exposition of the station of divinity (uluhiyyah), introducing people to their true Lord, and bringing people within the sphere of worship of Allah alone is the central theme and axis of this surah. Observe how the Holy Qur'an treats this theme on various occasions and in various stances.

At the moment of testimony and decisive stance, where the station of divinity firmly settles in the heart of the believer, and where this stance is made clear to opponents with great force and great certainty, the style of the Qur'an is as follows:

(Verse) ﴿2﴾:

"It is He who created you from clay, then decreed for you a term of life, and there is a further term appointed with Him, yet you are those who doubt."

After the cosmos, now a glimpse of human existence within this cosmos is shown. Earlier, the cosmos and the great phenomena arising in it, the night and the day, were presented for reflection. Within this lifeless cosmos, a living and magnificent creature, the human being, is presented for reflection: that Allah, by bringing about a transformation within lifeless and dark clay, created from it a living and fresh creature. Within the two glimpses there are two further glimpses: one, that a time is coming when this life will come to an end, and the other, that all these dead people will be gathered together in the place of assembly. All the dead and still people will be set in motion at once, and the Plain of Gathering will be established, in which there will be movement everywhere, just as clay is still and every living thing is moving. Between these dead and living there is a great difference and distance in their reality. The demand of all these scenes and phenomena was that the heart of a sound-natured person would be filled with faith, and that he would be certain of standing before Allah on a day. But the addressees of this surah, the people of disbelief, nonetheless doubt it. (Verse) ﴿Then you doubt﴾ (2:2): "yet you are those who doubt." The nature of the third glimpse is that it contains within itself all the preceding phenomena. In it is shown that this entire cosmos, this entire life, and especially the whole of humanity, falls within the sphere of Allah's dominion.

(آیت) ” نمبر 3 :

"And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth. He knows what you conceal and what you disclose, and He knows what you earn (of good or evil)."

He who created the heavens and the earth is the absolute ruler of the heavens and the earth. In this sovereignty He is unique. His sovereignty must be acknowledged over both the heavens and the earth. The majesty of Allah's sovereignty is fully operative in the heavens and the earth, in that the cosmic order (ناموس کائنات) established by Allah encompasses them completely, and they cannot disobey it. Likewise, it is Allah's will that the command, law and Shari'ah of Allah also operate within the life of human beings, because just as Allah created the heavens and the earth, He has also created man. At the time of his initial creation, man was brought into being from the dust of this earth. Within him were placed the characteristics by which he became a human being, and from this same earth his sustenance was arranged. Man, in terms of his physical creation as well, is subject to that law of nature which Allah has prescribed, in which the will of the individual human being has no role, nor does the will and intention of his mother and father have any role in it. The two of them do indeed come together, but they cannot breathe a soul into the child, nor can they bestow existence upon the fetus. This child, in accordance with all the laws of nature, completes the period of gestation and, in accordance with that natural order which the Lord of Majesty has ordained for him, emerges from the womb. He breathes the air which Allah has made according to His measures, and he breathes in the quantity and manner which the law of nature established by Allah has set out. His feeling of sorrow and pain, his sensation of hunger and thirst, his eating and drinking, and in general his remaining alive, all occur in exact conformity with the natural order. In these there is no role for his own will. In terms of his natural existence, there is no difference between man and the nature and order of the heavens and the earth.

Allah is the One who knows the secrets of man and also knows his outward affairs. Whatever deeds he performs, whether outward or hidden, Allah is well aware of all of them. Therefore, the truth is that he should also follow the order and law of Allah which He has prescribed for his volitional life. In both his thoughts and his life, which are bound within the cosmic order, and the life which is volitional, he should be subject to the Shari'ah of Allah, so that both lives are in harmony with one another. There should be no contradiction or conflict within these two lives, no practical clash, and these two orders should not collide and be shattered, such that in this universe and life there is a divine order while the volitional, legal and Shari'ah life is established on tyrannical (طاغوتی) and non-Islamic foundations.

Lesson No. 56 At a Glance:

After the opening of the Surah, this is another wave. The effects of the first wave were extremely far-reaching. It had filled this entire universe with the reality of the existence of God. Through the creation of the heavens and the earth and the manifestation of light and darkness alone, arguments were made for this reality. Then it was explained that Allah created a being like man from that dark matter, gave him a fixed time for the end of his life, and it was stated that there is also a fixed time for resurrection after death, the knowledge of which belongs to none but Allah. It was also made clear that the Divine Being knows all the actions and words of people. He knows what is hidden and what is apparent, and He is aware of their entire deeds.

The existence of God, which shines within the self and the horizons, is a unique and singular existence. There is no other existence like it, and there is no creator besides Allah. It is a full, luminous and extremely pervasive existence of truth. In the light of these signs and proofs, denying it is an extremely detestable act for which there is no authority, and such a denier will be considered unexcused.

Therefore, in this wave the position of the polytheists is presented in the light of that true existence: that these people are rejecting the call of Islam in circumstances where clear proofs of the Divine Being are plainly present in their selves and the horizons. Hence their position is extremely detestable and disliked. The conduct of these deniers is detestable even by the standard of their own perception and consciousness, because the Qur'an was presenting these proofs before them. Thus in the very first encounter the Holy Qur'an defeats them and implants this truth into the depths of people's nature, although apparently they are caught in obstinacy, while in reality they are displaying enmity.

In this era the Holy Qur'an presents a picture of their enmity, arrogance and obstinacy, sometimes in a highly threatening tone and with bitter words, and sometimes invites them thus: just consider the history of the outcomes of those who denied before. In it there are countless lessons and insights. At times it also places before them the end of those deniers and provides countless guidance and indications.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 4–6:

(Verses) No. 4 to 6.

These people adopted the stance of obstinacy and of insisting upon falsehood, although there was no shortage of proofs and signs which, on seeing them, they would have believed, nor was there a shortage of proofs and indications through which it would have become clear that the call of the Prophets is an extremely truthful call. It was not the case that there was any shortage of proofs for the truth of this call and its caller. Proofs and evidences for the existence of God were also present. In short, there was no shortage of these things among them; rather, what was lacking was that they would not submit by accepting. They insisted upon falsehood, harboured enmity towards the movement, and because of this turning away, the opportunities for reflection upon this religion and movement were lost to them.

(Verse) ﴿And never does there come to them any sign from among the signs of their Lord but that they turn away from it.﴾ (4)

"The condition of the people is that no sign from the signs of their Lord has come before them but that they have turned away from it." When the situation reaches the point where people deliberately turn away from the truth, although the proofs and signs are present and the realities have become as clear as the light of day before them, then at times warning and threat open their eyes. The eye is opened with a jolt and the windows of nature are opened, provided that the veils of pride and enmity do not intervene.

(Verse) ﴿So they have denied the truth when it came to them; but there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock.﴾ (5)

"So now, when the truth came to them, they also denied it. Very well, concerning that which they have continued to mock, certain things will reach them in time." The guidance that came from the Creator of the heavens and the earth was truth. It was truth from the One who creates light and darkness, who created man from clay, who is the ruler of the heavens as well as the earth, and who knows their open and hidden affairs. He knows whatever they earn. It is truth, and they have denied the truth. Now they insist upon this denial, turn away from the signs of God, and mock the Islamic call. Therefore, they should now await the outcome and the final news of this matter.

Now this is an extremely general threat and warning, for neither are its details given nor is any time fixed for this evil end. They are only given the impression that they should await this outcome at every moment. The punishment of God may come upon them at any time. The truth will become manifest to them, and they will see the punishment with their own eyes.

At this point of threat and warning, they are reminded and directed to look back and cast a glance to see what has been the end of those who denied in human history. Some of them were also aware of the fate of some of these. The story of the destruction of the people of 'Ad in al-Ahqaf and of the people of Thamud in al-Hijr was well known among them. When the Arabs travelled north in summer and south in winter, they would see the ruins of those peoples with their own eyes. The places where destruction came upon the people of Lut were also known to them, and the people living around those places were acquainted with them. Therefore, their attention is drawn here to these realities.

(Verse) ﴿Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established upon the earth in a way We have not established you, and We sent down upon them abundant rain from the sky and made rivers flow beneath them? Then We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them another generation.﴾ (6)

"Have they not seen how many such peoples We have destroyed before them, whose dominion was flourishing in their time? We gave them power on the earth such as We have not given you. We sent abundant rains upon them and made rivers flow beneath them (but they were ungrateful). So, in the end, We destroyed them for their sins and raised up after them other generations." Do these people not take lessons from the evil end of the past nations? God had granted those nations a very great power over this globe. He had provided them with the means of strength and sovereignty, and they were so advanced and powerful that there was no comparison between them and the Quraysh, the addressees of the Qur'an. Continuous rains fell upon them, their land was lush, and there was abundance of every kind of produce. Then what happened? They began to disobey their Lord. God seized them for their sins. He destroyed them and brought other nations into being in their place, and the authority over the earth was handed over to them. The earth did not mourn for those who departed, because the heirs of the earth were now other people. Look at how insignificant those deniers and turners-away have become. How light they are in the sight of God, and how light they are upon this earth. They were destroyed, annihilated and wiped out, and the earth did not even feel it. Nor did the earth remain empty; other nations filled that gap, and this earth kept revolving in such a way as though these perished nations had never inhabited it, and life continued in such a way as though the previous people had never been alive.

When God grants someone establishment upon this globe, those in power first of all forget this truth: that this authority has come to them by the will of God, and that it is a great trial for them. The trial is whether they use this authority in accordance with God's covenant and condition, and in it serve God alone and take guidance from Him alone, because He alone is the true owner of this authority, and man is only His vicegerent; or whether they assign to themselves the position of tyranny (taghut), take for themselves the powers of God, and use those powers not as vicegerents but as self-willed owners.

This is the reality that people forget, unless someone has been protected by God. When people forget this reality, they begin to disregard God's covenant and the conditions of being His vicegerent on earth, and they go against the Sunnah of God. At first they do not sense what the consequences of this deviation will be, and so corruption begins to appear among them gradually. They have no awareness of it at all, until they reach the appointed time and the promise of God comes. Their ends then vary: sometimes such a punishment comes upon them that they are uprooted and thrown away from the root. This punishment sometimes comes from the sky and sometimes from below the earth. Many nations of the world were destroyed through this punishment, and sometimes this punishment takes the form of famine and drought. Fruits and produce perish, and people begin to die of hunger. Several nations of the world have suffered this punishment. Sometimes they fight one another, and each becomes a punishment for the other; some afflict others with suffering, some annihilate others, some torment others, and some do not grant security to others. In this way their strength and grandeur come to an end, and God then imposes upon them other of His servants, who are either obedient to God or disobedient, and they break their power and deprive them of the supreme authority upon which they had been established. After this, God grants establishment upon the earth to some new people, so that now the period of their trial may begin. Thus the Sunnah of God continues, and among the nations of the world, the fortunate nations are those who comprehend the Sunnah of God, who understand that this is a trial, who keep the covenant of God. The unfortunate nations are those who are heedless of this reality and begin to suppose that this authority was granted to them because of their own knowledge and excellence, or by some stratagem and planning, or that it came to them by chance without any design.

What deceives people is that they see a rebellious, wicked, corrupt and atheistic person who is the supreme ruler upon this globe, and no accountability from God is being imposed upon him. They become disheartened, but such people act hastily. They see the beginning of the path, they see the middle part too, but when God's punishment comes upon such rebels, they are annihilated and only stories and tales remain about them, and then the reality becomes visible. The Qur'an presents some manifestations of the outcome awaiting such people, so that such heedless rebels may come to their senses, because such people are so absorbed in their individual circumstances that they cannot see the destination and their final end. These people can only see this brief life and regard it as the final goal.

This verse of the Qur'an, "Then We destroyed them for their sins" (6:6), and other similar verses, have been repeated again and again. In such verses an unchangeable Sunnah of God is pointed out, and in them the Islamic view of history is explained with great clarity.

These verses state that the Sunnah of God is that wicked people are, in the end, destroyed and ruined because of their wickedness. This destruction and ruin comes upon them from God, and this Sunnah is continuously in operation in this universe forever, even though an individual may not be able to understand it in his brief life, or this destruction may not come within the lifetime of a limited and specific generation. But it is such a Sunnah of God that when crimes and wickedness become very widespread in a people, and the entire system of life is founded upon wickedness and crime, then punishment from God certainly comes. The Islamic view of history is that the real and effective factor in the rise and fall of nations is that when wickedness and crime permeate their body, they become subject to ruin and destruction. This ruin comes either through heavenly calamities, as happened in ancient history, or through a very gradual natural decline, just as a body falls into temporary decay when it sinks up to its ears in wickedness and crime.

In modern human history we have before us many examples of such decline, in which nations were destroyed through moral laxity, immorality and vice, indulgence, extravagance and frivolity. For instance, the destruction of Greece had these very causes. After that, the decline and fall of the Romans had these same causes. These nations, despite their greatness, vanished in such a way that only their stories and tales remained. Within advanced modern nations too, the causes of this great destruction and decline have begun to appear; for instance, the decline of France and Britain has begun, although in material, military and technical power they are at the summit, and are extremely advanced and wealthy.

This moral dimension of history is absent from the view of those who write material interpretations of history and narratives of the rise and fall of nations, because for those with a material outlook the moral elements remain hidden from the very beginning. The fundamental principle, that is the Sunnah of God, is hidden from their sight. Those who interpret and comment upon history solely from a material point of view, and make extremely ridiculous statements regarding the rise and fall of nations, are mistaken. Whereas a reasonable interpretation of the events after the rise and fall of nations can only be made from the doctrinal and moral standpoint.

The historical outlook of Islam is extremely comprehensive, realistic and true, and because of this comprehensiveness it gives importance to the material factor as well, and it regards material decline among the causes of the fall of nations. Nevertheless, Islam also takes into account other factors, which only the opponents deny. Islam first of all establishes the Sunnah of God and the decree of God as the principal agent.
