Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 4–6:

(Verses) No. 4 to 6.

These people adopted the stance of obstinacy and of insisting upon falsehood, although there was no shortage of proofs and signs which, on seeing them, they would have believed, nor was there a shortage of proofs and indications through which it would have become clear that the call of the Prophets is an extremely truthful call. It was not the case that there was any shortage of proofs for the truth of this call and its caller. Proofs and evidences for the existence of God were also present. In short, there was no shortage of these things among them; rather, what was lacking was that they would not submit by accepting. They insisted upon falsehood, harboured enmity towards the movement, and because of this turning away, the opportunities for reflection upon this religion and movement were lost to them.

(Verse) ﴿And never does there come to them any sign from among the signs of their Lord but that they turn away from it.﴾ (4)

"The condition of the people is that no sign from the signs of their Lord has come before them but that they have turned away from it." When the situation reaches the point where people deliberately turn away from the truth, although the proofs and signs are present and the realities have become as clear as the light of day before them, then at times warning and threat open their eyes. The eye is opened with a jolt and the windows of nature are opened, provided that the veils of pride and enmity do not intervene.

(Verse) ﴿So they have denied the truth when it came to them; but there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock.﴾ (5)

"So now, when the truth came to them, they also denied it. Very well, concerning that which they have continued to mock, certain things will reach them in time." The guidance that came from the Creator of the heavens and the earth was truth. It was truth from the One who creates light and darkness, who created man from clay, who is the ruler of the heavens as well as the earth, and who knows their open and hidden affairs. He knows whatever they earn. It is truth, and they have denied the truth. Now they insist upon this denial, turn away from the signs of God, and mock the Islamic call. Therefore, they should now await the outcome and the final news of this matter.

Now this is an extremely general threat and warning, for neither are its details given nor is any time fixed for this evil end. They are only given the impression that they should await this outcome at every moment. The punishment of God may come upon them at any time. The truth will become manifest to them, and they will see the punishment with their own eyes.

At this point of threat and warning, they are reminded and directed to look back and cast a glance to see what has been the end of those who denied in human history. Some of them were also aware of the fate of some of these. The story of the destruction of the people of 'Ad in al-Ahqaf and of the people of Thamud in al-Hijr was well known among them. When the Arabs travelled north in summer and south in winter, they would see the ruins of those peoples with their own eyes. The places where destruction came upon the people of Lut were also known to them, and the people living around those places were acquainted with them. Therefore, their attention is drawn here to these realities.

(Verse) ﴿Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established upon the earth in a way We have not established you, and We sent down upon them abundant rain from the sky and made rivers flow beneath them? Then We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them another generation.﴾ (6)

"Have they not seen how many such peoples We have destroyed before them, whose dominion was flourishing in their time? We gave them power on the earth such as We have not given you. We sent abundant rains upon them and made rivers flow beneath them (but they were ungrateful). So, in the end, We destroyed them for their sins and raised up after them other generations." Do these people not take lessons from the evil end of the past nations? God had granted those nations a very great power over this globe. He had provided them with the means of strength and sovereignty, and they were so advanced and powerful that there was no comparison between them and the Quraysh, the addressees of the Qur'an. Continuous rains fell upon them, their land was lush, and there was abundance of every kind of produce. Then what happened? They began to disobey their Lord. God seized them for their sins. He destroyed them and brought other nations into being in their place, and the authority over the earth was handed over to them. The earth did not mourn for those who departed, because the heirs of the earth were now other people. Look at how insignificant those deniers and turners-away have become. How light they are in the sight of God, and how light they are upon this earth. They were destroyed, annihilated and wiped out, and the earth did not even feel it. Nor did the earth remain empty; other nations filled that gap, and this earth kept revolving in such a way as though these perished nations had never inhabited it, and life continued in such a way as though the previous people had never been alive.

When God grants someone establishment upon this globe, those in power first of all forget this truth: that this authority has come to them by the will of God, and that it is a great trial for them. The trial is whether they use this authority in accordance with God's covenant and condition, and in it serve God alone and take guidance from Him alone, because He alone is the true owner of this authority, and man is only His vicegerent; or whether they assign to themselves the position of tyranny (taghut), take for themselves the powers of God, and use those powers not as vicegerents but as self-willed owners.

This is the reality that people forget, unless someone has been protected by God. When people forget this reality, they begin to disregard God's covenant and the conditions of being His vicegerent on earth, and they go against the Sunnah of God. At first they do not sense what the consequences of this deviation will be, and so corruption begins to appear among them gradually. They have no awareness of it at all, until they reach the appointed time and the promise of God comes. Their ends then vary: sometimes such a punishment comes upon them that they are uprooted and thrown away from the root. This punishment sometimes comes from the sky and sometimes from below the earth. Many nations of the world were destroyed through this punishment, and sometimes this punishment takes the form of famine and drought. Fruits and produce perish, and people begin to die of hunger. Several nations of the world have suffered this punishment. Sometimes they fight one another, and each becomes a punishment for the other; some afflict others with suffering, some annihilate others, some torment others, and some do not grant security to others. In this way their strength and grandeur come to an end, and God then imposes upon them other of His servants, who are either obedient to God or disobedient, and they break their power and deprive them of the supreme authority upon which they had been established. After this, God grants establishment upon the earth to some new people, so that now the period of their trial may begin. Thus the Sunnah of God continues, and among the nations of the world, the fortunate nations are those who comprehend the Sunnah of God, who understand that this is a trial, who keep the covenant of God. The unfortunate nations are those who are heedless of this reality and begin to suppose that this authority was granted to them because of their own knowledge and excellence, or by some stratagem and planning, or that it came to them by chance without any design.

What deceives people is that they see a rebellious, wicked, corrupt and atheistic person who is the supreme ruler upon this globe, and no accountability from God is being imposed upon him. They become disheartened, but such people act hastily. They see the beginning of the path, they see the middle part too, but when God's punishment comes upon such rebels, they are annihilated and only stories and tales remain about them, and then the reality becomes visible. The Qur'an presents some manifestations of the outcome awaiting such people, so that such heedless rebels may come to their senses, because such people are so absorbed in their individual circumstances that they cannot see the destination and their final end. These people can only see this brief life and regard it as the final goal.

This verse of the Qur'an, "Then We destroyed them for their sins" (6:6), and other similar verses, have been repeated again and again. In such verses an unchangeable Sunnah of God is pointed out, and in them the Islamic view of history is explained with great clarity.

These verses state that the Sunnah of God is that wicked people are, in the end, destroyed and ruined because of their wickedness. This destruction and ruin comes upon them from God, and this Sunnah is continuously in operation in this universe forever, even though an individual may not be able to understand it in his brief life, or this destruction may not come within the lifetime of a limited and specific generation. But it is such a Sunnah of God that when crimes and wickedness become very widespread in a people, and the entire system of life is founded upon wickedness and crime, then punishment from God certainly comes. The Islamic view of history is that the real and effective factor in the rise and fall of nations is that when wickedness and crime permeate their body, they become subject to ruin and destruction. This ruin comes either through heavenly calamities, as happened in ancient history, or through a very gradual natural decline, just as a body falls into temporary decay when it sinks up to its ears in wickedness and crime.

In modern human history we have before us many examples of such decline, in which nations were destroyed through moral laxity, immorality and vice, indulgence, extravagance and frivolity. For instance, the destruction of Greece had these very causes. After that, the decline and fall of the Romans had these same causes. These nations, despite their greatness, vanished in such a way that only their stories and tales remained. Within advanced modern nations too, the causes of this great destruction and decline have begun to appear; for instance, the decline of France and Britain has begun, although in material, military and technical power they are at the summit, and are extremely advanced and wealthy.

This moral dimension of history is absent from the view of those who write material interpretations of history and narratives of the rise and fall of nations, because for those with a material outlook the moral elements remain hidden from the very beginning. The fundamental principle, that is the Sunnah of God, is hidden from their sight. Those who interpret and comment upon history solely from a material point of view, and make extremely ridiculous statements regarding the rise and fall of nations, are mistaken. Whereas a reasonable interpretation of the events after the rise and fall of nations can only be made from the doctrinal and moral standpoint.

(Verse 7)

These people do not deny the signs of God because there is some weakness in the proof of their truth, or some complexity in grasping them, or because different minds think about them in different ways. Rather, they deny them out of obstinacy, stubborn arrogance and open hostility. They have resolved to reject this truth before even considering the evidence and argument.

Even if the Qur'an had descended in the form of written pages from the sky, which they could touch with their hands and see with their eyes, and had not come to the Messenger (ﷺ) through revelation for him to recite, they would still say about this tangible, observed reality: ﴿This is nothing but clear magic.﴾ (6:7)

This is such a repugnant picture of these people that human nature recoils from it. It is a picture which, upon seeing it, every person moves forward to erase, because there is no need for debate, argument or reasoning with such people. There are two benefits, indeed several benefits, in this manner of portrayal. (This manner of depiction is such that the Qur'an presents a commonly observed example before them.)

The first benefit is that the Qur'an itself places before these people their own repugnant and objectionable position, and shows them to see how ugly their picture is. For example, if someone hands a mirror to a person of repulsive appearance and says, "Look, this is what you are," and that person, seeing his own face, becomes ashamed.

Along with this, another benefit of this portrayal is that through it the hearts of the believers are stirred, and they defeat the aims of the polytheists. They confront the deniers' denial, and their own hearts remain firm upon the truth. They are not influenced by the atmosphere in which there is denial, mockery, sedition and persecution from every side. By this it is also intended to show that God is extremely forbearing, and that He does not seize quickly those who reject and deny, even though they deny in a most detestable manner and are immersed in open hostility. All these matters are weapons and provisions for the Muslims in the struggle that exists between the community of Muslims and the polytheists.

After this, the Qur'an presents before them some proposals that came from the people of polytheism. From these it becomes clear how cunning these people are in their malice and hostility, and how shallow their thinking is. They propose that if Muhammad (ﷺ) is truly a Messenger, then there should be an angel with him at the time of his preaching, who would continually confirm him. After mentioning this proposal, it is also criticized: what is the flaw in it? First, these people are not even acquainted with the nature of the angels. Second, they are also unaware of the sunnah (way) of God regarding the sending of angels. Then it is explained that it is a great mercy of God that He is not sending angels and does not accept their proposal.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 8–9 (part 1 of 3):

(Verse) "No. 8 to 9."

This proposal came from the polytheists, and before these polytheists several nations had also made the same proposal. Every nation demanded from its Messenger the descent of angels. In other places the Qur'an has presented such demands, and here this proposal is refuted with arguments. Regarding this proposal, it is appropriate that we present all the facts here as far as possible.

The first fact about this is that the polytheists of Arabia did not deny Allah. Rather, they demanded a clear proof on this matter, by which it would become known that the Messenger ﷺ is a sent prophet and that the book he recites before them is revealed by Allah. In this regard they gave other proposals. The Qur'an has mentioned these proposals in several places. For example, in Surah al-Isra these proposals are mentioned. In it, alongside this proposal, other proposals are also given, which show the obstinacy and enmity of these people. Apart from enmity, their own proposal is clear evidence of their shallow understanding, because these people have neither understood this order of the universe well nor do they understand true values. In Surah al-Isra it comes:

(Verse) "And they said, 'We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, (90) or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly, (91) or you cause the heaven to fall upon us in pieces as you claim, or you bring Allah and the angels before us face to face, (92) or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky, and we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book which we can read.'" Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?" (93) And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them was only their saying, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?" (94) Say: "If there were angels walking securely upon the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger." (95)

These proposals and demands are such that they display, on one hand, their obstinacy, and on the other, their ignorance. For the book of the conduct of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was open before them. They knew him well through a long experience, and from his character they knew that he was truthful and trustworthy, and it was these very people who had given him the title "al-Amin" (the Trustworthy). Despite their severe ideological differences with him, these people would keep their trusts with the Messenger ﷺ. When he migrated, he handed over the trusts that were still in his custody to his paternal cousin Hazrat Ali ؓ, although they had so much opposition with him that they were plotting his murder. His trustworthiness and integrity were as well-established as his truthfulness, because when he first gave them open invitation on Mount Safa, that was when Allah's command came that he should begin open proclamation of the call. On that occasion he asked them: "If I give you news of something important, will you confirm it?" And they all together replied: "You are indeed a most truthful man." If these people only wanted to know whether he was truthful or not, his past was itself a proof and argument for them. They knew that he was a most truthful man. In this same Surah it will come that Allah Himself says that these people do not reject you, but they reject Allah.

(Verse) "We know indeed that what they say grieves you; but it is not you whom they deny, rather it is the signs of Allah that the wrongdoers reject." (33)

The aim of these people was to refuse. This refusal was only due to enmity and arrogance. As far as the truthfulness of the Messenger ﷺ is concerned, there was no doubt about it in anyone's mind.

The fact is that for the Arabs there was a great testimony within the Qur'an itself. This testimony was greater than the proofs they were demanding. The Qur'an itself was a witness. The style of its expression and its contents also bore witness that it is from Allah. These people were not deniers of the Divine Being, and they too were aware of the inner testimony of the Qur'an. By the literary and linguistic taste they possessed, they knew that human beings have a limit to their literary and linguistic ability. They also knew that the Qur'an is beyond human limits. Those who have artistic and literary taste know this truth better than those who lack literary taste. Anyone in the world who has any taste for styles of speech (whether Muslim or non-Muslim) knows that the style of the Qur'an is far above human capability; humans cannot reach that level. Only a person who is an opponent, who is perceiving a truth but hiding it in his heart due to enmity, can deny this reality. Moreover, the concepts that the Qur'an has presented within this excellent style, the style in which it conveys these concepts and beliefs to the human soul, differs greatly from the human psychological mode of expression; the style of the Qur'an is unique and miraculous. The deep consciousness of the Arabs and the inner state of their psychology was such that they accepted this reality. Their circumstances and sayings also clearly show that they had no doubt that this Qur'an is from Allah.

It is also well known that the demands they made of the Messenger ﷺ were not because they sought a proof for acceptance, but rather it was their obstinacy. It was a manner through which they wanted to show that they were firm in their stubbornness, and they were making these demands purely out of enmity and refusal to accept. Allah said:

(Verse) "And even if We had sent down to you a written book on paper, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, 'This is nothing but clear magic.'" (7)

The second fact is that the Arabs did accept angels, and their demand was that an angel should descend upon the Messenger ﷺ and, as he preached, it should confirm and support him. But it did not occur to them what the reality and nature of the angels is. They were utterly confused in their belief and conception about this creation. They did not know what the relationship of the angels with their Lord is, or what their relationship is with this earth and its inhabitants. The Qur'an has mentioned several examples of the intellectual confusion of the Arabs, and it has also described their idolatrous notions regarding the angels. The Qur'an has corrected all these intellectual errors so that these people might become holders of a pure and clean belief and be guided on the right path. Regarding the universe and the creatures living in it, the Qur'an also gave correct understanding. In this respect, Islam nourished reason and consciousness in the same way that it gave correct thinking to the heart and conscience, and on the foundation of this correct thinking it also corrected the deeds and conduct of people.

The Qur'an has discussed several aspects of the Arabs' superstitions and false beliefs, showing how far they held false views. For example, they believed that the angels are daughters of Allah, although Allah is far above and exalted beyond such a notion. They also believed that these angels possess the authority of intercession that cannot be refused. The truth is that most of the idols prevalent among the Arabs were built on the concept of these angels, and this is confirmed by their notion and demand that an angel who supports and confirms should descend upon the Messenger ﷺ.

The Qur'an corrected their crooked thinking in Surah al-Najm as follows:

(Verse) "Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, (19) and Manat, the third, the other? (20) Is for you the male and for Him the female? (21) That, then, is an unjust division. (22) They are not but names you have named them, you and your forefathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow not except assumption and what the souls desire, although there has already come to them guidance from their Lord. (23) Or is there for man whatever he wishes? (24) So to Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first life. (25) And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves. (26) Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with names of females. (27) And they have no knowledge of it; they follow not except assumption, and indeed assumption avails not against the truth at all. (28)" (53:19–28)

Furthermore, in these two verses the Qur'an has also corrected their second crooked notion regarding the nature of the angels. In other Surahs as well, their intellectual errors were corrected:

(Verse) "And they say, 'Why has an angel not been sent down upon him?' Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved." (8)

It is explained here regarding those among the creatures of Allah who hold this view. These people propose that Allah should send down an angel along with the Qur'an. But Allah's practice regarding the descent of angels is that when they descend, they destroy the people who have denied a prophet, and they then carry out Allah's commands regarding that destruction. If Allah had accepted this proposal and demand of the polytheists of Arabia, the matter would have been decided, and they would have been destroyed. After that they would not be given any respite. Do these people wish to be saved from a great destruction and punishment? Thus, in the context of the discourse, it is directly made clear to them that Allah is giving them respite and dealing with them with great mercy and forbearance. This is because they do not understand even their own benefit, and they are completely unaware of Allah's practice. They are so immersed in this ignorance that it may be that their very lives would be ruined in this way. Because of this ignorance, they continue to deny Allah's mercy, flee far from guidance, and keep making demands for proofs, miracles, and the descent of angels. Another aspect of correcting their shallow understanding is:

(Verse) "And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have covered over them what they [currently] cover." (9)

"If We had sent down an angel, We would have surely made the matter decided, and then they would not have been reprieved. And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have covered them with the same confusion which they are already covering." (Qur'an 6:8–9) — hmm, that is not the task; let me translate the passage as given.

"If We had sent down an angel, We would still have sent him in human form, and thus We would have plunged them into the same doubt in which they now are." Their demand was that Allah send down an angel to His Messenger, and that this angel attest to the claim of prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. But the question is: angels are a creation entirely distinct from humans. They have a special nature and constitution, the knowledge of which belongs only to Allah. These angels (as their Creator informs us about them) cannot walk on this earth in their present constitution, since they are not inhabitants of this earth. However, if they perform some duty concerning humans on this earth, they come here by taking on human form, such as the duty of conveying the message of prophethood and destroying those who deny, and so on. Or the duty of consoling and encouraging the believers, or the duty of killing the enemies of the Muslims, or other such duties which Allah directs them to carry out, and in carrying them out they do not disobey Allah's guidance even to the extent of an atom's weight.

Even if Allah sends an angel to attest to the Messenger, he would appear before the people only in the form of a human being. He would never come in the original form of the angels. And when the angel comes in human form, they would still be afflicted with the same doubt and the same perplexity would befall them. They are already afflicted with this perplexity, although what Muhammad ﷺ says to them is in summary: "I am Muhammad, you know me well. I have been sent by Allah as a Messenger so that I may warn you of an evil end and give you the good news of a good end." But if an angel came and appeared in the form of a man they did not know, and said: "I am an angel, and Allah has sent me to attest to the Messenger of God, Muhammad ﷺ," then they would see that this person is just a man like themselves. Obviously, in that case too the same doubt would befall them. In short, if an angel came in the form of a man, they would still be afflicted with the same doubt they were already afflicted with, and they would be unable to say anything certain.

Thus in these verses Allah shows how ignorant these people are about the realities of the universe and how unaware they are of the Divine way (sunnah), while being themselves extremely hostile and obstinate without any knowledge or justification, entirely without proof.

The third truth which these verses create in human thinking is: what are the basic components of the Islamic conception of life? Among these components are all the phenomena of nature which Islam guides a Muslim to perceive and to bring his life into harmony with. Also included among these basic components is the unseen world (ʿālam al-ghayb), which includes the angels. Islam has included in the basic elements of faith that you will believe in the angels as well. Faith is not complete without belief in the angels: belief in Allah, belief in the angels, belief in the books, belief in the messengers, belief in the Last Day, and belief in good and bad destiny.

In the first volume of Ẓilāl al-Qur'ān, when we explained the opening verses of Surah al-Baqarah, we discussed the topic whose summary is that belief in the unseen brings a great revolution into human life. A person goes beyond the limited sphere of the perceptible world and believes that there is another world which we do not know. Although we cannot conceive of it, it is undoubtedly and unquestionably coming. This conception lifts a person out of the perceptible sphere of animals and brings him into the sphere of human perception; and those who close the door to going beyond the perceptible for humans drag humans down from the station of humanity and take them back into the animal sphere, and they call this progressivism. In this surah, when we speak of the unseen world, we will further clarify this point, under the commentary on the verse "with Him are the keys of the unseen," God willing.

In the Islamic conception of the unseen world, there is a creation that is not visible, and that is the angels. The Qur'an has mentioned some of the attributes of this creation, which is sufficient for a general conception of them, and the conduct a person has towards the angels within his own limits should be based on this.

The angels are a creation among the creatures of Allah; at all times they are ready in obedience and servitude to Allah. They are absolutely obedient; they are close to Allah. We do not fully know the nature of how they are close to Allah.

[Quranic verses 21:26–28, 40:7, 39:75, 39:71–73, 66:6 (as quoted), 3:124–126, 61:? etc.]

"And [remember] when your Lord inspired the angels, 'I am with you, so strengthen those who believe. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, so strike [them] upon the necks and strike every finger of them.'"

These angels are also occupied with the affairs of the believers. They glorify Allah, and they constantly seek forgiveness for those who are believers, and they supplicate for them with such devotion as a most loving person supplicates for his beloved.

(Verse) "Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify the praise of their Lord and believe in Him and seek forgiveness for those who believe: 'Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire. Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses and descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And protect them from evil deeds; and whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day, You have had mercy upon him. And that is the great achievement.'" (40:7–9)

When angels take the souls of the believers, they give them the good news of Paradise, and they receive them with glad tidings, and in the Hereafter they will honour them with greetings and salutations.

(Verse) "Those whose souls the angels take in a state of purity, saying, 'Peace be upon you; enter Paradise for what you used to do.'" (16:32)

(Verse) "Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses and descendants; and the angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], 'Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.'" (13:23–24)

Among their duties is also that they will receive the disbelievers in the Hereafter with a humiliating manner, and in the struggle between belief and disbelief in this world they fight against the disbelievers, and when they take the souls of the disbelievers, they take them with severity, torment and in a humiliating manner.

(Verse) "If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are extending their hands [saying], 'Bring out your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and were arrogant toward His verses.'" (6:93)

(Verse) "So how will it be when the angels take them, striking their faces and their backs?" (47:27)

From the time Allah created Adam, the father of mankind, there has been a special relationship between the angels and humans, and this continues throughout life and will continue until the Day of Resurrection, as is well known from the excerpts of the Quranic verses mentioned above. The relationship between the angels and the human world has been discussed at several places in the Holy Quran, and Surah al-Baqarah gives its full detail.

(Verse) "And [remember] when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority (khalifah).' They said, 'Will You place upon it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?' He said, 'Indeed, I know that which you do not know.' And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, 'Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.' They said, 'Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise.' He said, 'O Adam, inform them of their names.' And when he had informed them of their names, He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal?' And [remember] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers." (2:30–34)

This is a vast field in which the life of humans and the life of the higher realm are connected, and because of this connection a kind of expansiveness arises in human thought, and a person can perceive the realities of this universe from a broad perspective. His psychological awareness becomes wide and the scope of his intellectual activity opens up, and this breadth of thought and vision gives a Muslim a comprehensive Islamic outlook. The Holy Quran presents this vast and observable universe to man in such a way that its final connection is with that vast field of the unseen world.

The world of the unseen is a vast world and an open field. Those who want to close the doors of the unseen upon man commit a most vile enmity against him. They want to confine the human world within his extremely limited conception, indeed within the realm of the perceptible, and want to include him in the world of animals, whereas Allah bestowed honour and nobility upon man by granting him the power of reflection. By this power of reflection, man can perceive things of which animals and beasts are deprived. Through this capacity, man attains abundance of knowledge and recognition, and his awareness becomes extremely wide. Through his intellect and his heart he reaches the expanses of the higher realm; he acquires pure morals, and with his being he travels through the luminous higher world.

Despite the ignorance in which the Arabs were immersed, and in which their conception of life was based on extremely wrong principles, they were far more advanced than the scientific ignorance of the modern age. The followers of this modern ignorance mock the unseen world and consider belief in such unseen matters to be unscientific and non-scientific. They place the unseen world on one pan of the scale and the world of science on the other, which is a most mistaken comparison. I will address the refutation of this notion under the verse (With Him are the keys of the unseen), because this claim of modern ignorance is one for which no proof can be produced according to the principles of science, nor can any proof be presented for it in religion. Here we will only make a brief point about the existence of the angels.

We ask the scientists only this: those who deny the angels, what scientific principle do they have for their denial? Why do they remove the existence of the angels from the realm of conception and affirmation? Let them state any scientific formula by which they would be compelled to hold the belief that the angels do not exist.

The condition of their science is such that it is unable even to affirm or deny the existence of beings on other celestial bodies which are present on this earth, let alone those bodies whose atmosphere, chemical and physical composition and distance differ from the earth and whose atmospheres are different. The question is: on what principle do they deny those other worlds, when they have no proof for the negation of the existence of the angels?

We do not seek a judgment from them about our beliefs, nor do we seek any argument from them about the word of Allah. We seek from them an assessment of that knowledge and science of theirs which they have made into a deity. In reply to this question they have nothing but obstinacy. Their science, which inclines them to deny the unseen world and the angels, is rendered speechless by this question, and the denial is mere denial only because these realms are hidden behind the veil of the unseen.

In truth, the very science due to which they deny the unseen world and the angels is what definitively establishes the unseen world; indeed, that science has in a way transformed the unseen world into the observable world and has revealed many things that were previously among the hidden matters. Today we are seeing those hidden matters.

This discussion concludes with a mention of the end suffered by all those who mocked the messengers throughout human history. Then those who denied were invited to study, in human history, those places of slaughter in which the punishments of their predecessors came. Let them travel about this earth and observe the end of the deniers. These events speak, as it were, in the language of the present state: what has been the end of those who deny and mock?

Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And protect them from evil deeds; and whoever You protect from evil deeds that Day, You have had mercy upon him. And that is the great achievement.'" (40:7–9)

When angels take the souls of the believers, they give them the good news of Paradise, and they receive them with glad tidings, and in the Hereafter they will honour them with greetings and salutations.

(Verse) "Those whose souls the angels take in a state of purity, saying, 'Peace be upon you; enter Paradise for what you used to do.'" (16:32)

(Verse) "Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses and descendants; and the angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], 'Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.'" (13:23–24)

Among their duties is also that they will receive the disbelievers in the Hereafter with a humiliating manner, and in the struggle between belief and disbelief in this world they fight against the disbelievers, and when they take the souls of the disbelievers, they take them with severity, torment and in a humiliating manner.

(Verse) "If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are extending their hands [saying], 'Bring out your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and were arrogant toward His verses.'" (6:93)

(Verse) "So how will it be when the angels take them, striking their faces and their backs?" (47:27)

From the time Allah created Adam, the father of mankind, there has been a special relationship between the angels and humans, and this continues throughout life and will continue until the Day of Resurrection, as is well known from the excerpts of the Quranic verses mentioned above. The relationship between the angels and the human world has been discussed at several places in the Holy Quran, and Surah al-Baqarah gives its full detail.

(Verse) "And [remember] when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority (khalifah).' They said, 'Will You place upon it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?' He said, 'Indeed, I know that which you do not know.' And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, 'Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.' They said, 'Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise.' He said, 'O Adam, inform them of their names.' And when he had informed them of their names, He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal?' And [remember] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers." (2:30–34)

This is a vast field in which the life of humans and the life of the higher realm are connected, and because of this connection a kind of expansiveness arises in human thought, and a person can perceive the realities of this universe from a broad perspective. His psychological awareness becomes wide and the scope of his intellectual activity opens up, and this breadth of thought and vision gives a Muslim a comprehensive Islamic outlook. The Holy Quran presents this vast and observable universe to man in such a way that its final connection is with that vast field of the unseen world.

The world of the unseen is a vast world and an open field. Those who want to close the doors of the unseen upon man commit a most vile enmity against him. They want to confine the human world within his extremely limited conception, indeed within the realm of the perceptible, and want to include him in the world of animals, whereas Allah bestowed honour and nobility upon man by granting him the power of reflection. By this power of reflection, man can perceive things of which animals and beasts are deprived. Through this capacity, man attains abundance of knowledge and recognition, and his awareness becomes extremely wide. Through his intellect and his heart he reaches the expanses of the higher realm; he acquires pure morals, and with his being he travels through the luminous higher world.

Despite the ignorance in which the Arabs were immersed, and in which their conception of life was based on extremely wrong principles, they were far more advanced than the scientific ignorance of the modern age. The followers of this modern ignorance mock the unseen world and consider belief in such unseen matters to be unscientific and non-scientific. They place the unseen world on one pan of the scale and the world of science on the other, which is a most mistaken comparison. I will address the refutation of this notion under the verse (With Him are the keys of the unseen), because this claim of modern ignorance is one for which no proof can be produced according to the principles of science, nor can any proof be presented for it in religion. Here we will only make a brief point about the existence of the angels.

We ask the scientists only this: those who deny the angels, what scientific principle do they have for their denial? Why do they remove the existence of the angels from the realm of conception and affirmation? Let them state any scientific formula by which they would be compelled to hold the belief that the angels do not exist.

The condition of their science is such that it is unable even to affirm or deny the existence of beings on other celestial bodies which are present on this earth, let alone those bodies whose atmosphere, chemical and physical composition and distance differ from the earth and whose atmospheres are different. The question is: on what principle do they deny those other worlds, when they have no proof for the negation of the existence of the angels?

We do not seek a judgment from them about our beliefs, nor do we seek any argument from them about the word of Allah. We seek from them an assessment of that knowledge and science of theirs which they have made into a deity. In reply to this question they have nothing but obstinacy. Their science, which inclines them to deny the unseen world and the angels, is rendered speechless by this question, and the denial is mere denial only because these realms are hidden behind the veil of the unseen.

In truth, the very science due to which they deny the unseen world and the angels is what definitively establishes the unseen world; indeed, that science has in a way transformed the unseen world into the observable world and has revealed many things that were previously among the hidden matters. Today we are seeing those hidden matters.

This discussion concludes with a mention of the end suffered by all those who mocked the messengers throughout human history. Then those who denied were invited to study, in human history, those places of slaughter in which the punishments of their predecessors came. Let them travel about this earth and observe the end of the deniers. These events speak, as it were, in the language of the present state: what has been the end of those who deny and mock?

**Verses 10–11**

This is a glimpse that comes after the disbelievers' turning away and obstinacy, and after their foolish and ignorant demands. Had Allah not, in His mercy, declined to accept their challenge and their demands by destroying them, they would have perished. At this point, this glimpse is intended to serve two purposes.

The first purpose is to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that the sorrow in his heart may be lifted. Because of the turning away and mockery of those who opposed him, and their persistent obstinacy, the Prophet (ﷺ) was greatly distressed. Through this, the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ) would be reassured that the final outcome for those who deny and mock is ultimately ruin. The Prophet (ﷺ) is being taught that this attitude is not a unique matter in the history of the call and the history of the messengers. The same attitude was adopted towards the messengers before him. The outcome for those who mocked has always been the same: the very thing they mocked enveloped them in the end, the punishment they regarded as a mere threat came upon them, and truth ultimately prevailed over falsehood.

The second purpose is to jolt the hearts of these deniers and mockers and draw their attention, so that they may cast a glance at the history of their own predecessors, who denied the prophets and mocked them, and whom the punishment of Allah enveloped as a result. These people were stronger and more powerful than you in might and splendour. They were more prosperous and more developed. Thus, they are being directed to this so that perhaps they may accept guidance, just as at the beginning of the surah they were also commanded to take a lesson from the events of history. The following words of the Holy Qur'an are worthy of reflection:

﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and then observe what was the end of those who denied."﴾ (6:11)

Say to them: "Go about the earth and see what the end of the deniers has been." The purposes of travelling through the earth are that the traveller gains knowledge, reflects upon circumstances, and takes a lesson from them. Then, after reflection, the traveller comes to know how the *sunan Ilahiyyah* (the divine laws or patterns of Allah) operate in events and occurrences. The *sunan Ilahiyyah* can be known from ancient monuments that are visible and still standing, and they can also be known from the historical events recorded in the traditional histories of every land and every people. To travel the earth for this purpose and in this manner was a novel matter for the Arabs. This verse shows the immense revolution in thought and outlook that the Holy Qur'an was bringing among a nomadic and simple people like the Arabs. It was teaching the philosophy of history to an unlettered and illiterate nation.

They used to roam the earth; they were accustomed to travelling. They were used to moving in caravans for livelihood and trade, but the matters before them were only those concerned with trade, hunting and the like. Travelling for educational purposes had never been their objective. This journey was entirely new to them. This new system of life was giving them a new line of truth, and, like children, it was taking them by the hand and bringing them out of the depths and darkness of ignorance. It was placing them upon a high and open highway and leading them to the station of exaltation. History bears witness that it was by acting upon the Qur'an that they reached that lofty station.

This methodology of studying history, which the Holy Qur'an was teaching the Arabs, from its beginning to its end, was an entirely new methodology for the study of human history. In accordance with it, in that era the Islamic system of life presented human history before the human intellect. This manner of study makes it clear that when certain causes come together in accordance with the will of Allah, their results necessarily manifest, and human beings see with their own open eyes events and occurrences in history appearing in accordance with the divine laws. Before the Islamic system, only a few events from human history and its traditions had been enumerated, and some observations and some customs and practices of people had been recorded. Nowhere had there been any discussion or commentary on the causes and reasons of events, nor had there been any analysis of how these causes produced these results. These were the stages and upheavals of history. It was the Islamic system and the Qur'an that gave humanity the philosophy of history and taught it to study the causes and effects within historical events. The Qur'an has not presented any stage of the philosophy of history, nor has it carried forward any old idea. Rather, the Qur'an has given humanity a methodology of historical analysis, and human history can be analysed only in accordance with that methodology.

Some people are astonished that the Islamic system and the Prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) brought about, in a short period of barely a quarter of a century, a great and unparalleled cultural and economic revolution in the lives of the Arabs. This period appears extremely brief for a revolution so great and so all-encompassing. If they study the real factors of that economic revolution, they will by no means be astonished. They will come to know what the factors were that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought from the All-Knowing, All-Aware God. The truth is that this economic revolution too was a miracle displayed by the Islamic system of life, and its secret lies within that very system. Those who are seeking in the modern economic theories of this age, and in the lost economic principles, what they are looking for, and who offer a material interpretation of history, should seek this secret within the Islamic system.

If they do not seek its causes within the system of life, then what causes will they be able to name for the economic revolution that took place among the backward, nomadic Arabs as a result of the Prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ)? As a result of it, people received a doctrine and a conception of life, a system of government, a new style of thought and outlook, morals, values, social conditions and customs, and all this within a very brief period, namely a quarter of a century. (﴿Produce your proof, if you are truthful﴾)

Reflect once again upon this glimpse:

﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and then observe what was the end of those who denied."﴾ (6:11)

And renew in your mind the earlier remark in the initial part of this wave:

﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established upon the earth as We have not established you? We sent the sky upon them with abundant rain and made rivers flow beneath them. Then We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them other generations.﴾ (6:6)

These verses, and similar verses found in this surah and throughout the Qur'an, present humanity with a new methodology of thought and outlook. This is a living methodology, and it is an unparalleled and peerless system of life. (For details, see my book *Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami wa Tawmanuhu*, the chapter "Islam's Philosophy of History".)

**Lesson No. 57: At a Glance**

This wave is very high, and its impact is very frightening. Immediately after the discussion of denial, turning away, mockery and ridicule of the Islamic call, this wave rises. Amid the earlier discussion of turning away and mockery, a warning was given, and fear of an evil end was placed in their hearts, and people were directed to reflect upon the historical end that those who denied and mocked had met. Before the wave concerning the deniers, in the opening wave of this surah, the reality of the Divine and His sovereign authority over the entire universe was discussed. This majesty was shown in the universe as a whole and also within the human self. Now in this wave too, further aspects of the supreme authority of the Divine Being and His dominion are shown, with a new rhythm and some new factors. Thus, the opening wave and the theme of this wave are one and the same; the difference is that between the two a severe warning has come to the deniers and mockers, intended to show that this act of the objectors is a most vile act. Those who turn away from the call are committing a very wicked deed.

In the first wave, the majesty of Allah was shown in the creation of the heavens and the earth: how the system of darkness and light was established, and how humanity was created from clay within this universe. The first stage of its life was fixed, and the second stage was set for its resurrection and recompense. It was also explained that the lordship of God encompasses the heavens and the earth. It also encompasses all the activities of this creature, humanity, on the earth, whether they are manifest or hidden, whether they are with a loud voice or secret, whether their deeds are open or concealed. All these matters were not brought forth because the Qur'an had in view some theological or theoretical debate, but so that the demands of these realities would manifest practically in human life. The whole of human life should bow before the One God, and a human being should not bow before anyone other than the Lord of the worlds (*Ilah al-'Alamin*), and there should be no doubt in monotheism. He should understand and acknowledge that the sovereignty of Allah encompasses this entire universe and the outward and inward life of the human being, and thus the human being should make his entire life subject to the sovereignty of Allah, just as his created existence is subject to the sovereignty of Allah.

The purpose of this new, lofty wave is also to manifest the reality of divinity and the sovereignty of Allah, in this way: that Allah alone is the owner of this entire universe. He alone acts. He alone gives sustenance and He alone sustains. He is the Almighty and the Dominant; He is the Benefactor and the One who harms. But these beliefs are not merely negative and theoretical. It is necessary that in the light of these beliefs Allah alone be accepted as *wali* (protector and friend), that one turn to Him, render Him complete servitude, and remain obedient to Him. All these matters will manifest in this way: that Allah is accepted as one's friend and ruler, because He is our Lord and the One who feeds us, while nothing is given to Him by us. Secondly, He Himself has forbidden taking anyone other than Allah as protector, ruler and friend, or associating anyone with Him in these matters.

For this purpose, in this form, alongside the explanation of the reality of divinity, the factors and influences that disturb the heart have also been explained. The beginning is made with this: Allah is the owner of all things; then He is the Lord, but in such a way that He feeds all people, while no one feeds Him, and He is not in need. Then the mention is made of Allah's punishment, that if someone is spared from it, he has achieved a great success. Then, that Allah has power over good and evil, that He has power over every act, that He is the Dominant, the Wise and the All-Aware. All these matters are brought together in an impactful manner of expression, and they are stated with the most lofty majesty. Say, say, say.

This deep and impactful statement of the reality of divine sovereignty concludes with great solemnity. The doctrine of monotheism, the rejection of polytheism, and the distinction between them are declared with great force, and this declaration is also made in a most regal manner. It is said:

﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾ Say: "Allah." (6:19) Say, "Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you."

Say: Allah. Say: I do not bear witness to polytheism, for Allah is only one Being, the One God. Because of these sentences and questions and answers full of warning, a dangerous and frightening atmosphere is created, and the environment suddenly becomes solemn.
