Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-An'am (6), verses 17–18:

﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none who can remove it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent. And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.﴾

He pursues every thought of the human soul and every whisper within its breast. He knows the inner desires and the hidden apprehensions as well. He knows every form of doubt and suspicion, and He resolves all these matters with the light of creed. Through proof and argument He clarifies the human conception and grants the correct recognition of His divinity. Since this is an important matter, the Noble Qur'an, as at other places, also clarifies it here.

Now this wave is at its peak, and it produces most profound effects. The matter reaches testimony, proof and reproach. Now separation and disavowal are declared: that we cannot be partners with you in your associating matters. In a very loud voice, and in a most awe-inspiring and decisive declaration:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-An'am (6), verses 17–18:

﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none who can remove it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent. And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.﴾

He pursues every thought of the human soul and every whisper within its breast. He knows the inner desires and the hidden apprehensions as well. He knows every form of doubt and suspicion, and He resolves all these matters with the light of creed. Through proof and argument He clarifies the human conception and grants the correct recognition of His divinity. Since this is an important matter, the Noble Qur'an, as at other places, also clarifies it here.

Now this wave is at its peak, and it produces most profound effects. The matter reaches testimony, proof and reproach. Now separation and disavowal are declared: that we cannot be partners with you in your associating matters. In a very loud voice, and in a most awe-inspiring and decisive declaration:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 19 (part 1 of 2):

(Verse) "19.

"Ask them: Whose testimony is the greatest? Say: Allah is witness between me and you. This Qur'an has been revealed to me by inspiration, so that I may warn you and whoever it reaches. Do you truly bear witness that there are other gods besides Allah? Say: I do not bear such witness. Say: He is only one God, and I am utterly free of the shirk in which you are involved."

The stopping of the speech at various points, the forceful opening, and this rising and falling within a single verse, is a wondrous style of speech. A whole position is stated in one word, and each word presents a scene, through which the doubts and perplexities and their nature also become known.

The Prophet ﷺ himself is addressed and commands are given. Then, under those commands, the Prophet ﷺ addresses those polytheists who have taken other than Allah as their guardians. They assign some of the rights specific to Allah to others than Allah, and they make these guardians partners with Allah. Then these people invite the Prophet ﷺ to leave them in their state, so that in exchange they may become partners in the Prophet's ﷺ religion. In their view this was possible; they thought that Islam and polytheism could be gathered in one heart. They had lodged such a notion in their minds. Even in the modern age of today, this kind of thinking sits in people's hearts. Ordinary people think that they can be Muslims in relation to Allah while at the same time taking guidance in the affairs of their lives from other than Allah. They may be obedient servants of other than Allah, they may seek unseen help from other than Allah, and they may make other than Allah their friend and guardian.

Now the Prophet turns toward the polytheists here and proclaims that at this point the paths of his religion and their religions part. His tawhid and their shirk can no longer remain together. His Islam and their jahiliyyah cannot live in one place. Now he decides the matter with them: "Now there can be no union or connection between me and you. Union is possible only if you abandon your religion and join my religion; otherwise, there is no reason that this union could take place, because the paths of both have separated from the very beginning."

The Prophet ﷺ speaks with them in such a way: what authority and testimony do they have? Let them bring forward in the arena any testimony and any proof for their position.

(Verse) "Qul ayyu shay'in akbaru shahadah" (6:19): "Ask them: whose testimony is the greatest?" What is the greatest testimony in this whole universe? What is that testimony which holds the rank of confirmation? What proof in the case is final, after which no further proof is needed?

This is a most general question. The question is asked with the word shay' (thing), meaning: bring any thing of the whole universe as proof, which would be the greatest testimony.

Just as the Prophet ﷺ is commanded to ask them, so too he is commanded to give them the answer, because the opponents themselves acknowledged that the true answer is the one which the Prophet ﷺ is commanded to give. (Verse) "Qul Allah" (6:19): "Say: Allah." Yes, indeed, He is the greatest witness. It is He who is declaring this truth. It is He who issues the best judgments, and after His testimony there is no other testimony; after His word there is no room for any word. When Allah speaks, all speech ends and the matter is decided.

When the truth was proclaimed that Allah is the greatest testimony, now it is announced that between me and you there is only Allah as witness, and only He will decide this matter.

(Verse) "Shahida baini wa baynakum" (6:19): "He is witness between me and you." The meaning is: (Verse) "Huwa shahid" – He is the witness between me and you. At this point, a pause after the word Allah is appropriate, because here the speech is in short phrases. That is, a pause after the word Allah is more suitable than continuing. If one joins them, it would read "Allahu shahidun baini wa baynakum" in continuity.

When this principle was established, that in this matter the decision belongs solely to Allah's decision, it is then explained that Allah's testimony has come in the form of the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted has sent down this Qur'an solely so that I may warn you and all the other people to whom it reaches, whether during your lifetime or after your death. Therefore, the Qur'an will be a proof even for those people to whom it reaches after the Prophet's ﷺ death, as well as for those to whom it was conveyed during his presence. This is because in this fundamental matter of human thinking, the Qur'an is the decisive testimony, and upon this thinking depends the salvation of this world and the Hereafter; upon it the human existence stands.

(Verse) "Wa uhiya ila hadhal-Qur'anu li-undhirakum bihi wa man balagh" (6:19): "This Qur'an has been revealed to me by inspiration so that I may warn you and whoever it reaches." Whoever the teachings of the Qur'an reach, in a language he understands and from which he can derive the call of the Qur'an, the proof is established upon him. The Prophet's ﷺ duty of warning is fulfilled, and if he disobeys and denies, then punishment becomes obligatory for him. (However, a person who does not know Arabic, and for whom the call of the Qur'an is not present in his language, the proof will not be established upon him, and the Muslims will be held accountable for this, because they did not transmit the meaning of the Qur'an in the language he understands. If the Qur'an has been translated into his language, the proof will be complete.)

When it was announced that Allah's testimony is recorded within the Qur'an, the content of that testimony was also stated. This was stated in the form of a challenge and in the manner of a severe warning. Those who bore testimony were rebuked: "Do you present your own testimony against Allah?" It was made known that we reject your testimony. You announce the opposite position and proclaim that Allah's essence is one without partner. Only Allah is God, and in this matter there is complete separation between us and you; our paths are different. In the most emphatic and decisive words, the disavowal is declared.

(Verse) "Qul ayya shay'in akbaru shahadatan. Quli-llahi shahidun baynee wa baynakum wa ooHiya ilayya hadha al-Qur'anu li-undhirakum bihi wa man balagh. A-innakum la-tashhaduna anna ma'a-llahi alihatan ukhra. Qul la ashhadu. Qul innama huwa ilahun wahidun wa innanee bari'un mimma tushrikun" (6:19)

"Do you truly bear witness that there are other gods besides Allah? Say: I do not bear such witness. Say: He is only one God, and I am utterly free of the shirk in which you are involved."

These verses, their closing phrases and their blows strike the human heart so powerfully that it is impossible to describe their effects in words. Therefore I do not consider it appropriate to limit their effects and their beauty by my own words, because no commentary can express their beauty.

On the theme taken up in this group of verses, it is necessary to say something. This theme concerns guardianship, tawhid, and complete separation from polytheists. It is a fundamental matter of the Islamic worldview and a great and important truth in this religion. Today's Islamic groups and Islamic movement should consider this matter, keeping this lesson in view, pause for a fairly long time, and reflect and ponder.

At present the Islamic movement confronts the system of jahiliyyah that has spread over the whole globe, just as the Islamic movement that arose at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an confronted the jahiliyyah of that time. Therefore the Islamic movement today should determine its position in the light of the position of the Islamic movement at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, so that with the help of that light it can see its path well. Thus it is a need of the Islamic movement to reflect long and thoroughly upon these verses and to seek guidance from the footsteps of the first Islamic movement.

The age has returned to the very point where the first Islamic movement stood. Humanity has come to the same point on which it stood at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was alive and present. Islam was revealed upon him, and its foundation was the testimony that Allah is one, and there is no other God besides Him. This testimony, that there is no God but Allah, we too must give in the same way as Rib'i ibn Amir gave it, when he went to Rustam, the commander-in-chief of the Persians, as an envoy of the commander-in-chief of the Muslims. Rustam asked Rib'i: "Why have you attacked us?" His answer was: "Allah has raised us so that He may take out those of His servants whom He wishes from servitude to men, bring them out of that bondage and admit them solely into the service of Allah. Then He will lead them into the vastness of this world and the Hereafter, and rescue them from the oppressions of other religions and admit them into the justice system of Islam." Rib'i ibn Amir gave this testimony knowing that Rustam and his companions did not worship anyone in the sense that they believed him to be God, or the creator of themselves or of this universe, nor did these people perform the well-known rites of worship before Khosrow. Rather, they took their law and legislation from Khosrow. Thus they served Khosrow, which was contrary to Islam. Rib'i told them that they wanted to bring people out of human systems and into the system of sovereignty of Allah, in which obedience and servitude are reserved for Allah alone; and in contrast to this is the Islamic way of life, in which sovereignty, obedience and servitude belong to Him alone.

Nowadays the age has returned to the point at which Islam once presented to people the testimony of (La ilaha illa Allah). Today humanity has returned and entered into servitude to men; it suffers the oppressions of other religions, and it has turned away from this great testimony. Although a portion of humanity proclaims day and night, through the calls to prayer from the mosques, the testimony of (La ilaha illa Allah), it does not know what the meaning and implication of this testimony and this declaration of faith is. Nor, when giving this testimony, do these people bring that meaning to mind. Nor do they reject the sovereignty that some people have reserved for themselves, although their position is equal to a proclamation of divinity, whether or not they openly announce this position. For example, in the case of the legislative assemblies prevalent in the world, or the condition of certain nations, the ruling of individuals and assemblies is the same. The status of individuals and nations is one. Since these individuals, these assemblies and these nations are not gods, they have no right to legislate for mankind, unless humanity apostatises and denies (La ilaha illa Allah), and hands over these powers to someone other than Allah; in that case it denies the doctrine of tawhid and Allah will not be its protector and guardian.

Now the situation is that the whole of humanity, including those who night and day proclaim (La ilaha illa Allah) from the mosques through the calls to prayer without understanding its meaning, will be the greatest sinners on the Day of Resurrection and most deserving of punishment, because after becoming Muslims they have turned back and adopted the servitude of men. After this truth was revealed to them and reached them, and after they had entered the religion of Islam, therefore in this age the Islamic movement has the greater need to reflect well upon these verses:

(Verse) "Qul a-ghayra-llahi attakhidhu waliyyan fatiras-samawati wal-ard, wa huwa yut'imu wa la yut'am. Qul innee umirtu an akuna awwala man aslama wa la takunanna mina al-mushrikeen" (6:14)

"Say: Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds and is not fed? Say: I have been commanded to be the first to submit, and do not be among the polytheists."

Whatever meaning is taken from it, it means humbling oneself before Him, obeying Him, seeking His help and seeking His aid. All these matters are contrary to Islam, because they are acts of shirk, and Islam came precisely to extract people from these acts of shirk. The Islamic movement should know that the first place in which guardianship is manifested is when someone accepts the sovereignty of other than Allah in his ideology or in the system of his life. This is the matter in which the whole of humanity born on the earth at this time is involved without exception. And so that the Islamic movement may well understand that its goal is to bring the common people out of servitude to men and into the servitude of Allah alone, and that it faces the same kind of jahiliyyah which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the first Islamic movement faced when these verses were being revealed.

Moreover, the Islamic movement is in dire need of the draught of faith which these verses pour into the heart of the believer, when the believing heart stands arrayed against any jahiliyyah:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 6, verse 19 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Say: "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day."﴾ [6:15] ﴿Whoever is spared it on that Day, Allah has had mercy on him, and that is the clear success.﴾ [6:16] ﴿And if Allah touches you with adversity, there is none to remove it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent.﴾ [6:17] ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.﴾ [6:18]

Say: "If I disobey my Lord, I fear the punishment of a great (dreadful) Day." On that Day, whoever is spared from the punishment, Allah has shown him great mercy, and that is the manifest success. "If Allah afflicts you with some harm, there is none who can remove it except Him; and if He bestows upon you some good, then He is competent over all things." He has complete authority over His servants, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware.

Every movement that confronts jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance and rejection of divine guidance) and its satanic powers, every movement that confronts the tyranny, oppression, enmity and rebelliousness of jahiliyyah, and every movement that stands arrayed against the conspiracies and malice of jahiliyyah and seeks the removal of the corruption, immorality and wickedness it spreads, needs to comprehend these realities in the face of all this shirk, and these sentiments and this consciousness must exist within that movement. Otherwise there is a danger that it will take non-Allah as its protector, and lest, as a consequence of this disobedience, it become deserving of the punishment of the Hereafter. The Islamic movement must be convinced that benefit and harm lie solely in Allah's hand, and that Allah has complete control over His servants. After His decree there is no other decree, and no one can reject His command and decision. The heart that lacks this conviction and this consciousness cannot in any way bear the hardships of the revival of Islam, while the resurgence of Islam is taking place against the established system of jahiliyyah, because jahiliyyah can never tolerate the movement for the revival of Islam calmly. Mountain-like difficulties have always been placed in its path.

Having become convinced of how important and difficult the goal of the Islamic movement is on the earth today, having properly grasped its creed and belief, and having fully understood what its requirements are, namely that Allah, glorified is He, is One without partner, and that this tawhid has many aspects, and alongside all these matters, the awareness of what difficulties lie on this path, today's Islamic movement needs, by Allah's command, witness (shahadah) and complete boycott of, and decisive separation from, jahiliyyah, because jahiliyyah is afflicted with exactly the same shirk that the jahiliyyah of earlier generations was afflicted with. Therefore the Islamic movement should make the same declaration that Allah, the Exalted, commanded the Prophet ﷺ to make. Just as the Messenger ﷺ hurled his teachings into the face of the jahiliyyah of his time, today too the movement should throw the false ideas of the jahiliyyah of the modern age into its face, and implement these commands of Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say: "Allah is witness between me and you. And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. Do you really testify that there are other gods along with Allah?" Say: "I do not testify (to that)." Say: "He is only one God, and indeed I am free from what you associate."﴾ [6:19]

Ask them: whose testimony is greatest? Say: Allah. Allah is a witness between me and you. This Qur'an has been sent to me by revelation so that I may warn you and all those to whom it reaches. Do you truly testify that there are other gods besides Allah? Say: I cannot testify to that. Say: God is only one, and I am definitely free from the shirk in which you are involved.

It is the duty of the Islamic movement to adopt this stance against the jahiliyyah that now prevails over the earth. It should proclaim its true principles openly against it, and announce its verdict in a thunderous, awe-inspiring voice. After that, it should leave the outcomes to Allah, who is competent over all things. He has complete control over the affairs of His servants. These oppressive satanic powers, too, are included among His servants, and they do not possess even the strength of a fly in the face of Allah. If a fly were to snatch something from them, they could not even retrieve it from it. These oppressive forces cannot cause anyone any harm without Allah's permission, nor can they bring anyone any benefit. Allah, the Exalted, is fully dominant over the affairs of the universe, but people do not see Allah's dominance.

The Islamic movement must firmly be convinced that, according to Allah's promise, it cannot attain establishment (tamkin fil-ard) on earth until it completely separates the paths of its life from jahiliyyah, until it severs all relations with it, until the Islamic movement declares the truth openly against the satanic powers, and until it bears witness to the truth against jahiliyyah in the manner that these verses command it to do. Until it challenges jahiliyyah in exactly this manner, completely boycotts it, and declares its disassociation from it.

The Qur'an was not specific to the reform of one particular period of history. The Qur'anic guidance is free from the restrictions of place and time. The Qur'an is indeed a methodology of revolution, and whenever any movement adopts this methodology, it will have to work in the same way the first Islamic movement had to. Today we face the same circumstances as those at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an. We have returned to the same position that existed at the time of the Messenger ﷺ, when Islam was being introduced to the world. We must have complete trust in the reality of this religion. We must have complete trust in Allah's power and His dominance. The Islamic movement should prepare itself in exactly this manner. Allah is the best protector, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.

Lesson No. 58 at a glance:

This is a new wave. The address is directed to those who deny the Qur'an, and especially to those who reject the Qur'anic doctrine of resurrection after death. However, this wave does not depict their stubbornness and enmity, nor does it tell what became of their predecessors who denied the Qur'an and resurrection. Rather, some scenes and glimpses of the Day of Resurrection are presented before them, and their eschatological evil end is depicted, and this evil end is presented in the form of extremely vivid and living scenes and sights. These people are in the place of assembly on the Day of Resurrection, facing extremely shameful questions to which they have no answer, being disgraced in public. They cannot find any answer.

﴿Where are your partners whom you used to claim?﴾ [6:22] This question comes with such majesty that a state of wailing and anguish overtakes them. Now they swear with extreme humility and extreme naivety, and acknowledge Allah's lordship.

﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists!﴾ [6:23] But when they reach the edge of the Fire, with shackles upon them, drowned in regret and shame, frightened and terrified, they speak thus:

﴿Oh, would that we were returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers!﴾ [6:27] Now Allah, glorified is He, Himself puts a question to them, while their condition is that they are melting with shame and their souls are departing from them out of fear and dread.

﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ [6:30] Now they answer with extreme humility and shame: ﴿Yes, by our Lord!﴾ [6:30] Now this admission is of no benefit to them. The command is given:

﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.﴾ [6:30] In such circumstances they encounter this state of affairs, having lost themselves, having lost everything. Now they carry all their evil deeds upon their shoulders, and because of their wrong stance regarding the Hereafter and this losing bargain, they are deeply distressed and worn out with grief.

One scene after another appears on the screen. Every scene is such that the heart trembles, the whole body is shattered, and the whole being is about to be broken into pieces. The windows of heart and mind are now fully open. Now that truth which the Messenger ﷺ was presenting becomes clearly visible to them. But guidance to accept the truth, on seeing these scenes, was granted only to those for whom the Divine will had decided that they would accept the truth. As for those who had been given the Scriptures before the Qur'an, they recognized this truth just as they recognized their own children, yet despite this they did not accept it.

(Verse 20)

The Qur'an repeatedly mentions that the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, recognise the Qur'an exactly as they recognise their own children. They know well that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the true Messenger and that this Qur'an is being revealed to him by Allah. This fact is stated while addressing the People of the Book, and it is also presented as an argument against the polytheists of Arabia. The People of the Book, in general, in Madinah had taken up a stance of enmity, hostility and opposition to the Islamic movement, while the polytheists were everywhere. This fact is brought forward because the polytheists of Arabia acknowledged that the People of the Book were more learned than them and were more informed about the revealed scriptures and the nature of revelation. Therefore it is stated that the People of the Book recognise the Qur'an well, without any doubt, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) is receiving revelation from the same Lord who sent revelation to the earlier messengers.

Just as we have preferred the view that this verse is Meccan, and the manner in which the People of the Book are mentioned in it indicates that the address in this verse was to the polytheists of Mecca: the book that you deny, the People of the Book recognise it just as they recognise their own children; and if a large majority of the People of the Book did not believe, they have indeed put themselves into a very great loss. Despite their knowledge, in this matter they have become equal to the polytheists, who, by putting themselves into loss, have deprived themselves of the wealth of faith. The matter before and after this verse is, in any case, concerning the polytheists of Mecca. Therefore, as we stated at the introduction of this surah, we prefer the view that these verses are also Meccan. In the exegesis of this verse, the mufassirin have cited: "Those whom We have given the Book recognise it as they recognise their own sons" (6:20), and have said that they affirm that this speech is sent down from Allah and is true, or that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a true Prophet of Allah and this Qur'an is being revealed to him through revelation. This interpretation is, in any case, included in the implication and meaning of this verse. However, in the light of historical events, and keeping in view the attitude of the People of the Book that they adopted against the religion of Islam, we say that there is another aspect to the meaning of this verse. Allah's purpose was that the community of Muslims should also have this dimension in mind, so that in later ages they may determine their own attitude towards the People of the Book and know what their attitude towards Islam will be.

The People of the Book knew well that this Book is the true Book from Allah, because they were acquainted with the power of influence of this Book. They were aware of the goodness and reform that it contains. They were also well informed about how, when a people embraces the ideas contained in this Book, a tremendous power of spreading arises within them. They knew how far-reaching are the moral strengths that emerge in a people as a result of this Book, and how firm is the system of life that this Book presents. The People of the Book knew a great deal about this Book and its followers. They were certain that in this Book there is no room for them, nor room for any other religion. They knew very well what a great truth is in this Book, and what a great falsehood they themselves were clinging to. These people were also acquainted with the system of ignorance (jahiliyyah) into which they had fallen, and into which their people, their customs, their morals and their social order had reached. Now the situation is that this true religion cannot make any compromise with them, nor is coexistence between them possible. Therefore the struggle that confronts them will continue until ignorance is removed from the face of this earth, until this religion prevails everywhere and the religion of the whole world is established upon the worship of God, and until the sovereignty of Allah is established on this earth. Until those who lay hands upon the rights of Allah's dominion and sovereign authority are driven off from the face of this earth, no reconciliation can take place between the two groups, because only in this way can the kingdom of God be established.

The People of the Book knew well that this truth exists in this religion, and they knew this truth exactly, without any doubt, as they knew their own children. The People of the Book have studied this religion generation after generation, and they know that within this religion lie the sources of strength and majesty, and the paths along which it leaves its effects upon the human soul. Therefore they are constantly engaged in investigations as to how they may nullify the effects of these powers of the religion. How can they create doubts and misgivings in the hearts of the followers of Islam? How can they distort the texts of the religion of Islam, in words and in meaning? How can they reduce this religion, in its confrontation with falsehood and ignorance, from the station of a movement for the implementation of Islam and a movement for the establishment of the government of Allah, into a mere cultural and academic movement, and by turning its living texts into mere theological and doctrinal discussions, render them lifeless? Thus their constant endeavour has been to turn this religion into an arena of merely theological, jurisprudential and sectarian disputes. They cast the meanings and concepts of the religion of Islam into forms and notions that have no connection with this religion, but are in fact deadly to it. Yet despite these conspiracies, they assure the Muslims that your belief is safe and worthy of respect. In this way, the void they create is filled by them with new concepts, new ways and new priorities, and thus they uproot Islamic thought from its root.

The People of the Book study the religion of Islam very deeply, and they strive to understand Islam with great seriousness and depth. But they are not seeking any truth through this. Some of our simple-minded people think that perhaps they are seeking the truth, or that they wish to do justice to this religion, as some of our simple-minded people think when any of the orientalists expresses favourable impressions about certain aspects of Islam. But the reality is not that these people are in search of truth, or that they wish to make any fair comment upon the religion of Islam. Rather, the reality is that through these investigations they remain in search of the point from which they may attack the religion of Islam. These people want to close all those springs of the religion of Islam through which human nature may be quenched, or through which human nature may be influenced in those aspects. They want to close all such springs. They seek out the secrets of the powers of this religion so that they may defend against these powers well. These people want to know how this religion nourishes itself within human psychology, so that, finding the Muslims heedless, they may insert some of their own concepts into it and fill whatever void remains in people's souls with concepts contrary to the religion.

Therefore, in order to achieve these aims, these people know and recognise the religion of Islam just as they know and recognise their own children. We must have knowledge of these realities. It is also our duty that we should have complete knowledge of our own religion, and that we should recognise our religion just as we recognise our own children.

The practical situation of the Islamic history of the last fourteen hundred years confirms what the Qur'an had told in advance:

"Those whom We have given the Book recognise it as they recognise their own sons" (6:20). There is no doubt in this. In the recent historical period this situation has become very clearly manifest. The discussions taking place today about Islam are so extensive that the writings of a single week could be collected and published as a book. This is the case in all foreign languages. From these discussions it becomes clear that the People of the Book are aware of every small and great matter concerning this religion. They are thoroughly informed of its temperament and its history. They know the sources of this religion's strength, and they are fully aware of its power of resistance. They also know the methods by which this religion can be corrupted, but the majority of the People of the Book keep this intention hidden. They keep their aims secret because, if an open attack were made upon the religion of Islam, people would rise to defend it and speak in its support. The movements that were established to defend this religion against armed attacks, for example against the colonial powers, were founded upon a religious understanding and a religious zeal. They performed the duty of defending the religion in their own time. But today there is an intellectual war against the religion, and Islamic movements have repeatedly risen to defend against this intellectual and ideological war as well, and the People of the Book always fear this. Therefore they adopt extremely deceitful methods, namely that they first praise the religion of Islam to some extent, and lull to sleep the feelings of defence and support for Islam, so that the sentiment of support for Islam is numbed, and the reader's heart is made to feel at ease. In this way such writers keep pouring poison into the cup while the reader keeps drinking it sip by sip. The speech of such people usually goes like this: "Undoubtedly Islam is a great religion, but its meanings and concepts need to be reshaped in a developed form, in accordance with the demands of modern civilisation, so that it may meet the needs of the modern age. It is not appropriate that this religion should obstruct the process of modernity and development that is taking place in societies in the present age; rather, it is appropriate that this religion should adopt modern moral values and should not interfere with modern systems of government and public affairs. Let whoever wishes keep Islamic beliefs seated in his heart, but in the practical life of man, modern ideas and the ways of Western civilisation should step outside its sphere. Let him also hand over his collective affairs to those who are set up as gods and lords upon this earth and who run their own religion; in this way Islam will be recognised as an all-encompassing religion."

In the course of this manner of discourse, these writers explain to their peoples the secret of what the power and firmness of the religion of Islam consists of. Outwardly they are praising it, but inwardly they give their peoples the impression that this religion is extremely dangerous. Thus, under the garb of praise, they inform their peoples about the secret of the power of this religion, so that through these disclosures the destructive forces may attack the vulnerable points of the religion, and their blows and bombardments may strike precisely on target, and they may continue to acquire such knowledge and understanding of it as they have of their own children.

The secrets and mysteries of the Qur'an will continue to be unveiled to those who know it. This Book will always remain new and fresh. In the last fourteen hundred years it has always remained new. Muslims have fought battles in its light and have continually reflected upon their history in its light. They have continually reviewed their past and present in its light, and have seen their affairs in the light of Allah, through which the paths of truth become clear.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 21–24 (part 1 of 2):

(Verses) 21 to 24.

In the flow of the discourse, the reality on which the polytheists stood in the world is now set before them. In its light, their position and conduct are measured against the standards of God. First, they are asked to reflect on their own attitude, that they do not hesitate to fabricate lies against Allah. Along with this, they also claim that they are upon the religion with which Prophet Abraham was sent. And among their presumptions was this: regarding the things they themselves declared lawful and unlawful, they held the belief that these came from Allah, as is mentioned in the words "bi-za'mihim" (by their claim) at the end of this surah. Yet Allah had given no command regarding the lawfulness or unlawfulness of those things.

Just as today in our age countless people make a claim of Islam and call themselves Muslims, while their claim is utterly false and is a fabrication against Allah. They themselves issue laws and decrees from their own side, they themselves create the patterns, customs and rituals of life from their own side, and they introduce new things from their own side. In this way they usurp Allah's supreme authority in these matters and themselves become the supreme authority. Even so, their claim is that they are upon the religion of Islam, which is utter falsehood. Among them, the educated people who have sold their religion and have had for themselves the worst level of Hell allotted, they convince such people that they are still Muslims. In these verses, the rejection of the signs they presented is also rebuked. They rejected the signs of God, opposed and denied them, and they also made the accusation that these verses are not from Allah, and that the jahiliyyah (ignorance) upon which they act is from Allah. This position is exactly like that which the people of modern jahiliyyah claim in today's age. The stance of both is entirely identical.

(Verse) "Wa man aẓlamu mimmani-ftara 'alallahi kadhiban aw kadhdhaba bi-ayatih" (6:21): "And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah, or denies His signs?" Here, injustice (ẓulm) means shirk (associating partners with Allah). Shirk is called injustice because the word "ẓulm" is used to express its vileness and ugliness clearly. In the Qur'an, shirk is mostly described as injustice, with the purpose that people regard it as a very evil act and turn away from it. And the reality is that shirk is injustice against the truth, injustice against the human soul, and injustice against the common people. This is because greatness belongs to Allah alone, He alone deserves to be worshipped, and no one should be made His partner, for that would be a violation of Allah's right. It is injustice to the human soul because through it he falls into everlasting destruction. And it is injustice to people because they will be deprived of knowledge of the truth, and their lives will continue under principles that are oppressive. In short, shirk is a great injustice from every aspect, and this is why at the end of this verse the Lord of the worlds Himself says: "Innahu la yufliḥu aẓ-ẓālimūn" (6:21): "Indeed, the wrongdoers never prosper."

Here Allah states a general rule, and the judgment is given that the end of the polytheists and of injustice and the unjust will be what it is. The shortsighted eyes of human beings can see only what is apparent, and what they see is not a reliable reality. A human's sight extends only to a very near distance. A human can see only worldly success and deliverance. This is the plan by which Allah brings these people to an evil end, and it is evident that no one can be more truthful in speech than Him.

On this occasion, the Qur'an depicts their failure, their non-success, and the wrongness of their position in very vivid, moving and striking words:

(Verses) "Wa yawma naḥshuruhum jami'an thumma naqūlu lilladhīna ashrakū ayna shuraka'ukumu alladhīna kuntum taz'umūn" (6:22). "Thumma lam takun fitnatuhum illā an qālū wallāhi rabbinā mā kunnā mushrikīn" (6:23). "Unẓur kayfa kadhabū 'alā anfusihim wa ḍalla 'anhum mā kānū yaftarūn" (6:24).

(Translation of meaning:) "On the day We shall gather them all, and We shall say to those who associated partners: Where are your partners whom you used to claim? Then their response will be nothing but to say: By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists. Look how they lie against themselves, and how what they used to fabricate has vanished from them."

The truth is that shirk has many kinds, and the partners associated with Allah also have many categories. The situation is not what people generally understand today from the words shirk, partners, and polytheists, namely that some people worship idols and stones, or worship natural phenomena such as stones, trees and fire. That alone is not the meaning of shirk.

In reality, shirk is that someone acknowledges, concerning anyone other than Allah, that some of the attributes peculiar to the Divine Being are found in that person as well. Whether these are doctrinal matters, in which some matter of the governance of this universe is attributed to someone other than Allah, or acts of servitude performed before someone other than Allah, such as worship, vows and offerings, or whether the principles and rules for organizing the system of life are taken from someone other than Allah. All of these are the varieties and kinds of shirk. This shirk is committed in such a way that some people commit one kind of shirk and others fall into another kind, and the partners and objects of worship of the different kinds of polytheists also vary.

The Qur'an has applied the word shirk to all these categories, and perhaps by presenting living scenes of these polytheists and their partners within the scene of the Resurrection, it seeks to make the believers understand the reality. The Qur'an has not confined the word shirk to a single meaning, nor has it called a person who has one of these meanings a polytheist alone, nor has it made any distinction in the end, punishment, or relationship with all these kinds of polytheists in this world and the Hereafter.

All these kinds of shirk existed among the Arabs. Among the Arabs there was the belief that some of Allah's creatures are partners with Allah. This partnership was such that what they said before Allah was necessarily accepted. They also had a share in the decisions about people's destinies and the manifestation of events. For example, angels were regarded as partners, or it was held that these creatures could harm human beings. For example, jinn were believed to cause harm. Or it was believed that they could harm humans in both ways. For example, the souls of ancestors could also cause harm. As indications of these jinn, soothsayers and the spirits of ancestors, these people would make idols attributed to them. Their belief was that the spirits of those God-favoured creatures would enter these idols. The soothsayers would then converse with these spirits and idols. Thus, through this manner and conjecture, the soothsayers would make certain things unlawful for them and make others lawful. In this way, it was indeed the soothsayers who did this work, and it was they who held the rank of partners.

Moreover, they committed shirk in another way as well: they performed acts of servitude before these idols, sacrificed at their shrines, and made vows to them. These sacrifices, vows and acts of worship were in reality offered to those soothsayers. Some Arabs, under Persian influence, also held the belief that the stars too had influence in the affairs of the world, and thus these stars were in effect considered partners of God. Accordingly, star-worship entered among the Arabs. The story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) brought in this surah is also presented from this viewpoint, and the theme of this surah connects this story (as we shall explain ahead, Allah willing).

A third form of shirk also prevailed among these Arabs. These people, with the help of soothsayers, made their own constitutions and laws, and they themselves framed the ways of life and customs for themselves. Although Allah had not permitted lawmaking in this manner, by making law themselves they claimed that this was the law and sharia of Allah, just as some political thinkers today make such a claim.

So in that scene, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will summon people concerning all kinds of partners and ask: Bring now those whom you used to associate as My partners. Today there is no trace of them. Today they cannot help their followers at all, nor can they save them from this terrifying situation.

(Verse) "Wa yawma naḥshuruhum jami'an thumma naqūlu lilladhīna ashrakū ayna shuraka'ukumu alladhīna kuntum taz'umūn" (6:22): "On the day We shall gather them all and say to the polytheists: where are your partners whom you used to claim?"

This scene is set right before the eyes. Though the Day of Assembly is established, and we see that these polytheists are being interrogated, and this questioning is extremely painful for them: "Where are your partners you used to claim?"

This terrifying questioning leaves them stunned. Now the veils that had fallen over their nature are removed. Those temporary conditions are erased from their nature and their memory, because the foundation of those conditions was never their nature; they were unnatural, mere temporary mirages. Their awareness now tells them how they could ever have set up partners. They will say that neither did any partners exist, nor did they make anyone a partner. This scene will now become the cause of a new trial for them. In that true court, the wicked and baseless ideas are erased from their minds, just as when things are heated in a furnace, the impure elements are expelled in the form of foam.

(Verse) "Thumma lam takun fitnatuhum illā an qālū wallāhi rabbinā mā kunnā mushrikīn" (6:23): "Then their response will be nothing but to say: By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." These people, completely cut off from their past, acknowledged the lordship of Allah alone, but they did this at a time when acknowledgment was no longer beneficial to them. Their renunciation of that false acknowledgment will not benefit them now. Rather, it will be a calamity for them, and their acknowledgment will no longer be a cause of salvation for them. The time will have passed. Today is the day of the recompense of deeds. Today is the day of final judgments. It will not be a day of remand.

Nor did those partners have any reality. Today that fabrication has vanished from them. They acknowledged the truth at a time when their false enchantment had disappeared.

(Verse) "Unẓur kayfa kadhabū 'alā anfusihim wa ḍalla 'anhum mā kānū yaftarūn" (6:24): "Look how they lie against themselves, and how their fabricated deities have vanished." They have lied against themselves. When they associated someone with Allah, at that very moment they lied against themselves and deceived themselves. They fabricated against Allah, and now all their deities are lost and missing, and now it is the day of resurrection and reckoning.

In my view, this is the most satisfying interpretation of this verse, because the scene is that of the Day of Resurrection, they stand before Allah and swear by the Divine Being that they were not polytheists, since on the Day of Resurrection their lie will work against them in this sense: on that day they will be unable to lie to Allah or deliberately swear a false oath. As for those who interpreted this verse to mean that they will knowingly lie, that is not correct, because by the principle of "wa la yaktumūna Allaha ḥadītha" (4:42), they will not be able to conceal anything from Allah on the Day of Resurrection. Rather, in that terrifying scene of the Resurrection, their nature will become pure and clean, and the impurities of shirk will be removed from it. Yet Allah marvels at them: look how they lived their lives in the world in such falsehood, and today in the Hereafter this falsehood has no effect on their thinking. (And Allah knows best what is meant.) In any case, this is also one of the possible interpretations.

In the following verses, another group of the polytheists comes onto the screen, and now their case is decided. This scene is another of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection. They cry out in utter humiliation, and they wish, in a most regretful manner, that if they were returned to the world they would change their position, which is why they have had to face this evil day. Accordingly, their wish and desire are rejected in a most contemptuous manner.

The Qur'an has not confined the word shirk to a single meaning, nor has it called a person who has one of these meanings a polytheist alone, nor has it made any distinction in the end, punishment, or relationship with all these kinds of polytheists in this world and the Hereafter.

All these kinds of shirk existed among the Arabs. Among the Arabs there was the belief that some of Allah's creatures are partners with Allah. This partnership was such that what they said before Allah was necessarily accepted. They also had a share in the decisions about people's destinies and the manifestation of events. For example, angels were regarded as partners, or it was held that these creatures could harm human beings. For example, jinn were believed to cause harm. Or it was believed that they could harm humans in both ways. For example, the souls of ancestors could also cause harm. As indications of these jinn, soothsayers and the spirits of ancestors, these people would make idols attributed to them. Their belief was that the spirits of those God-favoured creatures would enter these idols. The soothsayers would then converse with these spirits and idols. Thus, through this manner and conjecture, the soothsayers would make certain things unlawful for them and make others lawful. In this way, it was indeed the soothsayers who did this work, and it was they who held the rank of partners.

Moreover, they committed shirk in another way as well: they performed acts of servitude before these idols, sacrificed at their shrines, and made vows to them. These sacrifices, vows and acts of worship were in reality offered to those soothsayers. Some Arabs, under Persian influence, also held the belief that the stars too had influence in the affairs of the world, and thus these stars were in effect considered partners of God. Accordingly, star-worship entered among the Arabs. The story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) brought in this surah is also presented from this viewpoint, and the theme of this surah connects this story (as we shall explain ahead, Allah willing).

A third form of shirk also prevailed among these Arabs. These people, with the help of soothsayers, made their own constitutions and laws, and they themselves framed the ways of life and customs for themselves. Although Allah had not permitted lawmaking in this manner, by making law themselves they claimed that this was the law and sharia of Allah, just as some political thinkers today make such a claim.

So in that scene, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will summon people concerning all kinds of partners and ask: Bring now those whom you used to associate as My partners. Today there is no trace of them. Today they cannot help their followers at all, nor can they save them from this terrifying situation.

(Verse) "Wa yawma naḥshuruhum jami'an thumma naqūlu lilladhīna ashrakū ayna shuraka'ukumu alladhīna kuntum taz'umūn" (6:22): "On the day We shall gather them all and say to the polytheists: where are your partners whom you used to claim?"

This scene is set right before the eyes. Though the Day of Assembly is established, and we see that these polytheists are being interrogated, and this questioning is extremely painful for them: "Where are your partners you used to claim?"

This terrifying questioning leaves them stunned. Now the veils that had fallen over their nature are removed. Those temporary conditions are erased from their nature and their memory, because the foundation of those conditions was never their nature; they were unnatural, mere temporary mirages. Their awareness now tells them how they could ever have set up partners. They will say that neither did any partners exist, nor did they make anyone a partner. This scene will now become the cause of a new trial for them. In that true court, the wicked and baseless ideas are erased from their minds, just as when things are heated in a furnace, the impure elements are expelled in the form of foam.

(Verse) "Thumma lam takun fitnatuhum illā an qālū wallāhi rabbinā mā kunnā mushrikīn" (6:23): "Then their response will be nothing but to say: By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." The reality emerged that dispelled the trial, or in its light the trial became clear. These people, completely cut off from their past, acknowledged the lordship of Allah alone, but they did this at a time when acknowledgment was no longer beneficial to them. Their renunciation of that false acknowledgment will not benefit them now. Rather, it will be a calamity for them, and their acknowledgment will no longer be a cause of salvation for them. The time will have passed. Today is the day of the recompense of deeds. Today is the day of final judgments. It will not be a day of remand.

Upon their condition, Allah, addressing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, makes this comment: when they committed shirk and made those beings partners of Allah, they practised falsehood and deception against their own souls, because in fact there was no existence of any partner with Allah. Nor did those partners have any reality. Today that fabrication has vanished from them. They acknowledged the truth at a time when their false enchantment had disappeared.

(Verse) "Unẓur kayfa kadhabū 'alā anfusihim wa ḍalla 'anhum mā kānū yaftarūn" (6:24): "Look how they lie against themselves, and how their fabricated deities have vanished." They have lied against themselves. When they associated someone with Allah, at that very moment they lied against themselves and deceived themselves. They fabricated against Allah, and now all their deities are lost and missing, and now it is the day of resurrection and reckoning.

In my view, this is the most satisfying interpretation of this verse, because the scene is that of the Day of Resurrection, they stand before Allah and swear by the Divine Being that they were not polytheists, since on the Day of Resurrection their lie will work against them in this sense: on that day they will be unable to lie to Allah or deliberately swear a false oath. As for those who interpreted this verse to mean that they will knowingly lie, that is not correct, because by the principle of "wa la yaktumūna Allaha ḥadītha" (4:42), they will not be able to conceal anything from Allah on the Day of Resurrection. Rather, in that terrifying scene of the Resurrection, their nature will become pure and clean, and the impurities of shirk will be removed from it. Yet Allah marvels at them: look how they lived their lives in the world in such falsehood, and today in the Hereafter this falsehood has no effect on their thinking. (And Allah knows best what is meant.) In any case, this is also one of the possible interpretations.

Just as today in our age countless people make a claim of Islam and call themselves Muslims, while their claim is utterly false and is a fabrication against Allah. And the reality is that shirk is injustice against the truth, injustice against the human soul, and injustice against the common people. This is because greatness belongs to Allah alone, He alone deserves to be worshipped, and no one should be made His partner, for that would be a violation of Allah's right. It is injustice to the human soul because through it he falls into everlasting destruction. Here Allah states a general rule, and the judgment is given that the end of the polytheists and of injustice and the unjust will be what it is. The shortsighted eyes of human beings can see only what is apparent, and what they see is not a reliable reality. A human's sight extends only to a very near distance. A human can see only worldly success and deliverance. This is the plan by which Allah brings these people to an evil end, and it is evident that no one can be more truthful in speech than Him.

On this occasion, the Qur'an depicts their failure, their non-success, and the wrongness of their position in very vivid, moving and striking words:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 25–28:

(Verses) 25 to 28.

This picture has two aspects. One aspect relates to the world, in which the colours of enmity, hatred and rebelliousness are present; the other relates to the Hereafter, and in it are the colours of regret and remorse. The Qur'an depicts both of these states in a manner that is extremely effective and suggestive. The rigid nature melts, and movement and fervour arise within it, so that perhaps the layers of ignorance that have been placed upon it may be removed, the closed doors of human nature may be opened, and, before time runs out, it may come onto the right path.

﴿And among them there are those who listen to you; but We have placed coverings over their hearts, so that they do not comprehend it, and in their ears is a heaviness. And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it.﴾ (6:25)

"Among them are some who listen to you with attention, but the state is that We have placed veils over their hearts because of which they understand nothing of it, and in their ears We have put heaviness. (So that despite hearing everything, they hear nothing.) Whatever sign they see, they will not believe in it."

These are such examples of humanity that, outwardly, they hear, but there are veils upon their hearts. Akinnah means coverings, and these coverings close off the faculty of perception. Al-waqr means a burden; that is, their ears are heavy, and because of this heaviness they are unable to perform the duty of hearing. People of this kind are part of humanity and exist in every age and in every place. Such people are found in every nation and every tribe. They are fully human. Outwardly they hear the matter, but they pay no heed and let it pass. Their ears are, as it were, deaf. They do not perform the natural function assigned to them. Their faculty of perception is, as it were, wrapped in coverings, and the Qur'anic meanings do not reach it.

﴿Until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients."﴾ (6:25)

"To the extent that when they come to you and dispute with you, those among them who have resolved on denial say (after hearing the whole matter), that this is nothing but a tale of bygone times."

Their eyes too are seeing, but in reality they are not seeing anything. The scene they behold has no effect upon their hearts and minds.

The question is: what has happened to these people? And what is it that prevents them from understanding and accepting? Although they possess hearing ears, seeing eyes and a sharp intellect, Allah says: "But the state of them is that We have placed veils over their hearts, because of which they understand nothing, and in their ears there is heaviness. Whatever sign they see, they will not believe in it."

Thus the decision of Allah concerning them is described: their perception will not reach this truth, nor will they comprehend it; their faculty of hearing will cease to function. That faculty will not guide them to their own perceptive capacity so that they may understand and accept, even if they are seeing the realities with their own eyes and the proofs of faith are before them. Yes, it is our duty to try to read the Sunnah of Allah in this decision. Allah says:

﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths.﴾ And elsewhere:

﴿And by the soul and Him who proportioned it, and inspired it with its wickedness and its piety; he has indeed succeeded who purifies it, and he has indeed failed who corrupts it.﴾ (Ash-Shams 91:7–10)

The Sunnah of Allah is that He guides everyone who strives to be guided, and brings to success everyone who purifies and cleanses his soul. The conduct of the people mentioned above was that they made no effort to accept guidance, and they did not turn the natural powers for accepting the truth in such a direction that Allah would grant them the ability to accept the truth. They, in fact, rendered their natural faculties inoperative, and thus Allah placed a veil between them and the truth. Concerning them, in accordance with the Sunnah of Allah, the decision was that they be left to their earlier deeds and their intention and will. Every affair happens by the command and decree of Allah, and the command and decree of Allah is that whoever strives shall be provided with guidance, and whoever purifies himself shall succeed. It is the command of Allah that He places veils upon the hearts of those who turn away, so that they cannot understand; their ears become deaf, so that they cannot hear; they see signs and proofs with their own eyes, yet they are not guided. Those who think that their testimony, their associating partners with Allah, and all their wrongdoings are the result of Allah's will, and that Allah has already decided these matters concerning them, have fallen into error in this thinking. Allah presents the reality before them, and by quoting their statements He exposes their flaw. Reflect carefully on this verse:

﴿And those who associated partners said, "If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have made anything unlawful without His permission." Likewise did those before them act. Is there upon the messengers anything but clear notification? And We did certainly send into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut." And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was deserved. So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ (16:35–36)

From this it is understood that Allah expressed displeasure at their statement, and that their misguidance was decided because the duty of conveying the message had been fulfilled for them. After that, this treatment was meted out to them because of their conduct.

Those who engage in idle debates about the issues of divine decree, patience and free will, and about the servant's will and his action, and who turn these simple matters into complex, abstruse discussions, follow whatever their intellects reach. Such people go on arguing in terms of hypothetical and speculative decrees, but they abandon the affirmative, simple and realistic outlook of the Qur'an. That simple reality decides that whatever occurs happens in accordance with the decree of Allah, and that a person's inclination towards one side or the other is part of the nature upon which Allah has created him. This nature too is in accordance with the decree of Allah, and it is as the decree of Allah is. A person's inclination towards something, and the consequences of this in this world and the Hereafter, also lie within the bounds of the decree of Allah. All matters return to the decree of Allah, yet all these results are established upon the person's own will, and this will of his is also created by the decree of Allah. This is the true reality, and whoever argues beyond it gains nothing except further complications.

The situation of the polytheists was that the signs of guidance had been presented to them. The proofs of truth had been made clear, and the indications of faith had been made manifest to them. In the Qur'an, the proofs scattered across the souls and the horizons had been gathered together for them. If their hearts had turned towards this, the Qur'anic proofs alone would have been sufficient and adequate to make the strings of the polytheists' hearts sing, to awaken the hidden recesses of their perception, to give them life, and thus their hearts would have accepted guidance and responded with "Here I am." But they did not take the trouble to achieve the goal by which they would have found the way of guidance; rather, they rendered their nature and its correct inclinations inoperative. Thus veils came between them and the indications of guidance. When they came to the Messenger ﷺ, they did not come with open eyes. Their ears were not ready to listen, their hearts were not ready to understand, and they did not reflect upon the Qur'an in the manner in which seekers of truth and reality reflect upon it. Rather, they studied the Qur'an only in order to dispute with it, and sought opportunities to deny it and refute it.

﴿Until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients."﴾ (6:25)

"Asatir" is the plural of "ustura." The term "ustura" was applied to stories that spoke of extraordinary, supernatural matters concerning gods, or that mentioned the events of great leaders, heroes and idol-worship. Among the Arabs, the tales of Persian idol-worship were especially well known, because they were close to the Arabs.

The truth is that the polytheists knew well that the Qur'an had no connection with these ancient tales. This was merely their form of disputation, and they were seeking pretexts to reject and deny the Qur'an, and they would search far and wide for matters from which to refute it. Since the Qur'an contained the accounts and narratives of the messengers and their peoples, and also mentioned the nations whom Allah had destroyed, they brought forward only deceit, extremely feeble objections, and far-fetched points. Accordingly, concerning these passages, and indeed the entire Qur'an, they made this remark: "This is nothing but a tale of bygone times."

In order to deepen the conspiracy to keep people away from this Qur'an, to establish it upon extremely firm foundations, and to instil in the minds of the common people that the Qur'an is a tale of bygone times, Nadr ibn al-Harith, a thinker of Makkah, would memorise the stories of Rustam and Isfandiyar of the Persians, and collect in this way the stories and tales of the other leaders and heroes of the Persians. He would set up his gathering near the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the time when the Messenger ﷺ was reciting the Qur'an to the people. He would tell the people: "If Muhammad recounts to you the tales of the people of old, I have more literary material than he has." Then he would begin relating the stories of Rustam and Isfandiyar, and he adopted this stratagem so that people would not listen to the Qur'an.

These people also prevented the common folk from listening to the Qur'an, because they were the leaders of that society. They kept people away from such occasions, fearing that they might be influenced by the recitation of the Qur'an.

Verse 26 of Surah al-An'am (6): "They forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves, and they destroy none but themselves, yet they are not aware."

﴿وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَيَنْأَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَإِن يُهْلِكُونَ إِلَّا أَنفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ (26)

"They prevent people from accepting this truth, and they themselves also run away from it. (They think that by this conduct they are harming you in some way), yet in reality they are preparing the means of their own destruction, but they are not aware of it."

They knew well that the Holy Qur'an was not merely a collection of the stories of earlier peoples, and that it would not benefit them through tales of the past. If people kept listening to the Holy Qur'an, the number of those influenced by it would keep increasing. The great intellectuals of Quraysh themselves feared that the recitation of the Holy Qur'an could affect even them. Regarding their followers, they were seriously apprehensive. Therefore, in the struggle between this powerful, expanding and formidable movement and the weak and false society of the people of Makkah, it was not sufficient for them merely that Nadr ibn al-Harith should set up a gathering in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and present the literary masterpieces of the Persians there. So, as preventive measures, they used to forbid their followers from listening to the Holy Qur'an, and they themselves also kept away from such occasions where they might hear the Holy Qur'an, merely out of the fear that they themselves might be affected and accept it. The story of Akhnas ibn Shariq, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and Amr ibn Hisham is very well known. These people would try to counter the attractiveness of the Holy Qur'an, but the Holy Qur'an would still draw them towards itself. (See Ibn Hisham, Part One, and Zilal al-Qur'an, Para Six.)

They endured all these hardships so that they could keep themselves and their followers away from listening to the Qur'an, lest they be influenced by it and accept it; and this action was in reality a cause of their own ruin. Allah the Exalted says: "In reality they were bringing about their own destruction, but they were not aware of it."

Whoever keeps himself and others back from the path of guidance, the path of truth and the path of salvation, brings upon himself loss and destruction in both this world and the Hereafter. Those who keep themselves and their followers from the way of Allah are in reality wretched; although they appear to be mighty tyrants and great oppressors, in this world and the Hereafter they have authority only over themselves. Although they and their followers sometimes appear, for a brief period in this world, to be very much profiting and successful, in reality they are bankrupt. Now, let us look at the other side of the picture regarding their final outcome:

"If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they will say, 'Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers.'" (6:27)

This is a scene that stands in contrast to the brief picture of this world. It is a scene of utter disgrace, shame, despair and regret. In the world they used to act with arrogance, dispute, prevent people from coming close to Islam, and make grand promises. But here their longing is this, when they are made to stand at the edge of the Fire. This scene will be worth seeing. They will be brought forward, seized and presented before the Fire. Now they will have no strength left to turn away in defiance or arrogance. Now they can neither argue nor create confusion. In this scene worth beholding, their wish will be expressed, and if you were present at that time, they would speak thus: "Oh, would that there were some way for us to be sent back to the world, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers."

Now they know that these were the signs of God. Now they wish to be returned to the world. Now they cannot deny these signs, and now they will become firm believers. But what can be done now, when the birds have eaten the crops (i.e., the opportunity has passed)?

Now these people have forgotten their innate nature. They possess a disposition that does not submit to acceptance. Their statement that, if they are returned, they will not deny and will certainly believe, is also a false wish. It is a wish that does not fit with their true nature and reality. Even if this wish were granted, they still would not act so. And then their words would not be this, and they say this because their deeds and their evil end will become clear before them, whereas before this they used to conceal from their followers their deeds and this evil end, so as to keep them deceived into thinking that they are the upholders of truth and that they will be successful and prosperous in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 28:

(Verse) "Nay, but there has become manifest to them what they used to conceal before; and even if they were returned, they would revert to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars." (6:28)

In truth, they will say this merely because the reality that they had covered up will by then have been unveiled and will stand before them. Otherwise, if they were sent back to their former life, they would again do all that they had been forbidden from doing; they are, after all, liars. Here the discussion about them ends, and they recede into the background, in that wretched condition, with contempt, as liars.

Now certain further aspects of such people come to light, and in contrast to this otherworldly scene, two more scenes are presented. One is the scene of the world, in which they expressed with firm resolve the belief that there is no life after death, that Allah will not raise anyone again, and that there is no reckoning. The other scene concerns the Hereafter: a glimpse in which they are shown standing before their Lord, and Allah, the Lord of the worlds, questions them: (Is this not the truth?) (6:30). Is this Resurrection not true, and is it not a reality? This is a question by which they are broken, indeed melted, and they answer like a utterly wretched and humiliated person: (Verse) "Yes, by our Lord!" (6:30), "Our Lord, by Your oath, it is a reality." And now they are seized by the painful punishment because of their deeds.

Another glimpse also comes into view. Suddenly the hour arrives of which they were utterly disbelieving, this "meeting" with Allah. Now they are drowned in despair and regret, carrying the burden of their sins upon their shoulders. And in the Hereafter it is shown what the reality of the world is in the balance of Allah, and what the station of the Hereafter is.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 29 (part 1 of 2):

(Verses) 29 to 32.

The doctrine of the recompense of the Day of Judgment and the abode of the Hereafter is the foundation of Islamic beliefs and ideas, and this doctrine has always been presented by Islam alone. After the doctrine of tawhid (the oneness of God), the structure of the Islamic system rests upon it. The beliefs and ideas, the morality and conduct, and the law and constitution of the religion of Islam can be established and firmly rooted only when a sense of accountability before the Hereafter arises within people.

This religion, which Allah has perfected, and through which Allah has completed His blessings upon the believers, has been chosen by Allah as the system of life for the Muslims. As the Qur'an itself says, this religion is in reality a complete system of life, and in its structure its parts are interconnected and mutually related. There is a deep connection between its moral principles and its beliefs and ideas. Furthermore, both beliefs and morality are related to its law, constitution and the administration of the state. All these matters are established upon the basis of belief in Allah's sovereignty and accountability before the Hereafter.

According to the Islamic outlook on life, life is not the brief span that an individual spends in this world, nor is life the brief span in which a nation remains alive, nor is life the known period that has been given to humanity and which we are seeing. According to the Islamic concept of life, life is a long and never-ending period. It expands across the horizons of the universe and has gone deep into all worlds. In its reality it is diverse and multicolored, and it is entirely different from the life which those who deny the Hereafter, or who are heedless of it, consider to be life, which they live, and which they think is just this life, and that there is no other world after this one. In this way they do not believe in the Hereafter.

According to the Islamic concept of life, life is very vast. It includes this period which we are seeing, that is, the world. It also includes the period of the Hereafter, which no one except Allah knows. In comparison with this long life of the Hereafter, this life is so short that it can be called no more than "a part of a day," that is, a portion of a day.

In terms of space, this concept is so broad that it recognizes further galaxies and worlds beyond this world and this earth. It believes in a Paradise whose breadth exceeds the heavens and the earth. Hell too is so vast that its belly cannot be filled with all the humans and jinn who have inhabited this world since the beginning of humanity, and this inhabitation spans millions of years.

Then this concept extends to unknown worlds. Beyond this world there are many worlds, of which only the Divine Being has knowledge, and we know about them only what Allah has told us. This life of the Hereafter begins with death and reaches the abode of the Hereafter. The world of death and the world of the Hereafter are both unseen worlds, and in them human existence advances in a form whose true nature is known only to Allah.

This life also expands. It proceeds beyond this world that we are seeing, and in the Hereafter it is seen flowing onward in Paradise and Hell. These are the different colors of this life, and in the life of this world its forms and tastes differ. In the Hereafter too it has its own features, but this entire life of the world is so worthless in comparison with the life of the Hereafter, just as a single wing of a mosquito is worthless in comparison with the world.

This is the human personality according to the Islamic concept of life, whose existence extends beyond the limits of time, whose sphere of influence extends beyond space into the horizons of the universe, and whose rank is more profound than the worlds found in this universe. Its concept extends to the whole universe and embraces the entire human existence. Its taste for life is very vast. In it there is importance for humanity, importance for human relations, and importance for human values. Just as this concept is broad, transcending the bounds and restrictions of time and space, those who do not believe in the Hereafter have a thinking about the universe itself that is extremely limited and weak. Their thinking about the human concept of life is very limited. They confine themselves, their values of life and their ideas, to the narrow confines of this limited world.

Because of this difference in outlook, differences arise in the values of life, in the detailed system of life and in its practical form. From this it becomes clear how comprehensive and complete the Islamic system of life is. It also becomes clear how much the belief in the Hereafter contributes to the formation of this system, in terms of ideas and concepts, in terms of morality and conduct, and in terms of the system of law and the system of constitution.

The person who lives through this long era, this vast universe, and all the creations found within it, is certainly different from the person who is confined in the cave of this narrow world, and who, even within that narrow cave, is at war with other people. He does not hold the belief that if he is deprived of something in this world, he will find something better in the world to come, and that if he receives no reward for a deed in this world, he will surely receive a better reward in the Hereafter. If this conviction arises within him, this person will adopt a very strict attitude toward the people and interests of this world.

The more a person's thinking expands and the deeper his perception of realities, the greater his personality becomes.
