His aspirations become lofty, his consciousness becomes elevated, and as a result his morality and conduct become very pure. The conduct of such a person is far superior to that of those who are confined in holes. When the thought of the belief in the Hereafter and the thought of recompense and punishment in the Hereafter enters the mind of such a person of expansive thinking, his very world changes. Refinement and purity enter his thinking. His heart becomes ready to spend in the path of goodness and in hope of the reward of the Hereafter, because he knows that this is the command of Allah and that the reward of the Hereafter is established upon it. Thus his morality and conduct become righteous, and he becomes the possessor of firm character. This firmness remains as long as this belief overshadows his heart and mind. Such people are constantly striving for reform and goodness, because they are convinced that if they remain silent, not only will their world fall into corruption, but in the Hereafter they too will suffer loss.

Those who fabricate falsehoods about the life of the Hereafter say that calling people to the life of the Hereafter is a negative attitude toward this world. As a result, people become indifferent to this world, and then they do not strive to beautify this world and reform it. The outcome is that the authority of the world falls into the hands of corrupters, because the eyes of those righteous people are fixed only upon the Hereafter. Those who level this accusation against Islam are ignorant. They do not distinguish between the Islamic doctrine of the Hereafter and the monastic system and the renunciation of the world practised by the People of the Scripture. According to the Islamic concept of life, the idea of the Hereafter is that this world is a field for the Hereafter, and whatever we sow in this world, we will reap in the Hereafter. The Islamic doctrine of jihad is also for the reform of this world. It is enjoined so that evil and corruption may be completely eradicated from this world, and so that those who transgress against Allah's right of sovereignty and supreme authority in this world may be restrained. Here the government of all oppressive tyrants is to be ended, a just system is to be established on the earth, in which there is welfare and goodness for all humanity, and all this is done for the sake of the success of the Hereafter. That is why Allah has opened the gates of Paradise for the mujahideen fi sabilillah (those who strive in the way of Allah), and in their struggle against falsehood, Allah rewards them there, and for the suffering they endured in His path, He gives them comfort.

How is it possible that a system of life whose thinking is this should cause human life to become stagnant and rot? Or that this life should be afflicted with corruption and disorder, or that oppression and rebellion should prevail in it, with no one to stop the oppressor's hand? Or that it should leave life in a backward and undeveloped state, when the people holding such a view have their eyes fixed upon the Hereafter and seek reward in the Hereafter?

It is true that in some periods of history people have held negative ideas. They have been advocates of evil, corruption, oppression and rebellion. Backwardness and ignorance have covered their lives, and these people have also claimed to be Muslims despite these conditions. But these conditions were not because of Islam; rather, their understanding of Islam was unsound. Their concept of Islam was distorted. They had deviated from the straight path and no longer had any certainty about the Hereafter. Their faith was unstable. These conditions were not because they were truly following the religion and were fully convinced that they would have to appear before God. If that had been so, they would never have lived in the conditions in which they spent their entire lives, because a person who truly grasps the reality of the religion cannot live as those people lived; that is, one who holds a negative outlook, is backward, and is content with evil and corruption.

A Muslim lives in this world, but he regards himself as far above this world. He considers himself far greater than this insignificant world. He makes use of the pure things of this world, or he keeps himself free even from lawful and permissible things, solely for the sake of his success in the Hereafter. He strives with all his might for the conquest of the forces of the world and for the progress and development of worldly life, but from the perspective that this struggle is imposed upon him as a duty by virtue of his station as vicegerent (khalifah), and that it is his obligation to wage jihad in this world against evil, corruption, oppression and rebellion, and to sacrifice his life and wealth in the path of this jihad, so that he may attain the success of the Hereafter. His religion teaches him that the world is the field of the Hereafter, and that the only path to the Hereafter is this world. Every person must pass through this world to reach the Hereafter. Yet in comparison with the Hereafter, the world is extremely insignificant and small. In any case, the world is also a limited blessing, and through this limited blessing a person crosses over and enters the unlimited blessings.

Every component of the Islamic system serves as a ladder for the life of the Hereafter. Because of this outlook of the Islamic system, expansion, beauty and elevation arise in a person's conception. As a result of this outlook, loftiness, purity and tolerance come into being, and a person becomes enthusiastic for this path. He becomes cautious and God-fearing, and in human striving and life, self-confidence, firmness and assurance arise.

This is why Islamic life can be founded only upon the concept of the Hereafter, and for this reason the Qur'an, from beginning to end, has repeatedly emphasized the fear of the Hereafter and certainty of the Resurrection, and has presented the subjects and scenes of the reality of the Hereafter.

The Arabs were immersed in a profound jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance of divine guidance), and because of this jahiliyyah, the concept of the world to come did not fit within the narrow limits of their thinking and consciousness, and they could think of nothing beyond this world. They could see only this world which was before their eyes. They could not extend their personality and their thought beyond the limits of this limited world, nor could they conceive of the further vastness of the universe. Their thinking and their consciousness were at a purely animal level, and they thought exactly as modern jahiliyyah thinks, although the people of the modern age call themselves advanced in scientific terms. Thus was the thinking of the Arabs.

(Verse) "And they said: There is naught but our life of the world, and we shall not be raised again." (29)

"Today these people say that life is nothing but this worldly life, and that we will certainly not be resurrected after death."

It was known to Allah that a pure, noble and exalted life cannot come into being as a result of the aforementioned ideology and beliefs. These limited circles of consciousness and imagination cast a person down and bury him in the dust, and they confine his thinking to sensations like those of animals. When a person becomes confined within this limited world, the appetite for the world arises within his self, and greed and avarice regarding worldly resources arise. And the person becomes a slave to the wealth and goods of the world. Just as when lusts are unbridled, they run riot, and continue in excess without restraint, without pause and without any limits, so too: if these desires and lusts are not fulfilled, the person considers himself deprived, because he has no hope of any reward in the Hereafter, even if these desires are very base, very trivial, and of a purely animal nature.

The situation of the world today, and the conduct of people in response to it, is shaped solely by considering this limited sphere of the world, in which people have before them only the restricted circle of time and place. In it there is no trace of justice, sympathy or compassion. In it every human being is at war with another human being, every class is at war with another class, and one nation is busy in the destruction of another nation, and all human beings roam freely in the jungle of this world like wild animals. Like savages, everyone is ready to do whatever comes into his heart. These scenes we see day and night in today's so-called civilized world, and they appear everywhere. All of these are the result of this limited conception of the world.

God, the Exalted, had knowledge of all these circumstances: that the community entrusted with the duty of watching over all of humanity, and whose responsibilities included raising all of humanity to that lofty station and developing it in such a way that the human aspect of man would emerge in its true form, cannot fulfill these duties until it comes out of this limited sphere of the world. Until its concepts and its values rise out of this limited and confined cave and become universal, and until this community comes out of the narrowness of the world and takes a tour of the vastness of the Hereafter. This is the reason why the Qur'an has laid such great emphasis on the belief in the Hereafter. Firstly, because it is a reality that is to come, and the Qur'an has been revealed to state realities. Secondly, because without this belief no human being can become a complete human being: neither in terms of concepts and beliefs, nor in terms of morals and conduct, nor in terms of their system of law and system of governance.

This is why there is such intense ebb and flow in this wave, and why there is such a frightening atmosphere in it that makes a person's hair stand on end. God knew that these frightening scenes affect a person very, very deeply, and through them the windows of a person's heart and mind are opened. The natural capacity for accepting truth that has been placed within a human being awakens. Movement appears within him; he appears as a living person, and he has the ability to accept the truth at all times. However, in its reality, this is a manifestation of a great truth.

"If only you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord. He will say, 'Is this not the truth?' They will say, 'Yes, by our Lord.' He will say, 'Then taste the punishment for your disbelief.'" This is the end of those who said: "There is nothing but our worldly life, and we shall never be raised again."

This is a most dreadful, humiliating and shameful scene. These people stand in the presence of Allah, and they used to deny that they would be presented here. Now they cannot even hold on to that position. They stand as though they are bound, with a terrifying end before them. They are asked: "Is this not the truth?"

This question itself is deeply shaming. Upon hearing it, a person breaks out in sweat from shame. What else can they say? "Yes, our Lord, this is the truth." They acknowledge this truth at a time when they stand before the Creator, in a place they had strongly denied. Now their end is announced in a most majestic manner, in a most concise judgment, and in a most frightful way. A very brief verdict comes from the higher realm, but it is final: "Then taste the punishment for your disbelief." This end is entirely fitting for those who have shut upon themselves the doors of Islam's broad vision of life, and who, having abandoned the breadth of that vision, have confined themselves within the narrow circle of the senses. They refuse to rise from the world of flesh and blood to the lofty station of humanity, and they cling to earth and matter. They have built the whole system of their life upon a base that is low and weak. These people have fallen so low that they have made themselves deserving of the punishment that suits the disposition and temperament of those who deny the Final Hour, who have adopted such a base life, and who hold such debased ideas. The scene that concludes with this judgment is completed with these terrifying remarks, which are, in their awe and majesty, befitting the glory of the Lord. He says:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 31:

(Verse) "Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost, until when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, 'Alas for us, for our neglect concerning it,' while they bear their burdens upon their backs. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear." (6:31)

They have suffered loss, those who denied the meeting with Allah. The news of meeting Allah they took as a lie. When that hour comes suddenly, these same people will say, "Alas! What a shortcoming was ours in this matter!" Surely this is a great loss. In the world they lived a base and reckless life, and in the Hereafter their condition will be what has been mentioned. Now that hour arrives suddenly, which those heedless ones did not expect and did not reckon with. But "when that hour comes, these same people will say, 'Alas, what a shortcoming was ours in this matter.'"

Now observe the next scene of these people. They appear as beasts of burden on which a heavy load is laid.

(Verse) "And they will be bearing their burdens upon their backs." (6:31)

"Rather," the animals are better than them, since they are beasts of burden that carry loads, but these people will be carrying the burden of their crimes. Animals deliver their loads to their destination and then rest, whereas these people will enter Hell carrying the burden of their sins, and they will be sent there as criminals.

(Verse) "Behold, evil is the burden they carry." (6:31)

Now comes the last section of this paragraph; the matter ends in this scene of loss and ruin, and of these frightful circumstances. Allah places on the scale of the balance the worth of the world on one side, and the value of the Hereafter is placed on the other, and values are weighed in this manner:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 32:

﴿And the life of this world is but amusement and diversion. And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Then will you not reason?﴾ (6:32)

The life of this world is nothing but a game and a pastime; in truth, the state of the Hereafter is better for those who wish to avoid ruin. Will you not then use your reason?

This is the true weight of the life of this world and the life of the Hereafter according to Allah's measure, and it is the real weight. On this small sphere called the earth, what reality can a life of one hour have? It can only be amusement and diversion, especially when it is compared with the long and eternal life of the Hereafter. It is evident that in comparison with the world to come it can only be called amusement and diversion, because that is an everlasting and perpetual life, and Paradise is very vast.

This is the true worth of this world in comparison with the Hereafter. But the Islamic concept of life has not left this brief world futile, nor has it adopted a negative attitude towards it, nor has it taught the renunciation of the world. The monastic renunciation and ascetic withdrawal that appear in some scenes of Sufism and the ascetic life do not have their source in the Islamic concept of life. These things entered the Islamic concept of life through monasticism and the church, or came in from some institutions of the Persians, or came because of some Hindu and Greek ideas, at the time when the cultures of other societies were transferred into Islamic society.

According to the Islamic concept of life, the complete model of practical life was the Companions (ṣaḥābah) of the Messenger (ﷺ). They adopted no negative attitude towards the world and did not take the path of renouncing it. They overcame the satanic self within their own souls. They subdued the dominant system of jāhiliyyah on the earth, in which the sovereignty of judgment belonged to other chiefs and kings rather than to Allah. The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all) also understood the true worth of this worldly life according to the balance of Allah. In their practical lives they worked for the Hereafter, and they also adopted a positive attitude towards this world. They took an active part in the affairs of life, settled the matters of the world with zeal and enthusiasm, and worked on every aspect of worldly life. But the teaching from Allah about the reality of the world benefited the Companions greatly. Therefore they did not become slaves of the world alone, but also worked for the Hereafter. They rode upon the world; the world did not ride upon them. They made the world their servant and thereby honoured it, and they did not become slaves of the world, nor did they submit to the authority of the world's kingdoms. They remained upon this earth as Allah's vicegerents and successors; they discharged the right of vicegerency well, built this world well, and reformed it well, but they did all this seeking the pleasure of Allah and hoping for the reward of the Hereafter. The result was that in the field of the world they surpassed even the worldly-minded people, and in the field of the Hereafter they were, of course, ahead of them.

The Hereafter is indeed hidden behind the veil of the unseen, so whoever believes in the Hereafter has a broad outlook and a lofty understanding, and those who possess reason know that this is good. ﴿Indeed, the abode of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Will you not then use reason?﴾

Those in this age who deny the Hereafter, and deny it because it is hidden behind the veil of the unseen, are in truth utterly ignorant, although they claim knowledge. The knowledge they claim is human knowledge, and no reality has yet emerged in human knowledge that could be called the final truth. If any reality has emerged, it is this: that we do not have knowledge, and the unseen is concealed from us.

Lesson No. 59 at a glance:

In this wave of the surging waves of this surah, the address is directed to the Messenger (ﷺ). Allah consoles him, so that he should not be distressed by the attitude his people have adopted towards him. His people regard him as truthful and trustworthy, so they do not consider him a liar; rather, they insist that they will not accept Allah's signs and will not believe. They do this not because they consider him a liar, but because for other reasons they reject the Islamic worldview. For his reassurance, reference is also made to the stories and events of his earlier brothers and messengers, who were subjected to greater torment than he, yet they endured with patience and faced hardships. In the end Allah granted them victory and success, and all this happened in accordance with the principles of Allah's established way (sunnah), which will never change. When the Messenger (ﷺ) had been comforted and reassured, Allah places before him an important truth for reflection concerning the call to Islam: the work of the call proceeds in this world in accordance with Allah's sunnah, and the role of the caller is only to convey the message to those addressed and to keep speaking. All affairs are in Allah's hand; He turns this world in whichever direction He wills. The caller's task is only to continue his struggle according to the commands of Allah, not to deviate from his path by a single step, and not to begin offering suggestions to Allah Himself. Even if the caller were the Messenger (ﷺ) himself, he is not permitted to do so. Nor is it the caller's task to consider the proposals of opponents and deniers, or to reflect on what the common people's work should be to shape the method of the call, nor to accept their demands for proofs and miracles. This is because living hearts will listen to his words and accept them, but those whose hearts are dead will never be ready to accept his message. It is Allah's work whether He leaves people dead in this way or grants them life. This sunnah of Allah will continue until the Resurrection and the Gathering.

When these people, like the nations before them, demand signs and miracles, Allah—although He is capable of producing every kind of miracle—is wise, and He does not bring about those miracles according to His wisdom. Now the Messenger (ﷺ) is told that if this situation is burdensome to him, then, if he has any power within himself, he should himself arrange some miracle. Allah is the Creator of all creatures; He knows the secrets of all creation and understands their temperaments and capacities well. In accordance with His wisdom, He leaves those who deny in darkness, as they are like the dumb and the deaf. He guides whom He wills and leaves in misguidance whom He wills. All these matters proceed under His wisdom.

(Verse 33) — Part 1 of 2

The polytheists of Arabia in general, and the Quraysh in particular, especially those who stood firmly against the Islamic call and were held captive by jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam), did not doubt the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ). These people knew that he was truthful and trustworthy. There was not even one small incident in their knowledge in which he had told a lie, for he had lived among them for a long period before prophethood. Likewise, those groups that stood opposed to his call also had no doubt that he was a truly sincere Messenger. They also knew that the Qur'an is not human speech and that a human being cannot produce this kind of speech. Yet, despite this knowledge and conviction, they refused to express it, and they kept refusing to enter this new religion. They did not refuse because they were denying the Prophet (ﷺ), but rather because by doing so their own influence and influence and their social position would be affected. This was the real matter that led them to take the path of denial and disbelief, and they remained fixed in their false, polytheistic denial.

Islamic history and the body of hadith contain numerous narrations that clearly demonstrate this policy of the Quraysh and the other Arabs. They concealed their true opinion about the Qur'an.

Ibn Ishaq narrated from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and Akhnas ibn Shariq ibn Amr ibn Wahb al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, went out secretly one night to listen to the Qur'an from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He used to recite the Qur'an in prayer at night in his house. Each of them sat in a hidden place and kept listening to the recitation. None of the three knew about the others. They listened the whole night, and when morning came they dispersed. On the way, they accidentally saw one another. They blamed each other and said to one another that no one should do this again, because if ordinary foolish people saw them, they would leave a bad impression on their hearts. After this agreement, they left. When the second night came, each of them again came and hid in his place, and they listened the whole night. When morning came, they dispersed again. Accidentally, they met again on the way. They again reproached one another harshly, as on the first night, and left. When the third night came, they again came and sat in their respective places and listened to the Word of God the whole night. When morning came, they began to leave again, and on the way they once again saw one another. They said, "We will not leave one another until we make a firm pledge that we will not come this way again." So they made a formal agreement not to return and went away. On the next morning, Akhnas ibn Shariq took his staff and went to the house of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and met him. He said to Abu Sufyan: "Tell me, Abu Hanzalah, what is your true opinion about the speech you heard from Muhammad last night?" He said: "Abu Tha'labah! By God, I heard from him some things that I understand well and know their meaning, and some things that I heard whose meaning and purpose I did not understand." Akhnas said: "By God, in whose name I swore, my condition is the same." Then Akhnas left them and came to Abu Jahl, went to his house, and said to him: "Abu al-Hakam, tell me your opinion about the speech you heard from Muhammad." Abu Jahl said: "What did I hear?" And then he said: "We and Abd Manaf have always been in competition. They began feeding people, and we also fed people in competition. They gave mounts to people, and we also began giving mounts. They gave gifts, and we also rained down gifts, until we rode on horses side by side, knee to knee, and we advanced past one another as two racing horses advance past one another. Now they say that a prophet has arisen among us and revelation descends upon him from heaven. Where will we get a prophet to match them? By God, we will never believe in him, and we will never confirm him."  The narrator says that Akhnas left him and got up.

Ibn Jarir narrated, regarding the verse "Indeed We know..." (6:33) and onward, from al-Suddi through Asbat, that on the day of Badr Akhnas ibn Shariq said to Banu Zuhrah: "O Banu Zuhrah, Muhammad is your nephew, and your duty is to defend your nephew. If he is truly a prophet, you will be spared the sin of fighting against a prophet. If he is a liar, your duty is still not to lay hands on your nephew. Withdraw until he meets Abu Jahl. If Muhammad prevails, you will return safe and sound, and if Muhammad is defeated, your people will not hold you accountable." Therefore, after the event of Badr, his name became Akhnas (the one who withdraws, the one who hides), although previously his name was Ubayy. Afterwards, Akhnas met Abu Jahl. This meeting was in private. Akhnas said: "Abu al-Hakam, tell me about Muhammad: is he truthful or a liar? Here there is no one of Quraysh except you and me who is listening to our conversation." Abu Jahl said: "Woe to you! By God, he is truthful; Muhammad has never told a lie. But the matter is this: if the descendants of Qusayy take the banner, the watering duty and the custodianship of the Ka'bah, along with the rank of prophethood, what will remain for the rest of the tribes of Quraysh?" This is the meaning of the verse: "They do not deny you, but these wrongdoers are in fact denying the signs of Allah."

It should be noted here that this surah is Meccan, and this verse is also certainly Meccan, but the event of Badr took place in Medina. However, when it is established that the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all) would say in a verse "that is His saying" and then mention an event, the meaning was not that this verse was revealed concerning that event, but rather that this verse applies to that event and guidance can be derived from it for that event, whether this verse was revealed before that event or after it. Therefore this narration is not strange in this respect.

Ibn Ishaq (rahimahullah) narrated from Yazid ibn Ziyad, who narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi. Muhammad said that it had been conveyed to him that Utbah ibn Rabi'ah was among the chiefs of Quraysh. One day he was sitting in a gathering of Quraysh, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting alone in al-Masjid al-Haram. Utbah said to Quraysh: "Is it appropriate that I go to Muhammad (ﷺ), present some proposals before him, and whatever demands he makes, we fulfill them, and he stops criticizing us? Perhaps he will agree." This was at the time when Hamzah had become Muslim and the Prophet's companions were increasing day by day. The assembly unanimously said that the proposal was entirely correct: "Abu al-Walid, arise and speak with him." Utbah got up, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), sat down in front of him, and said: "Nephew, you know that you hold a high position among us, your tribe is numerous, and your lineage is of noble standing, but you have put your people into a great calamity. The unity and harmony of the people has ended. You have ridiculed the beliefs of the people, reviled their religion and their gods, and you declare the forefathers of the people who have died to be disbelievers and people of Hell. I present to you some proposals; listen to them carefully. Perhaps they will be acceptable to you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Abu al-Walid, say it; I am listening." Then Utbah said: "Nephew, if the movement you have started aims at gathering wealth, we will collect for you so much wealth that you will become the richest of us all. If you want leadership, we will make you our leader so that we will decide nothing without you. If you want kingship, we will make you our king. And if the situation is that the thoughts that come upon you are a kind of psychological illness from which you are powerless and cannot rid yourself, then we will arrange great physicians for you and spend so much that you become healthy and sound, because sometimes a person's companion overcomes him and he must be treated." (These were approximately his words.) Utbah said this and finished. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) listened attentively to his words. After that he asked him: "Abu al-Walid, have you finished your speech?" He said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Now listen to my words attentively." Utbah said: "Speak." He began to recite:

"Ha Mim. A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Ever Merciful. A Book whose verses are detailed, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know, bringing good tidings and warning, but most of them turn away, so they do not hear." (41:1–4)

He recited the verses of Surah Ha Mim al-Sajdah up to the verse of prostration and then prostrated. Utbah listened silently, placed his hands behind his back on the ground, and leaned on them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Abu al-Walid, you have heard; this is my answer." Utbah got up and went to his gathering. When they saw Utbah coming, they said to one another: "By God, Abu al-Walid has not come back with the face he left with." But when he sat with them, they asked: "Abu al-Walid, what have you brought back?" He said: "I have this to say: I heard a speech such that, by God, I have never heard anything like it before. By God, it is neither magic, nor poetry, nor soothsaying. O people of Quraysh, my advice to you is that you obey me and leave this matter to me. My advice is that you do not interfere with this man and do not block his path; leave him to his affairs. By God, the word I heard from him will bring you some great news one day. If the Arabs kill him, others will settle your problem for you. And if he prevails over the Arabs, his sovereignty will be your sovereignty, his honor will be your honor, and you will become an exceedingly prosperous people because of him." Upon this, the people of the gathering said in one voice: "Abu al-Walid, by God, he has bewitched you with his speech!"

Allamah al-Baghawi, in his Tafsir, narrated the report of Hazrat Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while reciting Surah Ha Mim al-Sajdah, reached the verse: "But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud" (41:13), Utbah placed his hand over the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and appealed to him by the ties of kinship not to say such things. After that Utbah went back to his family and did not come to Quraysh, and he shut himself away.

Afterwards, when Utbah was spoken to about this matter, he would say: "I placed my hand over the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and appealed to him by the ties of kinship that he should not proceed further. Do you not know that when Muhammad says something, it comes to pass? So I was afraid that a punishment might descend upon you too."

Ibn Ishaq narrated that a group of Quraysh's leaders gathered at the house of al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah was among them as an aged, experienced thinker. It was the season of Hajj. He said to these leaders: "O people of Quraysh, the season of Hajj is approaching, and all the Arab delegations will come, and they have heard about your companion. So agree upon one opinion about him, and if you speak with different statements, you will be contradicting one another, and your own words will refute you." They said: "Abu Shams, you yourself offer suggestions; I am listening." They said: "We will call him a soothsayer." He said: "This is completely wrong, because he is certainly not a soothsayer. We have seen many soothsayers; he does not chant or murmur like soothsayers, nor does he rhyme in sajc." Then they proposed: "We know well that he is not possessed, nor do whisperings come into his heart, nor do doubts arise in his heart." Then they suggested that they should call him a poet, and he said: "He is not a poet either. We know poetry well: its types are rajaz, hazaj, qarid, maqbud and mabsut, so the Qur'an does not fall into the category of poetry." Then they said that they should call him a magician. He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is not a magician either. We have seen magicians and their magical tricks; he does not perform blowing and incantations, nor amulets and charms." Then they said: "Abu Shams, then you tell us what we should say." He said: "By God, his words have great sweetness; its root is fruitful and its branches bear fruit, and whatever you say about it, people will consider it false. In my opinion, if any reasonable statement can be made about this speech, it is only this: you should accuse Muhammad of being a sorcerer, that he speaks words of magic by which a rift is created between father and son, enmity arises between brother and brother, discord arises between husband and wife, and a person is cut off from his family." So these people spread this claim, sat on all the roads during the Hajj season, and whoever came, they warned him and cautioned him, and informed people about the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 33 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Jarir reported, through ʿAbd al-Aʿla, Muhammad ibn Thawr, and Maʿmar, from ʿAbbad ibn Mansur, from ʿIkrimah, the following narration: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah came to the Prophet (ﷺ). He recited the Qur'an to him, and the Qur'an had a very great effect upon him. When Abu Jahl ibn Hisham learned of this incident, he came to al-Walid and said to him, "Your people wish to collect wealth for you." Al-Walid said, "Why?" He replied, "They are collecting it for you as a donation, because you went to Muhammad (ﷺ) and sought a gift from him." (This wretched man wanted to strike at his self-respect, because al-Walid considered himself wealthy and took pride in his wealth.) Al-Walid said, "Do the Quraysh not know that I am the wealthiest among them?" Thereupon Abu Jahl said, "Then it is fitting for you to say something about Muhammad that shows you utterly dislike him and oppose him." Al-Walid said, "Tell me, what can I say about him? By God, none of you is more knowledgeable than I am in the forms of poetry, nor does anyone know rajaz verses more than I do, nor does anyone know qasidas more than I do, nor does anyone know the poetry of the jinn more than I do. By God, what Muhammad says does not fall under the category of poetry. By God, what he speaks is very sweet; its outward form is extremely polished. Whatever comes before it, it breaks. In short, his speech remains exalted and lofty, and nothing can rise above it." Abu Jahl said, "By God, the people will never be pleased with you; you will have to say something." He said, "Then let me think." When he had thought carefully, he said, "This is magic that has an effect, and it is taken from another source." Upon this, this verse was revealed: "Leave me with the one whom I created alone..." up to "...over it are nineteen."

In another narration it is stated that the Quraysh said, "If al-Walid becomes a Sabian, all the Quraysh will become Sabians." Abu Jahl said, "I will take care of this. Do not worry." Then he met him, and after great reflection he said, "This is speech full of magic. Do you not see that as a result of it a man is divided from his father, his brother, his wife, and his household?"

From all these matters it becomes clear that the opponents of the Messenger (ﷺ) did not believe that the message he was conveying to them contained any lie on his part. Rather, according to these narrations, they took up opposition to him for certain other reasons and causes. Among these causes, the greatest was that they thought that through this call and movement they would lose the leadership and sovereignty they currently held, over which they had seized control unlawfully.

Yet sovereignty, leadership, and authority belong exclusively to God, and this is the meaning of "There is no god but God" (La ilaha illa Allah), which is the foundation of the Islamic call. These people were, in any case, well acquainted with the Arabic language and its meanings, and they were not prepared to accept this meaning of the testimony of faith. This is because the testimony of faith was a revolutionary call against all sovereignties and leaderships, whose aim was to eliminate the worship of other than God from human life.

"Indeed, We know that what they say grieves you. But it is not you whom they deny; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of God." (6:33)

"And messengers before you were denied, but they were patient over what they were denied and what they were harmed, until Our help came to them." (6:34)

Here, "the wrongdoers" (al-zalimun) means "the polytheists" (al-mushrikun), and in most places in the Qur'an, "al-zalimun" refers to the polytheists. The discourse proceeds to console the Prophet (ﷺ) and explains the true causes for which those who deny him reject his call and deny the signs of God, although the truth of the divine signs is entirely self-evident. Then it is further explained that the deniers throughout human history adopted this same attitude toward messengers like you, and the Qur'an has described some of their circumstances, showing in what difficult conditions the messengers continued their work. They were patient over their hardships until God's help arrived. This allusion is made because this is the nature of God's way (sunnah). The sunnah of God never changes, and God's sunnah does not change in exchange for anyone's proposals or anyone's desires. Moreover, because of someone's denial, because of someone's afflictions, or because of someone's personal difficulties, decisions in God's sunnah are never made before their appointed time.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 34:

(Verse) No. 34.

The call to worship of God is an ancient call. Its history stretches back into the distant valleys of antiquity. This path is perfectly straight and perfectly clear. Its lines are perfectly straight. The feet that have walked upon it have always remained firm. Various kinds of criminal-minded people have attempted to block this path. Moreover, the misguided and their most fervent followers have always obstructed the way of this call. Many callers on this path have faced severe hardships, have had to give their blood, and have had to give their lives, yet the caravan of the callers to truth has always continued its journey in the perfectly straight direction. This caravan did not deviate from this straight path for a single moment. Nor did it abandon the path and turn away from it. But the outcome is in the hand of Allah, and in the end the help of Allah comes only in accordance with the principles and decisions of Allah.

﴿Messengers before you were indeed denied, but they were patient over the denial and the harm that was inflicted upon them, until Our help came to them. And there is none who can change the words of Allah. And certainly there has come to you some of the news of the messengers.﴾

These are the words that Allah is addressing to His Messenger. This is a reminder and a form of consolation. The hand of sympathy and consolation is being passed over your head. And within these words the lines of the path for the callers who come after the Messenger ﷺ are also clearly drawn. A clear way is shown; their role is also determined for them, and they are informed that by saying "There is no god but Allah," mountains of difficulties may be shattered, and that the difficulties which earlier people faced are encountered by every caller to truth.

These words tell the callers to truth that the Divine way (sunnah ilahiyyah) for the call to truth is one and the same, and the call to truth is also one and the same. Multiplicity in it is not possible. It is a call such that most people deny it, and the conduct of deniers has always been like this. Those who carry this call have always been persecuted, and upon this denial and harassment the callers must be patient, and then after the stage of patience, the callers are at last granted victory and success. But the help comes according to the principles laid down by Allah and at its appointed time. This help does not come prematurely merely because some pure-natured and innocent callers are denied and persecuted, or because misguided people and leaders of misguidance are capable of harming these pure-natured people. Nor can this matter hasten the course of the Divine way, namely that a sincere worker and caller, free from personal desires and of the purest nature, harbours an intense wish in his heart that his people come onto the right path, and he is very worried and grieved by the reality that his people have fallen into error and have set out upon the path of worldly ruin and the punishment of the Hereafter. None of these matters can bring forward the Divine way before its time. Allah, Exalted is He, does not hasten in any of His affairs because of the haste of His creatures. And there is no change possible in the words of Allah, whether those words relate to the final victory of the righteous servants or to some decree fixed concerning them.

This is a decisive, firm and serious judgment. Its purpose is to console and reassure the Messenger ﷺ, and it is an expression of sympathy and solidarity with him on the difficulties of the path.

Now this serious judgment carries its effects to their utmost limit. The apprehensions that might have arisen in the heart of the Messenger ﷺ are also blocked off. This is because, by natural disposition, a human being wishes that his people reform, and a Messenger is eager for the guidance of all mankind. He desires, and waits, for the moment when his people will respond to his call and when they will be guided. Desires of this kind also surged in the hearts of some Muslims at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, to which there are allusions in the other verses of this same surah. Such desires are highly natural and innate in human beings. But, keeping in view the decisive manner of this Islamic call, its real nature, the conduct of the Messengers regarding it, and then the conduct of the common people, the Holy Qur'an addresses in a stern tone as follows:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 35:

(Verses) "No. 35 to 36."

Fountains of awe flow forth from amidst a most majestic style. No one can grasp the terror of these words and the depth of this matter unless he keeps fresh in his mind the fact that these words come from the Lord of the Worlds, and that with them Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, addressed His Prophet, whose important attributes include being patient and being one of the Messengers of firm resolve (Ulul-Azm). He bore the harms inflicted by his people with the utmost patience and sincerity. Like Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him), he did not invoke curses against them, although for a long time they kept inflicting cruel pains upon him, and he continued to display the utmost patience and forbearance.

O Muhammad! This is Our practice. If you cannot bear the indifference of these people and their continuous denial, and you nonetheless wish to show them some miracle, then, if you have the capacity, seek out a tunnel in the earth or set up a ladder to reach the sky, and thus present to them some astonishing miracle.

Their guidance, in reality, does not depend on your presenting a miracle before them. It is not merely a matter of a miracle appearing so that they accept guidance, as though they were fully prepared and sitting ready. In that case, if Allah willed, He could have gathered them upon guidance. Either Allah would have created them from the beginning in such a way that they would accept no path other than guidance, such as the angels; or He would have turned their hearts toward the path of guidance by His power, so that they became ready to accept guidance; or Allah would have sent down a miracle by which their necks would bow, or He would have guided them by some means or without any means at all, for He is Omnipotent.

However, by reason of His wisdom which pervades this entire universe, Allah created this honored creation, man, for a specific purpose. According to this heavenly plan, for the sake of that purpose it was necessary that this creation be given certain capacities, and that these capacities be distinct from those given to the angels. Among these distinctive characteristics is that differences be placed among the capacities of human beings: that people's capacity for accepting guidance and faith should vary, and that the measure of the substance of acceptance of truth within people should also vary. This is done in accordance with Allah's sphere of power, in accordance with His law of justice, and in precise conformity with His law of reward and punishment.

This is the reason why Allah did not gather people upon the path of guidance through any compulsion. He commanded them to take the path of guidance and gave them the choice of accepting or rejecting it, and He will enforce just reward and punishment for it in the Hereafter. This reality must be known and one must not be heedless of it.

(Verse) "And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance, so do not be among the ignorant." (6:35) "If Allah had willed, He could have gathered them all upon guidance. So do not become a fool."

The majesty of this speech is worth observing, and the decisive guidance is also worthy of reflection, but the very occasion and context of the matter required this forceful statement and this plain guidance.

After this, it is explained what disposition and nature Allah created human beings upon, and what stance they take in the face of guidance, even though the call to truth never lacks proof and argument.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 36:

(Verse) "Only those who listen will respond; as for the dead, Allah will raise them up, and then to Him they will be returned." (6:36) Those who respond to the call of truth are only those who listen. As for the dead, Allah will raise them from their graves, and then they will be brought back (to appear before His judgment).

When a messenger comes to people with the call of truth, people divide into two groups in response to that call. One group consists of the living and awake, who have within them the capacity to accept the truth. This capacity is at work, and the windows of their hearts are open. Such people accept guidance, because guidance and truth have an inherent strength, a clarity, and a harmony with human nature, and such people accept it as soon as they encounter it. (Verse) "Innama yastajibu alladhina yasma'un" (6:36): that is, those whose faculty of hearing is functioning accept the truth. The second group is one that is in reality dead. Its nature has become inactive. It neither hears nor accepts. It is neither affected nor does it respond with "Labbaik." It is not that there is no evidence in favour of this truth; truth itself is evidence, "The sunrise is the proof of the sun." When a perceptive nature turns towards it, it sees the truth within it and immediately makes its final decision and accepts it. The deficiency in the second kind of people is that their nature has died and their capacity to accept the truth has departed, so that merely hearing the call does not produce in them the capacity to accept the truth. There is no remedy for such people even with the Messenger of the time. No argument works on them. Their matter is bound to the will of Allah. If Allah wills, He brings such people to life, and if He does not will, they remain dead, whether alive or dead, until the Day of Resurrection. And on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will raise them.

(Verse) "Wal-mawta yab'athuhumu Allah thumma ilayhi yurji'un" (6:36): As for the dead, Allah will raise them from their graves, and they will appear before His judgment. This is the account of the acceptance of truth and of deprivation. Through it the reality of guidance and misguidance becomes clear. The duties of the Messenger are defined, and the final decision in all matters is entrusted to Allah. He does what He wills.

After clarifying this reality to the Prophet (ﷺ), the discourse now turns back to the unreasonable demand of the disbelievers and polytheists, in which they asked for extraordinary signs and miracles. It is explained that their demand is based on ignorance, and that these people are completely unaware of the Sunnah of Allah in this matter. For the Sunnah of Allah is that when a miracle manifests, then not only those who reject it but even those who believe in it must face a great destruction. Therefore, if Allah does not accept the demand of these people, it is not because He is unwilling to show them mercy, but because He wants to spare them from that great destruction. At this point, Allah's wise arrangements concerning all living creatures are also described, from which it becomes known that the wise Sunnah of Allah extends to all living creatures. Here the wisdom is explained that operates behind the decisions of guidance and misguidance, and in which Allah's unrestricted will is at work.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-An'am (6), verses 37–39 (part 1 of 3):

(Verses) 37 to 39.

These people were demanding from Muhammad ﷺ the kind of miraculous signs that breach normal custom, such as had been given to the messengers before him. They were not content with the Qur'an, the living miracle that remains until the Day of Resurrection, that addresses human understanding and perception, and that declares that humanity has now reached intellectual maturity. For this reason, humanity is addressed through such a philosophical and lofty discourse, and this discourse is so enduring and everlasting that it does not come to an end with any generation but remains forever, addressing human consciousness and perception until the Day of Resurrection.

These people demanded extraordinary miracles, but they could not grasp that, after such miracles appear, a punishment comes in accordance with the Sunnah of God, and that all people are caught up in that punishment and such people are destroyed in this world. Moreover, these people also could not perceive the wisdom for which God did not send down such a miracle. This is because God knew that even if a miracle were sent down, these people would not believe. Some nations before the Prophet ﷺ had done this very thing and had become deserving of destruction. Whereas the wisdom of God required that these people be given respite, and among them there were some whose destiny it was to believe. Even if one of them did not believe, God knew that from his progeny a community of believers would arise. Yet these people do not thank God for this respite, that God, despite their demand, saved them from this trial, while they were unaware of the consequences of that demand.

After mentioning their demand, the Qur'an decides that these people are ignorant and unaware of the outcomes that would have emerged once their demand had been fulfilled. The command is given: the power to send down miracles of every kind lies with God, but His wisdom requires that these people, despite their demand, not be afflicted with these hardships and destructions. It is also a part of His mercy that He has made it obligatory upon Himself to show mercy.

(Verse) "And they say: Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord? Say: Indeed God is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know." (37)

"They say: Why was no sign sent down to this Prophet from his Lord? Say: God has full power to send down a sign, but most of them are plunged in ignorance."

After this warning, the context now seeks, by a very subtle path, a way to bring the Qur'an into the heart of the addressee. The power of observation and the power of reflection of a human being are awakened, so that he may contemplate this universe and reflect upon the proofs of faith that lie within it. If he reflects, he can come to know a great deal.

(Verse) "And there is no creature moving on the earth, nor a bird that flies on its two wings, but they are communities like yourselves. We have neglected nothing in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered." (38)

"Look at every creature that walks upon the earth and every bird that flies with its wings in the air: they are communities like you. We have left nothing out in the Book's decree. Then to their Lord they will all be gathered."

This universe is not inhabited by humans alone, so that we might say that they came into existence by chance and that their life may be spent as they please, in vain. Rather, around the human being there are other living creatures, and the life of all these living beings is conducted in a particular orderly manner. From the study of their lives it also becomes evident that this life is purposeful, conducted according to a plan and in a wise manner. And from the study of the lives of all creatures there also becomes manifest the truth that all this creation is made by one Creator, that there is one governing power working behind all these creatures and fully encompassing the universe.

The phrase "every creature moving on the earth" (wa ma min dabbah) includes all living beings down to the creeping things. Insects and worms, even all microbes, all birds that fly in the air, and all creation that lives upon this universe, form a community. They share similar characteristics, live in a similar manner, and the affairs of their lives are exactly as those of human communities. God has left nothing among His creatures without plan and design, nor has He kept anything outside the circle of His particular knowledge. In the Hereafter all these creatures will be presented before their Lord, and concerning them too God will make the final decisions, as He wills.

This verse, though very brief, places before us a decisive matter concerning living creatures, and at the same time it tells us that the whole of creation is under complete supervision from God. The entire creation lives under His active governance; He knows this entire creation well, and everything lies within the sphere of His power, He who is the Lord of Majesty.

In view of the style of our work in Zilal al-Quran, it is not possible for us here to discuss the various aspects of life found within the universe. (However, in my book Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami, the headings on the reality of Divinity, the reality of humanity and the reality of matter may be consulted.) Here, during this discussion, this truth has been brought in so that the minds and hearts of human beings may be directed toward the fact that all this creation and this system of life according to which existence flows, together with complete divine governance and knowledge concerning it, and the gathering of all these creatures before God in the Hereafter, are matters that contain proofs and indications more astonishing than any miracle. If a miracle were to appear, only the generation of people present at that time would witness it; but if the signs of God within these creatures are contemplated, living miracles will be seen at all times, and people of every era can observe them.

Now this passage ends with the truth that behind guidance and misguidance, in accordance with the Sunnah of God, the Will of God is at work, and how the Will and Sunnah of God influence and guide human nature.

(Verse) "And those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb, in darknesses. Whom God wills, He lets go astray; and whom He wills, He places upon a straight path." (39)

"But those who deny Our signs are deaf and mute, sitting in darknesses. Whomever God wills, He leaves astray, and whomever He wills, He places upon the straight path."

This is a restatement of the same truth: who are the ones who hear, and who are the dead who cannot hear at all; therefore they are deprived of accepting the truth. But here the matter is presented in a different context. Those who deny the signs of God and do not reflect upon the proofs and clear evidences scattered everywhere in this universe, and then do not reflect upon the signs present in the Qur'an either: why? Because they have rendered inoperative the very substance and capacity for accepting truth that exists within their own selves. They are deaf who do not hear, mute who say nothing, and immersed in the darkness of misguidance. They see nothing. Not merely in a material sense but in a real sense also they are deaf, mute and blind, in that their faculty of perception is inoperative. Their senses do not function, nor do their senses convey any good thing to their minds. The great proof of this is that the verses of the Qur'an are in themselves impactful, stirring and shaking; yet they have no effect upon them at all. They do not grasp the matter. Therefore, whoever turns away from these clear signs, corruption has arisen in his nature, and he is no longer capable of accepting guidance or becoming fit to live an advanced life.

And all this state of affairs takes place within the sphere of God's Will. The requirement of this Will was that the human being should possess both capacities, the capacity to accept guidance and the capacity to adopt misguidance, and that he should be free to choose one of the two paths, with no compulsion upon him and no decree that is irrevocably fixed. Thus God places upon the path of guidance whomever He wills, and leads astray whomever He wills. This is the meaning of the Will of God. The Will of God becomes a helper to the one who strives in His way, and whoever adopts the path of hostility goes astray by himself. God does not wrong any servant, but they wrong themselves.

The inclination of a human being toward the path of guidance, or his inclination and tendency toward the path of misguidance, both arise from the capacity created in this creature by God and operate only in accordance with His Will. Initially this inclination is created by God, and the guidance or misguidance that comes as a result of this initially created substance also lies within the sphere of the Divine Will. And this Will is unrestricted. The question is: then why is there accountability, reward and punishment? It is because the inclination of a human being is always toward freedom; in his choice he is free. Although this capacity is created within him by God and is under the Divine Will. (See the heading "al-Tawazun" in Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami.)

After explaining the verses of this passage, pause now so that from this study we may gain insight for those who carry out the work of Islamic da'wah in any age and in any community. The guidance given in these verses is beyond the bounds of time and place. It applies to all circumstances and all movements, and in them have been laid down the outlines of the call to religion that remain useful for every age. Here we cannot discuss all the aspects of this point; however, we can identify the signposts of the path.

The truth is that the path of Islamic da'wah is extremely perilous. Thorns are strewn along it everywhere. At every step one has to confront an unpleasant situation. Despite this, victory and success for truth have been guaranteed. Yes, it is correct that the time of victory is a destiny behind the veil, known only to God. It manifests according to His wisdom. Its knowledge belongs to God alone, and no one else knows anything about it, not even the Messenger of God ﷺ was given knowledge of this unseen matter. The difficulties that appear on this path arise from two fundamental factors. The first factor is that when the call to Islam begins, people first turn away from it. Then the second hardship is that a strong desire arises in the heart of the caller that people should accept the call of Islam, enter the path of truth, and be immersed in that zeal and passion with which the caller is filled. He is fervent for this and desires the exaltation of the word of his call. This desire is as painful as the aversion and denial from those addressed are painful. These two factors become, for the caller, the very spirit of that hardship.

In this passage the Qur'an gives guidance concerning both aspects of this hardship. The Qur'an says that those who turn away from the Qur'an's call and deny the Messenger of God ﷺ know with certainty that the Messenger ﷺ and his call are the very truth, and that the Messenger is truthful and brought this message from God. But despite this knowledge, they do not accept this call. They deny it merely out of personal desires and the caprice of the self, although this call is in itself a proof of truth.

"The sun's arrival is the proof of the sun" is applicable here, and it accords exactly with the natural requirements of a human being, provided that the nature is alive and holds within itself the substance for accepting truth. For (verse) "Only those who listen respond" (6:36): indeed, only those who hear accept the call of truth. As for those who insist on denial, their hearts and minds are dead. They themselves are dead, deaf, mute and blind, and immersed in darknesses. The Messenger does not have the power to make the dead hear, nor do the dead hear, even though someone calls out. The duty of a caller is not to bring the dead to life, for that is the attribute of God and is God's work. This is one aspect of the matter. Its other aspect is that God's help is certainly with the truth. However, it is also the established practice of God that it comes at the time appointed by Him, just as the Sunnah of God does not appear before its time and just as the words of God do not change. Likewise it is certain that in the end help does come, and it is also true that it does not come before its time; it appears only at its proper time, and God does not hasten in this matter. This is because trials and afflictions always come upon callers, even if the callers be Messengers themselves, for callers are expected to face difficulties without haste, impatience or urgency, and not to demand help before its time.

The role of the caller to Islam and of the Messenger is defined in these Quranic guidelines, for all eras and all matters. Their role is to convey the message, to advance along their path, and to bear the difficulties of that path. As for whether people come onto the path of guidance or not, this lies outside the limits of the power of the caller and the Messenger, just as it lies outside their duties. Guidance and misguidance operate according to the Sunnah of Allah (the established way of Allah), and there is no change in the Sunnah of Allah. Even if a Messenger earnestly wishes, with all his might, that a beloved person should come to guidance, if the Sunnah of Allah is not in that person's favour, he cannot attain the path of guidance. Conversely, even the enemies and hated people of the Messenger may be granted guidance. In this matter, the personality and essence of the caller and the Messenger carry no weight. The Messenger will not be held to account for how many people came onto the right path as a result of his call. He will only be asked how fully he discharged the duty of the call, how much hardship he bore, and how steadfastly he remained upon his way and his conduct. As for whether people accept guidance or not, that matter is entrusted to Allah.

﴿Whomever Allah wills, He lets go astray, and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path.﴾ (6:39)

﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance.﴾ (6:35)

﴿Only those who listen respond.﴾ (6:36)

Earlier we have already explained that the will of Allah regarding guidance and misguidance is not unconditioned, and that it is connected with people's inclinations and their striving. That explanation is sufficient and complete.

Therefore, the attitude of the caller to the truth should be that he does not give ear to the proposals presented by the people he invites, especially when those proposals concern the foundations of the religion and the method of the call. It is not proper for any caller to present the principles of religion dressed up according to the momentary desires and inclinations of the people. The demand of the polytheists was that the Messenger ﷺ should present extraordinary miracles that conform to the notions and familiar things of their time, and that they could understand; the Quran has mentioned this demand in many places, and this Surah also records their saying:

﴿Why has no angel been sent down to him?﴾ (25:7)

﴿And they say: Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾

﴿And they swear by Allah with their most solemn oaths that if a sign came to them, they would most surely believe in it.﴾ (6:109)

In another Surah, this demand appears in a most astonishing manner. In Surah al-Isra, Allah has described their demand and proposal in these words:

﴿And they said: We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth; or you have a garden of date-palms and grapes, and you cause rivers to gush forth in its midst abundantly; or you cause the heaven to fall upon us in pieces, as you claim; or you bring Allah and the angels before us face to face; or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky, and we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book that we may read.﴾ (17:90–93)

And in Surah al-Furqan it is stated thus:

﴿And they said: What kind of messenger is this, who eats food and walks in the markets? Why has an angel not been sent down to him to be with him as a warner? Or a treasure been bestowed upon him, or he been given a garden from which to eat?﴾ (25:7–8)

In this context, the Messenger ﷺ and the believers are directly forbidden from being affected by the demands of the disbelievers and from expressing, out of such influence, a wish that some miracle should simply appear. Accordingly, the Messenger ﷺ was addressed in these words:

﴿And if their turning away is hard upon you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a ladder into the sky to bring them a sign—but if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance—so do not be among the ignorant. Only those who listen respond; as for the dead, Allah will raise them, then to Him they will be returned.﴾ (6:35–36)

Some Muslims had an inclination in their hearts that the demands the polytheists made for miracles should be fulfilled, because they swore solemn oaths that if a miracle appeared they would surely believe. Such people were told:

﴿Say: Signs are only with Allah, and what will make you aware that when they come they will not believe? And We turn their hearts and their eyes away, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ (6:109–110)

Those who are mentioned here are not lacking in signs or in proof that would lead them to the truth; rather, what is lacking in them is that they do not listen at all. They are like the dead. Guidance is not destined for them. By the Sunnah of Allah, they have deprived themselves of guidance. Therefore, you should know that this religion proceeds according to the Sunnah of Allah, and its station is far too exalted for it to adopt a course according to the desires of people and the proposals of the masses.

Now we come into a wide circle of Quranic verses. Now there come guidances that transcend the bounds of time and place, and that are connected to no single event nor to any particular proposal. Times change, and the desires and demands of people also keep changing; therefore the callers to the truth should not allow the desires of people to divert them from the straight path. It is indeed the desires and demands of people, taken into consideration, that lead some callers to the truth to accept the Islamic ideology as a religion and then, like other religions, to reduce it to a paper religion, confining it to matters of individual life—just as there are many other religions on this earth which come into existence at some time for a limited purpose. Then, under the same impulse, some callers present the Islamic system as a paper scheme or as a detailed paper legal system, and through that scheme they confront the actual conditions of the jahiliyyah (age of ignorance) of the modern era, although the practical condition of the people of jahiliyyah has no connection with Islam. For the people of modern jahiliyyah openly say that Islam is a private belief and has no connection with the real and practical system of life. These callers arrange this practical jahili condition in an Islamic colour for the people. In accordance with it, people remain upon jahiliyyah as before, and they take their judgments to the court of tyranny (taghut). They neither judge according to the Shariah nor get judgments made according to it. All such efforts are extremely base and contemptible acts. A true Muslim should cast away these ideas dyed in modern intellectual colours, because these ideas are immature and cannot remain in their place under any condition, even if they are given the name of a modern style and modern technique of Islamic call.

Even more base and contemptible is the act of those who dress Islam in modern garb and apply to Islam attributes and terminology which were invented by human beings in some historical period, such as socialism and democracy and so on. The aim of this ungrateful effort of such people has been to serve Islam by presenting a developed interpretation of it. Consider carefully: socialism is a collective and socialist system, and it is entirely the product of human beings. Some things in it may be correct and some may be wrong. Likewise, democracy is also a system of government and a system of life. This democratic system has been devised as the result of human thought and reasoning. In it some things may be correct and some may be wrong. In contrast, Islam is a complete system of life, and these ideological principles, a collective social system, a separate economic system and a distinct practical and administrative structure, are all contained in it; and this system is a system devised by Allah. There is in it neither any defect nor any flaw. Therefore whoever does so is not holding a correct position regarding Islam, or he applies to it sayings which are human works.

The people of jahiliyyah were declared polytheists only because they made some of Allah's creatures intercessors with Allah and took them as friends:

﴿And those who take protectors other than Him, [saying]: We only worship them so that they bring us nearer to Allah in closeness.﴾ (39:3)

This is indeed shirk. The question is: those who, going beyond seeking intercession of some people in the court of Allah, seek nearness through the systems of life devised by other people—how much more detestable is their act than the act of the polytheists of Arabia? The polytheists of Arabia, at any rate, acknowledged religion to belong to God alone, though they associated certain persons with Him. These people adopt a system of life other than Allah's and yet seek the nearness of Allah.

Reflect well and understand that Islam is Islam, socialism is socialism, and democracy is democracy. Islam shall bear only that name and that title which Allah has set and designated for it. The other names and titles are those set by people. All these other systems have been devised by people from their own experiences; if someone adopts these systems, he should adopt them under his own name and title. It does not befit any caller to religion to adopt a colour which people have adopted and to claim that he is doing a favour to the religion of Allah.

In any case, we ask such people one thing: why has the religion of Allah become so worthless in your eyes, and why do you not place the greatness of Allah in your hearts in the manner that is His due? Why do you present Islam today in the colour of socialism and democracy? For these were the trials of the present age and the things beloved to the present age, in that people desired to escape from feudalism; yet before feudalism too, dictatorship was a beloved system, and through it people sought deliverance from small states and scattered oppressive states—as Germany and Italy passed through that stage, for example. Tomorrow, beyond the systems mentioned above, some new system may come into force in the world which will be a new experience or a new colour for the people of the world, and in which man will be the slave of man in a new form. Then will you again tomorrow affix the label of that new system and colour upon Islam, so that you may present Islam in a colour which people desire?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 37–39 (part 3 of 3):

The approach that the preacher of the religion should adopt, both in the section under discussion here and in other places in the Qur'an, is that he should advance with his call and his ideology while remaining self-sufficient, and should not give any ear at all to those who offer proposals for amending the Islamic call. Furthermore, he should present the religion of Islam with its original name and title, and should not strive to combine it with other current names and titles. He should endeavour to awaken people through the Islamic method and Islamic means alone. Allah is independent of all the worlds. If anyone does not accept this call in the manner in which he would serve Allah alone and emerge from all other servitudes, then the religion of Islam has no need of such a person, and Allah the Exalted has no need of any rebellious or any obedient one.

Islam, in terms of its fundamental elements and its distinctive characteristics, possesses a unique originality (Originality). It is Allah's intention that these characteristics and these foundational values should prevail. In the practical system of the world, this religion possesses originality. And the manner in which it invites man to reflection is also unique. The God who revealed this religion with its distinctive features and its constituent elements is the same God who created this human being, and He knows well what man thinks continually and what waves of desires rise in his heart.

In this section there is also an example of the style of address that the Qur'an uses when it addresses human nature. This is also one of its fundamental models of the style of address. The Qur'an creates a link and relationship between human nature and the natural operation of this universe. It turns the signs and indications of the cosmos toward human nature. In the course of this, the Qur'an inclines the natural structure of man to accept these natural indications. The Qur'an knows that when the creative indications of this universe reach the depths of human nature, man responds immediately.

(Verse) "Only those who listen respond" (6:36). This is the mode of expression that addresses us in this section. Let us observe it.

(Verse 37) "And they say: Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord? Say: Surely Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know."

This verse relates the words of those who denied the religion of Islam, opposed the Messenger ﷺ, and demanded supernatural miracles that their population could see with their own eyes. Here, after relating their demand, a notion is planted in their hearts: what would be the consequences if their demand were granted? That they would fall under the severe grip of Allah and be destroyed and ruined. It is evident that Allah is capable of sending down a miracle. But the requirement of Allah's mercy is that He does not send it down, and the requirement of Allah's wisdom is that He rejects the demand of these people.

The context now moves away from this limited subject and enters the vastness of the universe, and people are directed to: look at this universe spread around you; those signs and miracles exist within the book of the cosmos itself, in comparison with which those extraordinary things that they demand are not extraordinary at all. And these miracles and signs are established in the heart of this cosmos forever, so that not only one present generation but all generations may keep seeing them.

(Verse 38) "And there is no creature in the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered."

"Look at any animal that walks on the earth and any bird that flies through the air with its wings: all of them are kinds like you. We have left no deficiency in the decree of their destiny. Then all of them are being gathered toward their Lord." This is indeed a terrifying reality. It is that great reality which, at that time, their intellect could see through observation, since at that time they had no systematic knowledge in science. That is: the species and genera of all creatures around you are, each in its place, nations and communities. Each has its own distinctive characteristic and its own system. Yet this observation is such a great reality that as its scope expands, so does the certainty of its greatness grow. It increases human knowledge; yes, human knowledge increases. Human sciences can add to the knowledge of this universe, but through them no reality of this universe can be increased. Parallel to human sciences are the unseen knowledge of Allah, which carries out its work, and the divine knowledge and will continue their administrative operation over every matter; and in this universe, as our observation goes further, this reality becomes ever clearer.

The question is this: in comparison with the divine powers operating within this universe, which function in a most miraculous manner, what is the status of the miracles these people demand? These cosmic signs and miracles are realities; as human sight and insight advance, they see new aspects of them, and they will continue to see them until the Resurrection.

In this selection and example, the Qur'anic method of speech is that the Qur'an creates a connection and join between human nature and this universe. It opens the windows of nature to the secrets of the cosmos, and in this way the Qur'an, through the secrets of this great universe, leaves deep effects upon human personality and thought.

The Qur'an does not present to human nature merely dialectical theological discourses. It does not present before them merely dialectical scholastic theology and tawhidi discussions, nor does it present rational and sensory philosophies. These matters are contrary to the Islamic and Qur'anic method. The Qur'an presents to people the actual observable realities of the world of existence and the unseen world.
