The result of this was that the people of Europe concluded that devotion to God meant the denial of nature, and so they went astray in the desert of disbelief and atheism, and ran after mirages, living a life even more despicable than the monastic life of the Church. (See my book Al-Mustaqbal li-hadha al-Din, the chapter on "Unnatural Divergence.")

The Jews benefited greatly from this situation: they turned Christians away from their true religion, so that the leash would come into their hands, and they could spread immorality, sin and moral laxity among them thoroughly, and use them for their own purposes in the manner in which a donkey is used. They expressed this very explicitly in the Talmud and in the Protocols of the Jewish elders. The Jews could not have done this until they had misled people by criticizing that unnatural history of Europe with the Church, and by alienating people from the Church and making them atheists.

The final expression of this open and tireless deceitful struggle appeared in the form of international communism. It should be remembered that international communism was a great Jewish conspiracy to make people atheists and misguided. For more than half a century these people have been busy, through all governmental media, making people atheists; yet in the depths of the hearts of other nations the belief in God still exists. Even a savage man like Stalin eventually had to reconcile with the Church, and during the Second World War he released the clergy of the Church. The Second World War placed such a burden upon him that his neck too eventually bowed before the notion of God, because the notion of God existed within the nature of people, although Stalin and his handful of companions who held the reins of government were atheists.

Taking advantage of their crusader hirelings, the Jews also made extraordinary efforts to bring a false flood of disbelief and atheism into these nations as well. Although the belief in God had become extremely weak in the hearts and minds of Muslim nations, the movement of disbelief and atheism which they started in the Islamic world through the so-called leader Ataturk of Turkey failed miserably within Turkey itself, although the Jews and their hirelings beat the drums of this so-called leader's greatness and superiority and opened the doors of financial assistance from every side. They also wrote countless books on the atheist movement of Turkey, and in them its atheistic experiment was praised extremely. That is why they now do not call the other experiments they are conducting in the Islamic world after the Turkish experiment by the names of heresy and zandaqa; rather, here they spread atheism in the name of Islam, so that their movement does not collide with human natural inclinations, just as the experiment of Ataturk collided with the natural tendency of man and it was shattered to pieces in its place. Now these people spread filth, dirt and moral laxity under the shade of Islamic flags. In this way they destroy raw human intellects, and the Jews and their crusader hirelings do this work with great arrangement in the Islamic world.

But the reality that is revealed after all these experiments is that human nature knows its Lord well; it also acknowledges its Lord as One without partner. If at some time the dust of depravity settles upon human nature and it becomes buried beneath that pollution, then as soon as some sudden danger confronts it and a person is shaken, this dust and cloud is swept away, the true human nature becomes clearly visible, and the person calls upon his Lord in the way he called upon Him at the time when Allah created him. Suddenly he becomes an obedient believer and a person who is humble and submissive. The fabric of this worldwide conspiracy of the Jews and their hirelings is shattered by a single crashing cry of nature, and nature falls again at the threshold of the Lord. In whatever region this natural voice is raised, that conspiracy is annihilated there. And however much the Jews and their hirelings may strive, this voice of truth will continue to be raised upon the earth.

In such circumstances, the layers of the dust-cloud of shirk are swept away from the human heart and mind, human nature becomes clear and comes to the fore, and the belief in Tawhid, which remains present in the depths of human nature, comes to the surface, and human nature calls upon the One Lord alone.

﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, would you call upon anyone other than Allah? Tell [them], if you are truthful.﴾ (40)

"Say to them: Consider and tell: if a great affliction from Allah were to come upon you, or the final hour were to arrive, would you at that time call upon anyone other than Allah? Tell us, if you are truthful."

Here a frightening situation is presented before the mind, and some scenes of destruction and ruin in the world are brought before the eyes, or the imagination that the Hour suddenly comes to pass. When these scenes come before human nature, the natural feeling begins to stir. The horror of these scenes comes readily to the mind, and Allah, who knows well as the Creator of nature, knows that by this method nature fully perceives these scenes and easily attains the reality. All its powers are set in motion because of these scenes, for the reality contained in these frightening scenes exists within human nature. The Creator of nature knows well that this reality exists within nature, and so the Lord addresses nature in this style, and nature accepts this image, trembles, and, from beneath the layers of heedlessness and rebellion, clearly emerges. Allah asks them, or demands an answer, and wants the answer from their own tongue, so that it may be known that this answer is the true expression of their nature. ﴿Aghayra Allahi tad'un﴾: "Do you call upon others besides Allah? If you are truthful, then answer."

Without waiting for their response, the true and genuine answer comes, which in practice conforms to their nature. Even if they do not answer, their conduct on such occasions is indeed like this.

﴿Nay, it is Him alone you call upon, and He removes that for which you call upon Him, if He wills, and you forget what you associate [with Him].﴾ (41)

"At that time you call upon Allah alone. Then, if He wills, He removes that affliction from you. On such occasions you forget your associates whom you have set up."

Rather, you will call upon Allah alone, and in such circumstances you will entirely forget your shirkiyya notions. This frightening situation will bring your true nature to the surface, and now this nature will call upon Allah alone. It will not even remember that a person, while committing shirk, was also calling upon others besides Allah. Even the reality of shirk will be wiped from their minds, because knowledge of the Creator is that true reality which exists within human nature. As for shirkiyya notions, they are like a passing mirage, a temporary thing. Due to certain temporary factors and circumstances, these shirkiyya notions arise. These temporary veils fall upon human nature and conceal the true reality beneath. When some frightening circumstance shakes a person, the upper veils and dust are swept away, and the true reality emerges from below. Now this nature displays its reaction before the Lord of Majesty, and hopes that in such frightening circumstances only Allah can help a person, and in such situations no other recourse remains for a person.

This is the true natural course of man. Allah presents this natural reaction of man before the polytheists for reflection. But in such circumstances, what course does the self-sufficiency of Allah adopt? That if Allah wills to remove these difficulties from them, His will is unrestricted. None can reject His decree. If He wills, He accepts their supplications, and the afflictions are completely or partially removed. And if the demands of His will are that He does not accept their call, this decision depends upon His destiny, His knowledge, and His wisdom.

Although shirk is contrary to human nature, at times a person adopts shirkiyya notions. He adopts them when he deviates from the path of nature, and this deviation occurs due to various factors, and these factors suppress the pure nature that exists within a person, and beneath these factors the true recognition of the One Lord disappears from human sight. Because man has never been a denier of the existence of the Creator, nor has it been his natural position to deny the existence of the Creator.

As we have seen many times, those who outwardly declare that they are atheists and deny the existence of the Creator, in reality are not deniers of God. We cannot believe that those whom the hand of power has made, and upon every atom and every fibre of whose existence the imprint of the hand of power is present, could then become completely forgetful of their Creator and become true atheists. Every atom of their existence bears witness to the Divine Being.

There is a long history of this terrible punishment descending upon humanity: a long struggle continued for ages between the Church and human nature. The Church remained engaged in efforts to eliminate natural factors and motives. The people of the Church denied the legitimacy of human natural desires and inclinations, while in reality they lived a most despicable life full of debaucheries. Thus the enmity and conflict with nature persisted in Europe for centuries. The result of this was that the people of Europe concluded that devotion to God meant the denial of nature, and so they went astray in the desert of disbelief and atheism, and ran after mirages, living a life even more despicable than the monastic life of the Church. (See my book Al-Mustaqbal li-hadha al-Din, the chapter on "Unnatural Divergence.")

The Jews benefited greatly from this situation: they turned Christians away from their true religion, so that the leash would come into their hands, and they could spread immorality, sin and moral laxity among them thoroughly, and use them for their own purposes in the manner in which a donkey is used. They expressed this very explicitly in the Talmud and in the Protocols of the Jewish elders. The Jews could not have done this until they had misled people by criticizing that unnatural history of Europe with the Church, and by alienating people from the Church and making them atheists.

The final expression of this open and tireless deceitful struggle appeared in the form of international communism. It should be remembered that international communism was a great Jewish conspiracy to make people atheists and misguided. For more than half a century these people have been busy, through all governmental media, making people atheists; yet in the depths of the hearts of other nations the belief in God still exists. Even a savage man like Stalin eventually had to reconcile with the Church, and during the Second World War he released the clergy of the Church. The Second World War placed such a burden upon him that his neck too eventually bowed before the notion of God, because the notion of God existed within the nature of people, although Stalin and his handful of companions who held the reins of government were atheists.

Taking advantage of their crusader hirelings, the Jews also made extraordinary efforts to bring a false flood of disbelief and atheism into these nations as well. Although the belief in God had become extremely weak in the hearts and minds of Muslim nations, the movement of disbelief and atheism which they started in the Islamic world through the so-called leader Ataturk of Turkey failed miserably within Turkey itself, although the Jews and their hirelings beat the drums of this so-called leader's greatness and superiority and opened the doors of financial assistance from every side. They also wrote countless books on the atheist movement of Turkey, and in them its atheistic experiment was praised extremely. That is why they now do not call the other experiments they are conducting in the Islamic world after the Turkish experiment by the names of heresy and zandaqa; rather, here they spread atheism in the name of Islam, so that their movement does not collide with human natural inclinations, just as the experiment of Ataturk collided with the natural tendency of man and it was shattered to pieces in its place. Now these people spread filth, dirt and moral laxity under the shade of Islamic flags. In this way they destroy raw human intellects, and the Jews and their crusader hirelings do this work with great arrangement in the Islamic world.

But the reality that is revealed after all these experiments is that human nature knows its Lord well; it also acknowledges its Lord as One without partner. If at some time the dust of depravity settles upon human nature and it becomes buried beneath that pollution, then as soon as some sudden danger confronts it and a person is shaken, this dust and cloud is swept away, the true human nature becomes clearly visible, and the person calls upon his Lord in the way he called upon Him at the time when Allah created him. Suddenly he becomes an obedient believer and a person who is humble and submissive. The fabric of this worldwide conspiracy of the Jews and their hirelings is shattered by a single crashing cry of nature, and nature falls again at the threshold of the Lord. In whatever region this natural voice is raised, that conspiracy is annihilated there. And however much the Jews and their hirelings may strive, this voice of truth will continue to be raised upon the earth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 42–45 (part 1 of 2):

(Verses) 42 to 45.

This wave is a glimpse of the punishment of God and points to the real situation of human history, but instead of mentioning a specific event, it explains how people come within the grip of the punishment of God, and what their end becomes. Before the punishment, how God keeps giving them respite after respite, and how warning after warning is given to them. But they keep forgetting, and sometimes even the most severe punishment cannot awaken them from the slumber of heedlessness. And when blessings and favours are showered upon them, they do not give thanks, nor do they fear the loss of blessings and trials. Their nature becomes so corrupted that they become incurable. The corruption of their deeds in life becomes so great that reform of their condition is no longer possible. The proof is complete against such people, and God's punishment comes upon them in such a way that not a single soul of them remains alive.

"And We did send (messengers) to peoples before you, and We seized them with adversity and affliction, that they might humble themselves. Why then, when Our might came upon them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hard, and Satan made attractive to them what they used to do." (42–43)

"We sent messengers to many nations before you, and We afflicted those nations with troubles and hardships so that they would bow down in humility. Then, when Our severity came upon them, why did they not show humility? But their hearts became hard, and Satan assured them that what they were doing was excellent."

Among the nations of human history there are very many such peoples, and the Qur'an has counted many of them among mankind and described their conditions. The Qur'an described these conditions at a time when human history had not even been compiled. The books of history that humans have compiled relate only to very recent periods; they are of recent origin and newborn. Our history is not capable of understanding and explaining the longest history of man, because the history of human habitation on the earth is very long, and the history that man has compiled is indeed a bundle of falsehoods. It is also very brief, and it has not been able to encompass the real causes and factors of history. Some of these historical factors are hidden in the depths of the human soul, and some are causes concealed behind the veil of the unseen, and only a very small part of them has become manifest to man. Then, even those that have become manifest to some humans were erred in their collection and compilation. Even when events were collected correctly, errors were made in understanding them, and true and false events and causes could not be separated from one another. Only a few events could be correctly analysed. Therefore, for any human to claim that he has encompassed the events and causes of the whole of human history, and that he can scientifically interpret these events, and that he can correctly determine the direction of history's future and draw conclusions, is a very great lie that anyone could utter. A very surprising matter is that some people are not ashamed to claim such a lie. If such people said that these events are expected to appear in the future, their statement would be reasonable; but if a lying person finds people who are ready at all times to confirm his lie, what reason would he have left to refrain from lying?

God, however, states the truth, and He is the Truthful in speech. God knows what events have occurred in the world, and out of His mercy and grace He explains these realities to His servants. The word of God comprises the decree of God, His judgments, and His sunnah (way) in this universe, so that people may take care and draw lessons from events. They may understand that behind these events were causes and factors that operated, and what the apparent causes appeared to be, so that they may correctly understand these historical events and be able to explain, analyse and dissect them, and then understand the effects on future history and the results that will emerge, and so that their reasoning may be in the light of the sunnah of God, whose principles God has stated here in His Book.

In the verses under discussion, a picture is drawn of events that have repeatedly occurred among various peoples. Messengers from God came to these peoples, but when they denied the messengers, God put them to trial through difficulties and troubles. These afflictions were both material and physical. They were placed in difficult circumstances and difficult problems, but these afflictions had not yet reached the level of the punishment of God mentioned in the earlier verses. That is, these afflictions did not reach the level of destruction and ruin.

The Qur'an has presented some examples of these peoples and has also mentioned the afflictions and hardships placed upon them. Among them, the story of Pharaoh and his companions is very famous.

"And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and shortage of fruits, that perhaps they would take heed. But when good came to them, they said, 'This is ours by right'; and if an evil befell them, they ascribed it as an omen to Moses and those with him. Indeed, their omen is with God, but most of them do not know. And they said, 'Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not believe you.' So We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, as distinct signs; but they waxed proud, and they were a guilty people." (130–133)

"We afflicted the people of Pharaoh for several years with famine and a shortage of produce, so that perhaps they would come to their senses. But their condition was that when good times came, they would say that they deserved them; and when bad times came, they would hold Moses and his companions responsible as an ill omen. Hear this: their omen is with God, but most of them did not know. And they said to Moses, 'Whatever sign you bring to us to bewitch us, we will not be believers in you.' At last, We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and blood, as separate signs; yet they remained arrogant and continued in rebellion." This is one example of the events to which this verse points.

God afflicted this people with troubles and calamities for the sole reason that they might come to their senses, that they might look within their conscience and reflect upon their situation, so that perhaps, because of these hardships, they would begin to humble themselves before God and make themselves submissive and lowly before Him. They would abandon their pride and arrogance, adopt a serious attitude, and pray sincerely that God remove these difficulties from them, open the doors of His mercy for them. But they did not do what was proper for them. They refused to enter into the refuge of God and continued their obstinacy and rebellion, and even because of these difficulties their thinking did not turn in that direction. Their inner vision did not open, and their hearts did not soften. Satan was following them closely, adorning for them their misguidance and rebellion. "But their hearts became even harder, and Satan assured them that what you are doing is excellent."

A heart that does not turn to God in return for hardships and afflictions has dried up within in the way a stone dries, and there is not even a drop of moisture in it that hardships and afflictions could squeeze. This heart has died, and whatever pressure is applied to it, it will not feel anything. All the material for accepting truth has left this heart. It has fully died, so no matter how many pinches are given to make it feel, there will be no benefit. Yet living hearts awaken as a result of such jolts, and as soon as such afflictions come from God, they accept the truth. They wake up, their windows open, and thus they attain turning to God. They become deserving of that mercy, compassion and generosity which God has made binding upon Himself. For a person who is already dead, these afflictions become a reckoning and a punishment, and they bring him no benefit. On the contrary, all of his excuses are ended and all arguments become useless. He is declared deserving of an evil end and wretchedness. Therefore, God's punishment becomes certain for him.

These earlier nations, whose accounts God reveals to the Messenger of God ﷺ and conveys to us through him, did not take any lesson from these afflictions and hardships. They did not turn to God, nor did they supplicate before Him with open hands. Satan made their turning away and obstinacy appear attractive to them, and they were not ready to abandon it. God gives respite to such nations, leaves them free, and they transgress all limits.

"So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair. So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." (44–45)

"Then, when they forgot the admonition that had been given to them, We opened for them the doors of every kind of prosperity, until, when they exulted in what had been bestowed upon them, We suddenly seized them, and at once they were in despair. Thus the root of the people who did wrong was cut off, and praise belongs to God, the Lord of the worlds."

Prosperity is also in fact a trial, just as affliction and hardship are trials, but prosperity is more severe than poverty and misfortune. God tests human beings with prosperity just as He tests them with adversity. When a believer is struck by adversity and falls into trial, he endures patiently; and when prosperity comes to a believer, he gives thanks to God, so he is well in every condition. A hadith reports: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all his conditions are good, and this distinction belongs only to the believer. If prosperity comes to him and he gives thanks, it is good for him; and if he is in hardship and is patient, that too is good for him." (Narrated by Muslim)

As for those nations that denied their messengers, whose stories God has related here, they forgot the guidance that had been given to them. God knew that they were about to be destroyed; so God put some of them into hardships and afflictions, yet they did not come to their senses. And for some of them, God opened the doors of blessings, made everything abundant, and left the field open for them so that they might advance far in rebellion. Here the Qur'anic mode of expression is also very beautiful.

"We opened for them the gates of everything" (6:44): "We opened for them the doors of every kind of prosperity."

This includes every kind of goodness, every kind of necessity, equipment and great abundance of honour and standing. Everything came to them in flood-like plenty, without hindrance or restriction; blessings were made common for them, and they received them easily, cheaply, without any labour or toil. In truth, this is a very impressive scene and a rare example of the artistic mode of expression of the Qur'an. (See my book Al-Tasvir al-Fanni, chapter Tariqat al-Qur'an.)

"Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given" (6:44–45): they were drowned in the abundance of every kind of goodness and equipment, and they became absorbed in ease and luxury. In such circumstances they neither remembered God nor gave thanks to Him; the thought of the true Bestower faded from their hearts, and their hearts were emptied of the fear of God. They became completely enveloped in pursuit of comfort and the pleasures of food and drink, and they handed themselves over completely to these things. Lofty values lost their significance in their lives, and this is the common habit of people immersed in amusement, play and pleasure: from them lofty values disappear. After this, order and good habits disappear from their society, and they become completely ruined morally. Thus these conditions result in their whole life being destroyed, and this destruction then becomes natural. This is exactly the sunnah of God.

"Then We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair. So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off." The word dabir of a people refers to the one who comes last, that is, their last person. When the last person has been cut off, those before him are all the more cut off.

"Those who did wrong" (6:45): here it refers to those who committed shirk, and therefore the Qur'an in most places describes the polytheists as wrongdoers (zalimin) and applies the word zulm to shirk.

(Verse 45) "So the one who committed wrong was cut off, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." This is a comment on how Allah cut off the roots of the polytheists: having given them respite, He seized them suddenly. Is praise due to Allah only for His bounties and favours? Yes, but the purification of the earth from wrongdoers is itself a kind of blessing. Moreover, praise is due to Allah for His mercy, and clearing the earth is among the greatest mercies.

Allah seized the peoples of Nuh (peace be upon him), Hud (peace be upon him), Salih (peace be upon him) and Lut (peace be upon him). He seized Pharaoh, the people of Greece and the people of Rome, and in accordance with the same sunnah He seized other nations too after their rise. First He greatly advanced their civilisation and culture, and then He destroyed and ruined them. These are, in any case, the secrets of Allah's decrees. But the sunnah of Allah is evident in this story of rise and fall, and Allah records it here in this principled manner.

These peoples had their own civilisations, and in their time they enjoyed great ascendancy. They had great abundance and wealth. In some respects they were more prosperous than the developed age of today. They had splendour, pomp, equipment and plenty, and they were under the illusion that they would remain as they were. These nations were also deceiving other nations, which were unaware of the sunnah of Allah regarding prosperity and progress.

These peoples could not understand that the sunnah of Allah operates in this universe. Nor could they understand that they were being given respite, in exact accordance with the policy of that sunnah. Those who were moving in the sky of the sunnah of Allah had their eyes dazzled by the rain of Allah's blessings. Power and strength had produced in them very great confidence, and they had fallen into delusion because of the respite and reprieve granted to these prosperous nations. These people neither worshipped Allah nor had knowledge of Him. They rebelled against the sovereignty of Allah; rather, they claimed the right of sovereignty for themselves, although sovereignty is one of the important attributes of divinity. These people spread corruption on the earth and inflicted oppression on people, because they had claimed sovereignty against Allah. When I was in America, what I saw with my own eyes was an embodiment of this verse.

(Verse 44) "So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of every thing."

The scene depicted in this verse shows that these people had abundance of provision, and from every side there was a flood of facilities without measure rushing towards them. This scene was fully at its height in America.

I saw that this people is extremely proud of that prosperity, and it was clearly fixed in their consciousness that this abundance of facilities was reserved only for white-skinned people. Their conduct towards coloured people is extremely arrogant and savage. Americans regard the people of the whole globe as so worthless that compared with it even the Nazism of the Jews has no worth, although the Jews are very famous for it and national and racial pride is their hallmark. The attitude of white Americans towards coloured Americans is even worse and harsher than that of the Jews. This harshness becomes even greater especially when the coloured people are Muslims.

In America I kept watching all of this and kept expecting that the sunnah of Allah would surely do its work one day. I can see that the sunnah of Allah is moving slowly but surely towards American society.

(Verse 44–45) "Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair. So the root of the people who did wrong was cut off, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."

After the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), Allah showed this mercy to the nations of the world: they would not be transformed, nor would they be uprooted and cast away entirely. But various kinds of Allah's punishments still keep coming, especially upon the nations that have been given prosperity and abundance. Every day various kinds of punishment come upon them, even though the production of the necessities of life among them has exceeded limits and they have been blessed with abundance of provision and facilities.

Psychological torment, spiritual restlessness, sexual licentiousness and moral corruption have destroyed them. In their prosperity, material production and equipment they have no means of contentment, and their whole life is close to being drowned in wretchedness and anguish. (See my book Islam aur Mushkilat-e-Tehzeeb, the chapter Khabt wa Idtirab.) Despite this prosperity, the moral condition of these people is such that great political secrets are sold for a few coins, and the crime of treachery against an entire nation is committed; and what is gained? A few moments of debauchery, sexual pleasure and a few coins. These are signs which point to grave danger for such nations in the near future.

These are the very first signs of the destruction of the Western nations. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke the truth: "When you see that Allah gives someone everything he desires despite his evil conduct, know that he is being given respite." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse: "Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair. So the root of the people who did wrong was cut off, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." (Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim)

But it is also worth noting that the principle of destroying the people of falsehood, and the sunnah of Allah in His scheme, does not consist only of annihilating the people of falsehood; it also includes the establishment and dominance of the people of truth, and that these people of truth emerge in the form of a community. The fundamental principle is that Allah strikes falsehood through truth and through the people of truth, and smashes the head of falsehood. Falsehood is annihilated. Therefore the people of truth should not sit back in slackness, and should not sit with hands folded merely waiting for the sunnah of Allah, because the sunnah of Allah too is brought into effect through Islamic struggle. If the people of truth sit down inactive, they will cease to be the people of truth, and they will no longer be capable of achieving dominance or smashing the head of falsehood, especially if they sit down idle and inactive. Truth emerges in the form of a community which is striving for the position of Allah's sovereignty on earth, and defends itself against those who have established their own sovereignty against Allah, whereas the sovereignty of Allah is one of the distinctive attributes of divinity. This is the real and fundamental truth.

(Verse 46) "And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted."

Now the context brings the polytheists face to face with the punishment of Allah, and this proposed form of punishment relates to their own selves and their faculties. It concerns their power of sight, power of hearing and power of perception. The suggestion is: if Allah takes away these faculties, who is there who could restore them to you? There is no one. Having reflected, they too become certain that there would be no one who could give them back hearing, sight and perception if Allah were to take these faculties away.

They would abandon their pride and arrogance, adopt a serious attitude, and pray sincerely that God remove these difficulties from them, open the doors of His mercy for them. But they did not do what was proper for them. They refused to enter into the refuge of God and continued their obstinacy and rebellion, and even because of these difficulties their thinking did not turn in that direction. Their inner vision did not open, and their hearts did not soften. Satan was following them closely, adorning for them their misguidance and rebellion. "But their hearts became even harder, and Satan assured them that what you are doing is excellent."

A heart that does not turn to God in return for hardships and afflictions has dried up within in the way a stone dries, and there is not even a drop of moisture in it that hardships and afflictions could squeeze. This heart has died, and whatever pressure is applied to it, it will not feel anything. All the material for accepting truth has left this heart. It has fully died, so no matter how many pinches are given to make it feel, there will be no benefit. Yet living hearts awaken as a result of such jolts, and as soon as such afflictions come from God, they accept the truth. They wake up, their windows open, and thus they attain turning to God. They become deserving of that mercy, compassion and generosity which God has made binding upon Himself. For a person who is already dead, these afflictions become a reckoning and a punishment, and they bring him no benefit. On the contrary, all of his excuses are ended and all arguments become useless. He is declared deserving of an evil end and wretchedness. Therefore, God's punishment becomes certain for him.

These earlier nations, whose accounts God reveals to the Messenger of God ﷺ and conveys to us through him, did not take any lesson from these afflictions and hardships. They did not turn to God, nor did they supplicate before Him with open hands. Satan made their turning away and obstinacy appear attractive to them, and they were not ready to abandon it. God gives respite to such nations, leaves them free, and they transgress all limits.

"So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair. So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." (44–45)

"Then, when they forgot the admonition that had been given to them, We opened for them the doors of every kind of prosperity, until, when they exulted in what had been bestowed upon them, We suddenly seized them, and at once they were in despair. Thus the root of the people who did wrong was cut off, and praise belongs to God, the Lord of the worlds."

Prosperity is also in fact a trial, just as affliction and hardship are trials, but prosperity is more severe than poverty and misfortune. God tests human beings with prosperity just as He tests them with adversity. When a believer is struck by adversity and falls into trial, he endures patiently; and when prosperity comes to a believer, he gives thanks to God, so he is well in every condition. A hadith reports: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all his conditions are good, and this distinction belongs only to the believer. If prosperity comes to him and he gives thanks, it is good for him; and if he is in hardship and is patient, that too is good for him." (Narrated by Muslim)

As for those nations that denied their messengers, whose stories God has related here, they forgot the guidance that had been given to them. God knew that they were about to be destroyed; so God put some of them into hardships and afflictions, yet they did not come to their senses. And for some of them, God opened the doors of blessings, made everything abundant, and left the field open for them so that they might advance far in rebellion. Here the Qur'anic mode of expression is also very beautiful.

"We opened for them the gates of everything" (6:44): "We opened for them the doors of every kind of prosperity."

This includes every kind of goodness, every kind of necessity, equipment and great abundance of honour and standing. Everything came to them in flood-like plenty, without hindrance or restriction; blessings were made common for them, and they received them easily, cheaply, without any labour or toil. In truth, this is a very impressive scene and a rare example of the artistic mode of expression of the Qur'an. (See my book Al-Tasvir al-Fanni, chapter Tariqat al-Qur'an.)

"Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given" (6:44–45): they were drowned in the abundance of every kind of goodness and equipment, and they became absorbed in ease and luxury. In such circumstances they neither remembered God nor gave thanks to Him; the thought of the true Bestower faded from their hearts, and their hearts were emptied of the fear of God. They became completely enveloped in pursuit of comfort and the pleasures of food and drink, and they handed themselves over completely to these things. Lofty values lost their significance in their lives, and this is the common habit of people immersed in amusement, play and pleasure: from them lofty values disappear. After this, order and good habits disappear from their society, and they become completely ruined morally. Thus these conditions result in their whole life being destroyed, and this destruction then becomes natural. This is exactly the sunnah of God.

"Then We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair. So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off." The word dabir of a people refers to the one who comes last, that is, their last person. When the last person has been cut off, those before him are all the more cut off.

"Those who did wrong" (6:45): here it refers to those who committed shirk, and therefore the Qur'an in most places describes the polytheists as wrongdoers (zalimin) and applies the word zulm to shirk.

This is a comment on how Allah cut off the roots of the polytheists: having given them respite, He seized them suddenly. Is praise due to Allah only for His bounties and favours? Yes, but the purification of the earth from wrongdoers is itself a kind of blessing. Moreover, praise is due to Allah for His mercy, and clearing the earth is among the greatest mercies.

Allah seized the peoples of Nuh (peace be upon him), Hud (peace be upon him), Salih (peace be upon him) and Lut (peace be upon him). These peoples had their own civilisations, and in their time they enjoyed great ascendancy. They had great abundance and wealth. In some respects they were more prosperous than the developed age of today. They had splendour, pomp, equipment and plenty, and they were under the illusion that they would remain as they were. These nations were also deceiving other nations, which were unaware of the sunnah of Allah regarding prosperity and progress.

These peoples could not understand that the sunnah of Allah operates in this universe. Nor could they understand that they were being given respite, in exact accordance with the policy of that sunnah. Those who were moving in the sky of the sunnah of Allah had their eyes dazzled by the rain of Allah's blessings. Power and strength had produced in them very great confidence, and they had fallen into delusion because of the respite and reprieve granted to these prosperous nations. These people neither worshipped Allah nor had knowledge of Him. They rebelled against the sovereignty of Allah; rather, they claimed the right of sovereignty for themselves, although sovereignty is one of the important attributes of divinity. These people spread corruption on the earth and inflicted oppression on people, because they had claimed sovereignty against Allah. When I was in America, what I saw with my own eyes was an embodiment of this verse.

(Verse 44) "So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of every thing."

The scene depicted in this verse shows that these people had abundance of provision, and from every side there was a flood of facilities without measure rushing towards them. This scene was fully at its height in America.

I saw that this people is extremely proud of that prosperity, and it was clearly fixed in their consciousness that this abundance of facilities was reserved only for white-skinned people. Their conduct towards coloured people is extremely arrogant and savage. Americans regard the people of the whole globe as so worthless that compared with it even the Nazism of the Jews has no worth, although the Jews are very famous for it and national and racial pride is their hallmark. The attitude of white Americans towards coloured Americans is even worse and harsher than that of the Jews. This harshness becomes even greater especially when the coloured people are Muslims.

In America I kept watching all of this and kept expecting that the sunnah of Allah would surely do its work one day. I can see that the sunnah of Allah is moving slowly but surely towards American society.

Psychological torment, spiritual restlessness, sexual licentiousness and moral corruption have destroyed them. Despite this prosperity, the moral condition of these people is such that great political secrets are sold for a few coins, and the crime of treachery against an entire nation is committed; and what is gained? These are the very first signs of the destruction of the Western nations. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke the truth: "When you see that Allah gives someone everything he desires despite his evil conduct, know that he is being given respite." Truth emerges in the form of a community which is striving for the position of Allah's sovereignty on earth, and defends itself against those who have established their own sovereignty against Allah, whereas the sovereignty of Allah is one of the distinctive attributes of divinity. This is the real and fundamental truth.

Among the nations of human history there are very many such peoples, and the Qur'an has counted many of them among mankind and described their conditions. The Qur'an described these conditions at a time when human history had not even been compiled. The books of history that humans have compiled relate only to very recent periods; they are of recent origin and newborn. Our history is not capable of understanding and explaining the longest history of man, because the history of human habitation on the earth is very long, and the history that man has compiled is indeed a bundle of falsehoods. It is also very brief, and it has not been able to encompass the real causes and factors of history. Some of these historical factors are hidden in the depths of the human soul, and some are causes concealed behind the veil of the unseen, and only a very small part of them has become manifest to man. Then, even those that have become manifest to some humans were erred in their collection and compilation. Even when events were collected correctly, errors were made in understanding them, and true and false events and causes could not be separated from one another. Only a few events could be correctly analysed. Therefore, for any human to claim that he has encompassed the events and causes of the whole of human history, and that he can scientifically interpret these events, and that he can correctly determine the direction of history's future and draw conclusions, is a very great lie that anyone could utter. A very surprising matter is that some people are not ashamed to claim such a lie. If such people said that these events are expected to appear in the future, their statement would be reasonable; but if a lying person finds people who are ready at all times to confirm his lie, what reason would he have left to refrain from lying?

God, however, states the truth, and He is the Truthful in speech. God knows what events have occurred in the world, and out of His mercy and grace He explains these realities to His servants. The word of God comprises the decree of God, His judgments, and His sunnah (way) in this universe, so that people may take care and draw lessons from events. They may understand that behind these events were causes and factors that operated, and what the apparent causes appeared to be, so that they may correctly understand these historical events and be able to explain, analyse and dissect them, and then understand the effects on future history and the results that will emerge, and so that their reasoning may be in the light of the sunnah of God, whose principles God has stated here in His Book.

In the verses under discussion, a picture is drawn of events that have repeatedly occurred among various peoples. Messengers from God came to these peoples, but when they denied the messengers, God put them to trial through difficulties and troubles. These afflictions were both material and physical. They were placed in difficult circumstances and difficult problems, but these afflictions had not yet reached the level of the punishment of God mentioned in the earlier verses. That is, these afflictions did not reach the level of destruction and ruin.

The Qur'an has presented some examples of these peoples and has also mentioned the afflictions and hardships placed upon them. Among them, the story of Pharaoh and his companions is very famous.

"And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and shortage of fruits, that perhaps they would take heed. But when good came to them, they said, 'This is ours by right'; and if an evil befell them, they ascribed it as an omen to Moses and those with him. Indeed, their omen is with God, but most of them do not know. And they said, 'Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not believe you.' So We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, as distinct signs; but they waxed proud, and they were a guilty people." (130–133)

"We afflicted the people of Pharaoh for several years with famine and a shortage of produce, so that perhaps they would come to their senses. But their condition was that when good times came, they would say that they deserved them; and when bad times came, they would hold Moses and his companions responsible as an ill omen. Hear this: their omen is with God, but most of them did not know. And they said to Moses, 'Whatever sign you bring to us to bewitch us, we will not be believers in you.' At last, We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and blood, as separate signs; yet they remained arrogant and continued in rebellion." This is one example of the events to which this verse points.

God afflicted this people with troubles and calamities for the sole reason that they might come to their senses, that they might look within their conscience and reflect upon their situation, so that perhaps, because of these hardships, they would begin to humble themselves before God and make themselves submissive and lowly before Him. They would abandon their pride and arrogance, adopt a serious attitude, and pray sincerely that God remove these difficulties from them, open the doors of His mercy for them. But they did not do what was proper for them. They refused to enter into the refuge of God and continued their obstinacy and rebellion, and even because of these difficulties their thinking did not turn in that direction. Their inner vision did not open, and their hearts did not soften. Satan was following them closely, adorning for them their misguidance and rebellion. "But their hearts became even harder, and Satan assured them that what you are doing is excellent."

A heart that does not turn to God in return for hardships and afflictions has dried up within in the way a stone dries, and there is not even a drop of moisture in it that hardships and afflictions could squeeze. This heart has died, and whatever pressure is applied to it, it will not feel anything. All the material for accepting truth has left this heart. It has fully died, so no matter how many pinches are given to make it feel, there will be no benefit. Yet living hearts awaken as a result of such jolts, and as soon as such afflictions come from God, they accept the truth. They wake up, their windows open, and thus they attain turning to God. They become deserving of that mercy, compassion and generosity which God has made binding upon Himself. For a person who is already dead, these afflictions become a reckoning and a punishment, and they bring him no benefit. On the contrary, all of his excuses are ended and all arguments become useless. He is declared deserving of an evil end and wretchedness. Therefore, God's punishment becomes certain for him.

These earlier nations, whose accounts God reveals to the Messenger of God ﷺ and conveys to us through him, did not take any lesson from these afflictions and hardships. They did not turn to God, nor did they supplicate before Him with open hands. Satan made their turning away and obstinacy appear attractive to them, and they were not ready to abandon it. God gives respite to such nations, leaves them free, and they transgress all limits.

"So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair. So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." (44–45)

"Then, when they forgot the admonition that had been given to them, We opened for them the doors of every kind of prosperity, until, when they exulted in what had been bestowed upon them, We suddenly seized them, and at once they were in despair. Thus the root of the people who did wrong was cut off, and praise belongs to God, the Lord of the worlds."

Prosperity is also in fact a trial, just as affliction and hardship are trials, but prosperity is more severe than poverty and misfortune. God tests human beings with prosperity just as He tests them with adversity. When a believer is struck by adversity and falls into trial, he endures patiently; and when prosperity comes to a believer, he gives thanks to God, so he is well in every condition. A hadith reports: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all his conditions are good, and this distinction belongs only to the believer. If prosperity comes to him and he gives thanks, it is good for him; and if he is in hardship and is patient, that too is good for him." (Narrated by Muslim)

As for those nations that denied their messengers, whose stories God has related here, they forgot the guidance that had been given to them. God knew that they were about to be destroyed; so God put some of them into hardships and afflictions, yet they did not come to their senses. And for some of them, God opened the doors of blessings, made everything abundant, and left the field open for them so that they might advance far in rebellion. Here the Qur'anic mode of expression is also very beautiful.

"We opened for them the gates of everything" (6:44): "We opened for them the doors of every kind of prosperity."

This includes every kind of goodness, every kind of necessity, equipment and great abundance of honour and standing. Everything came to them in flood-like plenty, without hindrance or restriction; blessings were made common for them, and they received them easily, cheaply, without any labour or toil. In truth, this is a very impressive scene and a rare example of the artistic mode of expression of the Qur'an. (See my book Al-Tasvir al-Fanni, chapter Tariqat al-Qur'an.)

"Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given" (6:44–45): they were drowned in the abundance of every kind of goodness and equipment, and they became absorbed in ease and luxury. In such circumstances they neither remembered God nor gave thanks to Him; the thought of the true Bestower faded from their hearts, and their hearts were emptied of the fear of God. They became completely enveloped in pursuit of comfort and the pleasures of food and drink, and they handed themselves over completely to these things. Lofty values lost their significance in their lives, and this is the common habit of people immersed in amusement, play and pleasure: from them lofty values disappear. After this, order and good habits disappear from their society, and they become completely ruined morally. Thus these conditions result in their whole life being destroyed, and this destruction then becomes natural. This is exactly the sunnah of God.

"Then We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair. So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off." The word dabir of a people refers to the one who comes last, that is, their last person. When the last person has been cut off, those before him are all the more cut off.

"Those who did wrong" (6:45): here it refers to those who committed shirk, and therefore the Qur'an in most places describes the polytheists as wrongdoers (zalimin) and applies the word zulm to shirk.

(Verse 45) "So the one who committed wrong was cut off, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." This is a comment on how Allah cut off the roots of the polytheists: having given them respite, He seized them suddenly. Is praise due to Allah only for His bounties and favours? Yes, but the purification of the earth from wrongdoers is itself a kind of blessing. Moreover, praise is due to Allah for His mercy, and clearing the earth is among the greatest mercies.

Allah seized the peoples of Nuh (peace be upon him), Hud (peace be upon him), Salih (peace be upon him) and Lut (peace be upon him). He seized Pharaoh, the people of Greece and the people of Rome, and in accordance with the same sunnah He seized other nations too after their rise. First He greatly advanced their civilisation and culture, and then He destroyed and ruined them. These are, in any case, the secrets of Allah's decrees. But the sunnah of Allah is evident in this story of rise and fall, and Allah records it here in this principled manner.

These peoples had their own civilisations, and in their time they enjoyed great ascendancy. They had great abundance and wealth. In some respects they were more prosperous than the developed age of today. They had splendour, pomp, equipment and plenty, and they were under the illusion that they would remain as they were. These nations were also deceiving other nations, which were unaware of the sunnah of Allah regarding prosperity and progress.

These peoples could not understand that the sunnah of Allah operates in this universe. Nor could they understand that they were being given respite, in exact accordance with the policy of that sunnah. Those who were moving in the sky of the sunnah of Allah had their eyes dazzled by the rain of Allah's blessings. Power and strength had produced in them very great confidence, and they had fallen into delusion because of the respite and reprieve granted to these prosperous nations. These people neither worshipped Allah nor had knowledge of Him. They rebelled against the sovereignty of Allah; rather, they claimed the right of sovereignty for themselves, although sovereignty is one of the important attributes of divinity. These people spread corruption on the earth and inflicted oppression on people, because they had claimed sovereignty against Allah. When I was in America, what I saw with my own eyes was an embodiment of this verse.

(Verse 44) "So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of every thing."

The scene depicted in this verse shows that these people had abundance of provision, and from every side there was a flood of facilities without measure rushing towards them. This scene was fully at its height in America.

I saw that this people is extremely proud of that prosperity, and it was clearly fixed in their consciousness that this abundance of facilities was reserved only for white-skinned people. Their conduct towards coloured people is extremely arrogant and savage. Americans regard the people of the whole globe as so worthless that compared with it even the Nazism of the Jews has no worth, although the Jews are very famous for it and national and racial pride is their hallmark. The attitude of white Americans towards coloured Americans is even worse and harsher than that of the Jews. This harshness becomes even greater especially when the coloured people are Muslims.

In America I kept watching all of this and kept expecting that the sunnah of Allah would surely do its work one day. I can see that the sunnah of Allah is moving slowly but surely towards American society.

(Verse 44–45) "Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair. So the root of the people who did wrong was cut off, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."

After the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), Allah showed this mercy to the nations of the world: they would not be transformed, nor would they be uprooted and cast away entirely. But various kinds of Allah's punishments still keep coming, especially upon the nations that have been given prosperity and abundance. Every day various kinds of punishment come upon them, even though the production of the necessities of life among them has exceeded limits and they have been blessed with abundance of provision and facilities.

Psychological torment, spiritual restlessness, sexual licentiousness and moral corruption have destroyed them. In their prosperity, material production and equipment they have no means of contentment, and their whole life is close to being drowned in wretchedness and anguish. (See my book Islam aur Mushkilat-e-Tehzeeb, the chapter Khabt wa Idtirab.) Despite this prosperity, the moral condition of these people is such that great political secrets are sold for a few coins, and the crime of treachery against an entire nation is committed; and what is gained? A few moments of debauchery, sexual pleasure and a few coins. These are signs which point to grave danger for such nations in the near future.

These are the very first signs of the destruction of the Western nations. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke the truth: "When you see that Allah gives someone everything he desires despite his evil conduct, know that he is being given respite." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse: "Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair. So the root of the people who did wrong was cut off, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds." (Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim)

But it is also worth noting that the principle of destroying the people of falsehood, and the sunnah of Allah in His scheme, does not consist only of annihilating the people of falsehood; it also includes the establishment and dominance of the people of truth, and that these people of truth emerge in the form of a community. The fundamental principle is that Allah strikes falsehood through truth and through the people of truth, and smashes the head of falsehood. Falsehood is annihilated. Therefore the people of truth should not sit back in slackness, and should not sit with hands folded merely waiting for the sunnah of Allah, because the sunnah of Allah too is brought into effect through Islamic struggle. If the people of truth sit down inactive, they will cease to be the people of truth, and they will no longer be capable of achieving dominance or smashing the head of falsehood, especially if they sit down idle and inactive. Truth emerges in the form of a community which is striving for the position of Allah's sovereignty on earth, and defends itself against those who have established their own sovereignty against Allah, whereas the sovereignty of Allah is one of the distinctive attributes of divinity. This is the real and fundamental truth.

(Verse 46) "And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted."

Now the context brings the polytheists face to face with the punishment of Allah, and this proposed form of punishment relates to their own selves and their faculties. It concerns their power of sight, power of hearing and power of perception. The suggestion is: if Allah takes away these faculties, who is there who could restore them to you? There is no one. Having reflected, they too become certain that there would be no one who could give them back hearing, sight and perception if Allah were to take these faculties away.

This is a depiction of a scene in which, by their own beliefs, they find no way to escape this proposed punishment of Allah. Incidentally, it also makes clear that those others whom they associate with Allah as partners are themselves utterly powerless. In this scene, however, it is shown that the very suggestion of this proposed punishment has shaken these people deeply, because Allah, the Creator of human nature (fitrah), knows well that within this nature lies a genuine capacity to perceive the truth, and that human nature is not far from truth. Human nature recognises, with insight and clarity, that only Allah can do this, and no one else. He can take away the hearing, the sight and the understanding faculties, and He can restore them, and no other can do this.

Through this scene, which makes the heart tremble and the limbs quake, and after presenting the doctrine of shirk and the wretched condition of Allah's associates, the context now expresses wonder at the fact that those before whom these scenes and these arguments are placed still incline towards the sick camel and walk crookedly even on the straight path.

﴿Behold how We vary the Signs, yet they turn away.﴾ (6:46) This wonder is being expressed at their turning aside from the path of truth. The meaning of "yasdifun" (6:46) is well known among the Arabs. The act of "sadf" is attributed to a sick camel, and because of this a kind of brutish and repugnant image is given of these people, which is a subtle form of humiliation for them.

Before the effects of this anticipated, hypothetical scene had even faded, another anticipated scene is now presented before them. They themselves also believe that bringing this proposed scene into reality is no difficult task for Allah. In this scene they are shown that if the punishment of Allah comes suddenly, then consider: who will be caught in its grip other than the wrongdoers? It is the polytheists who will be destroyed first. A glimpse is shown that when the punishment comes suddenly, the wrongdoers and the polytheists are annihilated, whether this punishment comes suddenly or comes openly after an announcement.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 47:

(Verse) No. 47.

Allah's punishment certainly seizes the wrongdoers in every case. It comes suddenly, while they are heedless and have no expectation of it, and sometimes it comes openly, and they are fully prepared for it. Nevertheless, destruction befalls the wrongdoing peoples. (It should be remembered that, according to the Qur'an's usage, "the wrongdoers" (al-zalimun) refers to the polytheists (mushrikin).) When this punishment comes, whether suddenly or openly, they can offer no defence against it, because they are so weak before the punishment of Allah that they cannot resist it. Nor can the partners they have made stop this punishment, because those whom they make partners with Allah are themselves weak servants of Allah.

This is a probable situation which the Qur'an presents before them in such an effective manner that they may be frightened by it, take precautions for their own protection, and refrain from providing the causes for such a situation to occur. Allah presented this probable situation before these people because He knew that taqwa (God-consciousness) exists within human nature itself, and that the mere imagination of such a situation makes a person tremble.

Now, when this wave reaches the shore, and scenes that follow one another can be shown within it, and effective guidance has been given, and the impressions of that guidance penetrate to the depths of the hearts of listeners and viewers, then the duties of prophethood of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and of the other messengers are defined. This definition is made because the people of the messengers used to demand supernatural miracles from them. It is explained that messengers are only conveyers of the message: they give glad tidings and warn of the evil end. After the discharge of this duty, people are free to choose whatever path they wish. Reward and punishment will then be established on the basis of this free choice.

(آیت) ﴿Verses 48–49﴾

The purpose of the religion of Islam was to bring people to intellectual and rational maturity, and to make them capable of putting to use that great faculty which Allah has given to man alone, and of employing it fully in understanding the truth that lies in the pages of this universe, within the very ways of life, and hidden in the secrets of human creation. The Qur'an was the first to unveil these secrets to humanity and to direct the perceptive power of man towards them.

For this reason, people were lifted out of sensory, extraordinary miracles and brought into the realm of reason. Through sensory miracles, a person is indeed compelled to believe, but the true reality does not come within his understanding; a person's neck bows before an apparent, extraordinary event. In contrast to this, the religion of Islam directed human reason to study the craftsmanship of Allah Most High in this universe and to strive to understand it, because the secrets of this universe are themselves miracles. It is another matter that these miracles keep appearing at all times, and this universe stands upon their occurrence, and its constituent elements consist of these natural variegations. Islam granted man this perceptive power and this faculty through the Book of Allah. In its manner of expression and its style of exposition, this Book is itself a miracle. Its style, its collective structure and its dynamic mode of expression testify to the reality that its composition is unparalleled, and that since the revelation of the Qur'an until today, no equal to it has been produced.

To bring man to the stage of intellectual maturity, a long training and continuous guidance were needed, so that the great revolution desired could be brought about within the perceptive power of man, and humanity could rise to the lofty height of progress, and man himself, with his perceptive power, could comprehend this universe and the continuous journey of existents. But in the light of Qur'anic guidance, remaining within the Qur'anic principles and in the light of the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, man could understand the journey of the universe through positive reality and suddenly, within a short period. This understanding and this comprehension of his are entirely different from the conceptions and perceptions of the philosophies that were prevalent at that time, such as the Greek and Christian theological philosophies, or the purely sensory and material view of the universe that prevailed in that era in the form of Indian, Egyptian, Magian and Buddhist philosophies, and which would also remove people from that limited sphere of colour and scent that was common among the Arabs at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an.

This guidance and training was among the duties of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and as explained within these two verses, the true role of the Messenger ﷺ was this. The further explanation of this you will see in the next wave as well. In summary: the Messenger is a human being, whom Allah sends to the people of the world so that he may give them the good news of a good end and warn them of an evil end; with these matters his duty as Messenger concludes. From then on, the duty of the people begins, namely to accept the call of the Messenger. The acceptance by the people lies within the sphere of Allah's will, and whoever adopts whatever attitude towards this call will receive reward or punishment. Therefore, whoever believes and performs righteous deeds that manifest his faith, his end will be satisfactory, and he will not be overtaken by any fear, nor will he be left in unease. As for those who denied the signs that the Messenger brings, and whose indications are present within the Book of the universe, those people will suffer punishment. This punishment and chastisement will be given to them because of their denial, and its explanation is given as: bima kanu yafsuqun (because they had committed transgression), where fisq is interpreted as kufr (disbelief). In most places in the Qur'an, the word zulm (wrongdoing) is applied to shirk, and the word fisq is applied to kufr.

This is a very clear and straightforward concept, with no complexity in it. It is a clear indication regarding the station of the Messenger and his duties: what is the status and position of the Messenger in the religion, and what are his duties? It is a concept according to which the station of divinity is exclusively for Allah, with all its attributes, and all affairs are made dependent upon the decree and judgments of Allah. Within the sphere of Allah's decree and will, man has also been given the freedom of thought and decision, and for this reason man becomes accountable, and the consequences of reward and punishment are based upon his deeds. Through this clear concept, those intricate conceptions are completely negated which, among some people, have become prevalent as a result of false philosophies concerning the personality and nature of the messengers, or which were prevalent in the age of ignorance, which expected that if the Messenger is true, why does he not bring miracles, and why do people not obey him? Thus Islam brought man into the era of intellectual maturity, and in a very simple manner, without his becoming lost in intricate mental and philosophical conceptions, or wasting his perceptive power in the disputations of theological dialectics, as had happened in the dark ages.

Lesson No. 61: At a Glance

In this wave, the remaining part of the explanation of the reality of prophethood is given. The polytheists of Arabia are being made to understand what the reality of prophethood is and what the nature of the Messenger is, and the need to explain this reality arose because these people demanded from the Messenger ﷺ extraordinary miracles. Their mention has already occurred in the previous wave. Here, their erroneous conceptions regarding prophethood are being further corrected. In particular, it is made clear that Messengers are human beings, and that all Messengers have passed away as human beings, because among the Arabs and the surrounding ignorance there were many misconceptions regarding the reality of prophethood. Because of these conceptions, these people had strayed far from the right path regarding the reality of prophethood, the reality of revelation, the reality of nubuwwah, and the person of the Messengers, and all had entered a world of superstitions and fables and gone astray. They had linked prophethood and messengership with sorcery and witchcraft. They would describe revelation as madness. Their belief was that the Messenger gives news of the unseen; that the Messenger is one from whose hand extraordinary events and miracles proceed, and that he should perform the acts that jinn-controllers and sorcerers do. When the Islamic way of life came, it bombarded false beliefs and shattered falsehood at its root, and returned faith to its simplicity, realism, truth and clarity. Thus a true picture of a prophet came into view, the world found a clear concept of prophethood, and humanity was freed from all superstitions, fables and imaginary mythological conceptions which at that time had completely overshadowed the world. The conceptions prevalent among the polytheists were those which were generally found among the Jews and Christians in their vicinity. Within these two communities too there were many branches and sects, but among all the sects, the distortion of the reality of prophethood was a common feature.

In this wave, after presenting the reality of messengership and the reality of the Messenger ﷺ purged of false imaginations and superstitions, the Islamic way of life is now also presented in a very simple manner. It has been presented in its simple and genuine features, without exaggeration and without embellishment, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the presenter of this way of life, is himself a human being. He does not have the treasures of the world. He does not possess knowledge of the unseen, nor does he claim to be an angel. He only takes guidance from his Lord and is only the source of His command. All his knowledge comes to him from his Lord through revelation. Those who respond to his call are highly honoured in the eyes of people. Therefore, it is also the duty of the Messenger to keep them attached to himself and to welcome them. He should give them the good news that Allah has made it binding upon Himself to treat them with great mercy. Also, it is the duty of the Messenger to warn those in whose hearts the fear of God exists and who believe in accountability in the Hereafter, so that they may reach the lofty station of God-fearing. This alone is the duty of the Messenger of Allah, his office and his responsibility, and the reality of his role is confined within two words: "humanity" and "receiving revelation". Through these two words, the reality of the Messenger is also explained and the limits of his official duties are determined. Along with this correction of thought and the indication of the evil end, the path of the guilty is also defined, and the paths of believers and criminals separate from each other. Truth and falsehood are separated from one another, and all imaginations and superstitions regarding the reality of the Messenger and the station of messengership are refuted. Very clearly and openly, a line is drawn between believers and non-believers.

Along with the explanation of these realities, alongside the station of divinity, the other aspects are also placed before people. The nature of the relationship between the Messenger of God and God is also explained. Likewise, the limits and nature of the Messenger's relationship with his followers and with his opponents are also determined. It is also made clear what the manners of the followers are and what the ways of the misguided are. Those who are guided are people with sight, and those who are misguided are blind. Allah has made mercy binding upon Himself for His believing servants, and if any of them repents, Allah will surely forgive him, even if he has committed sins, provided that he committed them out of ignorance and, after repentance, adopts the path of reform. Furthermore, Allah wishes to make clear the way of the criminals. Therefore, whoever believes should believe with insight, and whoever goes astray should also go astray with insight. Every person, whatever stance he adopts, should adopt it after deliberation, with no basis in misunderstanding or conjecture and estimation.

The acceptance by the people lies within the sphere of Allah's will, and whoever adopts whatever attitude towards this call will receive reward or punishment. Therefore, whoever believes and performs righteous deeds that manifest his faith, his end will be satisfactory, and he will not be overtaken by any fear, nor will he be left in unease. As for those who denied the signs that the Messenger brings, and whose indications are present within the Book of the universe, those people will suffer punishment. This punishment and chastisement will be given to them because of their denial, and its explanation is given as: bima kanu yafsuqun (because they had committed transgression), where fisq is interpreted as kufr (disbelief). In most places in the Qur'an, the word zulm (wrongdoing) is applied to shirk, and the word fisq is applied to kufr.

This is a very clear and straightforward concept, with no complexity in it. It is a clear indication regarding the station of the Messenger and his duties: what is the status and position of the Messenger in the religion, and what are his duties? It is a concept according to which the station of divinity is exclusively for Allah, with all its attributes, and all affairs are made dependent upon the decree and judgments of Allah. Within the sphere of Allah's decree and will, man has also been given the freedom of thought and decision, and for this reason man becomes accountable, and the consequences of reward and punishment are based upon his deeds. Through this clear concept, those intricate conceptions are completely negated which, among some people, have become prevalent as a result of false philosophies concerning the personality and nature of the messengers, or which were prevalent in the age of ignorance, which expected that if the Messenger is true, why does he not bring miracles, and why do people not obey him? Thus Islam brought man into the era of intellectual maturity, and in a very simple manner, without his becoming lost in intricate mental and philosophical conceptions, or wasting his perceptive power in the disputations of theological dialectics, as had happened in the dark ages.

Lesson No. 61: At a Glance

In this wave, the remaining part of the explanation of the reality of prophethood is given.
