The polytheists of Arabia are being made to understand what the reality of prophethood is and what the nature of the Messenger is, and the need to explain this reality arose because these people demanded from the Messenger ﷺ extraordinary miracles. Their mention has already occurred in the previous wave. Here, their erroneous conceptions regarding prophethood are being further corrected. In particular, it is made clear that Messengers are human beings, and that all Messengers have passed away as human beings, because among the Arabs and the surrounding ignorance there were many misconceptions regarding the reality of prophethood. Because of these conceptions, these people had strayed far from the right path regarding the reality of prophethood, the reality of revelation, the reality of nubuwwah, and the person of the Messengers, and all had entered a world of superstitions and fables and gone astray. They had linked prophethood and messengership with sorcery and witchcraft. They would describe revelation as madness. Their belief was that the Messenger gives news of the unseen; that the Messenger is one from whose hand extraordinary events and miracles proceed, and that he should perform the acts that jinn-controllers and sorcerers do. When the Islamic way of life came, it bombarded false beliefs and shattered falsehood at its root, and returned faith to its simplicity, realism, truth and clarity. Thus a true picture of a prophet came into view, the world found a clear concept of prophethood, and humanity was freed from all superstitions, fables and imaginary mythological conceptions which at that time had completely overshadowed the world. The conceptions prevalent among the polytheists were those which were generally found among the Jews and Christians in their vicinity. Within these two communities too there were many branches and sects, but among all the sects, the distortion of the reality of prophethood was a common feature.

In this wave, after presenting the reality of messengership and the reality of the Messenger ﷺ purged of false imaginations and superstitions, the Islamic way of life is now also presented in a very simple manner. It has been presented in its simple and genuine features, without exaggeration and without embellishment, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the presenter of this way of life, is himself a human being. He does not have the treasures of the world. He does not possess knowledge of the unseen, nor does he claim to be an angel. He only takes guidance from his Lord and is only the source of His command. All his knowledge comes to him from his Lord through revelation. Those who respond to his call are highly honoured in the eyes of people. Therefore, it is also the duty of the Messenger to keep them attached to himself and to welcome them. He should give them the good news that Allah has made it binding upon Himself to treat them with great mercy. Also, it is the duty of the Messenger to warn those in whose hearts the fear of God exists and who believe in accountability in the Hereafter, so that they may reach the lofty station of God-fearing. This alone is the duty of the Messenger of Allah, his office and his responsibility, and the reality of his role is confined within two words: "humanity" and "receiving revelation". Through these two words, the reality of the Messenger is also explained and the limits of his official duties are determined. Along with this correction of thought and the indication of the evil end, the path of the guilty is also defined, and the paths of believers and criminals separate from each other. Truth and falsehood are separated from one another, and all imaginations and superstitions regarding the reality of the Messenger and the station of messengership are refuted. Very clearly and openly, a line is drawn between believers and non-believers.

Along with the explanation of these realities, alongside the station of divinity, the other aspects are also placed before people. The nature of the relationship between the Messenger of God and God is also explained. Likewise, the limits and nature of the Messenger's relationship with his followers and with his opponents are also determined. It is also made clear what the manners of the followers are and what the ways of the misguided are. Those who are guided are people with sight, and those who are misguided are blind. Allah has made mercy binding upon Himself for His believing servants, and if any of them repents, Allah will surely forgive him, even if he has committed sins, provided that he committed them out of ignorance and, after repentance, adopts the path of reform. Furthermore, Allah wishes to make clear the way of the criminals. Therefore, whoever believes should believe with insight, and whoever goes astray should also go astray with insight. Every person, whatever stance he adopts, should adopt it after deliberation, with no basis in misunderstanding or conjecture and estimation.

(Verse 50, part 1 of 2)

Among the hostile opponents of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the people of Makkah, there were those who demanded that he present some miracle that defies normal custom, and only then, they said, would they accept his call. But, as has already been stated earlier, the people of Makkah had not the slightest doubt about his truthfulness. This was nothing but pretext-making. At times they specifically mentioned this demand, namely that he should turn the hills of Safa and Marwah into gold. At other times they demanded that these hills be removed from Makkah, and that in their place there be green and fertile land, with crops and fruit growing in it. At other times they demanded that he inform them of certain unseen matters. At other times they demanded that an angel come before them. At other times they demanded that the Qur'an, written in the form of a book, be revealed to him before them, so that they might read it and also see it being revealed. These and other such demands were in fact made by them so that beneath them they could hide their malice and enmity, which was why they would not submit and accept.

These demands arose in their minds because of the notions which the jahiliyyahs spread around the Arabs had wrongly associated with the reality of prophethood and the person of the Messenger. All these superstitious notions had been given a place in the concept of prophethood by the People of the Book, and they had abandoned the guidance which their prophets had brought to the People of the Book.

In the various jahiliyyahs prevalent in the world, many people had presented themselves as prophets, and some simple-minded nations had even accepted them as prophets. Among these were claims of sorcerers, soothsayers, astrologers and those with jinn, who claimed prophethood. All such prophets always claimed to have knowledge of the unseen. Moreover, they told people that souls were under their control, that they had connections with jinn, and that they could change the order of nature through amulets and charms, or that they could accomplish affairs through worship and prayers, or accomplish their aims through other hidden means. All these religions agree on one point: that these people cause their followers to fall into delusion and mislead them from the path of truth. Yes, the forms of this superstition and misguidance may differ.

The prophethood of sorcerers was always connected with evil spirits. These sorcerers established relations with those evil spirits in order to learn unknown matters or to be able to influence events and circumstances. The form of soothsayers' prophethood was that it was connected with certain gods. These gods are not subordinate to the soothsayer, nor are they under his control, but they accept his request and worship, and they resolve the problems that confront the soothsayer, either in sleep or while awake, and they give him guidance through certain signs or dreams. But not all the requests and prayers of the soothsayer are accepted. Both these kinds of prophethood are totally different from the prophethood of ecstasy and frenzy, because both the sorcerer and the soothsayer understand what they seek. They pray deliberately; whatever they do, or whatever resolution they make, they do with thought and consideration. But the prophet of ecstasy is helpless in the hands of his ecstasy. Ambiguous kinds of words come out of his tongue. He does not say these things deliberately. Sometimes he perhaps does not even understand what he is saying. In most nations it happens that alongside the prophet overwhelmed by ecstasy there is an interpreter who claims to understand the speech of this one in ecstasy. In Greek, such a prophet is called "Manti" (Mantis), and his commentator is called "Prophet" (Prophet). The lexical meaning is: "one who speaks on behalf of another as a deputy." The people of Europe adopted this very word in their own language with various meanings of prophethood. Soothsayers and ecstatics never agreed with one another. Yet there is one situation in which the soothsayer and the ecstatic come to agree: that is when the commentator of the ecstatic's speech is a soothsayer, and his duty is to explain the hints and themes of the ecstatic. Often disagreements arise between them and disputes break out between them, because their social responsibilities are different and they have been trained in different circumstances. The ecstatic has a revolutionary temperament and is not bound by customs and social conventions, whereas the soothsayer is bound by and a guardian of social conventions, because very often this soothsayership is inherited by him; his forefathers too were soothsayers. Soothsayership operates in a society influenced by a temple or shrine far and near in a region, whereas ecstasy is not bound by any society or custom, because the one in ecstasy is sometimes cut off from the whole world, and his present condition cuts him off from the society around him."

"Among the tribes of the Children of Israel there was a great abundance of prophets, and in the long history of the Children of Israel their example is like the present-day circles of dhikr or the ways of the Sufis, because in some periods their number ran into hundreds, and they introduced among their followers the same methods of discipline and training that continue today among the Sufis, such as acquiring ecstasy through physical austerity, or acquiring ecstasy through instruments of listening and merriment."

(From "Haqa'iq al-Islam wa Aba'til a'da'ihi" by Ustad Aqqad, p. 226)

It should be remembered that we have cited from the book of beliefs only the wrong notions. However, we do not agree with the methodology they have adopted: their evolutionary discussion on the concept of God and the concept of prophethood, and their claim that even within the heavenly religions there was evolution, bringing it up to the concept of God and prophethood in Islam. In fact, all the heavenly religions had the same concept of God that Islam has presented. Yes, if the communities of the earlier prophets strayed and entered into jahiliyyah, the responsibility for this does not rest with the religions, because in later periods the communities distorted the correct teachings of the prophets and subjected the correct Islamic concept to their own jahili notions. The Qur'an confirms what we say. The scholars of the West who discuss religions, especially from the evolutionary standpoint, these are merely hypotheses and doubts. (Sayyid Qutb)

"In the First Book of Samuel it is written that:

"Saul sent messengers to seize David... So they saw the company of prophets prophesying, and Saul standing as their leader. Then the Spirit of God came upon Saul's messengers, and they too prophesied. Then he sent others, and they prophesied... So he stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel, and lay naked all that day and all that night."

Likewise, in the Book of Samuel it is also stated: "You will meet a company of prophets coming down from the high place, with harp, tambourine, flute and lyre before them, and they will be prophesying. Then the Spirit of the LORD will come upon them and they will prophesy with them, and will be turned into another man."

From the preceding account it is proved that prophecy was an art, connected with the transcendent. Sons learned it from their forefathers, as is stated in the Second Book of Kings: "When the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, 'Behold, the place where we dwell before you is too small for us. Now let us go to the Jordan.'"

There are some places where their services were assigned to the army, as in the First Book of Chronicles: "David and the commanders of the armies set apart for the service some of the sons of Asaph and others who were called prophets, with lyres, harps and cymbals." This was the condition of the ancient jahiliyyahs, and among them are also included those jahiliyyahs which became prevalent among the communities that believed in heavenly messages, because of intellectual deviation, and because of that deviation wrong ideas about the reality of prophethood and the nature of the prophet found their way among them. Because of these wrong ideas, ordinary people expected every claimant to prophethood to produce the events they desired. At times they expected him to give them news of the unseen; at other times they demanded that he change the natural laws of the universe through sorcery and soothsaying. It was this very concept that led the polytheists to make such demands on the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. And to correct these wrong ideas, the Qur'an repeatedly clarified the reality of prophethood and the nature of the Messenger; one of these clarifications is:

"Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me. Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal? Will you not then reflect?" (6:50)

"O Prophet, say to them: I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah, nor do I have knowledge of the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me. Then ask them: Can the blind and the one who sees be equal? Do you not reflect?"

The Messenger ﷺ is commanded by his Lord to present himself only as a human being, and not to attach to himself the superstitions and mythical stories of jahiliyyah which the people of jahiliyyah had introduced into prophethood and the person of the prophet. Moreover, the Messenger ﷺ is to present to them the Islamic way of life without any concealment, one in which there is no excess and no pretension. This is simply a belief which the Messenger has brought, and only the person whom Allah guides can benefit from it; the Messenger himself cannot guide anyone. The guide is Allah alone.

According to this way of life, the reality of the Messenger is only that he follows the revelation that comes from Allah. Allah teaches him things which he did not previously know. The Messenger does not become the master of Allah's treasures so that he may open their doors to those who are his followers. Nor do the keys of the unseen come to him so that he may tell his followers the events to come. Nor is he an angel, so that angels come to him and remain with him.

He is a human being and a messenger. This is the Islamic way of life: pure, clean, perfectly clear and plain.

This belief is the voice of human nature. It is the fundamental element of life and a lamp for the path to Allah and the Hereafter. It needs no adornment other than its own original form. If someone desires only this belief, then he is deserving of it, and this belief will be the highest value for him. If someone adopts this belief as a worldly commodity, he will not grasp its reality, nor will he understand its worth, and therefore this belief will give him nothing. Such a person will remain in need.

For these reasons, the Messenger ﷺ is commanded to present it in a manner free of contrivance and artificiality, because it needs no embellishment, so that it may be known that those who come under the shelter of this belief do not come for any worldly purpose or wealth, do not come for any status or grandeur, and seek no virtue other than piety. They come only to obtain Allah's guidance, which is Allah's great bounty and the greatest wealth. Consider again:

"Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me."

And let them know that by entering divine guidance they truly come within the realm of light and insight, and come out of ignorance and darkness.

"Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal? Will you not then reflect?" (6:50)

An important question is whether merely following revelation is guidance and insight, and whether the one who is deprived of revelation is considered blind. This verse has resolved this question in very plain words. The question is: what is the role of human reason in matters of guidance and misguidance?

The Islamic system of life has given a very clear and plain answer to this question. Reason, which Allah Himself has given to man, is in itself part of the religion of Allah. It has the capacity to receive divine revelation and to understand its meanings. It is both its duty and its sphere of authority to embrace the light of guidance and to bind itself to the firm code in which there is no flaw or error from any side.

But if human reason frees itself from the code of divine revelation, it always falls prey to error and deviation. Its study becomes faulty, its estimations become very wrong, and all its plans remain ineffective.

Human reason falls into this error because, due to its stationary nature, while it can perceive the parts of this universe, it is not possible for it to study the universe as a single whole or in its totality. Owing to individual and partial perception, reason repeatedly experiments: one incident occurs after another, one picture is formed and another is distorted. But it is not possible for reason, a weak creature, to view the entire universe as a totality and, as a result of a comprehensive study, pass judgments, or on the basis of that complete perception, to formulate a system that possesses complete comprehensiveness and balance. This is why, when reason makes decisions freed from Divine guidance and revelation, it must repeatedly conduct experiments and repeatedly change its rulings. It must repeatedly change the system and take a step that produces an opposite reaction. Sometimes reason inclines extremely to the left and goes far away, and sometimes it inclines to the right and goes very far. Thus it keeps destroying that most beloved creation of God, man, and reduces the honourable human structure to ruin and devastation. If reason, while remaining within its own sphere of work, had become obedient to revelation, the whole of humanity would have been saved from this destruction. We would have chosen the material field for experiments and customs, and in the field of industry and technology we would have left reason to work, because this is the field in which reason can work consistently. If any of its experiments turned out wrong there, humanity might suffer material loss, but it would not be afflicted with human and spiritual loss.

But what are the reasons that man is afflicted by these difficulties because of reason? Apart from the natural structure of his reason, there are some other reasons as well. Within him there are certain natural inclinations, desires and emotions. And these natural impulses, desires and emotions of man also need a code of conduct, so that he may keep the course of life going within those limits, advance, perform his natural duties, and not go beyond the protected bounds of natural law, which would cause his whole life to fall into ruin and destruction. Who will undertake this codification? Is it possible for human reason alone, which itself works under the influence of emotions, inclinations and bodily desires whose range is very vast, to do so? Therefore, codification from some other source is necessary. After this codification, that source can also be its guardian, and human reason will always be able to turn to it. In every command of human life, and in the codification of every experience, the direction will be towards that source and origin, and the qibla of man's motion and struggle will remain correct.

Those who regard human reason as decisive and real like Divine revelation, and argue that just as revelation comes from God, so human reason is also a gift of God, and God alone has given man reason, therefore it is not possible at all that there be any contradiction between Divine revelation and human reason, are those who give reason the status that human philosophers have given it. Allah the Exalted has said no such thing about human reason.

Those who say that the human intellect alone, if that person is very great, makes one independent of revelation from Allah, speak in a matter in which Allah has not said such a thing. Allah has made revelation and messengership a proof against people. He did not make the system of accountability depend merely on human reason. He has not only made man responsible for seeking the path of guidance and attaining knowledge of the Creator by the strength of his natural faculties alone. Allah knows very well that it is difficult for reason alone to reach the goal, and that one cannot rely on nature alone, because deviation is possible in nature when revelation does not guide it, since revelation is the trustworthy guide and the leader endowed with insight. (See the commentary of Fi Zilal al-Quran, Part Six, verse ... )

Those who believe that reason makes man independent of religion, or that science, which is the product of reason, makes man independent of the need for guidance from Allah, speak in a manner that is neither true nor corresponds to reality. This is because the practical situation shows that those whose lives are built upon a philosophical conception or upon scientific theories are living a most painful life, and in it man suffers the severest calamities, even though their lives may be showered with conveniences from every side, their production and income may be very great, and their means of living and causes of luxury and pleasure may be in excess. (See the chapter "Khabt aur Idtirab" in the book Islam aur Mushkilat-e-Tehzeeb.) On the contrary, the view that worldly life is based merely on ignorance and chance is likewise of no worth. Those who interpret this universe in the way that it came into existence on its own are self-interested and selfish people. Islam is a system of life in which reason is given such guarantees that, by them, man is purified of the weaknesses found in his own structure, and also saved from those weaknesses in which he is afflicted because of personal desires and inclinations. After this, Islam lays down principles and rules for reason, by which it works safely in the fields of science, experiment, and knowledge and recognition. As a result of these principles, the activities of reason also expand greatly in practical life. All these matters are settled in accordance with the Islamic Shariah, and in practical life there is no restriction upon reason, so that it does not fall into wrong paths and deviate from the straight path.

When reason receives the guidance of Divine revelation, it becomes endowed with sight. If it goes on freed from the guidance of Divine revelation, it becomes blind. Here, the mention that the Prophet takes guidance only from revelation, and then the statement that the blind and the sighted are not alike, and the questioning manner of saying this, and then the emphasis on reflection ("Do you not then reflect?"), is meaningful.

(Verse) "Inni attabi'u illa ma yuha ilayya. Qul hal yastawil a'ma wal-basir? Afala tatafakkarun" (50)
"I follow only what is revealed to me. Say: Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not then reflect?"

The mention of such indications here, one after another, and this style, is the particular style of expression of the Holy Qur'an. In Islam, reflection is desired, and the Qur'an emphasizes it again and again, but Islamic reflection has been regulated within the principles of revelation. Revelation functions for reason as sight. If there is no revelation, reason, weak and stumbling, also becomes blind, and thus it wanders about in darkness, stumbling without proof, without guidance, and without any luminous Book.

Now the question is: if reason is regulated within a code, does its sphere become restricted? No, revelation grants it a wide arena for its movement. The whole universe also falls within the field of activity of reason, and beyond that the unseen world too comes within its intellectual arena, while the field of the unseen is far wider than the world of witnessing. The depth of the human soul, human life and the events of life are all subjects of human reflection.

The fact is that Divine revelation at no turn becomes an obstacle in the path of human reason. If it does become an obstacle somewhere, it is at the point when reason adopts misguidance, thinks by a wrong method, and runs after desires and aims. Otherwise, Divine revelation directs reason to exercise itself and determines the field for its activities, because reason is that great power which Allah Himself has bestowed upon man. But this power has been given to man so that through it he may safeguard divine guidance and the divine system, not so that through it he may become misguided and rebellious by engaging in destructive corruption.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-An'am (6), verses 51–54.

(Verse) Nos. 51 to 54.

It is a sign of the superiority and dignity of the Islamic worldview that it gives no weight to the passing pomp of this world. It keeps lofty values in view and does not heed the petty concerns of worldly life.

Allah the Exalted commanded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to present this call in a pure and clean manner, without any artifice, in its true form, and not to entice people with any worldly aim in return for this call. It was also commanded that he should keep in view only those people who do not wish to derive any worldly benefit from this call, and who do not seek any gain from it himself. And he should gather around himself those who accept this call and are sincere: those who turn to Allah with heart and soul, and who work solely for the pleasure of Allah. He was commanded not to give any weight in the system of the Islamic call to the customs and traditions of the Jahili society or to its Jahili values, and not to attach importance to any of the worldly considerations and markers.

(Verse) "And warn by it those who fear that they will be gathered before their Lord, having besides Him no protector and no intercessor, that they may become righteous."

That is, the Islamic call should be presented first to those who believe that one day they will have to appear before Allah. There, their condition will be that no protector will be there who can help them, and no intercessor who can rescue them. This is because on the Day of Resurrection, no one can intercede with Allah without His permission. And even if someone is given permission to intercede, he will not intercede on behalf of these people before Allah, because those who are placed in the position of intercession will themselves have a keen sense of fear on that day, since on that day there will be no protector or intercessor except Allah. Such God-reaching and God-fearing people are expected to be more (in this regard): they will feel more fear, be more obedient, and benefit more from the guidance of Allah than other people. From such people one can expect more that in this worldly life they will avoid those matters for which they would be subjected to the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. Therefore, warning is a statement that is clear and has great effect. Thus, through warning, those matters will become clear to them which they already fear; therefore, through the explanation of these matters and the warning, they will become even more God-conscious, will fear transgressing the limits set by Allah, and will not fall into the things from which they have been forbidden. But this will happen only after the forbidden matters have been explained to them.

(Verse) "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face."

Do not drive away from yourself those who have dedicated themselves purely to Allah. Such people worship Allah and call upon Him morning and evening, and they do this solely for the pleasure of Allah. This is a station of sincerity and love, and an atmosphere of courtesy and reverence. These are the people who remember Allah with utmost humility and reverence and are engaged in worship. The attainment of Allah's pleasure occurs only when a person turns to his Lord with the utmost sincerity, loves Allah completely, and stands in the court of Allah with the utmost courtesy and humility. These are the people for whom the term "Rabbani" is used, that is, those who are for Allah and in Allah.

The question is: why was this command given to the Messenger (ﷺ)? What is the real matter? The event was that some of the notables of Arabia did not accept the Islamic call because the poor and weak people gathered around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). For example, Suhayb, Bilal, Ammar, Khabbab, Salman, and Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with them all), and others, and these people wore garments from which a bad smell came, because owing to their poverty they could not wash them often. The social status of these people was such that they were not considered fit to sit in the gatherings of the great men of Quraysh. For these reasons, the leaders of Quraysh demanded of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he remove these people from his gathering. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused this. Upon this, they demanded that he set up a separate gathering for them, and a gathering for people of standing in which none of these poor people would be present. They made this demand because in the gatherings of the Jahiliyyah, the notables of Quraysh had these distinctions by which they imposed their awe upon the common people. Regarding this second proposal, the Messenger (ﷺ) began to consider it, merely in the hope that through this the Islamic call might enter their hearts. Upon this, the command was revealed.

(Verse) "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face."

Imam Muslim narrates from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: We were six people sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The polytheists made a request of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Just remove these people from your presence, so that they do not become bold and nurture resolve against us." He says, I was one of those six; Ibn Mas'ud was there, a man from Hudhayl was there, Bilal was there, and two other persons whose names I do not remember. The words of Quraysh had an effect on the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as Allah willed. He began to consider their request. Upon this, this verse was revealed.

(Verse) "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face."

These great ones (kubara') used to say a great deal about these poor people. Meanwhile, the Messenger (ﷺ) showed them immense favour, and they had a special place in his gathering. The great ones would accuse them, speak ill of them, and criticize their poverty and weakness. The presence of these people in the gathering of the Messenger (ﷺ) was unbearable to them, and for this reason these great ones hated Islam and were unwilling to accept it. Then Allah the Exalted issued a decisive command on this matter. Their proposal was fundamentally rejected and declared null and void.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 52:

(Verse) "Mā min ḥisābika ʿalayhim min shay'in fa-taṭrudahum fa-takūna minaz-zālimīn" (52)

"The reckoning of them is not upon you in any respect, nor is your reckoning upon them in any respect; so if you were to drive them away, you would be among the wrongdoers."

They will bear their own burden and give their own account, and you will bear your burden and give your account. As for their being poor, this is what Allah has written for their destiny; you have no part in it. Likewise, O Messenger, you will not be asked about their wealth or poverty, nor about yours. In the matter of faith and disbelief, wealth and poverty carry no weight. If you were to give a place in your gathering to someone, or to drive away someone, you would be among the wrongdoers, and it is not possible that a Messenger should become one of the wrongdoers.

Those who were rich in heart but poor in pocket remained permanent members of the Messenger's gathering. Those who were weak in worldly terms but strong in faith and conviction remained in the station that their faith had fixed for them. They became deserving of that station because they called upon Allah alone and sought only the good pleasure of Allah. Thus Islamic values took on the form of traditions in the manner that Allah, the Exalted, desired.

The people of pride and arrogance turned away from the Islamic movement. Their impression was: how is it possible that such people among us should become the possessors of Allah's grace and bounty? "These wretched fellows! If there were any good in the movement established by Muhammad, and in the message that he has brought, these people would not be ahead of us in accepting it. Allah would have guided us to it before them." It does not appear to be a reasonable thing that Allah should choose these weak and destitute ones from among the Arabs for His grace and bounty, while we are men of standing and rank.

Those who were proud of lineage and wealth, Allah had in truth put them into a trial. The fact is that these people had not understood the religion of Islam, and furthermore they could not comprehend the new world into which this religion wished to lead humanity, whose horizons were extremely vast. This religion wished to take humanity to extraordinary heights in that new world. Neither the Arabs nor other peoples at that time had knowledge of this new Islamic world. Today, those who are running after a mirage under the names of democracy and other labels are also unaware of the world of the Islamic system.

(Verse) "Wa-kadhālika fatannā baʿḍahum bi-baʿḍin liyaqūlū a-hāʾulāʾi manna Allāhu ʿalayhim min bayninā" (6:53)

"Indeed, in this way We have tried some of them through others, so that they might say, 'Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?'"

The Qur'an answers this question thus, rejecting in this way the rhetorical denial of the elite class.

(Verse 53) ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

"Yes! Does Allah not know better than they do those of His servants who are grateful?"

This dialogue contains many directives and indications. The first guidance given is that Allah bestows His grace and favour upon those whom He knows, in His knowledge, will render due thanks for His blessings. Although no servant can fully discharge the right of Allah's bounties, whatever small effort a servant makes in the field of giving thanks for blessings, Allah accepts it, and in return for that modest thanks He grants a reward for which there is no equivalent.

In this verse it is shown that the blessing of faith is not connected with those petty values that hold sway in this world under the rule of the jahili oppressors. Allah bestows the wealth of faith upon those whom He knows will be grateful, even if they are slaves, weak and destitute, because in Allah's scales worldly wealth and property carry no weight. Only jahiliyyah attaches importance to them, although in the sight of Allah they have no weight at all.

This reply also settles the matter that those who raise such objections are in truth people who are unacquainted with the reality of things. When Allah distributes the wealth of faith, He knows full well who deserves it. Whoever raises an objection in this regard would, firstly, be ignorant and, in addition, would be extremely insolent.

Accordingly, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is instructed to begin his call with those upon whom Allah has bestowed His favour: first of all, He blessed them with the blessing of faith; they were given the excellence of the foremost (al-sabiqun al-awwalun), and those whom these chiefs and nobles despise. He is commanded to greet them first, and thereafter to give them the glad tidings that Allah has made mercy incumbent upon Himself for them, and that if any of them committed some fault in the days of jahiliyyah, it is forgiven, provided he repents and makes amends.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 54 (part 1 of 2):

﴿When those who believe in Our verses come to you, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has made mercy incumbent upon Himself, so that whoever among you does evil in ignorance and then repents and makes amends, then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful."﴾ (6:54)

After the blessing of faith, this is a great honour for them. It will bring great ease in the reckoning and abundant, generous reward. Such a great mercy, and a certain mercy, that Allah has made this act obligatory upon Himself. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is commanded to give these believers, after greeting them, the good news of Allah's verses: that they will be treated with pardon and forbearance, provided they repent and adopt righteous conduct.

For this reason, some commentators have defined ignorance (jahl) as persisting in the commission of sins. Otherwise, everyone who commits a crime does so out of ignorance. According to this interpretation, this text includes every sin that a person commits; when he repents and becomes righteous, the sin is forgiven. This view is also supported by those verses and texts which state explicitly that through repentance and subsequent amendment of conduct all sins are forgiven, because this is the mercy of Allah that He has made obligatory upon Himself.

Before concluding this discussion, it is appropriate to mention some important ahadith concerning the circumstances in which these verses were revealed. If these narrations and this verse are read together, it will be clear how great a revolution the religion of Islam was bringing about in humanity at that time. The social elevation to which Islam had raised humanity at that time, humanity has not been able to reach even in this advanced age.

Tabari has narrated, on the authority of Sinad, Abu Zayd, Ash'ath Kirdus and Ibn Mas'ud, that some of the chiefs (kubara') of Quraysh passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, Khabbab and people like them were sitting with him. Ibn Mas'ud said: We were among the oppressed (zer-dast) of all the Muslims. These chiefs said: "O Muhammad, have you chosen these people from among your people? Has Allah favoured only these people among us? Should we submit to the authority of these people? Drive them away from your presence. If you do so, it is possible that we will become obedient to you." On this occasion, these verses were revealed:

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for any part of their reckoning, nor are they accountable for any part of yours; so if you drive them away, you would be among the wrongdoers.﴾ (6:52) And ﴿Thus We have tested some of them through others, that they may say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ (6:53), up to ...

Tabari has narrated from Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad Anqazi, from his father, from some other people, and from Sudi and Abu Sa'id Azdi. They were reciters of the tribe of Azd. They narrated from Khabbab, concerning the verse:

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for any part of their reckoning, nor are they accountable for any part of yours; so if you drive them away, you would be among the wrongdoers.﴾ (6:52)

that Aqra' ibn Habis Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn Fazari came. They saw that the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting in the assembly of Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar, Khabbab and other weak and poor believers. When these people saw these weak ones, they considered them insignificant. These two came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We wish to sit with you in one place, so that we may gain honour among the Arabs, because delegations of the Arabs keep coming to you. But we do not like it that the Arabs should see us sitting with these inferior people. When we come to you, please remove these people from your presence. When we have gone, you are free to sit with them or not." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Agreed." Upon this, these people demanded that he sign a protocol to this effect. The narrator says that the Prophet (ﷺ) asked for paper and called Ali (RA) to write this matter down. The narrator says that we were sitting to one side when Jibril (peace be upon him) came and this verse was revealed:

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening...﴾ (6:52)

"And those who call upon their Lord day and night, seeking His pleasure, do not cast them away from you. You bear no part of their reckoning, and they bear no part of yours. Even so, if you cast them away, you will be counted among the wrongdoers." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited:

﴿Thus We have tested some of them through others, that they may say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ (6:53)

And then he recited:

﴿When those who believe in Our verses come to you, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has made mercy incumbent upon Himself."﴾ (6:54)

Upon this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the paper from his hand, called us, and was reciting this verse: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has made mercy incumbent upon Himself." After this, we would sit with him, and when he wished to leave, he would rise himself and go, and we would remain in our place. After this, the following verse of Surah al-Kahf was revealed:

﴿And restrain yourself to remain with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and do not let your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life.﴾ (18:28)

The narrators say that after this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would remain sitting with us, and when the time came, we would rise ourselves and leave the Prophet (ﷺ) alone so that he could rise and go.

(Ibn Kathir, in his commentary, made this remark on this hadith: "This hadith is gharib (unusual). This verse is Meccan, and Aqra' ibn Habis and Uyayna embraced Islam long after the Hijrah." But there is no justification for this criticism. Their narration relates to an incident before their Islam. They did not say that they had embraced Islam at the time of that incident. Therefore there is no contradiction between their Islam and this narration, because when the Prophet (ﷺ) did not accept their proposal, they then turned away from Islam.) (Sayyid Qutb)

After this, whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw these people, he would take the initiative in greeting them and say: "Praise be to Allah, who has placed among my ummah such people that Allah has commanded me to greet them first."

In Sahih Muslim, there is a narration from A'idh ibn Amr that Abu Sufyan came and Salman, Suhayb, Bilal (may Allah be pleased with them all) and other people were sitting in the assembly. These people said: "By Allah, the swords of Allah have not reached the enemies of Allah as far as they should have." Upon this, Abu Bakr (RA) said: "Are you making such remarks about the sheikh of Quraysh and its chief?" Abu Bakr (RA) came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of this incident. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Have you not angered them? If you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr (RA) immediately came to them and asked: "Brothers, have you not become angry with my words?" They said: "No, brother, may Allah forgive you."

Wait, this is a point for reflection, and pause at it at some length. Reflect on these verses. Rather, it is the right of all humanity that it should stop at this point and reflect for a long time. These verses do not merely mention the empty rights of man and shining principles and values. What is said in these verses is far higher and more important than human rights. Here a great truth is pointed out, which actually exists in people's lives, and this is the great revolution that the Islamic system of life actually brought about in the life of all humanity. Cast a glance at the horizon of humanity: there is a high and fine line which humanity once reached, and it reached it not merely on paper but in practice. Now consider how far that same humanity has fallen from that recorded height, because humanity has been deprived of the leadership of the religion of Islam. However far humanity may fall, the importance of that record remains in its place. The importance of that revolution has not diminished, because at one period of history humanity reached that level. This record was actually established, and humanity once inscribed this line on the horizon of humanity by its deeds. Humanity should strive to reach that lofty height again, because the Islamic revolution has once scaled that peak. It is possible to reach that point again. Look, on the horizon of humanity the footprints of the Muslims are still present. Even now people can reach there. Even now the religion of Islam exists. Only resolve, certainty and confidence are needed.

The importance of these verses is that in them the footprints of humanity's great journey have been permanently imprinted. In these verses that historical process has been recorded, through which Islam raised the Arabs from the depths and filth of jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) to that lofty height, and then placed in their hands the leadership of all humanity. They took hold of all humanity in the corners of the world and raised it up to that recorded line on the horizon of humanity, which no other system has been able to cross.

The abyss of humiliation into which humanity in general, and the Arabs in particular, had fallen is made completely clear in these verses through the words of the chief of Quraysh. They say: "Muhammad, have you chosen only these people from among your people? Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, leaving all of us? And now should we become obedient followers of these people? Our advice is that you drive these people away from your assembly. If you dismiss them from your assembly, we hope that we will obey you." ... The words spoken by Aqra' ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn Fazari also clearly show how far the world had fallen into the abyss of humiliation at that time. These people speak about the foremost companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) in such a contemptuous manner that Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab (may Allah be pleased with them all) are considered people of a lower class. "We wish to meet with you, but we do not like the Arabs to see us sitting in one assembly with such weak people and slaves." Because delegations from the Arab world keep coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at all times, their position was that sitting with such people was a cause of shame for them.

Here the black face of jahiliyyah is unveiled, and its base customs and weak values are revealed openly. The tribalism based on tribe, lineage, wealth and property becomes clear. Some of these poor people were not Arabs at all. Some had no connection with the so-called nobility of the time, and some were not wealthy. These are precisely the values that every jahiliyyah nourishes. Even the modern jahiliyyahs have not risen above this kind of concept of nationalism, concept of race, and class distinctions arising from wealth.

These are the baseness and lowliness of jahiliyyah, and this is the exaltation and loftiness of Islam. In the view of Islam, these national, racial and class slogans have no weight, and these base and superficial concepts have no value. Islam is a system that descended from heaven; it is not a system that grew out of the earth. This is because the earth contains lowliness, and this lowliness is so salty and barren that plants of such ideas cannot grow in it, since the Islamic plant is a most pure tree. The first to obey Islam is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who is the Prophet and Messenger of Allah and upon whom revelation descends from the heavens. He is a member of Banu Hashim, a leading branch of Quraysh. Then Abu Bakr (RA), who is the companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), obeys Islam. These noble people first act upon the Islamic guidance concerning these slaves and the oppressed. These slaves and oppressed are those who have cast off from their necks all servitudes except the servitude to Allah, and have become slaves of Allah alone. This is the reason why the revolutionary guidance mentioned above came concerning them.

Just as the lowliness of jahiliyyah is evident in the words of these chiefs of Quraysh, and these base attitudes are conspicuous in the mentality of Aqra' and Uyayna, so too the loftiness of the word of Allah is manifest in this part of the divine speech. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is given guidance in these words. Consider once more.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 54 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. Nothing of their account is upon you, and nothing of your account is upon them, that you should drive them away and thus be among the wrongdoers. And thus We have tried some of them through others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful? And when those come to you who believe in Our verses, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy, that whoever of you does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and makes amends, indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful."﴾

The loftiness of Islam is manifest in the manner that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) adopted towards those slaves, concerning whom Allah commanded the Prophet to greet them first and, when they were seated in the assembly, to wait until they themselves rose, although Muhammad was the son of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. Beyond that, he was the Messenger of God, the best of creation, and the leader of those through whom humanity and life were honored.

The mentality of these slaves also reflects the loftiness of the Islamic worldview. They are aware of their standing with Allah. They are also aware of the work and duties of those who are the swords walking in the path of Allah, that these are the swords of Allah. Abu Sufyan was the elder and chief of Quraysh, but he remained behind in the Islamic ranks because he believed as a result of the general amnesty after the conquest of Makkah. These slaves went into the front ranks because they answered the call of Islam in a difficult era and were subjected to severe trials. When Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه) rebuked them regarding Abu Sufyan, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) warned him severely and said, "Did you not perhaps anger them? If you have angered them, then you have indeed angered Allah." In today's age, no commentary of ours can reach this point. We can only relate this incident in simple words. Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه) immediately rose and went back to them and asked, "Brothers, have you not become angry?" They replied, "No, brother, may Allah forgive you."

How astonishing is this event that occurred in human history! How great was this revolution that took place in human life, in which values changed, customs changed, people's consciousness changed, and their thoughts changed, and all these transformations occurred in an instant, while nothing changed in the land. People had not changed, the economic system remained as it was, and all conditions of life remained as they were except for beliefs. Only a message came down from the heavens, upon a human being, and this was purely the message of the sovereignty of Allah. Human nature was sunk in layers upon layers of defilement. People were drowning in the depths of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). The bearer of this message called out, and by that call their powers were stirred, and in that stirring they rose from the depths and climbed to the highest peaks. This eminence was granted to them solely through the blessing of Islam.

Then history saw these people falling from those heights into the depths, step by step, until at last they returned to the lowest depths. Today, in the centers of so-called civilization, such as Washington, New York, Chicago and Johannesburg, these filthy prejudices are again at their peak. On the basis of color and race, people have once again set up a bazaar of prejudices. Here there is the fitnah of nationalism, there the propaganda of ethnicity, and there class warfare is raging, and the filth of these jahiliyyat is not a little less foul than the jahiliyyah of the Arabs.

But the Islamic system of life remains exalted even today. The line of its ascent is still recorded on the horizon of humanity. Even today this system is a mercy for humanity and a ray of hope, that perhaps humanity may again, under its leadership, reach that station and emerge from this filthy and foul vapor. May its eyes and gaze be raised upward; may it strive again to reach that recorded line. Perhaps it may again hear that sweet voice, and be stirred by the call of the herald of Islam, and by following the marks of Islam on the path, reach once more that highest target.

Because of the approach we have adopted in this tafsir, we cannot go beyond these brief indications. We cannot pause any longer than the pause we have already taken, so that we may invite all of humanity to reflect upon these verses and see how bright and radiant this event is within the whole of human history. Within it, humanity rose from the lowest depths by following the marks of Islam and attained heights, reaching very far into them. How, under the leadership of today's material and godless civilization, it fell again, and now its condition is that humanity is a body without any spirituality. They are human, but they are deprived of a worldview. Let it also be known how much capacity Islam has to regain its position of leadership, especially at a turning point in history where all experiments, all schools of thought, all patterns of life, all systems of living, all conceptions of life, and all ideas that were man-made and from which guidance had not been taken from the religion of Islam, have failed badly in solving the problems of life. None of these ideas were able to raise human life to that eminence which the Islamic system raised it to. None of these conceptions could give humanity that station of honor and dignity which it attained under the shade of Islam. They could not give people the tranquility that Islam bestowed upon them. Especially the revolution that the Islamic system brought about among the Arabs, without slaughtering millions of people, without subjecting tens of millions to oppression, without keeping people locked in camps without trial, without torture, without unrest, without harassment, without hunger and without poverty, and without those upheavals in whose grip humanity keeps being caught, and in which some people enslave others physically or spiritually. Other than the slavery to Allah, no other slaveries became entrenched.

I think that enough has been said here, and these verses themselves, in the profound effects they leave upon the human soul, do not need any explanation. (For further explanation, see the commentary on Surah Abasa in Part 30.)

(Ayat) "Number 55."
This is the conclusion of that wave. In it, the reality of prophethood and the disposition of the Messenger (ﷺ) are clarified with great excellence, and the Islamic vision of life is also explained without any ambiguity. The values of life for whose dominance Islam came into this world are made clear, and those things which Islam arose to eradicate are also set apart.

(Ayat) "Wa kadhalika nufassilu al-ayat" (6:55): (Thus do We explain Our signs in detail.)

Why? Because "li-tastabina sabilu al-mujrimin" (6:55): (so that the way of the criminals may become fully evident). That is, with this manner, this method and this style of speech, We state Our purpose, with great detail, after which no room for doubt remains in recognising the truth. There remains no vagueness or complexity in the matter, and after such clarity there is no need for a miracle to accept the truth. The truth becomes manifest, the matter becomes open, and in accordance with the Qur'anic style of speech, these matters, in accordance with the proofs and evidences set out throughout this entire surah and in the light of facts and events, fall within the meaning of the detailed verses.

The purpose is to separate the paths of the criminals. It is being shown what the method of the Qur'an is for establishing the Islamic vision of life and a movement upon its foundation. (Li-tastabina) The method and manner of the Qur'an is not merely to point out the paths of believers and the righteous; rather, the Qur'anic method of movement is that the Qur'an also explains the ways and practices of the misguided and the criminals. Clarifying the paths of the criminals through criticism of falsehood is extremely necessary, and it is necessary so that the path of the people of truth may be clarified. These are the clear lines of Islamic call along which we must walk. Here the methods of truth and falsehood become distinct.

The method of action of Islam has been determined by Allah, and it has been determined so that human souls may be treated in accordance with it. Allah knew well that firm conviction in truth and goodness is attained when, alongside goodness, evil is also kept in view, and against truth, falsehood is also kept in view, and it is known that this falsehood is pure lie and absolute evil, against which the truth is pure truth and absolute good. Furthermore, a person becomes ready to support truth and justice when he is convinced that the force opposing this truth is falsehood. Then it is also a reality that the force of falsehood is a traveller on the paths of the criminals, and the criminals are those forces about which the Qur'an explicitly states elsewhere that every prophet has an enemy. (Ayat) "Wa kadhalika ja'alna li-kulli nabiyyin 'aduwwan min al-mujrimin" (6:112): (Thus We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals.) This is so that it may firmly settle in the hearts of the Prophet and the believers that their enemy is a criminal, and that their belief is based on firm conviction, confidence and certainty of heart.

The clarification of disbelief, evil and criminal conduct is extremely necessary for faith, goodness and reform. This is because clarifying the paths of the criminals is one of the important purposes of the divine signs. Concerning the position and conduct of the criminals, any confusion or slight ambiguity itself creates doubts regarding the position, conduct and path of the believers, because both are two sides of one picture, two facing pages of one book, and two separate roads. Both have distinct colours between which distinction is necessary.

This is why, for an Islamic movement, it is first necessary that the way of believers and criminals be distinguished in the minds and vision of its workers. Every movement should first introduce its own path, and by criticising the paths of the criminals opposed to it, expose their weaknesses and clearly state the difference and distinction between the two. This distinction should be real in actual fact, genuine and not merely theoretical, because the callers and their workers must know who the believers and who the criminals are in the environment in which they are working. Furthermore, they must know what the method of these criminals is, what their methodology is and what their signs are, so that there is no doubt or confusion in their minds regarding the two paths and methodologies. Neither the title should be the same, nor the attributes and features. Believers and criminals should be clearly distinguished from each other in their conception.

At the time when Islam and polytheism first confronted each other in the Arabian Peninsula, this distinction between the believers and the criminals was completely clear. The two paths were well distinguished and separate. The path of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the path of the believers, and this was the path of his companions, and the path of the criminals was the path of those who had not joined him in the Islamic movement and had not believed. With this demarcation and this clarity the Qur'an was being revealed, and the divine signs were giving details, of which you saw examples in this surah. This last example clearly indicates the way of the criminals.

When Islam confronted polytheism, idol worship, atheism and those religions which, in their origin, were heavenly religions but in which later human beings had introduced distortions according to their desires, Islam gave the believers a clear position and a plain, straight path against these religions and ideologies, just as the path of those disbelievers and polytheists was clear and defined, with no doubt or uncertainty within it.

But today, between the movements running in the Islamic world and their opponents, there is no clarity and definition of the path, and this is a very great difficulty. These Islamic movements are operating among people who are Muslims by lineage and in regions which at one time were part of the Abode of Islam. At one time these regions were ruled by the religion of Islam and the Shari'ah was their fundamental law. Then these regions and these peoples truly abandoned Islam; they remained Muslims in name only, and they practically and doctrinally abandoned the fundamental elements of Islam, although they remained under the illusion that they had adopted Islam in terms of belief. Whereas the meaning of Islam is that someone bears witness that there is no deity and sovereign except Allah. Within this testimony are included the meanings that Allah is One without partner, that He is the Creator of this universe and its controller. Human beings shall worship Him alone and live their entire lives according to His commands. It is the duty of human beings to take their laws from Allah alone and to submit before the commands of Allah throughout their whole life. Whoever does not affirm the oneness of Allah with this meaning has neither recited the testimony of faith nor entered Islam, whatever his name, his title, his race or his lineage may be. In whatever land the testimony of faith is not proclaimed with this meaning, we cannot call that land the Abode of Islam, nor is that land a land of Islam.

On this earth there are great nations inhabiting it whose names resemble the names of Muslims, and these people are indeed from the lineages of Muslims. The territories of these people were also once the Abode of Islam, but today no nation among them bears witness to La ilaha illa Allah in accordance with this meaning, nor do the people of any country run their system of government in accordance with this meaning.

This is an extremely painful situation, and today the Islamic movements in those lands are confronting it. They have contact with those people mentioned above. The difficulty these movements face is that the meaning of La ilaha illa Allah is not understood among those who are Muslims in name only, nor do people understand the word Islam in its correct sense. These people are neither aware of the meaning of jahiliyyah nor of the reality of shirk.

In addition, Islamic movements also face the difficulty that the correct path is not defined even before righteous Muslims themselves. Their path is not separate from the path of criminals and polytheists. The marks and labels of both are one; the names and attributes of both are alike, and both are lost travellers in a boundless desert.

Islamic movements know this weakness well, but they remain silent about this great shortcoming. This silence is adopted out of mere broad-mindedness, misguidance, hypocrisy and the mixing of truth with falsehood. To the extent that at this point, the person who speaks a true and decisive word becomes himself the criminal in reverse. Seizure and persecution begin against him, and the accusation is levelled at him that this person declares Muslims to be disbelievers (takfir). Thus, in the view of these people, a Muslim is not one who is Muslim according to the sayings of Allah and the sayings of His Messenger, but rather one who is Muslim according to their own terminology and their own customs. This is the great difficulty that stands in the way of Islamic movements. Yet it is necessary for all those who call to Allah to resolve this difficult question and move forward, wherever they are and in whatever age they live.

It is appropriate that the call to Allah begin in such a way that from the very outset the paths of believers and criminals become entirely separate and defined. When the callers begin their work, they should express truth and sincerity in clear words without any compromise (mudahanah). They should speak without fear and without concealment. There should be no complexity in their speech, and they should not fear the reproach of any reproacher. There should be no fear or dread in their hearts. Nor should they allow in their hearts the fear that some opposing voice will rise against them and it will be said, "Look, these people declare Muslims to be disbelievers."

The position of Islam is not what these misguided people have adopted. The path of Islam is clear, just as the path of disbelief is perfectly clear. Islam is to affirm the testimony of faith with the meaning stated above. Whoever does not affirm the testimony of faith with this meaning, and whoever does not establish the testimony of faith within this meaning in his life, then the ruling of Allah and His Messenger concerning him is that he is a wrongdoer, a sinner, a disbeliever and a criminal.

Read once more: (Ayat) "Wa kadhalika nufassilu al-ayat wa li-tastabina sabilu al-mujrimin" (6:55)
"And thus do We explain Our signs in detail, so that the way of the criminals may become fully evident." Remember, for those who undertake the work of calling to Allah, it is necessary that they first scale this steep pass. They must remove this obstacle from their path. They must produce sincerity and devotion to Allah in their convictions, so that they may stand up in the way of Allah with all their strength. No doubt should block their way, no confusion, no compromise, and no misguidance should stand in their path, because their strengths cannot function openly until they are certain that they are true Muslims, and that those who stand blocking their way and blocking them and all other people from the path of Allah are criminals. Let it also remain in the view of those who carry the Islamic movement that as long as the matter of establishing the religion is not regarded as a matter of disbelief and faith, no one will be ready to accept the hardships of this path with steadfastness. Until a Muslim is convinced that his path and the path of his people are entirely separate, that his community and the community of his people are separate, and that their religion and the religion of his people are separate. Read it once more.

(Ayat) "Wa kadhalika nufassilu al-ayat wa li-tastabina sabilu al-mujrimin" (6:55)
"And thus do We explain Our signs in detail, so that the way of the criminals may become fully evident." Sadaqa Allah al-Azim.

Lesson No. 62: A Glance
After the statement of the reality of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the reality of prophethood, the discourse now turns once more to the reality of divinity (uluhiyyah). These realities were discussed in the previous wave. All these waves are deeply interconnected. After the reality of the Messenger and prophethood, it was also made clear that the path of the Messenger is the path of the believers, and against it all paths are the paths of the criminals.

In this wave, the manifestation of divine majesty appears in several colours and in several fields. Their details we shall give in the course of explaining the verses; here, however, we shall make only summary indications toward them.

The lamp of the reality of divinity is lit in the heart of the Messenger. The heart of the Messenger is filled with the pure wine of trust and certainty. Even if the whole world denies this reality, the Messenger remains steadfast, and there is no slip in the foundation of his certainty. Therefore the Messenger of Allah declares that he has become his Lord's, and in this matter he takes a completely separate path from those who waver about it, and this separation is due to the firm conviction and resolve of the Messenger.

(Ayat) "Qul inni nuhitu an a'buda alladhina tad'una min duni Allah..." (6:56-57)
"Say: I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah. Say: I shall not follow your desires; if I did, I would indeed have gone astray and would not be among the guided. Say: I stand upon a clear proof from my Lord, and you have denied it. What you are hastening for is not within my power. Judgment belongs only to Allah; He declares the truth, and He is the best of deciders."

Manifestation of divine majesty is also seen in the forbearance and patience that Allah shows towards these deniers. They demand that a miracle beyond the normal course of things occur for them, yet Allah responds to this demand with the utmost forbearance. This is because, if an extraordinary miracle were to appear and they still denied it, then in accordance with the Divine way (sunnah Ilahiyyah) the punishment would become binding upon them, and sending down any kind of punishment is no difficult matter for Allah. Had the power to send down punishment been placed in the hands of the Prophet ﷺ himself, there was the danger, given the attitude these people had adopted, that the Prophet ﷺ would have sent this punishment down upon them, since by repeatedly rejecting the truth they had distressed his heart, and this situation had gone beyond the limits of his capacity for endurance. Therefore, granting them respite even in such circumstances is clear proof that Allah is most forbearing and wise, and through this there is also a manifestation of divine majesty.

﴿Say: If that which you are hastening for were in my power, the matter would have been decided between me and you long ago. But Allah knows best the wrongdoers.﴾ (6:58)

Manifestation of divine majesty is also seen in the fact that He is the All-Knowing of the unseen (ʿĀlim al-Ghayb), and whatever event occurs in this universe, His knowledge encompasses it, and this knowledge belongs to none other than Allah. This particular form and character of the unseen is exclusive to Allah.

﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows whatever is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but that it is in a clear Record.﴾ (6:59)

It is also manifested in the fact that Allah has complete control over His servants. They are under Allah's control in every state, whether asleep or awake, alive or dead, in this world or in the Hereafter.

﴿And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein so that a specified term may be fulfilled; then to Him is your return. Then He will inform you of what you used to do. And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail. Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, His is the judgement, and He is the swiftest of reckoners.﴾ (6:60–62)

This majesty also appears at the very moment of the natural reaction of these deniers when they are confronted with some danger. At that time they leave aside their other associates and call upon Allah alone, asking Him to avert that danger; yet despite this, they again begin to associate partners with Him, and forget that the God whom they called upon to avert that danger is also able to afflict them with another punishment from which none of them would remain alive.

﴿Say: Who rescues you from the darknesses of land and sea, when you call upon Him humbly and secretly, saying, "If He rescues us from this, we will surely be among the thankful"? Say: Allah rescues you from it and from every distress; yet you still associate others with Him. Say: He is able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you into factions and make you taste the violence of one another. Look how We vary the verses, that perhaps they may understand.﴾ (6:63–65)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 56:

(Verses) No. 56 to 58.

This passage is full of guidance and indications. Through various influences that act upon the human heart, the reality of divinity (haqiqat al-uluhiyyah) is brought before the eyes. Among these impacts and blows, the important and deep influence is the repetition of the word "Qul" (Say): say, say, say. In it, the address is made to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that you should convey every message that comes to you from your Lord. This is the message which no other group possesses; no one else is the bearer of this message. Nor is this message revealed to anyone else.

"Qul inni nuhitu an a'buda alladhina tad'una min dunillah. Qul la attabi'u ahwa'akum qad dalaltu idhan wa ma ana minal-muhtadin." (56)

"O Prophet (ﷺ), say to them: 'I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah.' Say: 'I will not follow your desires; if I did so, I would have gone astray and would not be among those who are rightly guided.'"

The Messenger (ﷺ) is commanded to proclaim that he has been forbidden by God from worshipping and following those whom you polytheists worship and follow. I cannot, in any way, make your deities equal to my Lord. This is because I have been prevented from following the desires of people, and those who worship others besides Allah do so only because of their own base desires; they follow those people and make them equal to Allah. They are not doing this on the basis of any knowledge or proof, nor because they consider it to be the truth. Moreover, if I were to follow these people, I would go astray and would not remain rightly guided, because those upon whom their desires are imposed are necessarily afflicted with misguidance.

Allah the Exalted commands the Prophet (ﷺ) to speak with the polytheists in this manner, to address them in this straightforward way. Earlier in this surah, the Prophet (ﷺ) has already been commanded in this regard:

"A-innakum latashhadna anna ma'allahi alihatan ukhra. Qul la ashhad. Qul innama huwa ilahun wahid wa innani bari'un mimma tushrikun." (19)

"Do you indeed bear witness that there are other gods with Allah? Say: 'I do not bear witness to that.' Say: 'He is only one God, and I am truly free from what you associate with Him.'"

The polytheists of Makkah kept making this offer to the Messenger (ﷺ): that he should accept their religion and they would accept his religion; he should prostrate before their gods, and they would prostrate before his One God. Their thinking was that perhaps such a compromise (musalamat) was possible, and that shirk and tawhid could be combined in one heart. They thought that worship and obedience of other than Allah could be carried on alongside the worship and obedience of Allah, although this combination is not even possible, for why would Allah accept other partners alongside Himself? He demands that His servants worship Him alone. Allah does not accept at all that worship which contains even the slightest trace of shirk, whether it be little or much.

The purpose of the verse is that the Messenger (ﷺ) should address them thus: that he has been forbidden from worshipping those whom they worship, or whom they call deities. But here the expression uses the word "alladhina" for such beings, which deserves reflection, because the word "alladhina" is used for rational beings (dhawul-uqul). If only idols were meant, or other lifeless objects, then the word "ma" would have been used here, not "alladhina." Therefore, here some other creation is meant along with idols and other stones and trees, for which the word "alladhina" has been used. The use of the pronoun "alladhina" for these objects of worship indicates that the objects of worship were rational beings. This interpretation is supported by two things: first, by actual historical facts, and second, by Islamic terminology.

The historical fact is that the polytheists did not merely worship stone idols and trees; along with these, they also worshipped jinn, angels and human beings. They worshipped humans in the sense that they granted humans the right of legislation and of guidance for individuals. These humans made for them customs, laws and regulations according to which their collective affairs were conducted and their disputes were decided, in accordance with the opinions of these humans and the customs of other humans.

Now we come to Islamic terminology. Islam regards this as shirk. The Islamic concept is that to make some human beings rulers in the affairs of human life is like someone taking them as his deity and making them partners and equals of Allah. Islam forbids this act in the same way that it forbids the worship of idols and stones. In Islam's usage, these two acts are equal and of the same degree of evil (munkarat). This is clear shirk and the making of others equal to Allah. Now, the second blow follows immediately upon the first. This second strike is the completion of the first and is connected with it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 57:

(Verse) "Say: 'I am on a clear proof from my Lord, and you have denied it. What you are impatient for is not in my power. Judgement belongs to Allah alone. He declares the truth, and He is the best of judges.'" (6:57)

This is a command from Allah. Allah instructs the Prophet ﷺ to declare plainly, before the disbelievers and those who deny, that he has firm certainty in his message and complete resolve in this matter. In his consciousness there are clear proofs of the truth of this message, and within his being there is a deep intuitive sense that the message he is conveying is the truth. This is a consciousness that is fully present in all the prophets, and all the prophets have expressed this sense, consciousness and intuitive guidance in these very words. Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) said:
