(Verse) "He said: 'O my people, think: if I was upon a clear evidence from my Lord, and He had given me mercy from Himself, but it was hidden from you, shall we compel you to accept it while you are averse to it?'" (11:28)

And Prophet Salih (peace be upon him) said:

(Verse) "He said: 'O my people, consider: if I was upon a clear evidence from my Lord, and He had given me mercy, then who would protect me from Allah if I disobeyed Him? You would only add to my loss.'" (11:63)

And Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said:

(Verse) "And his people argued with him. He said: 'Do you argue with me concerning Allah, when He has already guided me?'" (6:80)

And Prophet Yaqub (peace be upon him) said:

(Verse) "Then when the bearer of good news came, he cast it over his face, and his sight returned. He said: 'Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?'" (12:96)

This is the reality of divinity, which shines like a lamp in the hearts of the people of Allah. Yet this lamp is lit only in the hearts in which Allah wills to light it. Such people find Allah present in their hearts, and this reality settles into the depths of their personality and fills their hearts with certainty. This is the reality about which Allah commands His Prophet to declare it openly before the polytheists. The polytheists in fact want to deny the call to Allah, and they make excuses and demand that you present miracles to make this reality accepted, although this reality already exists like a lamp in the heart of the Messenger.

(Verse) "Say: 'I am on a clear proof from my Lord, and you have denied it.'" (6:57) They would constantly demand either that some miracle beyond the normal course be sent down to them, or that the punishment of Allah be sent down upon them, so that they might accept the matter. Allah commanded that in answer to this demand the Prophet should declare before them the reality of the Messenger and of messengership, and explain the complete difference between the Messenger, messengership, and Allah with His divinity and sovereignty. He should also declare that he has no authority at all over the coming of the punishment or miracle for which they are showing haste; this matter lies solely in the power of Allah. He is not a deity; he is merely a bearer of the message.

(Verse) "What you are impatient for is not in my power. Judgement belongs to Allah alone. He declares the truth, and He is the best of judges." (6:57)

The occurrence of a miracle, and the descent of Allah's punishment upon them if they do not believe after it, is a matter connected with Allah's decree and command, and in this matter the judge and the one who decides is Allah alone. It is Allah who declares the truth and gives the information. It is Allah who holds the authority to decide between a prophet and his community's call. No human being has been given any authority or right of intervention in this matter.

In this way the Messenger ﷺ declares that he has no authority to make such a decision, nor can he interfere in these matters of divine decree and destiny. This belongs specifically to Allah's system of divinity and is among the attributes of divinity, while he himself is a human being. Yes, the distinction is that revelation comes to him. His duty is to convey it to the people and to warn them of the evil end. It is not his position to make decisions and punish people according to them. Just as Allah declares the truth and informs us of it, so also the authority of decision belongs to Allah. This is the manner beyond which there is no other way to distinguish between a human being and the divine Being.

After this, the Prophet is commanded to appeal to their hearts and insight, and to draw their attention to the strong proofs and signs that establish that this message is from Allah and that its decision also depends upon the will of Allah. If the occurrence of miracles and the descent of Allah's punishment were in the power of the Prophet, then by the demands of human nature he would have immediately accepted this challenge and would not have hesitated in the matter, since they were repeatedly and insistently demanding it. But the reality is that this matter was in Allah's control, and Allah is the One who is most forbearing towards His servants. For this reason Allah does not send down miracles that break the normal order, because after them a punishment would come upon them. They were set upon denial, and this is what has happened to nations and communities before them throughout history.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 58:

﴿Say: "If what you are impatient for were within my power, the matter between me and you would have been settled already. But Allah knows best the wrongdoers."﴾

As far as man is concerned, his capacity for patience, forbearance, endurance and granting respite is limited. When one human being rebels against another, a person's endurance comes to an end, because a human being does not tolerate defiance from a subordinate. But Allah is Forbearing (Halim), Patient and Powerful; He is the Supreme.

Reflect upon the word of Allah. Many times a person witnesses certain actions from other people that fill his cup of patience to overflowing, and his endurance gives way. In contrast, observe that people keep disobeying Allah, yet they still live upon Allah's earth. Allah provides them with food and drink, sends rain upon them, and opens the doors of abundance to them from every side. And there is nothing left for one to do but repeat the words of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). Once, they were in the battlefield. The battle was so fierce that a hand could not be seen before a hand, the disbelievers had launched a decisive attack, and there was fighting from every direction. He (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, You are so very Forbearing! O Allah, You are so very Forbearing!" In short, it is the forbearance and patience of Allah that keeps granting respite to the disobedient.

﴿And Allah knows best the wrongdoers.﴾

"And Allah knows best the wrongdoers." He grants them respite with knowledge and wisdom. He gives them rope with wisdom, and He is All-Knowing and also has the power to fulfil their demand and to afflict them with a severe punishment.

The discussion was about how Allah knows the wrongdoers well, and about the reality of divinity and the majesty of His greatness. In this connection, a broader field of His majesty is pointed to here, and that broader field is the unseen world (ʿalam al-ghayb). It is explained that Allah's knowledge encompasses all hidden matters. Here a unique and remarkable picture of the vastness of Allah's knowledge is drawn, and in this field the mind is directed to travel far into the expanses of Allah's knowledge.

(Verse 59)

This is a beautiful picture of Allah's complete and all-encompassing knowledge. His knowledge is so comprehensive that not even an atom of time or space lies outside it. Everything in the heavens and the earth is within His knowledge. All beings in land and sea are within the circle of His knowledge. All particles that exist in the expanses of the atmosphere and in the depths of the earth are also within His circle of knowledge. Every dry and moist thing, every living and dead thing, is within His knowledge.

The style of this verse differs from our present explanation as heaven differs from earth. The Qur'an's style is unique, comprehensive, complete, profound and deep, extremely impactful and meaningful.

Our thoughts gallop behind this brief verse. Our imagination rides its horses through the world of the known and the world of the unknown. When a person reflects on the unseen world and the visible world, his intuition and observation tremble, because in every valley and in every direction he sees new forms of phenomena and manifestations. Humanity's struggle for its unknown search continues at a rapid pace. It wants to tear apart the veils of the unseen and reveal everything. It wants to remove all the veils of past and future. It wants to peer deeply into the horizons and depths of time and space, but wherever it advances, it finds that the keys of the unseen are in the hand of Allah alone. At a certain limit, it finds the doors of knowledge and discovery locked, and the keys to what lies beyond are with Allah. In short, human intuition runs through the dark valleys of the universe and the depths of the seas. All these places are clear from the perspective of Allah's knowledge. Then our consciousness turns to every leaf that falls in autumn anywhere in the world, whose number humanity is unaware of, yet Allah's eye watches each one, how it falls by the command of its Lord. This knowledge extends in this universe to those leaves. The tiny seeds emerging from countless plants that grow in this universe, and every single grain that lies somewhere in the darknesses of the earth, are also within Allah's sight. Every dry and moist thing in this vast and wide universe is in Allah's view, and nothing is outside the knowledge of Allah.

In short, this concept makes the head spin and leaves the intellect stunned. This awareness takes us into the lengthy spans of history and eras. It evokes the vast distances of the horizons of the universe. When a person conceives of the known and observed world, and the unseen and unknown world, he sees only boundlessness in every direction. The horse of imagination tires and collapses, but a few words of the Holy Qur'an encompass those vastnesses and distances within their embrace. This is the miracle of the Qur'an, the miracle of expression and the miracle of thought. From whichever aspect we look at this brief verse, it is miraculous, and this miracle clearly leads us to the question: what is the source and origin of this great speech?

The Qur'an, which is the source and fountainhead of the Islamic worldview, and from which the Islamic mentality arises, explains that this universe has two realms: one is the unseen world (ʿalam al-ghayb), and the other is the observable or witnessed world (ʿalam al-shahadah). Therefore, the realm in which a person lives does not consist entirely of unseen realities, nor is its connection solely with the world of the unknown; rather, there is also the world of witness here.

Within this universe there are certain unchangeable laws and divine patterns (sunan), and Allah the Exalted has given man the capacity to acquire knowledge of the necessary aspects of the sunan of the universe. In accordance with this capacity and need, this ability has been given to him so that he can fulfill the duties associated with the office of khilafah fi al-ardh (vicegerency on earth), and so that he can harmonize his life with the sunan of the universe. Allah has given man as much capacity as he needs to fulfill the requirements of the office of khilafah, so that man can subdue the cosmic forces and cultivate this earth, advance life here, and utilize the treasures which Allah has deposited within this universe for the betterment of human life.

However, alongside these laws of nature, the will of Allah (mashiʾah) also exists as a reality. Although all these laws of nature are the result of divine will, these laws of nature operate in accordance with the decree of Allah (qadar) rather than the divine will itself. All these laws of nature function under the divine dominion. This is not an autonomous machinery or one that is beyond control. The power of Allah and His decree fully encompass these laws. Every movement of this universe is within the sphere of His power. Although apparently this universe moves on in accordance with a uniform order, this order was created by Allah. The system of divine decree (qadar) and destiny (qadaʾ) implements these laws of nature. The system of qadaʾ and qadar is part of the unseen world, and knowledge of it belongs only to Allah. The scientific principles that people have formulated are also speculative and probabilistic, and to this day, the secrets of this universe that humanity has discovered are acknowledged to be so.

Just consider this small human existence. Within it, millions of particles are constantly in motion. All these operations, from the human perspective, are unseen. Although all these movements and influences continuously operate within his own being, the influences working within this great universe are countless and innumerable. Man knows none of them.

The unseen world encompasses the past of man, and it encompasses the past of this universe. The unseen world also encompasses man and the universe spread around him and its present condition. Moreover, the unseen world encompasses their future. All these matters operate in accordance with the divine sunan, of which only an extremely small portion has so far become known to man. Man benefits from them and uses them in an organized and coordinated manner in fulfilling the duty of khilafah.

Man does not come into this universe according to his own desire. Nor does he know that he will now enter this world. When he departs from this world, his desire is not involved in that departure, nor does he know when he is to go. This is the condition of every living creature. No matter how much knowledge man acquires, and no matter how much his understanding and awareness expand, he cannot bring about any change in this state of affairs.

From the perspective of Islamic mentality and Islamic reality, belief in the unseen (ghaybi ʿilmi) has the character of knowledge, because the unseen and the absence of knowledge are, even scientifically, a genuine form of knowledge. Those who deny the unseen are ignorant, although they claim that they know a great deal.

The foundation of Islamic thought is that a Muslim affirms the existence of unseen realities, of which only Allah possesses true knowledge. The keys to this knowledge are in Allah's hand. Furthermore, Islamic thought also holds the conviction that this universe moves in accordance with the divine sunan, and some of these divine sunan are such that knowledge of them is necessary for the duty of khilafah on earth. It is also necessary to harmonize with these principles on firm foundations. Thus, because of the Islamic mentality and Islamic thought, man is neither deprived of knowledge and recognition, nor deprived of comprehending the reality of things. Beyond this world of witness there is a world of the unseen, and knowledge of the world of the unseen belongs only to Allah, and if Allah wills, He grants some measure of knowledge to whomever He wills among His servants.

Belief in the unseen (ʾiman bil-ghayb) is the arduous mountain pass that man must necessarily cross. Until he attains this station, he cannot rise above the animal level and reach the human level. This is because an animal can only perceive matters that fall within the range of its senses. Only the human being can realize the truth that this universe is not limited merely to what enters his senses; it is vast, and even vaster than what is being brought into the sphere of his perception through his instruments and developed senses. This Islamic concept is a far broader concept than the concept of the universe, and indeed it is a far-reaching transformation in human thinking about this universe. It is also a far-reaching transformation in human thinking about human personality. It also involves a revolutionary way of thinking about the forces operating within the human personality. Under this way of thinking, a new awareness arises within a person about this universe and about the forces working behind it. The effects of this concept also fall upon man's practical life on this earth, because the person who merely observes the environment in a limited way through his senses cannot be equal to the person who, through his insight and his convictions, holds a broader view of this universe. This wise person hears the voice of the cosmic nature from the hidden recesses of his personality and receives signals from the depths of his heart. He is aware that the scope of his activity is wider than the constraints of time and space, and that his personality is far vaster than what he thinks it is, or than what he can comprehend within the brief span of his life. He is aware that behind this apparent and hidden universe there is a great reality, and that this reality is greater than the universe and is its Creator. The existence of the entire universe is borrowed from the existence of this great reality. This is the reality of the Divine Being, which eyes cannot perceive and which cannot be encompassed by the human intellect.

Belief in the unseen is the unit at which the paths of man and animal diverge, and man rises above the realm of animality. But, as in every age, the materialists of our own era also want to pull man down from the lofty station of humanity and bring him back to the realm of animality, where only that is regarded as reality which falls within the range of the senses. These materialists call this progressiveness, although in reality it is regression and failure, from which Allah has so far protected the Muslims. Therefore, the distinguishing quality of the believers was declared to be that they are ﴿those who believe in the unseen﴾, and this is a great blessing of Allah, for which we thank Allah. This point is a place of destruction and ruin for those who fall away and turn their backs.

Those who debate by setting the unseen against science make definitive interpretations of historical events. In their view, the future is, as it were, present before them in a certain form, whereas the most recent scientific discoveries show that the future depends merely on probabilities. Man cannot make any conclusive statement about the future.

It was Marx's habit to make definitive decisions about the future in the light of historical causes. But today's human being can see with his own eyes what became of all of Marx's predictions!

Marx concluded that communism would first be implemented in England, because England had reached the peak industrially. There, on one hand, the capitalists were at their zenith, and on the other, the workers had reached their final stage in terms of poverty and hunger. But in later periods we saw that communism succeeded among extremely backward nations, for example in Russia and China, and not a single industrially advanced country experienced a communist revolution.

Lenin and Stalin predicted that a global war would occur at some time between the socialist world and the capitalist world, but their successor Khrushchev is holding aloft the banners of peaceful coexistence and honesty... I think we should not waste our time by further discussing the predictions of these people, because their definitive predictions are not worthy of serious discussion.

If there is any certain reality, it is this unseen reality, and apart from it all statements are merely probabilities. If there is any definitive matter, it is that which Allah's decree and destiny have already settled, and no one knows what Allah has decided regarding the future except Allah. Yes, despite the inviolable reality of the divine decree, there are also some divine sunan regarding this universe that are inviolable and that form part of the divine decree. Some of these divine sunan are within the reach of human understanding, and by attaining access to them, man can discharge the duties of his office of divine khilafah very well. However, despite these means, the decision of Allah and His decree are supreme, and the divine decree remains unknown. This is the real reality of this universe, and (﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾) (17:9) — this Qur'an points toward that which is most straight.

Now the discourse turns from the keys to the knowledge of the unseen toward a particular aspect of this universe, namely the human self, which is itself a part of this universe and is one of the most significant wonders of Allah's power, through which the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah is manifested very clearly.

(Verse 60 — Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran)

(Verse) "Number 60."

These are a few more words. Earlier, a few phrases had drawn the broad and far-reaching horizons of the unseen world, and the limited words of the previous verse had made clear how complete and all-encompassing God's knowledge is. Now these words under discussion and their concise phrases make it clear that a person's entire life is fully within Allah's power. All affairs are being settled according to Allah's knowledge, Allah's decree and Allah's management. A person's waking and sleeping, his dying and being born, his rising again and his reckoning, all are being settled in accordance with the command of God, and they will continue to be settled in accordance with it. This truth is expressed in the Qur'an's distinctive style, in a very concrete, concise and impactful manner. The style is so tangible and dynamic, and in such a manner, that the entire scene appears to move on a screen, carrying human consciousness and emotions along with it, in an extremely wondrous mode of expression.

(Verse) "It is He who takes your souls by night." (6:60) When a person sinks into the embrace of sleep, it is as though he dies. The state of sleep is indeed a kind of death. Just as in the state of death a person's senses become inactive, so too in sleep the senses become inactive and a person is heedless. The senses become lifeless, reason stops, and a person's understanding and perception also cease. This is a mystery that remains beyond human comprehension: how human faculties come to a halt in the state of sleep. Although we know the signs of the state of sleep, humankind has not reached the reality of how this state comes over a person. This too is an unseen state, just as other unseen states surround a person. But when a person enters this state, all his powers are taken from him, to the point that he is deprived even of the power of understanding and perception. For a specific time, a person is deprived of the signs of life and comes into the power of Allah. The reality is that when a person goes into sleep, it is solely and purely the will of God that brings him back to wakefulness. Consider well how weak and powerless a person is when he is in the power of Allah.

(Verse) "And He knows what you commit by day." (6:60) The limbs of human beings, during the state of wakefulness, perform the movements they make throughout the day: what they grasp and what they release, the good deeds they do and the evil deeds they do, all of them are within Allah's knowledge. The movements and stillnesses of all human beings are under Allah's watch, and not a single thing from their movements and stillnesses escapes Allah's knowledge.

(Verse) "Then He raises you up therein, that a specified term may be fulfilled." (6:60) That is, when you pass the night in sleep, He awakens you from that state of rest and cessation so that you may complete your appointed term of life until the true death. Thus all these people, in all these conditions, enter into Allah's power and decree. They cannot step outside the decree of God, nor does this decree stop anywhere.

(Verse) "Then to Him is your return." (6:60) Just as a flock, after grazing, returns to its place of residence and to its owner, so a person returns to his true Master.

(Verse) "Then He will inform you of what you used to do." (6:60) At that time their record of deeds, in which every act of theirs is written, will be presented, and they will be judged with a true justice in which not the slightest trace of injustice will exist.

In short, this verse consists of a few words, yet within these words a long thread is wrapped. Within it are hidden various images and scenes. Various decisions, various indications and guidance are inscribed. Various shades and colours are present: who is able to fill these few words with such hues? If these verses are not miraculous, then what speech could be miraculous? Yet it is astonishing that those who deny and adopt the attitude of disbelief are heedless of them, seek material miracles and marvels, and invite the painful punishment of Allah.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 61–62:**

(Verses) 61 to 62.

(Verse) "Wa huwa al-qahiru fawqa 'ibadih" (6:61): "He has complete power over His servants." That is, He is the powerful King, and all human beings are His subjects, under His complete control. There is no comparison between the true power of this King and the power of people. In contrast to Him, not only do they have no power, they also have no helper or supporter. All of them are completely His slaves, completely subject to Him and under His possession.

This is the complete slavery of a human being to a Subduer who has total dominion, and it is this true concept that brings about a real change in people's practical lives, even if Allah grants people complete freedom and authority, gives them abundant knowledge and recognition, and gives them abundant strength so that they may fulfil the demands of the duty of khilafah (vicegerency) on this earth. But despite all these things, every breath of human life is determined by Allah, and every movement and rest of a person is in accordance with the law of nature of Allah, which He Himself has set into operation within human existence, and a person cannot violate these laws of his own existence. And these laws too are fixed and determined within the human self and human movements.

(Verse) "Wa yursilu 'alaykum hafazah" (6:61): "And He sends over you guardians." Here the verse does not specify the nature of these guardians. Other passages state that these guardians are angels who are attached to human beings and record all the deeds that proceed from them. Here the only intention is to highlight that every human being is directly under Allah's supervision, and to instil in human thinking the awareness that the self is never left free even for a moment, nor is it ever alone. At all times there are beings with it who record all its movements and rest, and they prepare such a complete and comprehensive record that nothing escapes their sight. This is a concept and a way of thinking which, as a result, awakens the whole human personality, and it feels every matter.

(Verse) "Hatta idha ja'a ahadakumu al-mawtu tawaffathu rusuluna wa hum la yufarrituun" (6:61): "Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take his soul, and they do not fall short in discharging their duty." This is the same divine supervision in a different shade: for every human being, the number of breaths in this world is fixed. There is also a time fixed for those breaths to cease, but he does not know it. From the human perspective, the appointed term (ajal) is fixed, yet he does not know it. From the human standpoint the appointed term is fixed, which is unseen to him, and its knowledge can never reach him by any means. But in Allah's knowledge it is already recorded in writing, and it cannot advance or be delayed by even a second. Every person is completing his breaths of life. The time of his departure from this world is not far away but very near; there can be no change in it, nor can there be any error or omission in it. Allah's representatives stand ready; these are angels, and their system is extremely secure. The time of every person's death is recorded in writing, yet man is in deep heedlessness. These representatives discharge their duty with the utmost meticulousness; they deliver their message on time. This thought and this belief alone are sufficient and healing to shake a heedless person awake. A person who holds this belief feels that Allah's decrees encompass him completely. At all times he knows with certainty that in the very next moment his soul may be taken, and with the very next breath the movement of his heart may stop.

(Verse) "Thumma ruddu ila Allahi mawlahumu al-haqq" (6:62): "Then they are all returned to Allah, their true Master." The true Master is the One who provided them with the opportunities to live on this earth and appointed over them guardians to record the complete account of their whole life here, who make no deficiency or excess whatsoever. After that, it is the same Master who, when He wills, calls these human beings to Himself so that He may judge them according to His own will, and His judgment cannot be appealed.

(Verse) "Ala lahu al-hukmu wa huwa asra'u al-hasibin" (6:62): "Beware! Judgment belongs to Him alone, and He is the swiftest in reckoning." Only He decides; He Himself takes the account. He does not delay in deciding, nor does He delay in recompense and punishment. The effects of swift judgment are also very profound on human life. A person thinks that with Allah there is no delay in reckoning or in deciding.

A Muslim's conviction that Allah is his Creator, that one day he must die, and that he must present the full account of his entire life before Allah, does not allow him to be heedless even for a moment. According to this thought, the natural result of his beliefs is that he regards Allah alone as the true Sovereign, and it becomes his logical belief that all the affairs of the servants on this earth must be settled according to Allah's command.

The reckoning of the Hereafter and the decisions of reward and punishment in the Hereafter are in any case based on the deeds performed in this world, and people cannot adopt correct conduct in this world unless there exists for them a coherent code of action in the form of a Shariah, in which the limits of lawful and unlawful have been set for them, and upon which their accountability in the Hereafter rests. Thus, according to this worldview, it is established that in this world too the Sovereign is Allah, and in the Hereafter too the Sovereign is Allah.

If it were decided that in the world some other law than the Shariah of Allah would prevail, then on what code would they be held to account and reckoned in the Hereafter? Would their deeds be weighed on the Day of Resurrection according to laws that were not actually enforced in the world, and according to which these people did not get their decisions made? Such a situation is absolutely impossible.

People should understand well and be certain that Allah will take their account according to His own Shariah. If they have not conformed their whole life and their affairs to the Shariah of Allah, in the same way as they perform their acts of worship according to the Shariah, then they should know that when they are called to account, the first thing they will be asked is why they did not do so, and why they set up and accepted other deities as sovereigns and lawgivers besides Allah. Why did they not regard Allah alone, without partner, as Sovereign and Lord? In truth, the first account they will be called to give is why they denied Allah's right of sovereignty, or why they committed shirk by following other codes alongside the Shariah of Allah, and by serving others alongside the service of Allah. Why did they commit shirk, which is an unforgivable crime, by following others besides Allah in their collective life, in their economic and political system, and in their dealings and social relations? Allah's law is that He does not forgive shirk, and He forgives all other shortcomings besides shirk, if He wills.

Now Allah presents them before the court of nature, because human nature itself possesses awareness of divine reality. It is a characteristic of human nature that in difficult moments it seeks refuge in the presence of Allah. The Qur'an depicts such severe moments very swiftly, and this scene comes onto the screen and passes on. But this scene is extremely clear-cut, decisive, effective and astonishing.

This frightful and painful situation is not always deferred to the Day of Resurrection; sometimes in this world too a person encounters such circumstances. For example, in the difficulties a person faces on a sea voyage, the polytheists too always turn towards Allah, Glorified is His majesty, and it is Allah alone who then delivers people. But when they emerge safely from that difficult and frightening situation and return to normal life, they then begin to commit shirk.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 63–64:

(Verses) No. 63 to 64.

The conception of dangers and the remembrance of terrifying moments sometimes bring people themselves onto the right path. Through it even hard hearts become soft. Through it a person is given the awareness that he is very weak and needs Allah's help at all times, as a result of which his difficulties are removed and he receives the blessing of Allah in the form of deliverance.

﴿Say: Who delivers you from the darkness of the land and the sea, when you call upon Him humbly and in secret, saying, "If He delivers us from this, we will surely be among the grateful"?﴾ (63)

(Say to them, O Prophet (ﷺ): In the darkness of the desert and the sea, who saves you from dangers? Who is it that you call upon humbly and secretly (in times of calamity)? To whom do you say that if He saves us from this affliction, we will surely be grateful?)

This is a psychological experience that has befallen everyone who has ever been caught in difficulties, or who has seen people caught in difficulties, because on land and at sea alike a human being encounters such troubles. It is not necessary that darkness exist only at night, for helplessness is also a darkness, and danger is also a darkness. The unseen events of land and sea, for which the eyes of the whole world are fixed in expectation, are also darknesses. Whenever a person is surrounded by these darknesses of land and sea, he sees in this universe that Allah alone is the true disposer of affairs. In such circumstances a person, with great humility, single-mindedness and in a most private manner, raises his hands in supplication to Allah alone. In such circumstances human nature emerges in its true form, free of all veils. At that time the reality hidden in the depths of nature comes to the surface, and that reality is the sovereignty of Allah, the One without partner. The person turns towards the Exalted Lord and no longer associates anyone with Him. At that time a person comes to know how feeble conceptions of associating partners are. Now there is no trace of shirk, and those who are afflicted with this anguish and grief say: "If He saves us from this affliction, we will surely be grateful." At this juncture Allah commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to draw these people's attention to the true reality:

﴿Say: Allah delivers you from it and from every distress, yet you still associate partners with Him.﴾ (64)

(Say: Allah delivers you from it and from every distress, and then you associate others with Him.) Within this, they are also told that despite this, they commit the reprehensible act of shirk and turn back in a strange manner.

Here people are reminded of this situation: after this deliverance they may again fall into such difficult circumstances. It is not that these hardships were to come only once. This turn passed over them, and now they have, as it were, slipped out of Allah's power. If they think this way, it is their error. Consider the following verse in this regard:
