(Verse) 65.

If a calamity comes down upon you from above your heads, or erupts from beneath your feet, its imagining is more frightening than calamities that come from the right and the left, for the faculty of imagination of a human being thinks that he can confront a calamity coming from the right or the left. But a punishment that descends from above one's head, or that boils up from beneath one's feet, covers a person, shakes him, and overcomes his limited strength. Standing firm against it and confronting it is difficult. The manner of expression is such that it highlights this powerful factor in the consciousness and feeling of a person, and a person comes to believe that the punishment of Allah can encompass him whenever He wills and in whatever manner He wills. Allah has the power to seize His servants at any time.

After pointing to these kinds of punishment in this verse, reference is also made to those kinds of punishment which come upon a person at a very slow pace and after a long period of time. Their action is not completed in a moment or a short span. These kinds become companions of a person; they become woven into a person's settlements and his entire life, and remain his travelling companions night and day.

(Verse) "Or He will confuse you with factions and make you taste the violence of one another." (6:65) "Or confound you with factions and make some of you taste the might of others." This is yet another form of Allah's lasting and long-term punishment. This punishment comes upon people by their own hands, and they drink it sip by sip. It happens thus: Allah divides them into groups and parties; these groups and factions come to grips with one another. They become a kind of parties in which the common people cannot even distinguish between the sects. Dispute and contention persist among these sects. A long-standing enmity is established, and one sect becomes a calamity for the other.

Humanity, in various periods of its history, has felt this kind of punishment. Whenever people have expelled the Islamic system of life from their collective life, they have been afflicted with this punishment. Whenever people have abandoned Islam and begun to follow their desires and inclinations, and have made their shortcomings, weaknesses and ignorance their principle, they have been struck by this kind of punishment. Whenever people lose the way and begin to create for themselves a system of life, begin to make customs and collective laws for themselves, and begin to determine their own standards of good and bad, then as a result some people become slaves of other people. Some people want other people to obey the system of life they have devised, and thus they become slaves of others; and in opposition to this, some other people rise up against that system. Thus the first party begins to inflict as much oppression as it can upon these opponents. Now two parties are in the field. Their desires, inclinations, aims and interests collide. As a result of this collision, they taste each other's might. Some people become hostile to other people, they become angry at one another, and the sole cause of all these contradictions is that these two parties do not agree upon a single standard. The standard that the Worshipped One has laid down for all is that according to which all people are servants of the Lord of Majesty. No one hesitates to bow before this Lord, nor does he feel any humiliation in this worship and bowing.

The greatest fitnah on this earth is when some people rise with the demand that other people should regard them as gods, worship them, and acknowledge their rightful sovereignty. This is the fitnah because of which people split into groups and come to grips with one another, since apparently they appear to be one nation and one ummah, but in reality they are slaves and servants of one another. Among them, some people hold power, and they cling to that power, because in that power they are not bound by the Shariah of Allah. Other people, who do not hold power, harbour hatred and enmity for those in authority. These holders of power and those who plot to snatch power from them (the mutarabbisin, those who sit in ambush) taste each other's might and enmity. All these people are divided into parties. They are neither separated from one another nor is there any distance between them. Though they are one, they are separated from each other. Today all of humanity on this earth is afflicted with this punishment of Allah, and it is a punishment that works at a very slow pace.

The position that the Islamic movement holds on this earth is worthy of attention. It is necessary that the position of the Islamic movement be made entirely distinct and separate from the jahiliyyah (the ignorance of pre-Islamic times) that has overspread the world. The question is: what is jahiliyyah? Every situation, every government and every society over which the Islamic Shariah does not rule is jahiliyyah. Every situation in which the sovereignty of Allah alone is not acknowledged is jahiliyyah. A complete separation between this jahiliyyah and the position of the Islamic movement is necessary. The Islamic movement must, within every nation and every society that remains in jahiliyyah and wishes to enforce jahili laws and values, establish for itself a separate and distinct existence and identity, and it must appear distinct.

The Islamic movement can be saved from the threat of this punishment of Allah only if it becomes completely separate from the people of jahiliyyah in consciousness, in ideology and in its system of life. The words of this verse, "Or confound you with factions and make some of you taste the might of others," demand this. And this complete separation and distinct identity must remain until Allah grants us the ability to establish Dar al-Islam (the abode of Islam). Within the Islamic movement, the consciousness must remain alive that it alone is the true Muslim ummah, and that the society which actually exists around it has not yet become part of the Islamic ummah. These people are bearers of jahiliyyah. On this creed and this method, the Islamic movement must separate itself from other people. After that, it should raise its hands in supplication before the court of Allah, saying: O Allah, decide between us and this our people and this society in truth, for You are the best of deciders.

If the Islamic movement does not adopt this distinction and separation, it will become liable to the warning and threat mentioned above. It will become a group and sect within a particular society, and this sect too will be mixed up with other sects. It will have no separate identity, nor any distinctive standing within its surroundings. It will also be struck by the punishment that falls upon other people, and this will be a lasting and long-term punishment. And there will not even remain the hope that it will receive the victory and support that Allah has promised.

Because of complete separation and distinction from one's society, sometimes very great sacrifices have to be made, and mountains of trials also fall. But these trials and losses are far smaller than those that would come upon an Islamic movement if it were mixed up in a jahili society, its position were not clear or distinct, and it remained merged and entangled in the jahili society, until in the end "whoever goes into the salt mine becomes salt."

To understand this point, it is necessary that we study the history of the prophets and messengers. From the history of the messengers it appears that as long as the followers of the messengers did not completely separate themselves from the jahili society of their time, they did not attain the victory and support that Allah had promised to all the messengers, that the believers and the messengers would ultimately prevail. No nation has ever attained dominance and success until it was cut off and separated from the jahili society of its time, and until it had made its ideology and system of life distinct and separate from other people. This separation and distinction does not mean that the Islamic movement should socially boycott people; rather, it means that it should be distinct in its outlook on life, in its religion and in its system. This is the unit at which the paths of Islamic movements and other people part ways.

It must be remembered that the method of Islamic da'wah will be the same as that according to which the messengers gave da'wah. On this path there are the same stages that the messengers encountered.

(Verse) "Look how We variously explain the signs to them, so that perhaps they may understand." (6:65)

Lesson 63 at a glance:

The previous wave concluded with the theme of complete separation between the people of truth and falsehood. In this wave it is further detailed. It was the people of the Prophet ﷺ who denied the Book revealed to him, and that Book was indeed the truth. On this very point the paths of the Prophet ﷺ and his people parted, and he separated from them and took his own way. Allah commanded him to separate from them and to declare openly that he is not their guardian, and that now he hands them over to their fate, and that they are heading toward an evil end, which is approaching.

The Prophet ﷺ is also commanded that when they are finding fault with Islam, he should not sit in their assembly at a time when they are mocking the religion of Islam and not showing it the honour it deserves. But along with this separation and distinction, the command is that they should continue to be warned of their evil end, and the work of admonition and preaching should also continue. This situation must in any case remain: that the people of da'wah and the people of jahiliyyah, though one nation, should be two separate sects and two distinct ummahs. This is because in Islam, colour, race and lineage have no standing; here, unity and division depend on the basis of ideology and creed. It is this ideology and creed that is the point of agreement or the place of separation. When the religious foundation is present, people unite, and when the religious element is absent, all other ties are severed... This, then, is the brief theme of this wave.

(Verse 66–67)

Here the address is directed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Through this address, the hearts of the Prophet ﷺ and of the believers who come after him are filled with faith and certainty. Even when a caller's entire people and entire society reject the truth, he is certain that the truth will prevail, because deciding about truth is not the work of the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah); it is the work of Allah to decide between truth and falsehood. It is Allah alone who can declare that a certain thing is the truth and a certain thing is falsehood. Therefore, the decisions of those who deny have no reality or standing.

After this, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is commanded to disassociate himself from his people, to declare that he is free of responsibility for them, that now the paths of him and his people have separated, and also to declare that he has no authority or agency over them in any matter, nor is he a guardian responsible for them. His duty ends when he has conveyed the message and made it understood, because responsibility and guardianship are not part of the duty of messengers. When a messenger has conveyed the message and made it understood, his obligation is fulfilled. After that, the messengers leave the nations so that they reach their natural end, because every matter becomes manifest at its appointed time, and when the matter comes to light, everyone comes to know it.

﴿For every news there is a fixed time, and you will soon come to know﴾ (6:67)

"Every report has a time when it will be established, and soon you will know the outcome yourselves."

Here it is not stated what the matter is that is going to become manifest. In such places, leaving the matter vague is more frightening; hearts tremble with fear.

These verses enjoin steadfastness upon the truth and give assurance that however loud the apparent clamour of falsehood may be, its end will certainly be bad, and that at a fixed time Allah seizes the people of falsehood; that every matter has a time of manifestation, and every present situation has an outcome that is yet to come.

The reality is that the callers to truth face the denial and coldness of their people, suffer abuse from their own families, become strangers among their own households, and encounter nerve-wracking circumstances. In such conditions they truly need exactly this kind of consolation, and thus their hearts are filled with peace and certainty, and it is the Qur'an alone that can produce this tranquility and composure in their hearts.

When the Prophet ﷺ conveyed this message to them, and their unjust denial and rejection was answered by severing ties with them, then the Messenger ﷺ is commanded not to keep company with them, even for the purpose of preaching, if the situation is such that they are criticising Islam and not discussing Islamic matters with respect, seriousness and dignity. Where they are not observing the serious dignity and awe that Islam demands, but are instead mocking religion and passing remarks with jesting and levity, whether by their tongue or by their actions, in such circumstances it is commanded that one should not keep company with them, because a person who sits with them in this way is regarded, in effect, as endorsing these matters, or at least it will be thought that such a person has no religious jealousy. If Satan causes a Muslim to forget and he sits in such a gathering, then as soon as he remembers, it is his duty to rise up and leave that place.

(Verse 66–67)

Here the address is directed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Through this address, the hearts of the Prophet ﷺ and of the believers who come after him are filled with faith and certainty. Even when a caller's entire people and entire society reject the truth, he is certain that the truth will prevail, because deciding about truth is not the work of the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah); it is the work of Allah to decide between truth and falsehood. It is Allah alone who can declare that a certain thing is the truth and a certain thing is falsehood. Therefore, the decisions of those who deny have no reality or standing.

After this, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is commanded to disassociate himself from his people, to declare that he is free of responsibility for them, that now the paths of him and his people have separated, and also to declare that he has no authority or agency over them in any matter, nor is he a guardian responsible for them. His duty ends when he has conveyed the message and made it understood, because responsibility and guardianship are not part of the duty of messengers. When a messenger has conveyed the message and made it understood, his obligation is fulfilled. After that, the messengers leave the nations so that they reach their natural end, because every matter becomes manifest at its appointed time, and when the matter comes to light, everyone comes to know it.

﴿For every news there is a fixed time, and you will soon come to know﴾ (6:67)

"Every report has a time when it will be established, and soon you will know the outcome yourselves."

Here it is not stated what the matter is that is going to become manifest. In such places, leaving the matter vague is more frightening; hearts tremble with fear.

These verses enjoin steadfastness upon the truth and give assurance that however loud the apparent clamour of falsehood may be, its end will certainly be bad, and that at a fixed time Allah seizes the people of falsehood; that every matter has a time of manifestation, and every present situation has an outcome that is yet to come.

The reality is that the callers to truth face the denial and coldness of their people, suffer abuse from their own families, become strangers among their own households, and encounter nerve-wracking circumstances. In such conditions they truly need exactly this kind of consolation, and thus their hearts are filled with peace and certainty, and it is the Qur'an alone that can produce this tranquility and composure in their hearts.

When the Prophet ﷺ conveyed this message to them, and their unjust denial and rejection was answered by severing ties with them, then the Messenger ﷺ is commanded not to keep company with them, even for the purpose of preaching, if the situation is such that they are criticising Islam and not discussing Islamic matters with respect, seriousness and dignity. Where they are not observing the serious dignity and awe that Islam demands, but are instead mocking religion and passing remarks with jesting and levity, whether by their tongue or by their actions, in such circumstances it is commanded that one should not keep company with them, because a person who sits with them in this way is regarded, in effect, as endorsing these matters, or at least it will be thought that such a person has no religious jealousy. If Satan causes a Muslim to forget and he sits in such a gathering, then as soon as he remembers, it is his duty to rise up and leave that place.

This command was for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is also possible that Muslims who come after him are included in it. This command was for that period. At that time, the Prophet's (ﷺ) task was limited to invitation and preaching, and the wisdom of Allah required that he refrain from jihad and fighting. He was given the guidance that he should avoid confrontation with the polytheists. Accordingly, in that period he was commanded that when he saw that in a gathering of the polytheists the religion of Islam was being mocked with disrespect, he should avoid sitting in such gatherings. And if it ever happened that Satan led him into forgetfulness and he arrived at a gathering where blasphemous things were being said about Islam, then as soon as he remembered, he should rise and leave from there. Some narrations state that this instruction was for all the people of Islam as well. Here "the wrongdoers" (ﻇﺎﻟﻤﻮﻥ, al-zalimun) means the polytheists, as we have already said before. This is the general style of speech of the Qur'an.

But when the Islamic state was established in Madinah, the position of the Prophet (ﷺ) with respect to the polytheists became different. Now the position was that the Prophet (ﷺ) continued jihad and fighting against them until all the sources of mischief were eliminated and no one had the courage to utter any blasphemy against the signs of Allah.

After this, the context of the discourse once again repeats the matter of complete distinction and differentiation between the believers and the polytheists, just as earlier the separation between Allah and the polytheists had been decided. Here it is decided that there is also a difference between the ends and the responsibilities of the two.

(آیت) ” نمبر 69۔ [Verse 69 — the Arabic verse marker as it stands in the source]

In the Islamic order there is no shared responsibility between the righteous (muttaqin) and the polytheists, because the righteous and the polytheists are two separate communities, even though they may be one in colour, race, nation and government. This is because, by the Islamic measure, colour, race and nation carry no weight. The people of taqwa are one ummah, and the wrongdoers and polytheists are entirely a different ummah. The people of taqwa bear no responsibility for anything in the reckoning of the wrongdoers. However, their responsibility extends to this extent: that they must continue striving for the reform of the wrongdoers, so that they too may become people of taqwa and become part of their ummah. If there is no ideological unity between the people of taqwa and the people of wrongdoing, then no other form of partnership between them can be established.

This is the religion of Islam, and this is the word of Allah. If anyone speaks or adopts a course of conduct other than this, that act will be his own; but he should know that by this conduct he may also be expelled from the religion of Islam. Study a little further: the Qur'an gives further guidance, and further limits and boundaries of complete separation between the people of truth and the people of falsehood are explained.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 70:

(Verse) "Number 70."

In this verse we stand before the following realities:

First, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is commanded to sever relations with those who mock his religion and the Islamic system, and this same guidance comes for the believers after him as well. This severance and separation applies both in speech and in action. Those who do not give Islam its proper place, who do not make it the code of their lives, the source of their ideas, the system of their conduct, their system of morality and their system of law, and who do not render it dignified, they too are in reality mocking this religion. Those who debate the topics of this religion, speak about the Islamic Shari'ah and attribute ridiculous qualities to this religion, they too are counted among those who mock the religion. For example, those who speak about the unseen and ridicule the Lord of the unseen, although faith in the unseen is among the fundamental principles of belief; and those who joke about zakat, although it is among the foundations of the religion; and those who joke about modesty, chastity and purity, although these are among the principles of the religion. These people, in their speeches and writings, label these as the morals of the feudal and agrarian societies of early times, or they label them as bourgeois morality. And those who make derogatory remarks about the rights of spouses, and those who regard the principles of chastity and purity set for women as women's backwardness and their exploitation, and, lastly and above all, those who do not accept the sovereignty of Allah over the entire life of human beings, and who do not believe in the sovereignty of Allah over the political, social, economic and legal life of man, and who maintain that in these spheres people may exercise their authority in rebellion against the Shari'ah of Allah. All these people fall within the meaning of this verse, and they will be regarded as those who mock the religion of Allah. Therefore every Muslim is commanded to keep away from these people, except for the purpose of preaching, because these people are wrongdoers and polytheists, and they are among the disbelievers who are caught up in their disbelieving deeds, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be entertained with boiling water and they will remain in a painful punishment, because these people were engaged in the aforementioned disbelieving conduct.

Second, the reality that emerges is that although the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been commanded to leave such people aside, and this same command remains for the believers who come after him, yet along with this severance the Messenger was also given the guidance that he should, while ignoring those who have made mockery of this religion their practice and whom the temporary life of this world has deceived, continue to remind them. He should keep warning them that the evil they are gathering will be a burden upon their own souls, and that a time is coming when they will meet Allah, and besides Allah they will have no helper who could give any assistance at all. No intercessor will be theirs, and no financial ransom will be accepted from them by which they could free their souls from the things they committed in the world. The beauty and depth of meaning of the words in which the Qur'an has expressed this concept deserve consideration. Recite it once again.

(Verse) "And warn by it lest a soul be delivered to destruction for what it has earned; it will have besides Allah no protector and no intercessor, and if it should offer every compensation, it would not be accepted from it."

"And warn by means of this Qur'an, so that no soul is seized for what it has earned, and it shall have no protector or intercessor besides Allah, and even if it were to offer every possible ransom, that would not be accepted from it." (6:70)

Every person will be held accountable in his individual capacity; the responsibility will be individual and based upon his own deeds, and it will be in circumstances where there will be no guardian and intercessor besides Allah, and if anyone wishes to pay the greatest possible compensation and ransom, that too will not be accepted, and thus in no way will he be able to free his neck.

As for those who made their religion a target of mockery and were deceived by the few days of worldly life, they are the people who mortgaged their whole lives to their evil deeds, and for this reason the punishment mentioned in this verse has become due upon them, and this is the end that was decreed for them.

(Verse) "Those are the ones who are delivered to destruction for what they have earned. For them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve." (6:70)

"Indeed, such people are seized because of their own earnings; for them is a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment in return for their denial of the truth."

That is, they were seized because of their evil deeds, and this was a fitting punishment for them. What kind of recompense? Hot water that will roast their throats and stomachs. Because of their disbelieving deeds, this will be a painful punishment for them, and this punishment will be evidence that they kept mocking the religion.

Third point: Allah's statement that these people have made the religion of Allah a matter of play and amusement. The question is whether the true religion of Allah is in reality their religion. "Their religion" (dinahum) refers to those who have entered the religion, and after entering it they have made their religion a matter of play and amusement. In Madinah such people existed, and in common usage they were called hypocrites. In Madinah the matter was indeed of this kind.

The question arises whether this verse also applies to those people, for example the polytheists, who have not entered the religion of Islam. Yes, it applies to them as well, because the true religion is the religion of Islam. It is the religion of all humanity, whether or not anyone believes in it. For whoever rejects this religion and turns away from it, in reality he abandons his own religion, because this is the religion that is religion in the sight of Allah, and after the mission of the Seal of the Prophets, Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ), only this religion is accepted by Allah.

This is the meaning according to which Allah, in this verse, attributes the religion to them, saying that it is their religion.

(Verse) "And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and play, and whom the worldly life has deceived." (6:70)

As we have explained, this verse alludes to the same meaning: that the religion of Islam is the religion of all human beings. Therefore whoever makes the religion of Islam a matter of amusement and play is, in effect, mocking his own religion, even if the one doing so is a polytheist.

Fourth: how far is the company of wrongdoers and polytheists permissible, and what are the limits of sitting with those who make the religion of Islam a matter of amusement and play? Such sitting is permissible only for the sake of admonition and advice, and beyond that no kind of relationship with such people is permissible. That is, in circumstances where they are mocking the signs of Allah and finding fault, and this fault-finding and mockery may take various forms.

Imam al-Qurtubi, in his tafsir al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an, has written in this regard that "this verse explicitly refutes the view which says that religious leaders and their followers may, by way of taqiyyah, keep company with the corrupt and may, by way of taqiyyah, endorse their mistaken opinions."

I think that one may sit in the gatherings of the corrupt and mischief-makers, even for the purpose of admonition and reminder in gatherings of admonition, within the limits and conditions already mentioned in this verse. As for the matter of sitting in the gatherings of the wicked and the transgressors, remaining silent over their evil and mischievous talk, and doing so by way of taqiyyah, this is not permissible in any case, because it is an open affirmation of falsehood, a testimony against the truth, and a deception of the people. Moreover, such conduct involves a disrespect to the religion and also to those who carry out the work of the religion. Therefore in such circumstances sitting is forbidden, and leaving such gatherings becomes obligatory.

Imam al-Qurtubi has also quoted other statements. "Ibn Khuwayz Mindad says that whoever speaks disrespectfully about the signs of Allah, one should immediately walk out of his gathering, whether that person is a believer or a disbeliever. For this reason our imams have forbidden going into the land of the enemy. Likewise, going to churches and temples has been forbidden, and association with disbelievers and innovators has been prohibited. Furthermore, it is also forbidden that anyone should befriend them, listen to their talk, or debate with them." Reports state that some innovators said to Abu Imran al-Nakha'i, "Listen to my words," and he turned his face away from them and said, "I am not ready even to listen to half of your talk." A similar statement is also reported from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, and Fudayl ibn Iyad has said: whoever keeps friendship with a person of innovation, his deeds will be destroyed, and in this way Islam will depart from his heart. Whoever gave his daughter in marriage to an innovator has severed the ties of kinship, and whoever sits with innovators will be deprived of wisdom. If Allah knew that a certain servant regards an innovator with disfavor, I hope Allah will forgive such a person. Abu Abdullah al-Hakim has narrated from Hazrat Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever honours an innovator has helped in the work of demolishing Islam."

These matters concern a person who is an innovator but still a follower of the religion of Islam. As for the person who claims for himself one of the attributes of Allah's exclusive qualities, such as the attribute of sovereignty, he is a greater criminal than the innovator, and whoever attributes that quality to such a person is an even greater criminal. This crime is not merely like the crime of committing an innovation, but a great crime like disbelief and polytheism. Ascribing the attribute of sovereignty to any person was not present in the time of the righteous predecessors (salaf al-salih). For this reason they did not discuss this point. At no time in Islamic history has anyone regarded himself as a ruler against Allah, nor has anyone claimed sovereignty for himself or sovereignty for the people while at the same time claiming to be a Muslim. Before the French invasion of the Middle East, the system of Allah's sovereignty was established in the Islamic world. Only after the French invasion have people gone outside the sphere of Allah's sovereignty. Yes, some people remained protected from it. Therefore among the statements of the predecessors, few are found whose application we can make to this modern situation, because this modern situation is such that Muslims have left the Shari'ah limits far behind.

Lesson No. 64 at a glance:

This wave is a most fitting melody in the explanation of the reality of divinity and the special attributes of the Supreme Majesty. In it, with great severity, a person is warned who, after being guided to the path of right guidance, re-enters the darkness of polytheism after having advanced, and reverts backward, or who abandons the religion of Islam and apostatizes. The picture of such a person is drawn as one who stands in a desert and sees no road leading him to his intended destination. On the resolution and decree that guidance has been given, which is based on the guidance of Allah, the sweet melody of this wave concludes with its long resonance on the point that, regarding creation and the governance of affairs (amr), all authority belongs to Allah alone. The manifestation of this absolute authority will occur on the day of the blowing of the Trumpet, when believers and disbelievers alike will be raised from their graves, all standing before Allah. Then the one who did not hold the belief will also know with certainty that all authority now lies in the hands of Allah alone, and that all matters have now returned to Him.

(Ayah) No. 71.
Throughout this surah, the blows are being struck with the repeated "Say" (qul). This is an extremely impactful style of address, intended to convey that the authority to determine the limits and boundaries of the lawful and the unlawful belongs to Allah alone, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is merely a conveyor of the message and a warner against the evil end. This manner of speech also indicates that the matter is extremely important, grave and frightening. These concepts that the Messenger of God ﷺ is presenting are his duty, and he has been commanded by God to do so.

﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us?﴾ (6:71)

O Prophet ﷺ, ask them: Shall we forsake Allah and call upon those who can neither benefit us nor harm us?

The people used to call upon others besides Allah and seek help from them. Disapproving of this act, Allah the Exalted says: O Prophet ﷺ, tell them plainly that those whom you have taken as your authorities have no power over your benefit or harm. Why do you call upon them? By "other than Allah" are meant here idols, shrines, trees and stones, spiritual beings and angels, and also human beings and devils. All of them are equal in the sense that none of them has in his control any benefit or harm for anyone. They are far from being in a position to benefit or harm anyone. In this world, all movements and stillness, and all benefit and harm, become manifest in accordance with Allah's decree. Nothing can occur without Allah's permission, and whatever occurs happens in accordance with Allah's decree, pleasure and will.

To call upon other than Allah, to worship other than Allah, and to seek help from other than Allah are despicable acts. To humble oneself before other than Allah, and all such beliefs and deeds directed toward others than Allah, are corrupt. It is also possible that this refutation is in response to the things the polytheists were practicing, or that it came refuting their proposal, in which they suggested: "We will begin worshipping your God, O Messenger ﷺ, on the condition that you join in worshipping our gods." In any case, whether this is a spontaneous refutation or a rejection of their proposal, in both cases the Muslims are commanded to completely sever ideological ties with the polytheists. The beliefs and practices of the polytheists are, by the standard of human reason, extremely weak and flimsy, provided reason is invited to reflect in an atmosphere of enlightened thinking and reason is not buried beneath the layers of custom, tradition and inherited conventions, as was the case in the time of the Messenger ﷺ, when people's consciousness was buried under their environment.

These polytheistic beliefs and practices are presented here in the light of the guidance that Allah gave to the Muslims, so that their falsehood and their despicable nature in contrast with Islamic guidance may become clearly evident, because Allah has given the guidance that only Allah, the One, is to be worshipped, only He is to be accepted as God and Sovereign, and His prescribed system of life is to be accepted without any partner. Observe the manner of speech: "Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us?" If we were to do this, it would truly be apostasy, turning back on our heels, regression. Instead of progress and moving forward, it would be going backward, because Islam is the name of progress.

﴿And be turned back upon our heels after Allah has guided us?﴾ (6:71)

And when Allah has guided us, shall we turn back on our heels?

After this, another vivid and concrete scene appears on the screen.

﴿Like one whom the devils have enticed in the land, bewildered, having companions who call him to guidance, saying: Come to us.﴾ (6:71)

"Shall we make ourselves like one whom the devils have led astray in the wilderness, bewildered and wandering, while his companions call him, saying, 'Come here, the right path is present'?"

This is a vivid and living image of misguidance, confusion and bewilderment: the person who, after believing in the doctrine of Tawhid, adopts polytheism, whose conscience is caught in a state of indecision between the One Lord and many scattered lords, generally falls into exactly this condition. He is caught in mental conflict and cannot decide which path to take. Thus this is the picture of a wretched creature of Allah "whom the devils have led astray in the wilderness." The word "istahwathu" itself paints the picture of its meaning. Had he taken one path, it would have been no matter; he would have fallen onto one road, even if it were the road of misguidance. But the situation he is in is this: from the other side, some of his companions are rightly guided, and they call him to the straight path, repeatedly crying out, "Come, brother, come this way." He stands bewildered between this satanic misdirection and the calls of his friends. He cannot decide where to go, or which of the two callers to choose. He is in this psychological conflict, and through the words of the Qur'an the mental torment of this person is clearly visible.

Whenever I recited this verse, I would keep thinking what torment a person must suffer because of this mental tug-of-war, conflict and hesitation. A mental picture of such people comes before the mind, but that is only a mental imagination. In practical life, however, we have also encountered the real circumstances of some people to whom this scene fully applies, and they are seen to be suffering this torment. These are people who had indeed attained the Islamic worldview and gained understanding of it according to their mental and practical capacity, but afterwards they turned back on their heels and began to worship and obey false and spurious deities. They did this obedience out of fear and greed. I saw that they were in exactly such an agonizing mental conflict. By observing the practical conditions of such people, it became clear what the true meaning of this verse is, and how comprehensive and effective the Qur'an's manner of expression is.

While this frightening scene was still before the eyes, and the heart of the believer was still trembling at the sight of this evil end, the straight path is shown and a decisive command is given.

﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (only) guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds. (71) And that you establish prayer and fear Him.﴾ (6:72, 6:71)

"Say: Indeed, the true guidance is the guidance of Allah, and we have been commanded to bow in submission to the Lord of the worlds, the Sovereign of the universe," "Establish prayer and be mindful of Him."

This decisive statement comes in a most fitting psychological situation. When a person observes a picture of bewilderment and conflict before him, finding no peace or rest and suffering the most severe torment, then on seeing such conditions, any reader is inclined to accept the decisive and reassuring word and seek comfort and tranquility. What is this decisive word? It is the truth: "The guidance is only the guidance of Allah." The construction "Inna huda Allahi huwa al-huda" also shows that this statement is decisive and that it is certain that the guidance of Allah is the true guidance.

Whenever a human being turns away from the guidance of Allah, he becomes a wanderer in a desert. Moreover, if a person replaces some part of Allah's guidance with his own ideas, imposes his own formulas, creates laws of his own, adopts his own customs, introduces self-made standards, and does all this outside the sphere of divine knowledge, divine guidance and the guidance of Allah's luminous Book, then he will never find the right path and will keep wandering in the boundless desert.

There is no doubt that Allah has bestowed upon man certain faculties through which he has reached some of the laws of nature of this universe, has subdued some of the forces of the cosmos, and is benefiting from those forces to run the system of this earth and to advance worldly life. But Allah has not given him such vast knowledge and power that he can reach the depths of all the forces and all the realities of this universe, nor can this human being enter into the vastness of the unseen world that surrounds him on every side. Human reason, human thought, the functioning of the various organs of the body, and the way these causes and organs work together in such a coordinated manner, are all matters which, for man, still belong to the unseen world.

For this very reason, even regarding his own self, man is in need of divine guidance and direction. Human life, his beliefs, his creation and growth, the values and standards of life, the system and customs of life, and the rules and laws of life are matters in which man needs Allah's guidance, so that these things may be implemented in his life and his practical existence may be governed by these divine instructions.

When this man returns to the guidance of Allah and accepts it, he is truly regarded as a guided person, because the guidance of Allah is the correct guidance. Whenever he distances himself from the guidance of Allah, or deviates from some parts of Allah's guidance, or replaces some parts of it and inserts self-made parts into it, he goes astray, because whatever is not based on Allah's guidance is misguidance, for there is no third or middle path. ("Fa-madha ba'd al-haqq illa al-dalal") "What is there after the truth but error?" In his long history, man has tasted the bitterness of this error thoroughly; because of it he has suffered immense calamities, and to this day humanity remains in those calamities. Human history has issued its final verdict that this will be its end whenever it deviates from Allah's guidance. This is a historical reality and cannot be denied. Moreover, this is Allah's command and this is also what Allah has informed us. There is no other reality besides this one. Although many claims to realities are made, history has not confirmed any of them. Those who wish to study human suffering resulting from deviation from divine guidance need not go far away; they should observe the societies spread around them. An intelligent person can see everything with his own seeing eyes. He can touch these sufferings with his hands. They are tangible, and all the wise people of this world are crying out about them.

Thus, within the context, a repeated command is given: submit before Allah, submit before Allah alone. Fear Him, worship Him and serve Him. "Wa-umirna..." "And we have been commanded to bow in submission to the Lord of the worlds, and to establish prayer, and to be mindful of Him."

That is, O Muhammad, proclaim that guidance and direction belong only to the guidance and direction of Allah, and this is why Allah has commanded that one submit before Allah, the Lord of the worlds, because the worlds bow before Him. This whole universe is bound by His command. Therefore there is no justification that, within this entire universe, a rational creature like man should not bow before Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and deny His dominion and lordship, and adopt a course different from the heavens, the earth and the whole universe.

Mention of the whole cosmos and its lordship is not out of place here. This is a reality without acknowledging which the matter does not hold together. One must acknowledge that the entire world, both the visible and the unseen, and the laws of nature according to which it moves, this universe cannot deviate from by even a whit. This is because Allah is the Lord of the worlds. As far as man is concerned, within his natural life he too is bound by these laws of nature. Human physical life is confined within these regulations, and he is obedient to them; he cannot step outside their sphere. Therefore it is man's duty to observe Allah's regulations even within his limited life of choice, and this is a severe test for him. In this test it will be seen whether he attains the path of guidance or arrives at the desert of misguidance. If he observes divine regulations in the same way as he is obedient to the laws of Allah within his natural life, then his life will pass in good order, and his conduct and his natural life will be harmonious with each other. His body will be the companion of his soul, and his world will be connected with the Hereafter. For details, see (the book Risala Deenyat by the Amir of Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan).

To say that I and all Muslims have been commanded to bow in submission before the true Master, and therefore they have adopted the way of submission, is a most effective and gladdening manner of speech, and until the Day of Resurrection, all those who adopt the path of submission and contentment will consider themselves direct executors of the divine command.

Now come the directives that form the course of action following the declaration of submission and contentment.

﴿And that you establish prayer and fear Him.﴾ (6:72)

"Establish prayer and be mindful of Him."

The essential obligation is to acknowledge Allah's lordship, to acknowledge His sovereignty, and to set oneself right according to His pleasure. After this comes the stage of acts of worship, and the work of psychological reform begins, so that a picture of practical life may be formed on the foundation of submission and contentment. Practical life and a detailed system of life cannot attain stability unless its structure is built on firm foundations.

The final blow of this wave encompasses the foundational truths of the Islamic worldview. These truths are the original and fundamental elements of the Islamic worldview. For example: resurrection and gathering (al-hashr wa'l-nashr), the creation of the universe, divine sovereignty (hakimiyyah Ilahiyyah), knowledge of the unseen and knowledge of the witnessed, and that Allah is All-Wise and All-Aware.
