Disapproving of this act, Allah the Exalted says: O Prophet ﷺ, tell them plainly that those whom you have taken as your authorities have no power over your benefit or harm. Why do you call upon them? By "other than Allah" are meant here idols, shrines, trees and stones, spiritual beings and angels, and also human beings and devils. All of them are equal in the sense that none of them has in his control any benefit or harm for anyone. They are far from being in a position to benefit or harm anyone. In this world, all movements and stillness, and all benefit and harm, become manifest in accordance with Allah's decree. Nothing can occur without Allah's permission, and whatever occurs happens in accordance with Allah's decree, pleasure and will.

To call upon other than Allah, to worship other than Allah, and to seek help from other than Allah are despicable acts. To humble oneself before other than Allah, and all such beliefs and deeds directed toward others than Allah, are corrupt. It is also possible that this refutation is in response to the things the polytheists were practicing, or that it came refuting their proposal, in which they suggested: "We will begin worshipping your God, O Messenger ﷺ, on the condition that you join in worshipping our gods." In any case, whether this is a spontaneous refutation or a rejection of their proposal, in both cases the Muslims are commanded to completely sever ideological ties with the polytheists. The beliefs and practices of the polytheists are, by the standard of human reason, extremely weak and flimsy, provided reason is invited to reflect in an atmosphere of enlightened thinking and reason is not buried beneath the layers of custom, tradition and inherited conventions, as was the case in the time of the Messenger ﷺ, when people's consciousness was buried under their environment.

These polytheistic beliefs and practices are presented here in the light of the guidance that Allah gave to the Muslims, so that their falsehood and their despicable nature in contrast with Islamic guidance may become clearly evident, because Allah has given the guidance that only Allah, the One, is to be worshipped, only He is to be accepted as God and Sovereign, and His prescribed system of life is to be accepted without any partner. Observe the manner of speech: "Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us?" If we were to do this, it would truly be apostasy, turning back on our heels, regression. Instead of progress and moving forward, it would be going backward, because Islam is the name of progress.

﴿And be turned back upon our heels after Allah has guided us?﴾ (6:71)

And when Allah has guided us, shall we turn back on our heels?

After this, another vivid and concrete scene appears on the screen.

﴿Like one whom the devils have enticed in the land, bewildered, having companions who call him to guidance, saying: Come to us.﴾ (6:71)

"Shall we make ourselves like one whom the devils have led astray in the wilderness, bewildered and wandering, while his companions call him, saying, 'Come here, the right path is present'?"

This is a vivid and living image of misguidance, confusion and bewilderment: the person who, after believing in the doctrine of Tawhid, adopts polytheism, whose conscience is caught in a state of indecision between the One Lord and many scattered lords, generally falls into exactly this condition. He is caught in mental conflict and cannot decide which path to take. Thus this is the picture of a wretched creature of Allah "whom the devils have led astray in the wilderness." The word "istahwathu" itself paints the picture of its meaning. Had he taken one path, it would have been no matter; he would have fallen onto one road, even if it were the road of misguidance. But the situation he is in is this: from the other side, some of his companions are rightly guided, and they call him to the straight path, repeatedly crying out, "Come, brother, come this way." He stands bewildered between this satanic misdirection and the calls of his friends. He cannot decide where to go, or which of the two callers to choose. He is in this psychological conflict, and through the words of the Qur'an the mental torment of this person is clearly visible.

Whenever I recited this verse, I would keep thinking what torment a person must suffer because of this mental tug-of-war, conflict and hesitation. A mental picture of such people comes before the mind, but that is only a mental imagination. In practical life, however, we have also encountered the real circumstances of some people to whom this scene fully applies, and they are seen to be suffering this torment. These are people who had indeed attained the Islamic worldview and gained understanding of it according to their mental and practical capacity, but afterwards they turned back on their heels and began to worship and obey false and spurious deities. They did this obedience out of fear and greed. I saw that they were in exactly such an agonizing mental conflict. By observing the practical conditions of such people, it became clear what the true meaning of this verse is, and how comprehensive and effective the Qur'an's manner of expression is.

While this frightening scene was still before the eyes, and the heart of the believer was still trembling at the sight of this evil end, the straight path is shown and a decisive command is given.

﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (only) guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds. (71) And that you establish prayer and fear Him.﴾ (6:72, 6:71)

"Say: Indeed, the true guidance is the guidance of Allah, and we have been commanded to bow in submission to the Lord of the worlds, the Sovereign of the universe," "Establish prayer and be mindful of Him."

This decisive statement comes in a most fitting psychological situation. When a person observes a picture of bewilderment and conflict before him, finding no peace or rest and suffering the most severe torment, then on seeing such conditions, any reader is inclined to accept the decisive and reassuring word and seek comfort and tranquility. What is this decisive word? It is the truth: "The guidance is only the guidance of Allah." The construction "Inna huda Allahi huwa al-huda" also shows that this statement is decisive and that it is certain that the guidance of Allah is the true guidance.

Whenever a human being turns away from the guidance of Allah, he becomes a wanderer in a desert. Moreover, if a person replaces some part of Allah's guidance with his own ideas, imposes his own formulas, creates laws of his own, adopts his own customs, introduces self-made standards, and does all this outside the sphere of divine knowledge, divine guidance and the guidance of Allah's luminous Book, then he will never find the right path and will keep wandering in the boundless desert.

There is no doubt that Allah has bestowed upon man certain faculties through which he has reached some of the laws of nature of this universe, has subdued some of the forces of the cosmos, and is benefiting from those forces to run the system of this earth and to advance worldly life. But Allah has not given him such vast knowledge and power that he can reach the depths of all the forces and all the realities of this universe, nor can this human being enter into the vastness of the unseen world that surrounds him on every side. Human reason, human thought, the functioning of the various organs of the body, and the way these causes and organs work together in such a coordinated manner, are all matters which, for man, still belong to the unseen world.

For this very reason, even regarding his own self, man is in need of divine guidance and direction. Human life, his beliefs, his creation and growth, the values and standards of life, the system and customs of life, and the rules and laws of life are matters in which man needs Allah's guidance, so that these things may be implemented in his life and his practical existence may be governed by these divine instructions.

When this man returns to the guidance of Allah and accepts it, he is truly regarded as a guided person, because the guidance of Allah is the correct guidance. Whenever he distances himself from the guidance of Allah, or deviates from some parts of Allah's guidance, or replaces some parts of it and inserts self-made parts into it, he goes astray, because whatever is not based on Allah's guidance is misguidance, for there is no third or middle path. ("Fa-madha ba'd al-haqq illa al-dalal") "What is there after the truth but error?" In his long history, man has tasted the bitterness of this error thoroughly; because of it he has suffered immense calamities, and to this day humanity remains in those calamities. Human history has issued its final verdict that this will be its end whenever it deviates from Allah's guidance. This is a historical reality and cannot be denied. Moreover, this is Allah's command and this is also what Allah has informed us. There is no other reality besides this one. Although many claims to realities are made, history has not confirmed any of them. Those who wish to study human suffering resulting from deviation from divine guidance need not go far away; they should observe the societies spread around them. An intelligent person can see everything with his own seeing eyes. He can touch these sufferings with his hands. They are tangible, and all the wise people of this world are crying out about them.

Thus, within the context, a repeated command is given: submit before Allah, submit before Allah alone. Fear Him, worship Him and serve Him. "Wa-umirna..." "And we have been commanded to bow in submission to the Lord of the worlds, and to establish prayer, and to be mindful of Him."

That is, O Muhammad, proclaim that guidance and direction belong only to the guidance and direction of Allah, and this is why Allah has commanded that one submit before Allah, the Lord of the worlds, because the worlds bow before Him. This whole universe is bound by His command. Therefore there is no justification that, within this entire universe, a rational creature like man should not bow before Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and deny His dominion and lordship, and adopt a course different from the heavens, the earth and the whole universe.

Mention of the whole cosmos and its lordship is not out of place here. This is a reality without acknowledging which the matter does not hold together. One must acknowledge that the entire world, both the visible and the unseen, and the laws of nature according to which it moves, this universe cannot deviate from by even a whit. This is because Allah is the Lord of the worlds. As far as man is concerned, within his natural life he too is bound by these laws of nature. Human physical life is confined within these regulations, and he is obedient to them; he cannot step outside their sphere. Therefore it is man's duty to observe Allah's regulations even within his limited life of choice, and this is a severe test for him. In this test it will be seen whether he attains the path of guidance or arrives at the desert of misguidance. If he observes divine regulations in the same way as he is obedient to the laws of Allah within his natural life, then his life will pass in good order, and his conduct and his natural life will be harmonious with each other. His body will be the companion of his soul, and his world will be connected with the Hereafter. For details, see (the book Risala Deenyat by the Amir of Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan).

To say that I and all Muslims have been commanded to bow in submission before the true Master, and therefore they have adopted the way of submission, is a most effective and gladdening manner of speech, and until the Day of Resurrection, all those who adopt the path of submission and contentment will consider themselves direct executors of the divine command.

Now come the directives that form the course of action following the declaration of submission and contentment.

﴿And that you establish prayer and fear Him.﴾ (6:72)

"Establish prayer and be mindful of Him."

The essential obligation is to acknowledge Allah's lordship, to acknowledge His sovereignty, and to set oneself right according to His pleasure. After this comes the stage of acts of worship, and the work of psychological reform begins, so that a picture of practical life may be formed on the foundation of submission and contentment. Practical life and a detailed system of life cannot attain stability unless its structure is built on firm foundations.

The final blow of this wave encompasses the foundational truths of the Islamic worldview. These truths are the original and fundamental elements of the Islamic worldview. For example: resurrection and gathering (al-hashr wa'l-nashr), the creation of the universe, divine sovereignty (hakimiyyah Ilahiyyah), knowledge of the unseen and knowledge of the witnessed, and that Allah is All-Wise and All-Aware.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 73 (part 1 of 2):

(Verses) 72 to 73.

﴿And it is He to Whom you will be gathered.﴾ (72)

You will be gathered back to Him.

Therefore there is a need that you submit yourselves to Him alone, because ultimately you have to go to Him. Hence it is better for human beings to take along, for the Day of Resurrection, some things through which they will be saved. Do they not bow before the One before Whom all the worlds will be prostrate on the Day of Gathering? It is fitting that they bow before that Day arrives. By presenting the concept of the Gathering, human beings are here being motivated to begin prostrating themselves before Him today, since on the Day of Gathering no one will be able to escape.

﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:73)

﴿in truth﴾.

This is another reality, which is another most effective means of reforming conditions. That Allah, before Whom submission is here being commanded, is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth. That Being is the One who creates, who is the Owner, who is the Ruler, and who has disposal over all affairs, and He created the heavens and the earth upon truth. Truthfulness is a fundamental element in the creation of the cosmos, and it is a reality. In this phrase, on one hand, the Platonic idealistic theory about this cosmos is refuted, which said that this cosmos is an illusion and has no existence. On the other hand, it establishes that truth possesses reality within itself and is the fundamental element of this cosmos. Those who take refuge in truth, the nature of the cosmos turns towards truth in the same way. Thus the natural truth of this cosmos and the truth of the Islamic conception of life together become a terrifying and great power. Then before this great power, falsehood cannot even stand on its feet, because the roots of falsehood are not within this cosmos. Its example is like an evil tree which can easily be uprooted from the surface of the earth and cannot remain on the earth; or its example is like foam which has no physical reality within it and which soon subsides by itself. Therefore the foundation of this cosmos has not been laid on falsehood. This is a great and effective ideological reality.

The believer in whose consciousness is the understanding that he possesses truth personally and individually connects himself with the truth that exists within this cosmos. (In another verse it is said: "Indeed Allah is the Truth", meaning Allah is truth.) These two truths then attain connection with the Divine Being, who is Himself the great truth. When a believing man develops within himself the consciousness that he is connected with truth, then before him there is no longer any reality of falsehood, even if this false power apparently seems very great and massive, oppressive and dominating, and even if it possesses great power to inflict torment. Such a believing man understands that this situation is extremely temporary and insignificant. Its roots are not within this cosmos, and it will not attain stability or permanence. Soon this temporary state will end, and the circumstances will change in such a way that it will be as though it had never existed here. And when a denier and non-believer reflects upon this reality, sometimes he comes onto the right path and submits before Allah.

﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is.﴾ (6:73)

He is the Absolute Sovereign with absolute power, and His will is unrestricted. Re-creation and changing and altering His creation takes Him no time. Mentioning the power of Allah here has two purposes. On one hand, through it the Islamic conception of life is being implanted in the heart of the believer. On the other hand, for those to whom the call is being given, this matter is an effective means for them to accept the call and submit before Allah, the Lord of the worlds, because the one who says "Be, and it is" is indeed the Absolute Almighty.

﴿His word is the truth.﴾

His saying is also true by which He created the whole cosmos and said "Be". His command is also true by which He instructed His servants that they should obey Him alone and submit before Him alone. His rulings are also true by which He legislated for people. And His statements which give information about the past, present and future, namely about creation, resurrection, gathering and dispersal, and concerning reward and punishment, are also true.

﴿And His is the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown.﴾ (6:73)

And when the Trumpet is blown (the Trumpet means a hollow horn like a drum), it will be the day on which people will rise from their graves and scatter. How will this happen? The human mind cannot grasp this condition. It is among the unseen matters whose knowledge is preserved with Allah. What the reality and nature of the Trumpet will be is also among the unseen matters. How all the dead will rise up we cannot even imagine. Traditions state that the Trumpet is a luminous horn into which an angel will blow. All those in the graves will hear it, and wherever they are they will prepare to rise, and this will be the second sound. As for the first Trumpet, as a result of it all people will die and fall, meaning every creature of the heavens and the earth will give up its life, except whom Allah wills. In Surah Az-Zumar it is stated: "And the Trumpet will be blown, and all those in the heavens and the earth will fall dead, except those whom Allah wills to keep alive. Then it will be blown a second time, and suddenly they will stand looking on." (39:68) The Trumpet and the effects of its blowing mentioned here are such that they are not possible in the circumstances to which human beings are generally accustomed. An ordinary person cannot imagine such conditions, because this is one of the unseen realities of Allah, of which knowledge has not been given to us. Our knowledge is limited to what Allah has given us. Therefore we do not go beyond what has been given in this verse. Nor is there any benefit in going further. If someone speaks about its conditions, he will be like one groping in darkness, merely conjecturing and guessing.

Yes, on the day the Trumpet is blown, the real truth will become manifest even to the deniers, and even the blind will see it, that on that day sovereignty will belong to Allah alone and only Allah will be the King. Only Allah will issue judgments. Therefore those in this world who are rebellious should set their conduct right now, before they stand before the Almighty and Compeller and submit, that is, on the day of the blowing of the Trumpet.

﴿He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen.﴾

That is, the knowledge of the conditions of those matters which we do not understand is with Him. He knows those matters in the way that we know the world of observation, and nothing hidden in the servants is concealed from Him, and nothing can escape from Him. Therefore people should obey Allah and fear Him. This threat, besides being a reality and a part of belief, is beneficial for opponents and deniers.

﴿And He is the Wise, the All-Aware.﴾ (6:73)

He governs this entire cosmos according to His wisdom. He manages the affairs of His servants in both this world and the Hereafter with complete awareness and wisdom. Therefore people should follow Allah's guidance and His Shariah, benefit from the knowledge and wisdom of Allah, and return under the shade of His guidance and mercy. Emerging from bewilderment and confusion, they should enter His protective embrace and His wisdom and understanding, where they will find the straight path and become effective in knowledge and insight.

Lesson No. 65 at a glance:

This lesson, despite its length, is one piece. Its subject is one, and all its paragraphs are interconnected. It relates to the central theme of this surah. The central theme of the surah is that the Islamic conception of life is built by a correct definition and explanation of the station of divinity, in contrast to clarifying the reality of the servant and his manners of life, and stating the correct nature of the relationship between worshipper and worshipped. But in this lesson a new style has been adopted for discussing these realities and topics, which is entirely different from the style adopted earlier in this surah.

Here this subject and theme is taken up in the form of a narrative. But in this narrative all the impactful matters that were mentioned in all the earlier waves of this surah have come in, as we stated while commenting on this surah. For example, in the intervals between different waves, scenes of the appearance before Allah on the Day of Judgment are repeated again and again, and in a very orderly manner.

In this lesson, reference is also made to the continuous caravan of the Islamic call, which, from Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) to Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), spreads along the highway of long human history. Before pointing to this caravan, the explanation of the station of greatness has been given, and this explanation is given in the form of the natural impressions of a complete believer, Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him). The intention is to show that the sound nature is of this kind, and when this sound nature seeks the truth, its manner is of this kind. The correct concept of Allah's greatness is present within the sound nature itself; as for external manifestations, in them, at every step, correct concepts can be given to ignorance only after conflict. These concepts are in complete conformity with the human nature's own concept of the Divine Being. Their foundation rests on the internal evidences which exist within human nature, and which are stronger than perceptible evidences. When Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him), through his internal natural evidences, attains knowledge of the Divine Being, and through those internal natural evidences attains tranquility, the Holy Quran narrates this inner experience in these words:

﴿And his people argued with him. He said, "Do you argue with me concerning Allah when He has already guided me? And I do not fear those you associate with Him, except that my Lord wills something. My Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge. Will you not then take heed? And how should I fear what you associate, while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down to you any authority? So which of the two parties has more right to security, if you should know?"﴾ (6:80-81)

Now the discourse, along with the caravan of faith, moves forward. The leadership of this caravan is in the hands of Allah's messengers. It moves along the highway of history. On this long highway, the polytheism of the polytheists and the denial of the deniers appear weightless. And this caravan has kicked those things aside and thrown them from this highway. This caravan continues on its way. The last link of this caravan is joined to its first link. Thus a unified Ummah is formed. The last part of this Muslim Ummah is following the same guidance which its first part followed. In the formation of this Ummah, time and place have no consideration. Race and nation have no significance. Colour and lineage have no consideration. The only bond and the single rope among this Ummah is the religion of Islam, and everyone has held on to this rope and the cord of Allah.

This is an astonishing scene. Allah, naming the caravan of messengers one by one, then says:

﴿That is the guidance of Allah; He guides therewith whom He wills of His servants. And if they had associated [others with Allah], then worthless would have been for them what they were doing. Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture, judgement and prophethood. But if these disbelieve in them, We have already entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them. Those are the ones whom Allah had guided, so follow their guidance. Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward. It is not but a reminder to the worlds."﴾ (6:88-90)

Following the presentation of this position, harsh criticism is directed at those who claimed that God has sent no messenger and has revealed no book to any human being. It is said that such people are in truth shortsighted and have not gained a correct knowledge of the Divine Being. The essence of their view is that God created people and then left them as they are, handing the reins into the hands of their own souls and their own intellects, so that their desires, their deficient understanding and their rebellious souls may command them as they wish. This view is beneath the majesty of God's greatness and His divinity and lordship. His knowledge, His wisdom and His justice, and above all His attribute of mercy, could never allow such a thing. The demand of His knowledge, His mercy and His justice was that He should send, from among His servants, some chosen personalities as messengers, and reveal a book to some of these messengers, so that they might take the common people by the hand and lead them to God, and remove the layers of veils that have fallen over their pure natural disposition (fitrah). They should reopen the windows of their hearts and sight that have been closed, and they should respond to their call. In this context, the example of the book given to Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) is cited here, and then the Qur'an is presented as a just witness that confirms the earlier books.

This lengthy lesson concludes with a warning to those who fabricate lies against God and who falsely claim that revelation has descended upon them, although it has not. They claim that they can produce speech of the same kind that God sends down, and these claims are of the kind that false claimants to prophethood have always made in opposition to every prophet. Some claimed revelation and some claimed prophethood. At the end, a distressing scene of the polytheists is presented; this is a glimpse of the scene that will confront them at the end.

﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are stretching out their hands, [saying]: "Bring out your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say against God other than the truth, and you used to be arrogant toward His verses."﴾ (6:93)

﴿And indeed you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners [of God] in your affairs. Indeed, your connections have been severed, and that which you used to claim has gone astray from you.﴾ (6:94)

This is an extremely unnerving scene. Upon seeing it, a person is struck with fear. In this scene the wretched condition of those people is clearly visible, in which they appear bewildered and distressed, and their regret and their punishment are seen taking place. This is the recompense for their rebellion, their aversion, and their denial and fabrication.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 74:

(Verses) 74 to 79.

The scene that the Qur'an portrays in these verses is a remarkable one. It is a manifestation of human nature (fitrah). The human nature sees all the jahili (ignorant) notions and the polytheistic, idolatrous beliefs, and rejects them. Seeing these false notions, the fitrah shakes off its garment and sets out on the path of seeking the true Deity. This real truth is present within its own conscience, but man is not aware of it, and the fitrah is not alerted to it. Yet in this search for the truth, this fitrah connects itself with everything that might appear to be a deity, but when it examines deeply, it rejects the counterfeit gods, because the attributes of the true Deity that are deposited within the fitrah do not match with them. When, in its search, this fitrah reaches the Being of Allah, that reality is clearly visible to it, and this gives it immense joy. Enthusiasm and fervour arise within it, because it has reached that destination through proofs that are hidden within itself. This is the natural scene that is shown to the heart of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). The experience through which he passed is described in these brief verses. This is the strange story of natural thinking about truth and falsehood, and it has been brought here in this style. This is a matter of a way of life, which a believer declares openly and does not make any compromise in this matter. On this path he shows no softness towards father, family or people, just as Ibrahim (peace be upon him) adopted this same attitude towards his father and his people. He adopted an unchangeable and wholly unyielding stance, and he stated his position with complete clarity.

(Verse) "And when Ibrahim said to his father Azar: 'Do you take idols as gods? Indeed I see you and your people in manifest error.' (74)"

This is the natural cry that appears through the words of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Although Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had not, through his own understanding and insight, yet attained the true Deity, his sound fitrah from the very beginning was denying that the idols his people worshipped could be the true deities. The people of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) were the Chaldeans of Iraq. They were worshippers of idols, stars and planets. But the fitrah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) knew that the Lord, the Deity, the Divine Being to whom people turn in prosperity and adversity, and who created all people and all living creatures, is not these idols. The outward condition of the idols was itself showing that they neither create, nor provide sustenance, nor hear, nor respond, and therefore they cannot be the true deities. So his fitrah set out on the path of seeking the truth, and he pronounced the judgement that these deities which you worship are neither the true deities, nor are they fit to be made a means or intermediary for reaching the true deity.

The fitrah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) clearly finds this situation to be one of misguidance, and he does not take long to reach the correct judgement. This is the perfect model of that fitrah upon which Allah has created all His creation. Then this is the reaction of sound fitrah when it is confronted with clear misguidance: it immediately rejects it and feels aversion towards it. In the case of this manifest falsehood, the sound fitrah does not delay even slightly in proclaiming the truth, especially when the matter concerns belief and ideas.

"Do you take idols as gods? I see you and your people in clear error." Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said this to his father, although by temperament Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was extremely gentle, forbearing and mild-natured, and moreover he was in the position of a son. But the value of the way of life is more precious than the relationship between father and son, and than the qualities of patience and forbearance. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was that signpost, concerning whom his descendants were instructed to follow him, and this story too is being presented as an example and model.

Because of the purity of his fitrah and the sincerity of his intention, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) became deserving that Allah, the Exalted, should disclose to him certain special secrets of His sovereignty, and grant him those proofs which are the proofs of Allah's sovereignty within the heavens and the earth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 75:

﴿Thus did We show Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among those who have certainty.﴾

Abraham (peace be upon him) was thus shown the governance system of the heavens and the earth, and We showed it to him so that he would become one of those who have certainty.

With this pure nature, this clear insight, and this sincerity in the pursuit of truth, and because of his explicit rejection of falsehood, Allah disclosed to Abraham (peace be upon him) some secrets of the dominion of the heavens and the earth, in which were some principles of the divine kingdom in the heavens and the earth: some hidden secrets of this cosmos upon which this system is established. Then Allah gave him the proofs and evidences that exist in this cosmos. Within his own nature and within his own heart there were also similar proofs and evidences, which were showing the way of guidance, so that Abraham (peace be upon him) would move forward from the station of rejecting falsehood to the level of attaining truth and recognizing truth, and that he would be fully certain.

This is the profound method of nature. The insight that is granted in accordance with it can never become rusty, and a person develops an insight that sees with its own eyes the wonders of divine power in this cosmos. A person develops a contemplation that follows these wondrous observations and eventually reaches the secret of the cosmos. When a person strives in the way of Allah along with this, Allah in return guides that person.

In this way, Abraham (peace be upon him) began his journey through the cosmos, and through this path he attained the grace and connection of Allah. Previously, he was calling upon the Truth (Exalted is He) through his pure nature, but now his perceiving faculty and his knowledge contained the Divine Being. Previously, the awareness of the reality of divinity was in his conscience and his pure nature, but now this reality had come within his understanding and comprehension.

The journey of Abraham's (peace be upon him) truthful and pure nature is most fascinating. Its study should continue. It was a great journey, although to the eye of a superficial observer this journey appears to be an ordinary one. This journey was in truth a transition from natural faith to faith that is perceived and faith that is understood. Upon perceived faith and understood faith depend the religious duties and obligations, and then following the Shariah becomes obligatory upon a person. This faith and adherence to the Shariah is a station that Allah did not leave merely to people's rational journey; rather, Allah established prophethood for its explanation and clarification and continued the line of messengers, so that people would not know faith and Shariah through their intellect alone, but that messengers would convey and explain it.

For people, rather than rational faith, Shariah faith and Shariah proofs have been established as binding. On the Day of Judgment too, the reckoning of reward and punishment will depend upon those Shariah rulings that were not revealed through the messengers, and this system was established because Allah knew that a human being cannot settle the details of faith and Shariah by his intellect alone.

As for Abraham (peace be upon him), he was Abraham (peace be upon him). He was not an ordinary person. He was a friend of Allah, and he was the forefather of the Muslims (Abu al-Anbiya').

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 76:

(Verse) "Then when the night covered him, he saw a star. He said: 'This is my lord.' But when it set, he said: 'I do not love those that set.'" (6:76)

Translation of the Urdu rendering: "So when the night descended upon him, he saw a star. He said: 'Is this my lord?' But when it set, he said: 'I do not like those that set.'"

This is a portrayal of the inner state of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), in whom doubt, and indeed decisive rejection, of the ancestral deities had come to dominate completely. His mind has turned away from the false deities and idols which his father and his people were worshipping, and he is seeking the correct outlook on life and the correct belief, and this has become a great problem for him. The picture of this problem is well drawn by these words: (Verse) "When the night covered him." It is as though the night has enveloped Ibrahim (peace be upon him) alone, and this night is separating him from other people so that he may think in peace, in the darkness of the night, about this problem in his heart, and be able to solve it, the problem which troubles him and repeatedly attacks him. "So when the night came upon him, he saw a star, and said: 'This is my lord.'" His people also worshipped the stars, as we have already said.

When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) despaired that these idols corresponded with the image of the true God that lies within his nature, he perhaps hoped that the true God would be found in the form of other planets and stars besides the idols.

The situation was not that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was seeing his father and his people worshipping stars and planets for the first time, nor that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was seeing these stars and planets for the first time, but that tonight these stars were conveying to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) a message they had not conveyed before. Today they were showing Ibrahim (peace be upon him) a truth which was in exact accordance with his nature, the truth for which he was anxious and about which thoughts and ideas crowded upon him constantly.

(Verse) "He said: 'This is my lord.'" (6:76) Perhaps, because of its light, its brilliance and its lofty position, it seemed more possible that it was the lord rather than the idols. But no, no, even this possibility is remote; it cannot be so.

(Verse) "Then when it set, he said: 'I do not love those that set.'" (6:76) This star or planet disappears from people's sight? It goes far from creation and vanishes? If God sets and disappears from sight, then who is it that manages this universe? A lord that is hidden and absent? No, this star cannot be a lord. A lord cannot be hidden.

This is natural and self-evident reasoning. It is not logical or dialectical philosophical reasoning. It is intuitive reasoning that comes directly before the mind and easily creates certainty. All of humanity and all human thought accepts it, and it attains deep conviction.

(Verse) "I do not love those that set." (6:76) The true relationship between human nature and the Lord of the Worlds is a relationship of love, and this bond of love is a bond of the heart. For this reason, the nature of Ibrahim does not have love for those that set, and therefore does not accept them as god. And the demand of nature is that what is God will always be present and beloved.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 77:

﴿Then when he saw the moon rising, he said: "This is my Lord." But when it set, he said: "If my Lord had not guided me, I would surely have been among the people who go astray."﴾

Previous experience also comes to mind. It appears as though Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had never even seen the moon before. It is as though he did not know that his family and his people worshipped the moon, and that this night was entirely a new night (a night of reflection and contemplation).

﴿He said: "This is my Lord."﴾ (6:77) He said, "This is my Lord." It is pouring its light over the entire universe; it appears alone in the heavens, and its light is also pleasing. But look, it too is disappearing. Yet the Lord of the universe, whom the Abrahamic nature knew well, does not disappear. He was dwelling in the heart of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

At this point, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) feels that he cannot resolve this problem requiring a solution through his personal reflection alone, and that he needs assistance from that Lord of Majesty whom his nature recognizes and who dwells in his conscience. He loves that Lord, but He is not yet grasped by his perception and understanding. He declares that if his Lord does not guide him at this point, he will not be able to find the right path. Now there is a need for support from that Lord, a need for direct guidance from Him.

﴿He said: "If my Lord had not guided me, I would surely have been among the people who go astray."﴾ (6:77)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 78–79:

﴿Then when he saw the sun rising, he said: "This is my lord! This is greater." But when it set, he said: "O my people! Indeed I am free from what you associate (with Allah).﴾ ﴿Indeed I have turned my face toward Him who created the heavens and the earth, as one devoted to truth, and I am not among those who associate partners with Allah.﴾

This is the third experience, and it took place with the greatest sphere in this universe that can be seen, whose rays are manifest and whose heat is felt. This sun rises and sets every day, yet on this occasion it is, in the eyes of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), a completely new thing. (He is now viewing it from a new angle.) Today Ibrahim is examining all these things from the angle of whether any of them is worthy of being accepted as a deity, so that the heart may be satisfied, and so that in the long struggle to resolve this perplexing and bewildering problem, this matter may be decisive.

﴿He said: "This is my lord! This is greater."﴾ But it is strange that this too is disappearing. At this point the two realities collide with each other. From this contact and confusion a spark emerges. Here the sound nature and the Majestic Essence come into contact. The sound heart is filled with light, and then this light illuminates the whole universe. Through it, the intellect and thought of man are also illuminated. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) finds the divine object of his quest, just as it was present in his nature and his consciousness. Its conception also enters his understanding and perception, and there arises harmony and agreement between the consciousness, feeling and rational perception of his nature.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) finds his Lord and deity. Yet this deity is not in the form of a shining star, nor in the form of a rising moon, nor in the form of the sun ascending high; not in any form that the eye can see, nor in any form that a human can touch. Rather, this deity is within his consciousness and nature, within his intellect and understanding, and is present everywhere in this whole universe. He is the Creator of all creatures that the eye can see, that can be sensed, or that human reason can comprehend.

Now he perceives that the time has come for complete separation between himself and his people. The time has come to openly declare his disassociation from all these false deities, and to reject decisively, without any ambiguity or concealment, their viewpoint, their way of life and their polytheistic beliefs and ideas. It is worth noting that these people were not complete deniers of the Majestic Essence, but their situation was such that they associated these false gods with the true deity, whereas Ibrahim (peace be upon him) turned toward the Lord of the worlds in such a way that he associated no one with Allah.

﴿Then Ibrahim said: "O my people! Indeed I am free from what you associate (with Allah). Indeed I have turned my face toward Him who created the heavens and the earth, as one devoted to truth, and I am not among those who associate partners with Allah."﴾

Now, as it were, his face turned toward the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and it turned with such single-mindedness that not even a trace of association remained in it. He made a decisive statement, expressed firm certainty, and finally fixed his direction. Now there is neither hesitation nor confusion. Intellect and perception have become illuminated in the same way as his consciousness and conscience were already illuminated.

Once again we see a scene that dazzles the eyes with its joy. This is the scene of a worldview that has emerged within the human self, that has come to dominate and prevail over a heart, that has become fully clear and manifest, and from which every kind of dust has been swept away. This scene comes before us, and its state is that it has overspread the personality of a human being and covered every aspect of that personality. It has filled the cup of that personality's heart with the wine of tranquility. Now he has complete trust in his Lord, whom he has found in the manifest sense, and that Lord overshadows the existence around him. This is a scene that stands out clearly in the sentences that follow in the context.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) now sees his Lord within his conscience, within his intellect, and within the existence spread around him. His difficulty has been resolved and his heart is at rest. Now he perceives that the hand of divine power is guiding him along this path. Then his people appear before him, challenging the conclusions he has reached and of which he has attained certainty. The doctrine of Tawhid has settled in his heart. This people now threaten Ibrahim (peace be upon him) with their gods, saying that these deities will harm him, and he answers them with the confidence of a firm believer, and he gives this answer both outwardly and inwardly, keeping his faith in his Lord before him.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 80–81:

(Verse) No. 80 to 81.

When the human nature turns away from the path of safety, it goes astray and falls onto wrong paths. It travels very far along those paths. Now the angle keeps widening, and its arms move further and further from one another. The point from which this nature has deviated from the straight path remains far behind. The person himself goes so far from that path that returning becomes difficult for him. Look at the people of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him): they worship idols, stars and planets, yet they do not try to perceive and understand the transformation and change that appeared in the life of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Had they reflected even slightly, they would have begun to sense it. Instead, they turned around and started disputing with Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and began to protest, although they themselves held extremely flimsy notions and were clearly misguided.

But Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was a steadfast believer. In his heart and mind, and throughout the whole universe, he finds Allah, and he answers them with complete inner tranquility.

(Verse) ﴿And his people argued with him. He said: "Do you argue with me concerning Allah, when He has already guided me?"﴾ (6:80)

"You argue with me about Allah. I have felt that He is holding my hand and leading me onto the right path, opening the eye of my insight, calling me towards Himself, and bringing me close to Himself by granting me His recognition. Since He has taken my hand and guided me, He exists; this is for me a psychological and intuitive proof. I find Him within my conscience, I think about Him according to my understanding, and I see Him in the universe spread around me. Is it a matter that exists in my psyche and in my conscience and consciousness that you dispute with me about? When have I ever asked you for proof? He Himself has given me guidance towards Himself, and this is my proof."

(Verse) ﴿And I do not fear those whom you associate with Him﴾ (6:80)

"And I do not fear what you associate with Him."

A person who has found Allah, how could he fear partners? Whom should he fear, and why? All powers other than Allah are worthless, and all kingdoms other than the kingdom of Allah are not even worthy of being feared. Despite his firm faith and his being obedient to Allah's command, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) would not state anything categorically apart from the will of Allah. In every matter he would say "Unless my Lord wills", and he would refer every matter to the knowledge of Allah.

(Verse) ﴿Except that my Lord should will something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge.﴾ (6:80)

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) leaves his support and protection to the will of Allah, and declares that he does not fear the gods of the polytheists even an iota, because his reliance is upon the protection and support of Allah. He is fully certain that no harm can reach him until Allah wills it, and Allah is All-Knowing, and His knowledge encompasses everything.

(Verse) ﴿And how should I fear what you have associated, while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority? So which of the two parties is more deserving of security, if you should know?﴾ (6:81)

"And finally, how should I fear the partners you have set up, when you do not fear associating with Allah those things for which He has sent down to you no authority? Tell us, which of the two parties is more deserving of fearlessness and tranquility, if you have knowledge?"

This is the argument of a person who has comprehended the realities of this world. If someone fears, let him fear; Ibrahim does not fear, because Ibrahim is the believer who has placed his hand in the hand of Allah and is walking on His path. Why then should he fear helpless, present deities, whatever kind they may be? Because the mighty and tyrannical deities appear in the form of rulers whose grip seems very harsh. But before the power of Allah, they have no standing. There too they are helpless. Therefore, how can a monotheist like Ibrahim (peace be upon him) fear such weak and false gods, while those who should fear are the polytheists, who have, without any proof or evidence, made these weak deities partners with Allah, and these are so weak that they have no power within them? It is a most important question: which of the two parties is more secure and fearless? The one who believes in Allah, or the one who takes those weak idols as gods, which they associate with Allah, the Exalted, and which they themselves see with their own eyes have no authority or power? It is regrettable that they have no insight of understanding. In answer to this question, revelation comes, and the matter is decided thus.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 82:

Those who believed and did not mix their faith with any kind of shirk (association of partners with Allah), who did not obey anyone other than Allah and did not turn to any direction other than Islam, for them there is security and peace, and it is they alone who are guided to the right path.

It was this same conviction that enabled Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to refute all the arguments of those who disputed with him. Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) made clear to them that all their arguments were feeble, that all their notions about their deities were mistaken, and that their belief that their deities could cause him any harm was also baseless. It was an accepted matter that they did not deny the existence of Allah, nor did they deny that Allah possesses power, dominion and authority over this universe. Their only error was that they associated their deities with Allah. When Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) put before them the point that whoever believes in Allah alone does not fear anyone except Allah, and that it is rather the one who associates another with Allah who should fear others besides Him, and when he presented before them the truth which Allah had placed in his heart, then he became superior and exalted over all his opponents. Thus Allah raises the rank and status of whomever He wills among His servants, and these are the workings of Allah in accordance with the requirements of His wisdom.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 6, verse 83:

(Verse) "Number 83."

Before we leave the verses under discussion and move on, I think it appropriate to place before the readers some pleasant incidents from the lives of the noble Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all). The Qur'an was affecting them like a rain of mercy, and their souls were being thoroughly refreshed by it. They were alive through this Qur'an and alive for the Qur'an. They kept changing and aligning their lives with its hints, its meanings and its implications. They kept fulfilling its demands, and they took it with the utmost seriousness, the utmost understanding and the utmost firmness. One is left astonished at the beauty, the impact, the practicality and the seriousness of the Qur'an. It is astonishing how extraordinary a transformation the Qur'an produced in the group of the Companions, such that within just 25 years this miracle came to pass, for which there is no parallel in history. This happened because the group of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all) were people of extraordinary intellect.

Ibn Jarir, with his chain of narration, related from Abdullah ibn Idris, who said that when this verse was revealed:

(Verse) "Those who believed and did not mix their faith with wrongdoing" (Qur'an 6:82).

that this was very burdensome for the Companions. They said: "Which one of us is there who has not wronged himself?" It is said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not as you think; it is as Luqman said to his son:

(Verse) "O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is a great wrong" (Qur'an 31:13)."

They related with their chain of narration from Abu al-Ash'ari, Abdi and his father that Zayd ibn Humān asked Salman: "O Abu Abdullah, a verse of the Book of Allah has ruined my condition:

(Verse) "Those who believed and did not mix their faith with wrongdoing" (Qur'an 6:82).

So Salman said: "This is indeed shirk with Allah, and Allah has mentioned it." Zayd said: "Hearing this from you has made me so happy that if I were given as much again as all my wealth last night, I would not be as pleased."

From these three narrations it becomes known how sensitive this noble group of Companions was regarding the Qur'an, how much the Qur'an practically influenced their lives, and how they took the Qur'an: as commands that must be implemented immediately, and as guidance and decisions that must be obeyed, because these are final commands and decisions. When they perceived a gap between their capacity and strength and the required commands, and it became impossible for them to implement those commands, they would become restless, and Allah and His Messenger would grant concession and leniency in those commands. These are scenes that dazzle the eyes. These are the conditions of those who were the bearers of this religion. They were a veil of the divine decree, and they were the group chosen to implement the divine will, and this will was first implemented by them in their own lives.

Now, in the context of the discourse, there is mention of that great caravan of faith whose leaders were the prophets and messengers, from Noah (peace be upon him) to the Seal of the Prophets, upon all of them be the mercies of Allah. This long caravan is interconnected with one another. Especially from Abraham (peace be upon him) to Muhammad (ﷺ), in the mention of these personalities, the historical sequence has not been observed, as is seen in other places, because the aim here is not to state their historical order, but rather the aim is that the mission of all the prophets was one and the same, namely the creed of Tawhid:

This is Sayyid Qutb's commentary on Surah al-An'am (6:84–90), translated from the Urdu.

(Verse) "Nos. 84 to 90."

(Verse) "And from among their fathers, their offspring and their brothers" (6:87).

"And from among their fathers, their offspring and their brothers." And concerning this caravan of faith, comments have been made:

(Verse) "Thus do We reward the good-doers" (6:84).

"Thus do We reward the good-doers."

(Verse) "And each of them We preferred over the worlds" (6:86).

"And each of them We preferred over the worlds." And

(Verse) "And their brothers. We chose them and guided them to a straight path" (6:87).

"And We chose them and guided them to a straight path." Through all these comments it becomes clear how worthy of honour and how select this caravan of messengers was, and that it was guided to the right path. Presenting this group in this manner, and highlighting it in this form, was in fact a preface for stating an important matter. The matter was:

(Verse) "That is the guidance of Allah; He guides with it whom He wills of His servants. And if they had associated others with Him, then lost from them would be whatever they used to do" (6:88).

"That is the guidance of Allah, by which He guides whom He wills of His servants. But if they had committed shirk, all that they used to do would have been rendered worthless." This is the decision on the question: what are the sources of guidance on this earth? The guidance of humankind is the teachings of Allah the Exalted which were sent through the messengers, and among those divine guidances, those that are definitively established and preserved are in the Qur'an, this very source and fountain, concerning which Allah has decided that it is His guidance. And that this guidance is sent by Allah Himself through His chosen servants. If these chosen servants too were to abandon this path and forsake this fountain of guidance from which they take their guidance, and associate others with Allah in ideas, deeds, belief and worship, then their end too would be that all their deeds would go to waste, would be destroyed, and they would perish in the way an animal perishes and dies after eating poisonous grass. The lexical meaning of "ḥabṭ" is exactly this.

(Verse) "These are the ones to whom We gave the Book, the judgement and prophethood. But if these disbelieve in them, then We have entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them" (6:89).

"These are the ones to whom We gave the Book, wisdom and prophethood. Now if these people refuse to accept it, (no matter) We have entrusted this blessing to other people who do not deny it."

This is the second conclusion. In the first premise it was decided that the source of guidance is Allah. The guidance of Allah is that which has reached humankind through the messengers. In the second it was said that the messengers who were mentioned, and those who were alluded to in general terms, are the very people to whom Allah gave the Book, wisdom, rule and prophethood. In this verse the word "ḥukm" (judgement/rule) is used in both its meanings. (Verse) "That is the guidance of Allah; He guides with it whom He wills of His servants. And if they had associated others with Him, then lost from them would be whatever they used to do" (6:88).

This is the decision on the question: what are the sources of guidance on this earth? And that this guidance is sent by Allah Himself through His chosen servants. If these chosen servants too were to abandon this path and forsake this fountain of guidance from which they take their guidance, and associate others with Allah in ideas, deeds, belief and worship, then their end too would be that all their deeds would go to waste, would be destroyed, and they would perish in the way an animal perishes and dies after eating poisonous grass. The lexical meaning of "ḥabṭ" is exactly this.

(Verse) "These are the ones to whom We gave the Book, the judgement and prophethood. But if these disbelieve in them, then We have entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them" (6:89).
