The polytheists, out of their contentiousness and obstinacy, used to say that God had not sent any human being as a messenger, and had not sent down any book based on revelation from God. Yet the Jewish People of the Book lived right next to the polytheists, and the polytheists had never denied that they were People of the Book. Nor had they denied that the Torah was sent down by God upon Moses (peace be upon him). They did this out of enmity and sheer perversity. Their only aim was that, under this pretext, they could deny the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). That is why the Qur'an here criticises them: if you say that God has not sent down any book upon any human being, then why did you not say this about Moses (peace be upon him)?

(Verse) "وَمَا قَدَرُواْ اللّہَ حَقَّ قَدْرِہِ إِذْ قَالُواْ مَا أَنزَلَ اللّہُ عَلَی بَشَرٍ مِّن شَیْْء ٍ" (6:91)

"They did not measure God with His true measure when they said, 'God has not sent down anything upon any human being.'"

The polytheists of Makkah held this view in the age of ignorance (jahiliyyah). In every age such people have always existed, and today too some people hold this same view. These people think that all heavenly religions were made by humans, and that these religions too progressed step by step, just as humanity progressed gradually. In this matter they do not distinguish between those religions which people themselves created, such as ancient and modern forms of idolatry, and those religions which God's sent messengers brought and which remain, until today, upon their true foundations. All the messengers, one after another, remained upon these same religions. Although some people accepted these religions and some rejected them, in later times distortion occurred in their principles and their branches, and people, because of this distortion, returned to ignorance. After this, God felt the need to send messengers to those peoples. Finally, the religion of Islam came. The view of these people is simply that just as humanity progressed, so religions also progressed alongside it.

Whether this statement was made by the ancients or by the moderns, these people have not truly measured the being of God, and they are those who have not correctly recognised God's grace, His mercy, and His justice. The summary of their view is that God does not send any human being as a messenger. If God wished to send a messenger, He would send some angel, just as some Arabs used to say. These people say: why would the great Creator of this vast universe need to care so much about this lowly creature living upon a tiny particle of His creation, named the earth, as the followers of religions claim, that He sent messengers, sent books upon messengers, so that through them these lowly inhabitants of the earth might be brought to the right path? Or, as some ancient and modern philosophers have said, there is no god, no revelation, and no messengers. These are people's illusions, and in the name of religion some people deceive other people, just as today's modern atheists and materialists say.

All these people, in truth, err in estimating the being of God. How can a great and generous Being, a merciful and just Lord, and a knowing and wise Creator leave a human being without guidance and without wisdom and insight, when it was He who created this human? He knows every instinct of his, both hidden and apparent. He is aware of his powers and capacities. He knows his weaknesses and shortcomings, and He also knows well his needs and values. Then how is it possible that He would not establish for him principles and standards by which his deeds and actions are weighed, and by which his good and bad are identified? God also knew that the intellect given to this human is limited in power, and that many factors influence it. It is subject to desires of the self and personal inclinations. It is also affected by greed and interests. Moreover, the intellect has been assigned by God the duty of proposing a firm system and principles for this life, because proposing a system for life is not its task; this system will come to it from God. God has not left the task of proposing a system of life to human reason alone, nor has He entrusted it to that natural faculty by which it is incumbent upon the human to acquire a general recognition of God's being. At times of calamity he calls upon that very Lord, because upon this human's natural faculty certain factors press and corrupt him into disorder. These factors may be internal as well as external. Furthermore, the means of both humans and jinn that lead a person toward evil are many. This is why God entrusts the human regarding the system of life only to revelation and prophethood. He commands him to follow the guidance He has sent down in the books, so that his nature may remain correct and pure, and his intellect and thought may work in the right direction, and neither those influences from within nor those from without, which lead a person astray, may affect him. This very policy befits God's majesty, His grace and kindness, His mercy and justice, and His wisdom and knowledge. How could it be fitting for God to create a human and then simply leave him, to call him to account on the Day of Resurrection, yet send no messenger for his guidance, when God has declared:

"وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا" "We would never punish a people until We have sent a messenger." Therefore, in order to estimate correctly the divinity of God and to acknowledge His worth, it is necessary to acknowledge that He has sent messengers to His servants. The purpose of these messengers has been to purify people's nature from all impurities, and to free their intellect and perception from all influences, so that they are free to reflect purely and without restraint. God taught these messengers the method and manner of calling people, and gave some of them books which exist to this day, such as those of David and Moses (peace be upon them). To the final Prophet was given the Noble Qur'an, which to this day is free from all distortion.

Since the prophethood of Moses (peace be upon him) was well known among the inhabitants of the Arabian Peninsula, and the Arabs also knew the People of the Book, God commanded the Messenger to present before them the People of the Book and the Book of Moses as an example, that this is something you have never denied.

(Verse) "قُلْ مَنْ أَنزَلَ الْکِتَابَ الَّذِیْ جَاء بِہِ مُوسَی نُوراً وَہُدًی لِّلنَّاسِ تَجْعَلُونَہُ قَرَاطِیْسَ تُبْدُونَہَا وَتُخْفُونَ کَثِیْراً وَعُلِّمْتُم مَّا لَمْ تَعْلَمُواْ أَنتُمْ وَلاَ آبَاؤُکُم" (6:91)

"Say: Who sent down the Book which Moses brought, a light and guidance for mankind, which you make into scattered pages, showing some and concealing much, and by which you were taught what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers? Who sent it down?"

In the commentary on this surah we had explained that the view of those who say this verse is Madinan is not correct. They adopted this view because it contains the words: "which you make into scattered pages, showing some and concealing much." We had stated on that occasion that Ibn Jarir's opinion is that this verse is Makki, and that in it there is also a reading "yaj'aluna-hu yubdunaha" and "yukhfun," in which case the pronoun in the third person refers to the People of the Book. Although the addressees are the polytheists of Makkah, the matter concerns the People of the Book. Just as they had practically done, tearing the Torah into pieces, concealing some parts and displaying others according to their schemes and aims, thus deceiving the common people and mocking the commands and obligations. Some Arabs were also aware of these deeds of the Jews, as the Qur'an too is revealing them; so this verse is, as it were, a report about the Jews that comes in the course of the discussion with the polytheists of Makkah as a parenthetical statement. In this way it is established that this verse is also Makki, not Madani. I consider Ibn Jarir's opinion to be correct.

Now the meaning and content will be: "O Muhammad (ﷺ), say to them: the Book which Moses brought, in which new light was given to humanity so that people might find the way of guidance, while the Jews tore it into pieces, some parts of which they concealed and some they displayed, and they made a mockery of the Book of God for their personal aims. Just consider that God is telling you truths about which you did not know, so it is your duty to give thanks for this grace and kindness of God, and not to become outright deniers of the claim that God has neither sent revelation nor sent down any book."

After asking this question, God gave them no opportunity to answer. God commanded the Messenger (ﷺ) to answer himself, and to deliver a decisive and plain word, so that no dispute would remain and no further argument would be needed.

(Verse) "قل اللہ ثم ذرھم فی خوضھم یلعبون" (6:91) "Say: God. Then leave them to play in their vain discourses." God has sent it down. Simply say this, and after that there is no need for further discussion with them. Do not take account of their obstinacy, their stubbornness and their pretence, and then leave them, to remain engrossed in their perversity. This manner of speech is extremely threatening and contains a kind of contempt toward them. It also expresses truth-seeking and seriousness. When people's lack of seriousness reaches this level and they begin to speak such things, it is best to state plainly that this is our path, and you may do as you wish.

Next comes a brief comment about this new book, concerning which the deniers used to say that God does not send down any book at all. It is explained that this is not a strange thing; it is merely the latest link in the chain of heavenly books. God has been sending messengers before this, and has given books to whichever of them He wished.

(Ayah 92) "And this is a Book We have revealed, blessed, confirming that which was before it, that you may warn the mother of cities and those around it. And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are over their prayers, safeguarding them."

(Like the previous Book,) this is a Book which We have sent down. It is full of goodness and blessing. It confirms what came before it. It has been revealed so that through it you may warn the central town of the settlements (that is, Makkah) and those who live around it. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in this Book, and they are punctilious in observing their prayers.

Among the established patterns of Allah's dealings (sunan ilahiyyah) is this as well: that Allah sends Messengers. This new Book, about whose revelation these people entertain doubts, is a blessed Book, and by God, it is truly a blessed Book... It is blessed in every sense and in reality. Allah placed blessing in it at the time He sent it down. It is also blessed in that the recipient to whom it was revealed is blessed; that is, the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ) is generous and great. It is blessed also in its size and its subject matter. Compared with the long books written by humans, it consists of a few pages. Yet in meaning, guidance, teachings and effects it is so great that dozens of books written by humans cannot explain it, even if those books exceed the Qur'an many times over in volume and pages. Those who reflect on modes of expression, on their own speech or the speech of others, and who keep a critical eye on the ways meanings are conveyed through words, know that the text of the Qur'an is, in expressing meanings, an extraordinarily blessed speech, and that it is impossible for any human to speak in this manner. No person, even in the longest passages, can convey the meanings that the Qur'an conveys in its shortest sentences. In it there is a river of meanings, a flood of allusions and meanings, and moreover it is extremely impactful. A single verse conveys so much and so many truths are packed into it that it can be presented as the finest model of speech and writing and as a unique piece, for which no parallel is found even in the most eloquent human speech. Furthermore, this Book is very blessed in its effects. It addresses human nature and human personality comprehensively, and this address is delivered in a most gentle manner and directly. It penetrates human nature in an extremely subtle way. Thus this speech affects human nature in every aspect and every path, and it influences it in a way that no other speech can. The reason is that Allah has deposited in this speech a power from Himself, and there is no such power in the speech of others.

It is not possible for us to say more here about the blessings of the Book of Allah, and even if we continued discussing this subject, it would be impossible for any human to do it justice. Indeed, Allah's statement suffices as a complete cure: that this speech is blessed and contains decisive judgement.

(Ayah) "Musaddiq alladhi bayna yadayh" (6:92): It confirms what is before it. This means that it confirms all the books that have ever been sent down by Allah. But this Book confirms those books in their original form, not in the form in which their followers, through various conferences, presented them and claimed that they were from Allah. This Book confirms the earlier books because the truth it presents regarding principles and beliefs is also present in those earlier books. As for the law and the statutes, the sunnah of Allah is that He lays down a separate law and a separate path for each nation, but these paths and laws are determined in the light of the great principles of religion.

Those who, while praising Islam, say that it was the first religion that presented the complete concept of monotheism, and that it was the first to present a complete concept of prophethood and the Messengers, and the first to present a complete view of the Hereafter and of reckoning, have as their aim merely to praise Islam. Such people have in fact not studied the Qur'an. Had they studied the Qur'an, they would easily have learned that, according to the Qur'an, all the Messengers presented the complete and pure doctrine of monotheism, in which there was not the slightest trace of polytheism; that all the Messengers explained the reality of messengership, and all said that they do not own the benefit or harm of anyone; that they do not know the unseen; and that they have no power to decrease or increase anyone's provision. All the Messengers made their own nations and communities aware of accountability in the Hereafter and said that they would face reckoning and account there. All the Messengers presented one and the same kind of fundamental beliefs and principles. The Qur'an, which is the final Book, confirmed all those earlier books. These laudatory statements about Islam that have been mentioned are a copy of European concepts, and the European concept is that all heavenly religions are developing and have passed through different stages; as nations progressed, the concepts of those religions also kept developing. The fact is that the praise and commendation of Islam cannot be achieved by demolishing any principle of Islam; therefore all writers and all readers should not write such things nor read such things. And why was this final Book sent down? So that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would warn the people of Makkah and those living around it.

(Ayah) "Litundhira Umm al-Qura wa man hawlaha" (6:92): That you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it. Makkah Mukarramah was called Umm al-Qura because in it is the House which was first built for the worship of Allah alone, and it was made a place of security and a place for people to come and go. It was made a sanctuary not only for humans but for every living thing, and from Makkah the call went out to the inhabitants of the whole earth. Before this, the call of none of the prophets had ever been a general call. It is also called the Mother because all the believers come to it for Hajj, so that from here they may spread out into the world carrying the call of Islam.

What is not meant by this verse is what the Western orientalists have derived from it: that the Islamic call is only for the people of Makkah and those living around it. The orientalists derive this meaning from the verse by reading it in isolation from the rest of the Qur'an, and they conclude that initially the Prophet's aim was only to confine his call to the people of Makkah and a few other towns, but later he expanded his call, and after that he intended to take it further. They claim this idea arose in his mind due to certain circumstances, namely the migration to Madinah and the establishment of a government there. But these people have fabricated a great calumny against Islam and the Prophet (ﷺ), because in the very early days of the call, Allah had already told the Messenger (ﷺ):

(Ayah) "Wa ma arsalnaka illa rahmatan lil-'alamin" (21:107): And We have sent you only as a mercy to the worlds.

(Ayah) "Wa ma arsalnaka illa kaffatan lil-nasi bashiran wa nadhira" (34:28): And We have sent you only as a bringer of good tidings and a warner to all mankind. This was said at the time when the Islamic call was confined in Makkah in the Shi'b of Abu Talib and it faced severe hardships.

(Ayah) "Wa alladhina yu'minuna bil-akhirati yu'minuna bihi wa hum 'ala salatihim yuhafizun" (6:92): And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are punctilious in guarding their prayers.

And those who believe in the reality that one day we shall have to give account of our lives also believe that Allah certainly sends Messengers and reveals to the Messengers. Such people feel no difficulty in confirming the Qur'an; rather, this faith inclines them to confirm it. Then, because of their faith in the Hereafter and their faith in the Book, they guard their prayers, so that their connection with the Divine Being is established and maintained, and so that they may express obedience to the Lord in the form of prayer. It is a feature of human psychology that when fear of the Hereafter arises in someone's heart and they become certain of the Day of Resurrection, such souls automatically accept the sending down of a Book of guidance from Allah, and afterwards they establish their connection with Allah in the form of prayer. The human psychological states and conditions that are recorded throughout the Qur'an show that it is the true speech of the Lord of the worlds.

Now comes the final part of this wave and lesson. This section presents a frightening and dynamic scene. This scene is placed before the eyes on the screen through the picture of words. The characters of this scene are those who are polytheists and wrongdoers, and whose practice is to fabricate lies against Allah. These are false claimants to prophethood who assert that revelation comes to them, though no revelation comes to them. They are those who claim that they too can produce speech like the Qur'an. These people are in the throes of death, and their wrongdoing is so great that a person cannot even imagine it. At the time of death, the angels will come with the instruments of punishment in their hands to seize their souls. At that time, their faces will be ashen, and these people will give up their life, leaving behind everything of this world, and will depart.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 93–94 (part 1 of 2):

Qatadah (رضي الله عنه) and Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه) have narrated that this verse was revealed concerning Musaylimah al-Kadhdhab and his wife Sajah bint al-Harith, and also concerning al-Aswad al-Ansi. These were the people who claimed prophethood during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They also claimed that revelation had been sent down to them by Allah.

As for the words ﴿Sanuzilu mithla ma anzala Allah﴾ (6:93), or the one who said, "Revelation has come to me too": according to one narration from Ibn Abbas, this refers to Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh. He had accepted Islam and was a scribe of revelation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the verse of Surah al-Muminun was revealed, ﴿Laqad khalaqna al-insana min sulalatin min tin﴾ (23:12), the Prophet (ﷺ) summoned him and began dictating it to him. When the verses reached ﴿Thumma insha'nahu khalqan akhar﴾ (23:14), Abdullah was astonished at these details of the creation, and he said: ﴿Fatabaraka Allahu ahsan al-khaliqin﴾ (23:14). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said that the verse had been revealed in exactly this way. At this point Abdullah doubted: if Muhammad is truthful, then revelation has come to me as it came to him; and if he is not, then I have said what he said. Thus he abandoned Islam, became an apostate, and rejoined the polytheists. This is the referent of the verse ﴿Sanuzilu mithla ma anzala Allah﴾ (6:93). (Narrated by al-Kalbi from Abbas.)

The context here describes a terrifying and painful end for these wrongdoing polytheists. It appears that these wrongdoers are in the agony of death, and the word ghamarat (overwhelming agonies) is used for this state to show that their condition will be extremely painful. The angels will be stretching out their hands to take their souls, and this seizing by the angels will also be a form of punishment. These angels will extract their souls, and then the punishment of Allah will be present before them.

﴿Wa law tara idhi al-zalimuna fi ghamarat al-mawti wa al-malaikatu basitu aydihim, akhriju anfusakum al-yauma tujzawna 'adhab al-hun bima kuntum taqulduna 'ala Allahi ghayr al-haqqi wa kuntum 'an ayatihi tastakbirun﴾ (6:93)

"If only you could see the wrongdoers in the agonies of death, while the angels stretch out their hands, saying: 'Bring out your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say against Allah other than the truth, and for your arrogance toward His signs.'"

Because of their arrogance and rebellion, they will be afflicted with a great punishment. This humiliating punishment is being given to them because they fabricated lies against Allah. The mention of all these matters creates a terrifying atmosphere over this scene, and on seeing it a person is struck with fear and his heart rises to his throat.

Finally, this rebuke and reproach occurs when they stand before Allah. These are the very people who lied about Allah, and Allah's address to them in such circumstances is as follows:

﴿Wa laqad ji'tumuna furada kama khalaqnakum awwala marratin﴾ (6:94)

(Allah will say:) "Now you have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time." Now you have only your own selves. You are completely alone; you will not come before your Lord as a group, but individually, just as you came into this world alone from your mother's womb, naked and without helpers.

Now all your helpers have departed from you. Every support and means has been taken away from you. Now you have no control even over the things that Allah had placed in your possession.

﴿Wa taraktum ma khawwalnakum wara'a zuhurikum﴾ (6:94) "Whatever We had bestowed upon you in the world, you have left behind you."

The wealth and adornment of which you were masters in the world have been left behind. Children and status have been left behind. Power and authority have all come to an end. All these things remained in the world, and now you hold nothing in your hand, nor do you have any authority over any worldly matter.

﴿Wa ma nara ma'akum shufa'a'akumu alladhina za'amtum annahum fikum shurakaa'﴾ (6:94) "And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners in your affairs."

Those whom you used to think would intercede for you in difficulties, and whom you made partners in your life and your wealth, and whom you thought would be your intercessors with Allah. Elsewhere it is said: ﴿Ma na'buduhum illa liyuqarribuna ila Allahi zulfa﴾ "We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah." Whether they were partners, soothsayers, rulers of the age, stones, idols of trees and stones, jinn, angels, stars, planets, or saints and holy men, tell us: where are they? Concerning idols or stars, they used to ascribe their false gods to them, and in their wealth and their lives they made these people partners. Allah will ask: "Tell us, where have they gone?"

﴿Laqad taqatta'a baynakum﴾ (6:94) "All ties between you have been severed, and those you claimed have been lost from you." All connections have been broken, all relationships have ended, and all causes and means have ceased. Now all your alleged gods and deities have vanished, just as the partners have vanished; likewise your supposed beliefs have evaporated. You see that there is now no effect, no intercession, and no influence of theirs with Me.

In short, this is a scene that shakes a person to the core. It appears in a very embodied and dynamic form. Its shadow falls upon the human soul, and the believer's heart is filled with recognition. These shadows are extremely frightening and awe-inspiring. Indeed, this is the very style of the Qur'an, and a part of the Qur'an itself.

Lesson No. 66: An overview

It is appropriate that the commentary we made on this surah remain before us, and that we keep in mind that the themes of this surah come like surging waves of a river, one wave after another. Its style is so beautiful and so eloquent that, in terms of expression, it goes beyond the limit of what a person can imagine of persuasive speech. We said:

"This surah takes up its fundamental theme in a unique manner. At every moment, every stance and every scene, its style is dazzling. When a person reflects upon it and travels through its scenes, his feelings become captivated, and for a moment his breath almost stops, especially when one contemplates its scenes, tries to grasp its rises and falls, and feels its effects."

"This surah flows with its scenes, its allusions and its effects, its discourses and shades, in the way a river flows with its currents and waves. One wave has not yet struck the shore before another rises. Amid this turbulence of waves, the river of this surah advances at its own pace."

"With this surging of its waves and this collision of its currents, the surah appears so beautiful that a person is enchanted. Along with this beauty, its themes and meanings are presented with great harmony and graceful expression, and its ideas are conveyed in such a moving way that human sensibilities are astonished. Through living, dynamic, harmonious and forceful acoustic effects, it influences the human soul from every dimension and every direction, and enchants it." etc.

All the qualities mentioned above regarding this surah are fully evident in this lesson. The reader feels as though these scenes are moving one after another on a screen, appearing with brilliance. Just as a flood of words comes forward, so too a flood of meanings surges, and there is harmony between the two. Just as these scenes show everything, so the verbal expression clarifies the full meaning and purpose, and both proceed toward their target.

Each of these scenes and visions comes forth from some unknown treasure with great brilliance and charm, and after illuminating the heart, mind, and vision, it disappears.

Then the words and phrases flow as water gushes from a natural spring. The discourse proceeds as though a running commentary were being given on a scene, and the words and the meanings they convey walk together with great radiance.

These scenes, ideas and expressions move in sequence like waves and billows, one after another with balance. The eyes of a person follow them as if dazzled. Before one wave of thoughts and ideas has struck the shore and ended, many more waves of concepts rise. In this lesson, or this wave, all the characteristics mentioned at the beginning of the surah are evident.

Beauty is the distinguishing feature of this wave, a beauty so great that a person is astonished. The scenes in this lesson are very clear and selected for their beauty. Its words and phrases, in terms of meaning, verbal elegance, ideas and realities, are of the highest standard and most lovely. In short, meanings and realities shine like pearls.

The freshness and beauty of this lesson are also shown by the fact that Allah Himself directed attention to the beauty of a scene. He invites contemplation of the freshness and beauty of fruit within gardens. It is said:

﴿Unzuru ila thamarihi idha athmara wa yan'ihi﴾ (6:99) "Look at their fruit when they bear fruit and ripen; observe carefully the state of their fruiting and ripening." This is a direct invitation to contemplate: look at this natural beauty, reflect upon it, and keep taking delight in it.

Now comes a point where this beauty reaches its climax... the person is astonished, and his mind and heart are illuminated. Now this splendor goes beyond the realm of this universe and enters the boundaries of the transcendent, and this splendor, freshness and beautiful expression return to the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Majestic Being. Concerning the Majestic Being, what is said here retains the standard of eloquence. Read it in the words of the Qur'an itself:

﴿La tudrikuhu al-absaru wa huwa yudriku al-absara wa huwa al-latifu al-khabir﴾ (6:103)

"Eyes cannot perceive Him, but He perceives the eyes; and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware."

Now I take up another aspect. In this lesson we read the open book of this universe. Heedless people pass by it every moment, but they do not look at the wonders and miracles of the cosmos with a penetrating gaze.

As for those who are plainly blind, they do not perceive anything at all; how could they see what wonders are in it? But these verses of the Holy Qur'an set us face to face with each wonder one by one. It appears as though perhaps before this we were not in this world, and now we are descending into it. These verses place us before the strange signs of that book, and stir our curiosity toward those marvels over which heedless people of the world pass by without notice.

Now we stand before an extraordinary wonder that occurs in every moment of the night and day: that from dead things, living things emerge in this world. We cannot understand how this vegetation emerges from the dead earth. We find various forms of life on this globe, and we have no other explanation than that everything is occurring according to Allah's command and decree. A human being can neither accomplish bringing a living thing out of a dead thing, nor can he grasp its reality.

Now we stand before the revolution, indeed the revolutions, of the system of the heavens and the earth. These revolutions too are wondrous. The rotation of the earth, which produces day and night, is extremely astonishing and is being completed every moment and every second. Now we stand before the creative human being himself: from a single soul a human is born and multiplies through the system of reproduction.

Now we stand before the system of plant growth. Plants are being given life; rains are falling; fruits and flowers are growing. How beautiful they are and how delicious! Among them are various kinds of creatures and strange scenes. If we look at them with living feeling and luminous eyes, there is a lesson in each one.

Now we stand before this entire universe. Now it appears to us as though we are seeing it for the first time. It is a living universe. It loves us and we love it. It is in motion, with movement and vitality in every vein. It grasps the hem of our feeling and consciousness and wishes to speak of its Creator. In its unique and singular existence, it is a proof and demonstration of Allah's power and of His Being.

Here the discourse suddenly turns toward shirk (associating partners with Allah), and the polytheists and their belief are condemned. This notion runs contrary to the very nature of this universe and the disposition of its existence. Whoever studies this universe, filled with proofs and evidences, sees it as an ugly stain on the mirror of human nature. Shirk, and associating others with Allah! A deep study of this universe completely rejects it, and thus the heart of the one who reflects is filled with profound faith.

When the Qur'an addresses the human being about the Divine Being, its style of argument is this: Behold, He is your Creator and the Creator of the entire universe. On this earth He first brought forth life and vegetation. Then He arranged for the growth of all living beings and plants, and made the forces of the whole universe their helpers and supporters. Allah is the One by whose will and command alone all the workings of the world of causes, and all the changes and transactions within this universe, take place. It is Allah who has bestowed effectiveness upon all the apparent causes in this world. Therefore, you should worship Allah alone. Do you not perceive the signs of nature? Are not the many-colored variations of this world a clear proof for man, that he should worship Allah alone, perform acts of servitude before Allah alone, humble himself and submit before Him, and obey Him? By presenting this open book of the universe for study, the Qur'an issues an invitation: since the creation is His, the provision is His, and the sustenance is His, then the sovereignty and worship are also His, and it is our duty that we do not associate anyone with Him in lordship and in the rights of lordship. Worship is to be performed for Him alone, He alone should be the ruler, and He alone should have authority in all the affairs of life, and whoever claims these rights and attributes other than Him should be rejected. In this lesson it comes:

﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no god except Him, the Creator of all things. So worship Him, and He is the Guardian over all things.﴾ (6:102)

"All these matters belong to your Lord. There is no ruler except Him. He is the Creator of everything, so worship Him, and He is the Guardian over everything." This is the Qur'an's method of argumentation: since Allah is the Creator of everything and the Guardian of everything, worship belongs to Him alone, and He alone is deserving of it.

At the end of this lesson, after unfolding the book of the universe and showing from within it extraordinary signs and miracles, it is stated that those who, despite this universe, still seek further miracles and extraordinary events are extremely foolish. It is made clear that those who still deny do not deny because of a lack of proofs and miracles, but because there is no sight in their insight; otherwise, throughout this universe, heaps of proofs and miracles concerning the existence of the Creator and the attributes of divinity lie everywhere and invite contemplation.
