Among them are various kinds of creatures and strange scenes. If we look at them with living feeling and luminous eyes, there is a lesson in each one.

Now we stand before this entire universe. Now it appears to us as though we are seeing it for the first time. It is a living universe. It loves us and we love it. It is in motion, with movement and vitality in every vein. It grasps the hem of our feeling and consciousness and wishes to speak of its Creator. In its unique and singular existence, it is a proof and demonstration of Allah's power and of His Being.

Here the discourse suddenly turns toward shirk (associating partners with Allah), and the polytheists and their belief are condemned. This notion runs contrary to the very nature of this universe and the disposition of its existence. Whoever studies this universe, filled with proofs and evidences, sees it as an ugly stain on the mirror of human nature. Shirk, and associating others with Allah! A deep study of this universe completely rejects it, and thus the heart of the one who reflects is filled with profound faith.

When the Qur'an addresses the human being about the Divine Being, its style of argument is this: Behold, He is your Creator and the Creator of the entire universe. On this earth He first brought forth life and vegetation. Then He arranged for the growth of all living beings and plants, and made the forces of the whole universe their helpers and supporters. Allah is the One by whose will and command alone all the workings of the world of causes, and all the changes and transactions within this universe, take place. It is Allah who has bestowed effectiveness upon all the apparent causes in this world. Therefore, you should worship Allah alone. Do you not perceive the signs of nature? Are not the many-colored variations of this world a clear proof for man, that he should worship Allah alone, perform acts of servitude before Allah alone, humble himself and submit before Him, and obey Him? By presenting this open book of the universe for study, the Qur'an issues an invitation: since the creation is His, the provision is His, and the sustenance is His, then the sovereignty and worship are also His, and it is our duty that we do not associate anyone with Him in lordship and in the rights of lordship. Worship is to be performed for Him alone, He alone should be the ruler, and He alone should have authority in all the affairs of life, and whoever claims these rights and attributes other than Him should be rejected. In this lesson it comes:

﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no god except Him, the Creator of all things. So worship Him, and He is the Guardian over all things.﴾ (6:102)

"All these matters belong to your Lord. There is no ruler except Him. He is the Creator of everything, so worship Him, and He is the Guardian over everything." This is the Qur'an's method of argumentation: since Allah is the Creator of everything and the Guardian of everything, worship belongs to Him alone, and He alone is deserving of it.

At the end of this lesson, after unfolding the book of the universe and showing from within it extraordinary signs and miracles, it is stated that those who, despite this universe, still seek further miracles and extraordinary events are extremely foolish. It is made clear that those who still deny do not deny because of a lack of proofs and miracles, but because there is no sight in their insight; otherwise, throughout this universe, heaps of proofs and miracles concerning the existence of the Creator and the attributes of divinity lie everywhere and invite contemplation.

(Verse 95)

This is a miracle whose secret no one has been able to reach; it would be a great matter for anyone to produce such a miracle. What miracle? The creation of life, its growth and its movement. Constantly, a dead seed emerges from a living, growing tree, and a lifeless date-stone emerges from a growing tree. Then the life hidden within that seed and that stone takes the form of a plant and a tree. This is a hidden secret, the reality of which is known only to the Generous Being of Allah. The true source and origin of this life is known only to Allah Most High. Whatever practical progress man has made, however much he has studied the outward matters of life and however many characteristics he has determined, at its limit there is a secret which remains hidden. In this respect, just as the knowledge of earlier man was limited, so too the knowledge of the advanced man of this last age is limited. Man knows only the manifestations and properties of life, but he does not know the true source of life or its real nature. The situation is that life flows before our eyes, and this miracle occurs at every moment.

Allah is the One who, from the very beginning, gave life to man from a dead state. The universe existed, but there was no man; the earth existed, but there was no life upon it. Then life appeared by the command of Allah. How did it appear? We do not know. And from that time until today, life continues to emerge from the dead, and lifeless particles attain life through life. This lifeless matter takes on a living organic form, and then this life enters the cell, in the body of man and in the bodies of all living beings. These living particles, through further transformation, become living cells, and after that these living cells die again, because living cells are constantly taking the form of dead cells, until one day that living person or animal is transformed into dead particles. This is the meaning of this sentence.

﴿He brings the living out of the dead, and brings the dead out of the living﴾ (95)

No one other than Allah can do this, and it is also impossible that at the beginning of life anyone other than Allah could produce life, nor has anyone the power to turn dead particles into living particles. It is Allah who turns those living particles back into dead particles, and this cycle is such a cycle that no one knows when its beginning occurred or when it will end. The conjectures that scientists keep making are merely probabilities.

None of the theories that scientists have so far put forward about the emergence of life on this earth is satisfying. Only this theory is satisfying: that the creation of this world is the work of the Divine Being. And in Europe, in the Middle Ages, when the common people fled from the church like frightened donkeys or like animals running away from a lion, those who fled from religion, when they tried to solve the riddle of the secret of the creation of life on this earth, and then when they tried to unveil the secrets of the creation of this universe itself, and did this while adopting the theory of God, all their efforts failed, and in the twentieth century whatever was written on this subject was nothing but a joke, and all these writings were based on hostility and rejection of religion and were not sincere efforts.

Some of these scientists, who were men of sound mind, have acknowledged their helplessness and weakness. From the words of such people it becomes clear how limited human knowledge on this subject is. Among us there are still some people who copy the Western ideas of the seventeenth or nineteenth century, and claim that they are scientists who believe only in observation, while the people of religion believe in the unseen. To make such people understand, I think it appropriate to quote here the statements of some great scientists; for example, some American scholars have reached this point.

Dr. Frank Allen, a graduate of Cornell University and a professor of biology at McMaster University in Canada, in an article titled "Did this world come into being by chance or by design?", which is quoted from the book "Bitajalli fi Asr al-Ilm" translated by Dr. Mardash Abd al-Hamid Sarfan, writes:

"If this life was not brought into existence under some prior determined plan and scheme, then it must have come into existence by chance. What is that 'chance'? It must be known, so that we may reflect on it and see how the appearance of life occurs through this 'chance.'"

"The theories of chance and probability (bakht wa ittifaq) that exist at present are not as they were before. In the modern age, certain solid principles and rules of mathematics have now been formulated for them, and if a matter cannot be decided with certainty, then according to these principles the principles of chance are put to use, and the results that come forth according to these principles are closest to the truth, although the possibility of these results being wrong cannot be ruled out either. It is a fact that from the angle of mathematics, the theory of chance has made considerable progress. According to these rules and principles, it has become possible for man to speak about certain events which are said to have occurred by chance and whose causes and factors cannot be known by other means (for example, the throwing of a flower in a card game). As a result of these investigations, man has become able to say what can come into being by chance and what cannot come into being by chance."

(According to the Islamic conception of life, there is no chance in this world. Everything is created according to the divine decree. "Inna khalaqnahu bi-qadar": "We have created everything in measure." Allah has laid down unalterable laws for the creation of the universe. Whenever events occur, the divine decree operates each time in accordance with the sunnah of Allah. Similarly, these laws of nature are also sometimes set aside, and an extraordinary miracle that breaks the habit occurs. This too is in accordance with a particular divine wisdom, because these laws of nature and the apparently extraordinary are both in accordance with the decree of Allah. Although we have cited the statements of scientists, it is not necessary that we fully agree with the passage quoted above.) "It can also be stated how long after a given event it may appear by chance. After this preface, we now have to see whether the appearance of life on this earth could occur by way of chance."

In all living cells, protein is the fundamental constituent. These proteins are composed of five elements: carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen and sulphur. A protein contains forty thousand atoms, and the number of chemical elements is 29. And all of these are scattered in unorganized and unknown quantities.

(The "infinite intellect" ('aql la-intiha'i) is among the philosophical terms. A Muslim may apply to Allah only His Beautiful Names, so applying this word to Allah is not appropriate.)

To determine the probability of these five elements combining with one another, it is necessary to determine the quantity of that matter and the time period, and that the matter should remain constantly in the mixture containing these elements, and then that it should remain in that state for such a long period that "by chance" the event occurs and thus one protein is obtained. It is necessary to determine how much matter is needed for how long.

"A mathematician of Switzerland has made some calculations (Chart Lezuigen J.) and, having calculated it, he has said that, as a probability, a ratio of one to ten raised to the power of 160 (1 : 10^160) is applied to the formation of one protein. This amount is so large that it is difficult even to pronounce it with the tongue, and it cannot be expressed in words. And for this process to be completed by chance, that is, for the formation of one protein, such a quantity of matter is required that the entire universe could be filled with it many millions of times over; and if only one protein were to be produced by chance on the surface of the earth, it would require many billions of years, and that is 10 to the power of 243 (10^243 : 1). This period has been proposed by the aforementioned physicist."

"Proteins are formed from long chains of amino acids. So the question is, how are the particles of these components assembled together? Just as their formation is natural, if they are assembled by any other method, they no longer remain fit for life, and sometimes such proteins become poison. A British scholar, J. B. Sethor (J.B. Seather), has calculated the number of protein atoms in these chains, and according to him their number is 10 to the power of 48 (10^48). Therefore it is rationally impossible that this whole sequence of amino acids should be assembled purely by chance and become one protein in the world."

"But alongside all these matters, let it be kept in view that protein is a chemical substance in which there is no life, and life does not come into it until that hidden process takes place within it, which to this day is a strange secret, the reality of which we have no knowledge of; and this is known only through 'infinite intellect', and it is only Allah, by His perfect wisdom, that makes it possible for this protein component to become the basis of life. This is the stage of life which Allah made. He gave it an excellent form and bestowed upon it the secret of life."

Mr. Ertng William, an expert in the hereditary characteristics of plants and professor of physics at the University of Michigan, in an article titled "Materialism Alone Is Not Enough," writes:

"Science is not capable of explaining how extremely small atoms come into existence in countless forms, of which all the matter of the world is composed; and thus science cannot offer any reliable explanation of how living beings are formed by chance from these tiny atoms. And the theory that all living beings in their present developed form came into being from earlier forms due to the occurrence of gradual variations and the accumulation of [such] changes is a theory which is not founded upon any reasoning or logic that would give satisfaction; it is possible only by simply accepting it."

(It is also a delusion of scientists that the quantity of elements is not known. The quantity of these elements is also fixed.)

Dr. Albert Macomb Winster, professor of physics at Baylor University, gives one of his articles the title "Science Strengthened My Faith in God." He writes:

"I occupied myself with the study of biology. Biology is the science whose subject is life, whose field of study is very vast, and among all the creations of Allah the most fascinating thing is the living creature of this world."

"Just look at a plant. It is a very small plant. It has grown at the edge of a path. Can you present any of the countless human products and instruments to compare with it? It is a living instrument and it works continuously, day and night. Within it thousands of chemical actions and reactions take place, physical changes occur, and they occur under protoplasm. This is the substance which enters into the composition of all living creation."

"The question is: where did this living and complex instrument come from? Allah did not only make it in this form; Allah has also created the whole of life, and has given it the power of its own preservation. He also gives this life its continuity, and He has placed within it all those properties and all those special qualities by which we distinguish one plant from another. The study of this enormous variety among living things is also a great and interesting subject, and through it the diverse manifestations of the power of nature become apparent. The cell through which reproduction takes place and a new plant comes into existence is so small that it can be seen only through a microscope. What is surprising is that the characteristics of this plant, every vein, every fibre, every branch and every stem, every root and every small thread, are carried out under the supervision of such engineers that all these designs exist within that small cell and remain present within it. Who are these engineers? They are the chromosomes."

I think these quotations are sufficient. Now let us return once more to the beauty of expression found in the words of the Holy Qur'an:

﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾ (6:102). He is the originator of this miracle of life, and the manifestation of this miracle is continuous, yet the secret of life is known to no one. This is Allah, your Lord, and He alone is deserving that you should become devoted to Him, humble yourselves before Him and obey His commands.

﴿Then whither are you turned away?﴾ (95). "Why are you being led astray in this way?" You are turning away from this truth and walking on other paths, although this is the path of truth; it is clear to reason, it is a matter that touches the heart, and it is a satisfaction for the eye of insight.

This miracle, namely bringing the living out of the dead, the Qur'an has mentioned again and again, and the Qur'an has also repeated again and again the truth that Allah created this universe first, which indicates that the Creator of the universe is One, without partner. This is so that people may know that the Creator of the universe is one, and that it is this One, without partner, who alone must be worshipped. He should be acknowledged as One without partner in belief and doctrine, and His lordship should also be acknowledged as His alone. Acts of worship should be performed before Him alone, and the laws and regulations of life should also be derived from His commands alone. Only the legal system enacted by Him, that is the Shari'ah, should be followed.

(This author, in this treatise, refutes the view of Bertrand Russell that life comes into existence by chance and departs by chance.)

The Qur'an does not discuss these matters merely in a theological-philosophical manner. This is a very reasonable and serious religion, and it does not waste people's time in theological discussions and philosophical hair-splitting. The purpose of the religion of Islam is only that people's worldview be corrected, and that they be given correct ideas and correct beliefs, so that their outward and inward life may be set right. The reform of people's lives is possible only in the case that they return to the worship of Allah alone, and cast off from their necks the yoke of slavery to their fellow human beings. Until they adopt obedience to Allah in their entire lives and embrace the Shari'ah of Allah alone in their daily lives, their belief and outlook about life cannot be correct. In their lives there should be no authority of those people who have forcibly imposed themselves upon them, who, in other words, claim the right of divinity and, instead of Allah's right of sovereignty over people's lives, exercise their own right. Thus they have become among the false gods of this world; they have brought corruption into people's worldly lives, and this corruption exists only because people begin to obey someone other than Allah. This is why these matters are followed by the statement:

(Qur'an 6:95) ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; so how are you deluded away?﴾ All these works belong to Allah, your Lord; then where are you being led astray to? In your lives, the one who alone deserves rubūbiyyah, that is, complete obedience, is He. The meaning of rabb is murabbi (one who nurtures), the one toward whom a person turns, the one who is sovereign and ruler; with these meanings, there is no other rabb besides Allah.

(For an explanation of the word rabb, see the Amir of Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan's book al-Mustalahat al-Arba'ah fi'l-Quran.)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 96:

(Verse) "No. 96."

It is Allah who splits the grain and the date-stone. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living. He splits the veil of night and brings out the morning. And it is He who made the night for rest, and it is He who has appointed the sun and the moon for reckoning. This is the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing. (Qur'an 6:96)

Bringing the dawn out of the darkness of night is an act similar to splitting the grain and the date-stone and bringing forth from it a plant and a tree. In one movement the light of dawn appears, and in another movement the shoot of the plant emerges. The point of comparison in these two examples is that both contain movement, life, beauty and splendour, while both realities are alike in their nature.

The bringing forth of plants from the splitting of the grain and the date-stone, when they were inert, and the bringing out of the light of dawn from the darkness and stillness of night, is also a point of resemblance. Both the seed and the night contain stillness. The present order of this universe, with its morning and evening, time and rest, is closely connected with life and with the growing and flourishing of everything.

The rotation of the earth on its axis, its remaining at a fixed and measured distance from the sun, the present size, distance and temperature of the moon: these are the measures and decrees by which life on this earth has become possible, and by these measures and cosmic arrangements human and plant life have become possible. By means of these, the grain and the date-stone have been split and vegetation has been able to sprout.

This is a universe founded upon precise calculation and mathematical principles. Within it the life of every kind of living creature is also calculated in advance. The place and nature of this life is that of a universe in which there is no room for chance and accident. Nor is there any room here for the theory that existence came into being by chance, but that this chance has its own reckoning, accounting and fixed law.

Those who hold the view that life continues in this universe, yet that the universe has no harmony with life, but that the universe is opposed to and hostile to life, are mistaken. This small planet, the earth, upon which this life exists, shows that it is opposed to this life. Some of such people say that if this universe had a god, he would not have become involved in this small earth and the affairs of life upon it, and they utter other such nonsense. Sometimes they call it knowledge and science, and sometimes they call it philosophy, and these absurdities are such that they do not need any serious consideration.

These people follow their own desires which dominate their souls, and they do not accept even the scientific conclusions that they themselves have drawn. The state of these people is that they are not prepared to face even the clearest truth that is against the decisions they have already made in their religion. They run away clutching their decisions to their chests. They flee from the Divine Being, although Allah continually unveils the proofs of His oneness before them, the sights of His power are everywhere and invite them to observe, and whatever path they take in fleeing from the Divine Being, at its far end the Divine Being again stands before them. Thus, bewildered, they run down another lane, but there too they see the great reality of the Divine Being.

They are orphans both intellectually and rationally, empty-handed in knowledge, and extremely unfortunate. These people fled from the church and its god long ago, because the church had made them its slaves. They fled as donkeys bolt at the arrival of a lion, and they have been fleeing ever since. Until the early part of this century they kept running, and to this day they are running headlong, yet they do not look back to see whether the church is still pursuing them or not, or whether the church itself has abandoned its wrong position, or whether it still stands upon that position. Their breath is still short, yet they keep running.

These unfortunate people are wretched, and their misfortune is that the results of the discoveries they have made in the field of science are pursuing them. The question is how far these people will keep running. Frank Allen, from whose writings we have seen extracts earlier, says about the emergence of life in the world:

"The suitability of the earth for life has developed life in various forms on it. We cannot attribute this variety of life to mere 'chance,' nor can we interpret it through agnosticism, because this earth is a sphere suspended in the air. It revolves around itself, and as a result night and day come into being, and in its orbit it also revolves once a year around the sun. As a result, the various seasons come one after another, and because of them the greater part of our sphere becomes habitable. Various kinds of vegetation spring up. If this earth remained in one place, there would not be so many kinds of vegetation. Around this globe there is a shell of the gas ozone, in which are found gases that are important for life. The envelope of these gases extends to a great height."

"This gas is so dense that thousands of meteors coming towards the earth from the heavens strike against it and break up, and these break up at the rate of thirty miles per second. This envelope of gases also controls the temperature of this globe and keeps it within limits suitable for life. Because of these gases, water vapours travel far into the atmosphere, and because of this they turn into rain and bring the earth back to life after its death. From rain we obtain sweet water, and if there were no rains this earth would be a barren plain, and there would be no sign of anything growing or of any other animal life. From this we learn that the atmosphere and the other envelopes around the surface of the earth create a balance within the natural system."

In short, there is now a heap of scientific and rational arguments showing that no explanation of the traces of life and the varieties of life on this earth can be called a satisfying explanation. The factors at work in the beginning, growth and continued existence of this life indicate that this universe comes into being under a plan. Some of these proofs are those which the aforementioned experts in physics have mentioned. Besides these there are countless other signs and proofs, the knowledge of which belongs to Allah alone. And it is He alone.

(Verse) "Who gave everything its creation and then guided it." — "He who gave life and then guided, and who created all creatures, but with measure and design."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 97:

(Verse) No. 97.

This is the conclusion of the scene of the celestial system, in which the sun, the moon and the stars move in their orbits, and it is part of the scene of the whole universe, which is extremely vast and extremely astonishing, and all of whose movements are linked with human life and its interests and needs.

(Verse) ﴿So that you may find guidance through them in the darkness of the land and the sea﴾. (6:97)

"So that you may find your way through them in the darknesses of the desert and the seas."

In the vast distances of deserts and seas, human beings have always found their way by means of the stars, and today too the system is the same. The principles are the same, although the means have changed because of the discoveries of the modern age. Modern instruments have been developed for sea travel, but the fundamental principle remains the same: in those journeys, guidance is still taken from the Pole Star and the stars. The darkness of "the land and the sea" includes both physical and real darkness, and intellectual and imaginative darkness. Therefore, just as the text of the Qur'an was purposeful centuries ago, so too it is purposeful and applicable today. In today's sea-faring life too, it operates according to the same principle. Today too the Qur'an addresses human beings in the same way as before, even though in the present age, in the human self and in the horizons, Allah has blessed humanity with broad knowledge; yet even today our sea-faring life corresponds to this very verse.

The Qur'an still addresses human beings in a natural manner and sets before them the realities of creation. It does not address them merely on theoretical foundations, but presents to them the "actual" form. This is the characteristic that has remained to this day; in this form, as a result of the address, the operation of the Creator of the universe becomes clearly visible. The decree of Allah, His management and the attribute of His mercy appear clearly to reason and sight. Man acquires insight, his perception is polished, and he also reflects upon the universe. He takes admonition from it, and uses his knowledge, his recognition and his progress for the perception of the Supreme Reality operating in this universe. For this reason, after setting before man the fact that Allah arranges guidance for them in the darknesses of land and sea, the following statement comes:

(Verse) ﴿Indeed We have detailed the signs for a people who know﴾. (6:97)

"Behold, We have explained the signs clearly for those who have knowledge."

Because guidance by the stars in the vast expanses of the desert and the darkness of the sea can be taken only when a person has knowledge of the orbits of the stars, their courses, and their positions at different times; and in the darkness of meaning, only those who know that this universe was created by a wise Creator can take guidance. As we have said, guidance here means both kinds of guidance: the physical guidance of sea travel, and also the guidance of meaning, of the heart and sight that have gone astray. Those who use the stars for physical direction but do not derive from that direction the insight to reach their Creator are, in effect, deprived of knowledge, because they have taken from these things a false and trivial guidance but did not take the supreme guidance. These are the people who wish to sever the connection of this universe with the Lord of the universe, and they do not derive from the signs of this universe the guidance that points to the Great Originator. Sadaqa Allahu al-Azeem.

Verse 98.

Now this address is direct, and this touch is given to the human self and the human being. In its reality, human beings were created from a single soul (nafs), because man and woman are one in their essence. Therefore all of humanity is one reality. Between man and woman, life begins with the reproductive cell. For example, when the cell is in the father's loins, it is in its place of rest. When that same cell enters the mother's womb, it is a place of surrender for it. After this, life grows and spreads and is divided into various races and colours. It is divided into different groups and languages, and distributed among different nations and tribes. Life takes on so many forms that they become difficult to count. Then so many cultures come into being that life remains, and will continue to come.

(By "single soul" (nafs wahidah) I have taken the soul of humanity, because I have not found a reliable hadith stating that Eve was created from Adam.)

﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who know.﴾ (97)

"Behold, We have made the signs clear and explained them for those who have knowledge."

Here, the jurist (faqih) will be the one who understands Allah's craftsmanship in the creation of this human soul, and who then has expertise in the cultures and forms into which a human being is divided as it progresses, and in how humanity carries one soul forward through lineage. Through this process, countless men and women continue to be born, and the human population keeps growing. All of this is accomplished through the wisdom of Allah, which He ordained through the system of pairing (zawjiyyah). Through it, the population grows, children are raised within the sphere of humanity, and they become ready to perform the duty of humanity in their future lives.

Here in Zilal al-Quran we cannot give the full details of this subject, which would cover all relations between the two sexes of humanity. That would require a separate book.

(See the discussion of the reality of life in the book Khasais al-Tasawwur al-Islami (The Characteristics of the Islamic Concept).)

However, some mention here is necessary, namely how men and women come into being from a drop of semen, and how an unseen power and divine decree maintain the balance in the number of men and women, so that there is a suitable arrangement for the continuation of the human race and the uninterrupted flow of procreation and multiplication. Earlier, in the commentary on the verse ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ (6:59), we said that within the male seminal fluid there are chromosomes, and when they unite with the female's egg, only the divine decree is at work, which gives preference to the male chromosome over the female chromosome, or decides the opposite. This preference from the divine decree is the unseen of Allah, and in this matter no human being has any power.

This decree determines that one person is given a son and another a daughter. This decree maintains the required balance in the number of men and women across the whole surface of the earth, in terms of how many men are needed and how many women. Thus far, at the level of all humanity, this balance has not changed, and through this balance the chain of procreation and multiplication continues to this day. It is true that if men were fewer, the continuation of procreation could still have happened. But the decree and plan of Allah the Exalted meant not only that the arrangement for the propagation of the human race be made, but also that, rising above the animal level, balance and stability be created in the marital life of humans, because without this stability the goals of humanity could not be fulfilled. The most important of these goals was that children could not be raised on Islamic lines without the nurture of both mother and father, that is, within the peaceful atmosphere of a family, so that these children could fulfil their human role in their future lives. It is not enough that children merely reach maturity in material life like animals. These children can play their human role only when they remain for a long period under the nurture of both mother and father in a tranquil family life, because the human child, compared to animals, remains in childhood and dependent for a much longer time.

This balance between the number of men and women is a sufficient and conclusive proof of how the planning, wisdom and decree of the Creator of the universe are constantly at work in this universe. But this proof and sign is only for those who are jurists (﴿for a people who understand﴾ (li-qawmin yafqahun)). As for those who are blind and for whom reality is hidden from their sight, there is no cure for their blindness. Their leaders are those who call themselves scientists and are not ready to accept any unseen reality. Rather, they mock those who affirm the Knower of the Unseen. Such people pass over these divine signs as blind people pass over things, reading them without seeing. Reality remains hidden from their eyes, and their condition is this:

﴿And if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it.﴾

Now, in the next verse, the scene of life is brought forward, which is visible everywhere on this earth and which the eyes see every day. Within the scope of the senses, and by seeing it, hearts and minds also think about it. Our perception clearly sees in it the creation and craftsmanship of Allah. The divine word presents it exactly as these things appear, and by presenting their various colours and different scenes, it draws attention to them. Different forms and different kinds are brought forward. Human intuition is told to observe the growth of life and to try to understand what kinds of things nature has created. The human heart is directed to look at the beauty of this system as well, and to take delight in it.

(Verse) 99.

In the Qur'an, whenever the discussion turns to living things and vegetation, water is always mentioned as well.

﴿And it is He who sends down water from the sky, and with it We bring forth the growth of every kind of plant.﴾ (6:99)

The role of water in the creation of everything is quite evident, and both the unlearned and the learned, both the primitive and the advanced, know it equally. Yet the Qur'an, speaking in an apparent manner for the common people, indicates that water's role in the creation of everything is far greater. For instance, the availability of soil on the surface of the earth is dependent upon waters. I say this on the basis of the theories that are current today regarding the surface of the earth (if they are correct): that initially the surface of the earth was a ball of fire, then it became hard, so hard that there was no soil on its surface in which vegetation could grow; then, through atmospheric processes and water, soil began to accumulate on the surface of the earth, and after that water continued to play a vital role in keeping this earth fresh and green. Then, through the flashing of lightning in the heavens, nitrogen fell along with snow and rains in a form that could dissolve in waters, and in this way vegetation began to appear upon the earth. This is the fertilizer which man today is producing by adopting these very principles of the laws of nature, and it is the substance that, if the surface of the earth were devoid of it, there would be no freshness left upon the earth.

﴿So We brought forth thereby green growth; from it We produce grain piled up, and from the date-palm, from its spathe, clusters of dates hanging low, and gardens of grapevines, and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar.﴾ (6:99)

Every green plant produces grain piled in layers, such as ears of grain and the like. And on the date-palm, small branches emerge (qinw, plural qinwan), that is, the stalk on which dates grow. Then the phrase ﴿qinwan daniyah﴾ (6:99), "clusters hanging low," is a very delightful and subtle expression. The whole scene appears as though a person were strolling amid green fields and the dense shade of gardens, in which there are vineyards and olive groves. These plants also resemble one another in their various kinds and families, and yet they possess distinct characteristics of their own.

﴿Look at their fruit when they bear fruit and at its ripening.﴾ (6:99)

Look at them with a keen perception and an awakened heart: how fresh they are, and how beautiful they appear when they ripen. Look and derive pleasure from these beautiful sights. Here it is not said that you should eat their fruits once they have borne fruit, but rather that you should look with a discerning eye at how fruit comes forth and how beautifully it ripens, because this is a place for the display of beauty and an invitation to contemplate. Furthermore, it is a place for reflecting, through a deep study of these scenes, upon the signs of Allah, and for pondering the craftsmanship of Allah and His artistry.

﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ (6:99)

Faith is the blessing by which the heart opens, by which insight is illuminated, and by which the capacity in human nature to accept and acknowledge a truth is awakened. The bond of the human self with this universe is established, and the human intuition calls one to believe in Allah, the Creator of this entire universe. Otherwise, there are hearts that are closed, and some people's insight is darkened; the direction of their nature is turned backwards. They see Allah's craftsmanship and artistry, they behold all these signs and proofs, yet they feel no sensation and do not accept the truth.

﴿Only those who listen respond.﴾ (6:99)

Only those who are believers find these signs and indications.

When the discussion reaches this point, the book of this whole universe, filled with proofs of Allah's existence, His oneness, His power, and the various manifestations of His governance, is placed before the heart and sight of man, and the human intuition is thoroughly enveloped by the reflection of this universe. The human conscience transforms human life, and it begins to acknowledge the wise craftsmanship and creativity of Allah. When matters have reached this stage, then the polytheists' acts of association are presented. In such circumstances, where shirk appears strange and unfamiliar to a human being, and in this atmosphere of recognition of the Sustainer and acknowledgment of the Originator of creation, when the thoughts and fallacies of the polytheists are presented, they appear utterly baseless and hollow, and the disposition of a sound-natured person recoils from them. Human understanding and reason reject them, and immediate criticism is directed at these associationist notions, and the atmosphere is fully prepared for this denial and admonition.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 100:

Verses 100-101.

Some of the polytheists of Arabia used to worship the jinn, but they did not know what the jinn actually are. They regarded them merely as a vague, imaginary kind of creature, and believed that behind the idols there was some such creature. When a person deviates from the belief in Tawhid (Divine Oneness) even by a span's width, he goes on deviating until he ends up far away from the path of truth. In the end, a person sees that the deviation from the starting point, though small and seemingly insignificant, becomes a very great chasm between the two paths.

The polytheists of Makkah were initially upon the religion of Ismail (peace be upon him), and the religion of Ismail was the same religion of Tawhid that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had presented in this region. But these people denied that belief in Tawhid. Although this deviation was very slight in the beginning, it led to the abominable act of idol worship, and they reached the point of making the jinn partners with Allah, although the jinn are the creation of Allah.

﴿And they made the jinn partners with Allah, though He created them﴾ (6:100)

"Yet they made the jinn partners with Allah, though He created them."

Among all the idolatrous religions that have passed through the world, and whose nature has varied across the different jahiliyyahs (periods of ignorance), there has been the concept of an evil creature, and this concept has been much like the concept of Satan. All idolaters have always feared this evil creature, whether these evil creatures are evil spirits or evil persons. In these idolatrous religions, it has been the custom to offer certain sacrifices to protect themselves from the evil of these creatures. Gradually, these polytheistic religions began to worship them.

Arab idolatry too contained such notions; for example, they worshipped the jinn and made them partners with Allah, although the Being of Allah is free from such things. The Qur'an here shows the weakness of their beliefs and concludes the matter with a single word. (Khalaqahum): Allah Himself created them. It is only one word, yet that one word is sufficient to make their beliefs a mockery. When the Creator is Allah alone, and He has created them, how can His creation become a partner with Him, and how can that creation acquire the rights of divinity and lordship?

These people did not stop at this claim alone, because when idolatrous illusions begin, they do not halt at any limit, and the deviation keeps advancing. Thus they went further and adopted the belief that Allah has sons and daughters.

﴿And they invented for Him sons and daughters without knowledge﴾ (6:100)

"And they fabricated for Him sons and daughters without knowledge."

The meaning of kharaqu is that they fabricated this belief on their own. Kharaqa literally means to tear, and also to fabricate lies on one's own, as when someone brings a false report. According to the Jews, Uzair was the son of Allah; the Christians called Masih (Jesus) the son of Allah; and according to the polytheists of Makkah, the angels were the daughters of Allah. They regarded the angels as female, yet they never offered any reasonable explanation as to why they were female, because false claims are always made without knowledge, and therefore the claims of these people are also without knowledge.

﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe﴾ (6:100)

"Glorified is He and exalted above what they describe."

After this, Allah now brings forward the real truth in response to their fabrications. He refutes their false notions and shows what flaws they contain.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 101:

﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He has no companion (consort)? And He created all things, and He is, of all things, Knowing.﴾ (6:101)

"He is the originator of the heavens and the earth. How can He have a son when He has no life-partner? He created everything, and He has knowledge of everything."

Allah is the One who brought this entire universe into existence from absolute non-existence. Therefore, what need does He have to appoint someone as His successor? Successors and heirs are for one who is mortal, or one who is weak and needs help, or one in whom He might find joy by seeing them.

Furthermore, these people know what the law of procreation and multiplication is. For any individual, a mate of the same species is required. When Allah has no consort, how could there be a son? And He is also free from these things. There is nothing like Him, so how is it possible for a lineage to continue without marriage?

This is the reality. But the Qur'an makes this reality comprehensible to them and, in addressing them, takes their understanding into account, so that they may grasp the matter in the light of what they observe.

Here, in refuting them, the Qur'an presents only the reality of creation, so that not even a shadow of shirk remains.

That is, in no way can a created being become a partner of the Creator, because the very reality of the Creator and the creation is distinct. And the second argument Allah gives is that Allah alone possesses knowledge of realities, while they have no knowledge.

﴿And He created all things, and He is, of all things, Knowing.﴾ (6:101) That is: creation is also His, and knowledge too is His alone.

Just as earlier the Qur'an, refuting the polytheists of Makkah, said, "Allah has created everything," and through this their notions were refuted and it was made clear how could Allah have sons and daughters when He has no life-partner, or how could any partner of His be made from His own creation, so here the attribute of creation is brought back again, to establish that since He is the Creator, He alone is the deity, and we should worship Him alone, and implement His complete religion in our lives, for the Creator is He. Apart from Him, there can be no Allah or sovereign, nor can anyone else be their Lord...

(Verse 102, part 1 of 2)

When it is accepted that Allah alone is the Creator, the necessary consequence is that He alone is the King and the Owner. And when Allah is the Creator and the Owner, He is necessarily the Provider, because since He is the Creator and the Owner, the provision is His responsibility, and He gives this provision from His dominion, in which He has no partner. Whatever exists in Allah's dominion, or whatever benefit people derive, all of it is owned by Allah. And when creation, ownership and provision belong to Allah, it is definitively established that He is also the Lord. Therefore, it is the duty of every human being not to associate anyone with Allah in the attributes of lordship (rubūbiyyah). The important characteristics of lordship are: to be the sole authority and manager, to give guidance, to be the king, and to be in a position where obedience is owed to Him, and to give a system and a religion which people follow collectively. (See Al-Mustalahat al-Arba'ah fi al-Quran by Maulana Maududi, Amir of Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan, the discussions on Uluhiyyah, Rubūbiyyah and 'Ibadah.) Therefore, all forms of worship, servitude and obedience belong to Him alone, of which the most important are humility and the submission of one's head.

In the days of ignorance (jahiliyyah), the Arabs did not deny that Allah is the Creator of this universe. He is the Creator and Provider of people, and all the necessities of life are provided to all people from Allah's dominion. No one shares His ownership. Apart from the Arabs, all other jahiliyyahs also did not deny these realities (except a small number of the Greek philosophers, such as Kiya), and in that era there were no materialist religions like those of our modern age, whose propagation and explanation are being carried out far more extensively than in the Greek era. Therefore, in the early period of Islam, the gods who were associated with Allah were worshipped because they were considered a means and cause of nearness to the true God. This was one deviation, and the second deviation was that the people's lives were not governed by the Islamic system of life. Nor, in that era, did the Islamic movement face people like those found in our age who entirely deny the existence of the Creator, and who make this denial without knowledge, without guidance, and without any illuminating book.

The truth is that even today, those who deny the existence of the Creator, or insist on denying God, are very few, and such people will always remain a contemptible minority. The real misguidance was, as it is today, that people took their system of life from someone other than Allah, and this is the traditional shirk upon which the Arab jahiliyyah was founded, and upon which all other jahiliyyahs have continued.

Now, does this contemptible minority that insists on denying God have any scholarly proof? Is its denial based on science? Although it claims so, science does not confirm its belief? There is neither any scientific proof, nor is there any proof in the physics of this universe for it. This is in fact the deviation and rebellion that people adopted against the Church and its gods. The gods of the Church insisted that people should be enslaved to the Church, although there was no principle of the religion that permitted people to be enslaved. Moreover, the natural development of the personalities of these religious leaders was also flawed. They were suspending the human functions of man, for example, those people who were given baptism. (See Kitab al-Khasais, At-Tasawwur al-Islami, chapters on Uluhiyyah and 'Ibadah.)

It is a fact that the Quran does not mention the creation of the universe and the governing order of the universe in order to establish proofs for the existence of Allah's being, because the position of those who deny the existence of Allah is so feeble that discussing it in a serious book like the Noble Quran is not appropriate. The realities of creation and destiny have been brought in the Quran so that people may come onto the right path, so that they may enforce in their beliefs and deeds the divinity of Allah, His sovereignty, and His complete servitude, and so that they do not associate anyone with Allah. The situation is the same with the reality of life.

But from a scientific standpoint, creation and the creation of the world according to an extremely wise measure, and the bringing into being of various forms of life within this universe, are realities which are more than sufficient to demolish the arguments of these people. Those who engage in obstinate argument about the existence of the Divine Being cannot bring any strong proof against the existence of God in the presence of these realities, except that they act stubbornly and humiliate themselves.

Julian Huxley wrote two books, "Man Stands Alone" and "Man in the Modern World". This person is among those who deal with this matter with great audacity and stubbornness. This person says things that are merely the desires of his heart, and he has no scientific or scholarly proof for these things. In his book "Man in the Modern World"... This person is among those who deal with this matter with great audacity and stubbornness. This person says things that are merely the desires of his heart, and he has no scientific or scholarly proof for these things. In his book "Man in the Modern World" he speaks on the subject of religion thus:

"The progress of science, the progress of logic and the progress of psychology have brought us to the point where, in such circumstances, there is no benefit in postulating any God of this universe. The natural sciences have removed God from our reason. Consequently He is no longer the ruler and manager of this universe. Now this God, if He exists, is the First Cause (cause), and an obscure or incomprehensible foundation."

Will Durant writes in his book "Manahij Falasifah" (The Methods of Philosophers):

"Philosophy also discusses the being of God, but the God of philosophy is not the theological God whom they consider to exist outside the natural world, but rather the god of the philosophers is the 'law of the universe, its structure, its life and its will'."

Our readers cannot bear such statements, but nonetheless these things have been said.

We neither decide our issues by the Quran alone, nor do we pass judgment on these false sayings by our own reason alone, because our reason too benefits from the guidance of the Quran. We present the judgment on these people before scientists like themselves who have considered this issue seriously.

John Clifford Tran (?), the famous mathematician and physicist. He obtained a doctorate from Cornell University and is head of the physics department at another university. This person, in an essay titled "The Final Result", published in the book "Allah is like the sun in the age of science" [sic], writes:

"Can any intelligent person imagine that matter, which is devoid of reason and wisdom, could create itself, and that too by mere chance? Which wise person can hold such a belief, or can think that this lifeless and mindless matter devised this entire system and these laws of nature, and then imposed these laws upon itself? I think every reasonable person will answer this question in the negative. Indeed, the reality is that when matter changes into energy, or energy changes into matter, this process also occurs under determined laws; the matter which produces these results is also bound by the natural laws to which that matter was bound before."

"Chemical experiments show that some substances in matter are heading towards decay and extinction. Some of them are approaching extinction very rapidly, while others are moving towards extinction slowly. Nevertheless, it is an established fact that matter is not eternal, and when it is not eternal, it follows that it is not pre-eternal either, because there was a day on which the beginning of matter occurred. Chemical evidence and other scientific realities show that the beginning of matter did not happen in such a way that it came into being gradually or progressed by degrees, but rather the evidence shows that matter appeared suddenly. Today science has even determined the time at which matter came into existence. From these realities it became known that this world is created, and since it came into being it is bound by determined laws of nature. Therefore there is no possibility or room for the idea that affairs here are settled by chance."

"Since this material world is not capable of creating itself, or of determining the laws and rules by which the world is to run, it is thereby determined and proven that this material creation is produced by a non-material being. All indications and evidence prove that this Creator must possess reason and wisdom. Reason cannot perform any act in the material world without will being present with it. For example, the system of medicine and psychological treatment proves this, and the being who possesses will must necessarily have its own independent existence. Therefore, the conclusion that our own reason necessarily draws is that not only is there a Creator of this universe, but that Creator is also all-knowing and all-wise, and capable of everything. He has the power to create this universe and He also manages and governs it, and it is also necessary that the Creator be eternal and everlasting, with His signs and indications found everywhere. Therefore no reasonable person can solve the problem of this universe unless he believes in the existence of God, who is the Creator of this universe and to whom it turns, just as we said at the beginning of this essay."

After the time of Lord Kelvin, the extent to which the sciences have progressed makes this argument confirmed in an unprecedented manner for us. Before this there was no such emphatic argument that however deeply we reflect, science would very soon compel us to believe in God.

Another scholar of modern knowledge and an expert in biology, Frank Allen, in an essay titled "Is the Creation of the Universe by Chance or by Will?", which is also in the aforementioned book, writes:

"It is often said that this material universe does not need any creator. But if we accept that this world exists, the question will be how it came to exist. There can be only four answers to this question. One, that it is mere illusion and imagination; this possibility is wrong because we began the discussion by accepting its existence. The second possibility is that this universe came into being by itself. The third possibility is that it is eternal and has no beginning. And the fourth is that it has a creator.

As far as the first possibility is concerned, there is no difficulty in accepting it, except that our consciousness and perception will never accept that this world is mere illusion and has no trace of reality. In the recent past this view was adopted by Sir James Jeans. He expressed this opinion in physics. He says that this world has no actual existence but is merely an image within our minds. As a result of this view, we can say that we live in a world of fancies. For example, this train in which we travel and which we touch is mere illusion. The people who sit in these trains are also mere illusions, and the deserts and rivers through which these railways pass do not exist. The bridges over which they pass are also mere illusions. I think there is no more fanciful statement than this view and theory.

As for the second view, that this world and this entire material world came into being by itself, this idea and possibility is even more feeble than the previous one, more foolish, and even to argue or think about it is folly.

The third view, that this world is eternal and everlasting and has no beginning, shares eternity with the fourth view, because there the god is eternal, here matter is eternal. Now the question is whether we attribute the attribute of eternity to a lifeless world, or whether we attribute the attribute of eternity to a living, self-subsisting, sustaining Creator. I think that accepting these two possibilities does not involve as many doubts and difficulties as accepting the first two. But the laws of dynamic thermodynamics show that the necessity of this universe is gradually coming to an end, and that it will eventually come to an end, and a day will come when the temperature of the world will become extremely low, for example, down to absolute zero. On that day energy will be exhausted and life will become impossible. A day will certainly come when the temperature of all bodies reaches absolute zero. This state will occur after a long time. The blazing sun, the flaming stars, and this earth with its various forms of life show that it had a beginning at a certain time, and it came into being at that determined time. Therefore it is necessary to accept that this universe has a Creator who is eternal and everlasting, who has no beginning and no end, who knows everything, who is extremely powerful and whose power has no limit. Therefore the true matter is that by His mighty hand this universe was made."

The truth is that Allah is the Creator of everything, and there is no deity besides Him. Here the Qur'an establishes, on the basis of creation, the principle that because He is the Creator, it is necessary that He alone be worshipped, and that He alone is the Lord, in all of its meanings and implications. That is, He is also the Sovereign. He is the Nurturer and the one who trains, He is the Guide, and He is also the Qayyum (the Sustainer and Overseer of all).

﴿That is Allah, your Lord. There is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things. So worship Him. And He is Guardian over all things.﴾

Allah is the Qayyum and the Overseer. He is the supreme Sustainer and Administrator not only of human beings but of the entire universe, because He is the Creator of all. The purpose of mentioning this principle of creation here is exactly this. The polytheists of Makkah, even in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), did not deny that Allah is the Creator. But they did not give the Creator His due in His creation. That is, they did not acknowledge Allah's sovereignty, did not submit before Him, and did not adopt the system of life He has prescribed for their whole lives.

These people speak with great certainty, but human knowledge itself does not accept this. Moreover, the dynamic laws of thermodynamics are not final. Rather, they are only one of the various theories about the explanation of the universe. It is possible that this theory may be amended, and it is also possible that it may be entirely refuted. It is not our habit to argue for the soundness of Islam from the principles of science, nor do we regard science as a confirmer of Islam. We do not argue for the soundness of Islam from the principles of those people, nor do we regard science as a confirmer of Islam. We present these scientific evidences to those people who regard only science as their god. It is as if these statements are the statements of those gods in whom Julian Huxley believes.

After this, a description of Allah's attributes is presented here. It is a description that sheds light on every aspect of the subject, and I do not think any human language could describe Allah in such a manner. Therefore, we should look at the Qur'an as it is, without commentary, so that it may throw light on the Divine Being in a most clear and transparent manner, and depict the scene in which a most great and terrifying reality is hidden, so that a person may be fully satisfied regarding the attributes of the Divine, and his conscience may be enlightened.

(Verse) 103.

Those who, out of their simplemindedness, demanded that they should see Allah are like some other people who, because of their corrupt nature, present material proofs for the existence of the Divine Being. Both kinds of people, in reality, do not understand what they are saying.

The truth is that human sight, human senses, and human intellectual perception have all been given to man only so that he may arrange his affairs in relation to this universe, discharge the responsibilities of the office of vicegerency (khilafah) on this earth, and seek out, within the pages of this created universe, the signs that point to the existence of the Divine Being. As for the reality of the Divine Being's essence, they lack the faculty through which they could perceive it, for a created and mortal existence does not have the capacity to perceive the eternal and everlasting Being. Furthermore, it should also be kept in mind that for the discharge of man's responsibilities on this earth, there is no need for the sight of the Divine Being. As far as human duties here are concerned, man has been given adequate capacity for their fulfilment.

It is possible for a person to understand the simplemindedness of earlier people, but he may err in understanding the corrupt nature of those who came in the last era. These people speak of the atom and electricity, of protons and neutrons, yet none of them in their lifetime has seen an atom, any electricity, any neutron, or any proton, because the telescope for observing the nature of life has not yet come into existence. For these scientists, these matters are nonetheless accepted, and they posit their existence, because they have determined certain effects of these things. When those effects are found, these people become convinced that they exist, and that the universe exists, although it is merely a possibility that the universe is as they have supposed it to be. Yet when it is said to them that Allah exists, because His signs exist, and these signs prove that Allah exists, then these people begin disputation and contention about the existence of the Divine Being, without knowledge, without guidance, without insight, and without any illuminating Book. On the contrary, for the existence of Allah they demand such a proof that eyes could see Allah. The wonders of life on this earth evidently are not sufficient for them, although they are sufficient proof of the existence of the Divine Being.

After the statement of the cosmic proofs, which are scattered across the pages of this open book of the universe and are also present within human souls, and after the statement that:

﴿Vision cannot grasp Him, but He grasps vision, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ (103)

"Eyes cannot reach Him, and He reaches the eyes; He is the Most Subtle, the All-Aware."

Now, after this beautiful description of the attributes of Allah, the discourse proceeds thus.

(Verse) "Number 104."

This that is coming from Allah is the light of insight (basirah). Insight guides a person and shows the way. It is itself pure light. Therefore whoever looks at it will see clearly, and whoever closes his eyes will be blind. After these insights and lights have come, only the blind can remain deprived: the one whose senses are not working, whose door of consciousness is shut, whose conscience is blind.

After this, the Prophet ﷺ is commanded to declare his disassociation in this way: that I have not been appointed as a guardian and keeper over you. (Verse) "Wa ma ana alaykum bihafeez" (6:104), "I have not been appointed a keeper over you."

Here there is a remarkable coherence in the expression. When describing the attributes of Allah it was said:

(Verse) "La tudrikuhu al-absar wa huwa yudrik al-absar wa huwa al-latif al-khabir" (6:103)

"Eyesight cannot grasp Him, and He grasps eyesight. He is the most subtle, the all-aware."

(Verse) "Qad ja'akum basa'ir min rabbikum; faman absara fali-nafsihi wa man 'amiya fa-alayha" (6:104)

"Behold, there have come to you from your Lord lights of insight. Now whoever uses his sight will benefit himself, and whoever becomes blind will suffer harm himself."

In one place "absar" (eyesight) is paired with "basa'ir" (insights), and in another "basir" (seeing) is paired with "'amy" (blind). This is an excellent choice of words in the Arabic style.

After this, the address turns toward the Holy Prophet ﷺ, and it is explained that the mode of speech adopted in the Qur'an is not of a kind that could be produced by an unlettered person, and from which the people of insight would themselves conclude that it is certainly the Word of Allah. But the polytheists did not deny it because they lacked convincing proofs; rather they resorted to pretexts. That is why they used to say that Muhammad ﷺ was learning this great knowledge and eloquent speech from some People of the Book. Yet they knew that the People of the Book at that time had neither this message nor this sublime speech. Therefore the Prophet ﷺ is instructed to turn away from the polytheists and to continue following the commands of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 105:

(Verses) "No. 105 to 107."

Allah explains His verses in such a manner that neither did the Arabs have this style, nor were they capable of it, because it was not derived from their society. Neither did this message and this speech exist with the whole of humanity at that time, and therefore two results emerged from this speech.

"Those who did not want guidance at all, who had no interest in this message and knowledge, did not even try to reach the truth. The lofty station from which Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ) addressed them, they would present as a justification for their denial and lack of interest, because they knew Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ) well. This fact was also before them: the lofty speech that Muhammad presented was not his own. Whatever he was saying, they considered this excuse to be contrived, because they knew the Messenger (ﷺ) well, both before prophethood and after it. That is why they said: "O Muhammad, you have learned this speech from the People of the Book." Yet the People of the Book themselves did not have this message or this style of speech. The books of the People of the Book, which they read and which were in their possession, and which are still with us today, are miles and leagues apart from the message and speech of the Qur'an. What speech they have is merely the disordered historical narratives of the prophets, the history and stories of earlier kings, and these were authored by unknown persons. This is the matter of the Old Covenant. As for the books of the New Covenant, namely the Gospels, they contain nothing but the narrations of the disciples of Hadrat Masih (peace be upon him). Moreover, these too were compiled several years after his departure. Afterwards, various councils of the Christians made many changes to them, and these changes continued for years, to the extent that even moral teachings and spiritual guidance could not escape this distortion and alteration. These were the things that the People of the Book possessed at that time. Comparative studies have also been made of them against the Holy Qur'an, but in the age of ignorance, what other excuse did the polytheists have? It is surprising that the orientalists and so-called Muslims of our age also say such things. They call it scholarly research, claiming that it is the truth, and about them Allah says:

(Verse) "وَلِنُبَيِّنَهُ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ" (105)

"And We make it clear for a people who have knowledge."

After this, the command comes that those who have seeing eyes and know, and those who are blind and deaf, there must be complete separation between them.

Allah commands His Prophet (ﷺ): now that Allah has explained His verses in an elevated style, and as a result people have divided into two groups, you were commanded to follow the revelation that comes to you and to leave the polytheists aside. Now you should not converse with them at all, and should not pay attention to the base talk they engage in. Do not care about their contentious disputes, their denial of you, and their enmity toward you. For you there is now only one path: that you walk on the way of Allah, shape your life in accordance with it, and set the lives of your companions right in accordance with it. You are not responsible for the polytheists, and when you follow the revelation of your Lord, the responsibility of the servants will not rest upon you.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 106–107:

"O Prophet (ﷺ), follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord. There is no god but Him, and turn away from the polytheists." (6:106)

If it had been Allah's will to compel them to guidance, He would have made it obligatory upon them. Had Allah wished to create them upon guidance from the very beginning, like the angels, He would have done so. But Allah created man in this manner and placed within him the capacity for both guidance and misguidance, and left him free to choose whether he takes the path of guidance or of error. Then, whatever path he adopts, he will receive its reward or punishment. All of this happens within the sphere of Allah's will, beyond which nothing can go. However, Allah does not compel any person to guidance or to misguidance. He has done this because of His wisdom, the knowledge of which belongs to Him alone, so that man may perform the role assigned to him in this universe, according to his abilities and capacities.

"Had Allah willed, they would not have associated others with Him." (6:107) That is, if Allah had willed, He could have arranged matters so that these people would not commit shirk. Therefore, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is not accountable for their deeds. Allah has not appointed you as a guardian or custodian over the deeds of people. That task belongs to Allah alone.

This guidance sets the bounds of duty for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his rightly-guided caliphs, and all those who come after him, in every age, every nation, and every society.

It is not appropriate for a caller to Islam to dedicate his call, his heart, and his activities solely to those who deviate and oppose, when their hearts and minds are not open to accepting the call, its arguments, or the evidence of truth. The caller should keep his heart open and confine his hopes and activities to those who are ready to accept the call. Such people deserve to have their character built in the light of the principles of the religion, that is, in the light of the Islamic outlook on life. There is a need to instill in their hearts a deep conception of this universe and of worldly life in the light of the Islamic outlook on life. Likewise, such people deserve to have their morals and conduct properly reformed, and then a society of such individuals should be formed, founded upon this creed and outlook on life. This work is so weighty that it requires tremendous struggle, and it deserves continuous effort. As for those who have lined up in opposition to the call, they deserve to be left aside after the call has been given to them. When truth gains strength and prevails, Allah's practice is that truth attacks falsehood and falsehood is destroyed. What is needed is that the truth remain present; when the truth exists in its complete form, falsehood becomes weak against it and its days are numbered.

After commanding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to turn away from the polytheists, the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims were instructed that this turning away and disregard should be carried out in a most courteous and dignified manner. For example, they should not revile the deities of the polytheists, because in response they might insult Allah's majesty, since they have no knowledge of the exalted glory of Allah, may He be glorified. Thus the Muslims would revile their deities, which are worthless, and in return they would revile the exalted deity of the Muslims.

(Verse 108)

Allah has so created people that whoever among them performs any deed does so considering it good, and he defends his conduct. If he is acting upon good deeds, he still considers them good; if he is acting upon evil deeds, he still considers them good and defends them. If he is on the right path, he still regards it as good; and if he is on the path of misguidance, he still regards it as good. This is the nature and disposition of man. The polytheists of Makkah associated others with Allah, although they acknowledged that Allah alone is the Creator and the Provider. If the idols they had set up as partners were reviled by the Muslims, they would rise in defence of their idols and revile Allah, the Lord of Honour and Majesty. Therefore the Muslims were directed to leave them to their own state.

﴿Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.﴾

A believer whose heart is at peace with the Islamic religion, and who is certain that the religion he follows is the truth, has a tranquil heart, and he does not pursue matters from which no benefit comes, for reviling the idols adds nothing to the faith and certainty of the believers. It can only result in increased enmity in the hearts of the opponents. So what concern can the People of Faith have with this fruitless pursuit? Yes, there is the danger that in response, the People of Faith may hear from the opponents words they do not like, namely insolence against the Lord of Majesty.

Now this lesson is coming to its close. Throughout this lesson, Allah has presented proofs and evidences which are abundantly present in every moment of night and day for those with seeing eyes. The lesson concludes with the statement that these opponents swear by Allah that if a supernatural material miracle like that of the earlier messengers came before them, they would surely believe. Upon hearing this sworn declaration, some sincere believers proposed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he should supplicate to Allah for the occurrence of such a miracle. In response to this proposal, Allah gives a decisive answer: look, you do not even know the reality of these deniers and of their denial.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 109–110:

(Verse) "No. 109 to 110."

A heart that does not acknowledge the signs and proofs scattered throughout this universe, especially after the explanation and exhortation which this Book has presented in an incomparable manner, and the signs of God present in this universe and within the human soul itself fail to draw its attention, and it does not hasten back to its Lord, then such a heart is certainly an incurable heart. These people have rejected faith from the very beginning. So as for those Muslims who make requests to the Messenger of God ﷺ, asking that he pray to Allah for the manifestation of such miracles, there is no guarantee that they will not deny again after the miracle has appeared. Allah alone knows the condition of their hearts, and He knows it perfectly. It is the will of Allah that these people remain drowned in their rebellion, because Allah knows that the consequence of their denial is precisely this, and Allah also knows that even after the appearance of a miracle these people will not believe. Even if angels were to descend, they would still not be people who accept. Even if the dead were to rise from their graves and speak, they still would not believe. Even if all of creation were gathered and a Day of Assembly were established before them, and all of this creation invited them to faith, they would still not be people who accept. They will not believe until the will of Allah compels them to faith. And the will of Allah does not compel anyone, because people do not wish to come toward it. This is the psychological reality which many callers to truth forget. It is not the case that there is a lack of arguments and proofs before the people of misguidance; rather, they are sick in their hearts. Their nature has been rendered inoperative and their conscience has become corrupt. The truth is that guidance falls to the lot of those who turn toward it and strive to attain it. Butgram, 12 December 1990, 12:49 noon.
