Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 111 (part 1 of 4):

Para No. 8 at a Glance:
This para has two parts. The first part contains the remaining portion of Surah al-An'am, the first portion of which was in the seventh para. The second part comprises Surah al-A'raf. We introduced Surah al-An'am in the seventh para. We wish to recall a part of that introduction here as well, to refresh the readers' memory. As for Surah al-A'raf, its complete introduction will be given at its beginning, Allah willing!

This portion of Surah al-An'am also moves forward along the same pattern which we explained at the beginning of Surah al-An'am, that is, in the seventh para. Brief indications in a few sentences will suffice here. The following sentences of the introduction of this surah in the seventh para are worth bringing back to mind:

"This surah, taken as a whole, deals with the reality of divinity. In the sphere of this entire universe and also in the sphere of human life, in the sphere of the human self and conscience, and also in the sphere of the unknown secrets of this visible universe, and within the sphere of the unknown secrets of the unseen world, it presents the concept of the sovereignty of God, and in the mutual conflict of those who pass away and in the succession of those who take their place, it shows some colors of the sovereignty of God. In short, while casting a glance upon this universe, the theme of this surah is the sovereignty of Allah in the observable phenomena of nature, the sovereignty of Allah in the great events occurring in the world, the sovereignty of Allah in the prosperity and adversity of the world. The sovereignty of Allah in the various manifestations and sights of divine power, the sovereignty of Allah over the outward and inward grip on human life, the sovereignty of Allah in the events occurring in the world and the anticipated calamities, and at the very end, the scenes of the Resurrection, and especially the sovereignty of Allah in that scene in which all people will stand in the presence of God."

"Thus this surah takes the human heart to various dimensions and horizons and gives it a tour of their heights and depths, but throughout the surah the Meccan style of the Holy Qur'an remains, the style of which we have explained in the previous pages. Along with the Meccan style, the discourse style of the whole Qur'an also maintains its high standard in this surah. Rather, in a plain and simple manner, this surah introduces the Lord of the worlds to people, so that people may worship and serve their true Lord, their conscience and their soul may become a servant of Allah, their struggles and all their efforts may be in obedience to Allah, their customs and traditions may be in the color of Allah, and the entire situation of their lives may be under the sole sovereignty of Allah, besides whom there is no sovereignty of anyone else in the heavens and the earth."

"It appears that this surah, from beginning to end, is moving towards one defined objective: that Allah alone is the Creator, He alone is the Owner, He alone is the Possessor of powers, and He alone is the King and the Subduer. He alone knows the hidden things and the unseen. Just as He turns the night and the day, so He is also the turner of hearts and minds. Therefore, He should be the ruler over the lives of all people. The authority of command and prohibition in the lives of people should be exclusively His. No command and no law shall be except His command and His law. The authority to determine the lawful and the unlawful also belongs exclusively to Him, because all these matters are the constituent elements of Allah's divinity; therefore, only Allah can exercise control over these in people's lives. There is no creator besides Him, no provider, no one who gives life and no one who causes death, no one who benefits and no one who harms, no giver and no preventer. In short, none besides Allah can be the master of benefit and harm for anyone or for himself, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. In this surah, from beginning to end, proofs and evidences have been presented for this purpose, and these proofs are supplied through the observations, influences and natural circumstances that exist in this universe and that captivate thought and sight. And through the study of these natural scenes, the heart is addressed and influenced from every direction, through every door and every aspect."

The greatest issue on which this surah lays emphasis is the issue of the divinity and sovereignty of Allah within the heavens and the earth, the issue of the concept of divine sovereignty within the vast sphere of the heavens and the earth and the broad expanse of the universe. This surah presents this very issue, but in an applied manner, and the relevance of the matter is that the followers of jahiliyyah (ignorance) used to grant the authority to determine the lawful and the unlawful in the matter of certain slaughtered animals and certain foods to others besides Allah. Similarly, in the matter of vows, regarding certain sacrifices, certain fruits and certain children, the worshippers of jahiliyyah granted authority to other deities besides Allah. Because of this relevance, Allah, the Exalted, has expounded here in detail the doctrine of divine sovereignty within this entire universe, and the final verses of the surah contain allusions to this same relevance.

(Then, if you believe in the signs of Allah, eat of that over which the name of Allah has been pronounced. Why should you not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been pronounced, while He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except under compulsion? Indeed, most people, without knowledge, lead others astray by their own desires. Your Lord knows well the transgressors. Avoid both the open and the hidden sins. Those who earn sin will surely be recompensed for what they earn. And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been pronounced; that is indeed transgression. The devils inspire their associates with doubts and objections so that they may dispute with you. But if you obey them, you will surely be polytheists. (6:118-121))

(And they have assigned to Allah a portion of the tillage and cattle which He created, and they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "this is for our partners." But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, while what is for Allah reaches their partners. Evil is their judgment. And thus to many of the polytheists their partners have made attractive the killing of their children, to bring them to ruin and to confuse them regarding their religion. Had Allah willed, they would not have done so; so leave them and what they fabricate. They say, "These cattle and this tillage are forbidden; none may eat of them except whom we wish," by their claim, and there are cattle whose backs are prohibited, and cattle over which they do not pronounce the name of Allah, fabricating against Him. He will recompense them for what they fabricate. And they say, "What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females; but if it is dead, then both may share in it." He will surely recompense them for their description. Indeed, He is Wise and All-Knowing. Certainly lost are those who killed their children in foolishness, without knowledge, and forbade what Allah had provided for them, fabricating against Allah. They have certainly gone astray and were not among the rightly guided. (6:136-140))

This was a practical aspect in the life of the Muslim community, and in view of it this surah took up this great issue. In that period the environment of the Muslim community was also overshadowed by jahiliyyah. In regard to the correction of the polytheistic beliefs concerning legislation and the determination of the lawful and the unlawful, the issues of Allah's divinity, Allah's sovereignty, and the worship and servitude of all humans have been taken up here. Accordingly, just as this issue has been taken up throughout the Meccan Qur'an, so in this surah too it has been treated in great detail, and in the Madani verses, wherever the statement of the lawful and the unlawful and the right of legislation comes, the issue of divine sovereignty is likewise taken up.

In this context, the torrent of effective guidance, decisions and resolutions that is flowing forth, and the refutation of the polytheists regarding the animals, vows and slaughtered beasts they concern, in this connection the issue of Allah's divinity and Allah's right of legislation is also being stated here. It is explained that this legislation of the lawful and the unlawful is connected with Islamic beliefs and Islamic doctrines, and that doctrine is the doctrine of divine sovereignty and the worship and servitude of humans. This issue is not a trivial one; it is the issue of Islam and disbelief, and of Islam and jahiliyyah. From this torrent of guidance, we shall here present only a few examples in the introduction to this surah, but their full details will come when we discuss the verses of the surah in detail. In its effects, this torrent instills in the human self the true nature of the character of this religion, namely that human life, whether the matter is small or great, must be resolved under the rightful sovereignty of Allah, and that the sovereignty of Allah is recorded in the form of the Islamic Shariah. If this is not so, then it would be considered that such a person or society has left the religion, or that a person has gone out of the religion to the extent of a partial issue or even this trivial matter.

And this abundance of guidance also shows that the religion abolishes human sovereignty from all manifestations of human life and all affairs of life. It brings these matters, whether important or unimportant, great or small, within the scope of this great principle, namely that the meaning of Allah's divinity is that Allah, the Exalted, is the absolute ruler over this entire earth, exercises unshared control over this universe, and this principle is fully manifest and embodied in the religion of Islam.

The situation indicated in the above quotations existed in the life of the Muslim community, and around the community jahiliyyah also existed, which this surah was correcting in the manner described above. The part of Surah al-An'am which we shall discuss in this para relates to this very situation, whereas the part of Surah al-An'am that passed in the previous para also had as its theme the issue of divinity, sovereignty and human servitude, but that issue was taken up there in a general manner. Now the context takes up this same issue of divinity and servitude here in the form of specific jahili customs, and the connection between the two is clear: in one place there is a general principle, and in the other place its example.

In this para, with numerous and countless examples, certain jahili customs are now taken up: that the people of jahiliyyah had declared some foods unlawful and others lawful. Decisions of great effect and number were made in this connection concerning vows and offerings, certain fruits and certain children. The connection of these decisions is with certain realities and principles which are the foundation of this religion. The great differences and consequences of these rules and principles have also been presented. From all these matters it becomes clear that Islam attaches the greatest importance to human life being completely free from jahiliyyah, and entering fully into Islam, that is, coming under the sovereignty of Allah.

This para begins, by way of preface, with the statement that the will of Allah encompasses all servants, the jinn as well as humans, and that the events of all worlds take place in accordance with the decree and will of Allah. Among humans and jinn, those who are devils and enemies of the messengers, Allah gives them respite and leisure so that they may commit the evils they wish to commit. If Allah had willed, He would have compelled them to guidance and restrained them from misguidance, or He would have guided them and granted them ease of heart on the path of truth, or He would have prevented them from harming the messengers, troubling the believers, and their hands from reaching the messengers and believers. This is because the evils they commit and the harm they inflict upon the messengers are not done outside the sphere of Allah's will; they do it within the sphere of Allah's will and dominion. It is Allah's will that has granted them the authority to do all this: they may take the path of guidance if they wish, or the path of error if they wish. They are, in any case, within Allah's power:

"And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils among humans and jinn, who inspire one another with ornate speech as deception. Had your Lord willed, they would not have done so; so leave them and what they fabricate, that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline toward it and be pleased with it, and that they may acquire what they wish to acquire." (6:112-113)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 111 (part 2 of 4):

When it has been established that the devils among mankind and the devils among the jinn will, according to the sunnah of Allah, be enemies of the prophets and messengers, and that these devils, despite all their mischief, remain within the power of Allah, the Prophet ﷺ regarded it as a very grave matter that he should appoint anyone other than Allah as judge, whether the matter be small or great. Therefore, to accept the judgement of anyone other than Allah in these matters of food and drink means that we are appointing a judge other than Allah in all affairs. The meaning is that how could I acknowledge the lordship (rububiyyah) of anyone other than Allah?

After this it is said that with this Book and this Shariah the decisive word has come, so what room is there for anyone's word after the word of Allah, and what need is there for any ruling after the ruling of Allah? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was warned not to obey any human being in matters of the religion of Allah, because people merely proceed by conjecture and guesswork, and they have no certain knowledge. If anyone obeys them, they will lead him astray. Knowledge of who among His servants is guided and who is misguided rests with Allah alone.

This statement was made as a preface to the command: if you are believers, eat of the animals over which the name of Allah has been pronounced, and do not eat of those over which the name of Allah has not been pronounced. And he warned them that in the matter of lawful and unlawful they must not obey the friends of Satan; if they did so, they would themselves become among the polytheists like them. At the end, these rulings conclude with a clarification of what disbelief truly is, what the reality of faith is, and what are the causes that compel those disbelievers to commit wrongdoings. Consider these words of the Qur'an:

"Then, when this is the case, shall I seek a judge other than Allah, while He has sent down to you the Book in full detail? And those whom We gave the Book before you know that it has been sent down from your Lord with truth, so do not be among the doubters. The word of your Lord is complete in truthfulness and justice; none can alter His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And, O Muhammad, if you follow the majority of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah. They follow only conjecture, and they only guess. Indeed your Lord knows best who strays from His way, and He knows best who is upon the right path. So if you are believers in the signs of Allah, eat of that over which the name of Allah has been pronounced. Why would you not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been pronounced, when He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except in a state of necessity? Indeed, many people lead others astray by their desires without knowledge; your Lord knows well the transgressors. Avoid open sins and hidden sins; those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they have earned. And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been pronounced, for that is indeed transgression. The devils inspire their associates with doubts and objections so that they may dispute with you. But if you obey them, you will indeed be polytheists."

"Is one who was dead and whom We brought to life, and to whom We gave a light by which he walks among people, like one who is in darkness and cannot emerge from it? Thus their deeds have been made appealing to the disbelievers. And thus We have placed in every town its greatest criminals so that they may scheme therein. But they scheme only against themselves, though they do not perceive it. When a sign comes to them, they say, 'We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of Allah.' Allah knows best where to place His message. Soon those criminals will be struck with humiliation before Allah and a severe punishment for their schemes."

After this it is explained that the guidance of those who are guided and the misguidance of those who take the path of error can be completed only when it is the will of divine power. Both kinds of people are under the power and sovereign authority of Allah, and both remain within the sphere of Allah's power and will. It is said:

"So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast for Islam; and whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing up into the sky. Thus Allah places filth upon those who do not believe."

This section of the verses concludes with the point that all the commands and prohibitions which came before, and the beliefs and concepts which were expounded, are all the straight path. By linking the principles of Allah's will and power with these commands and prohibitions, they are presented as one package, which is called the straight path, and it is commanded that this way be adopted, so that they may attain the abode of peace and security with their Lord, and Allah is indeed their Protector and Helper. "And this is your Lord's straight path; We have made the signs clear for a people who take heed. For them is the abode of peace with their Lord, and He is their Guardian, because of what they used to do."

Before the discussion of slaughtered animals and their eating rules has ended, the Qur'an here also mentions the end of those who are devils, both from jinn and mankind, who were then in fierce dispute with the believers over these matters of slaughter. It is shown that the final outcome is in the hand of Allah, and He is the Absolute Powerful and the Ruler. It is Allah who grants the caliphate of this earth to whomever He wills, and He erases from this world, like a worthless word, whomever He wills. Strong warning is given that no one should act with self-will, because the freedom and choice given to a person is not given for arrogance, but to test him and to grant him respite to see which path he takes; and when the respite ends, he will be called to account and will bear the punishment for what he earned. "And on the day when Allah gathers them all together, He will say, 'O assembly of jinn, you have indeed taken much from mankind.' Their associates from mankind will say, 'Our Lord, we have benefited from one another, and we have reached the term which You appointed for us.' He will say, 'The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide forever, except as Allah wills.' Indeed your Lord is All-Wise and All-Knowing. Thus We make the wrongdoers allies of one another, because of what they used to earn." ... "O assembly of jinn and mankind! Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves, relating to you My signs and warning you of the meeting of this day?" They will say, "Yes, we bear witness against ourselves." The life of this world has deceived them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers. Your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware. Every person has a rank according to his deeds, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do. Your Lord is Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of Mercy. If He wills, He can take you away and replace you with whomever He wills, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people. What you are promised will certainly come, and you cannot escape Allah. Say, O Muhammad: "O my people, act according to your position, and I too am acting; soon you will know to whom the final outcome will be good. Indeed, the wrongdoers will never prosper."

Now consider: eating or not eating is a particular matter, namely which slaughtered animals are lawful and which unlawful. But against this jahili custom, the Qur'an presents the foundational concept of the Islamic worldview. Through highly effective indications and various kinds of observations, light is shed on certain realities of Allah's will; certain of Allah's cosmic dispositions are presented; certain principles of human psychology are unveiled; certain apparent and hidden inclinations of human life are revealed; certain realities concerning Allah's sovereignty over the heavens and earth are presented; and all of these matters are brought within what is, in appearance, merely a partial question of lawfulness and unlawfulness. The question is: why has this matter been given such importance? Because it is a foundational matter of this religion. It is the question of authority and sovereignty over this globe: to whom does this right belong? In other words, it is a question of divinity (uluhiyyah) and lordship (rububiyyah), and the decision to be made is who is the deity and who is the Lord. This is why, within the explanation of this partial matter, such fundamental doctrinal discussions have been brought here.

All these same matters are discussed in connection with the topic of vows and offerings, namely concerning fruits, livestock and children, as practised in pre-Islamic jahiliyyah. The reason is that the Arabs of jahiliyyah did not deny the existence of the Divine Essence. Likewise, the Arabs of the age of jahiliyyah would make someone else a deity alongside Allah in equal standing. Their crooked thinking was that they assigned to Allah other deities who were, in rank and status, lesser than Allah, and they would say that they took these other personalities as deities so that through them they might attain nearness to Allah. This was the very polytheism (shirk) in which they engaged, and for this reason the Qur'an calls them polytheists (mushrikin).

Moreover, among the forms of shirk was this: through their soothsayers and their elders they had fabricated for themselves certain laws and customs which had for them the status of a Shariah, and they believed that these laws and customs had been prescribed for them by Allah, and that Allah had commanded them to observe them. They were not so extreme in polytheism that they would attribute these laws and customs to themselves and claim that the right of sovereign authority belonged to them and that they had the right to legislate for themselves as they pleased. This arrogance has been learned by the polytheists of the present age, who say that they can legislate for themselves apart from Allah. This was their shirk, and for this reason they were called polytheists.

These laws and customs which they had fabricated for themselves, and which they claimed came from God, included their laws of vows and offerings concerning their fruits and livestock. These laws were either devised by themselves or devised by their soothsayers and elders. In any case, they were such that "what was for their associates did not reach Allah's share, and what was for Allah did reach their associates' shares." For example, they would vow a portion of their children, and thus, according to the laws they had made, they would kill their daughters.

Among these laws was one by which they would forbid certain crops, fruits and livestock, saying that their use would be lawful only for those whom Allah permits; yet they themselves declared these things forbidden, and they themselves determined who was entitled to their use. Some laws were such that they forbade riding certain livestock, such as the bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah and ha'm (see Surah al-Ma'idah).

Another law was that they would reserve certain offspring of livestock for men and forbid them to women, unless the young was born dead, in which case both would share in it. These people would declare one thing unlawful and another lawful. Another law was that they would declare carrion lawful, saying that it had been slaughtered by Allah Himself.

Islam launches an open assault upon all these things. In this critical assault, fundamental doctrinal decisions are made. Concerning these particular laws and matters, the Qur'an presents highly effective realities and evidences, which it brings throughout this entire period on the subject of faith and polytheism, because these particular matters are also connected with the fundamental principles of shirk and faith. These particular matters are those upon which the principles of faith and polytheism are applied and implemented.

Upon studying this critical assault, we find that these matters are not merely partial questions but foundational questions of this religion. They are connected with doctrines. These laws and customs were made attractive to these polytheists by those whom they associate with Allah. These associates ruin the lives of these polytheists and render the religion doubtful for them. This religious deception and the ruin of life are linked to each other: either people will follow the Shariah, and in that case their life will be sound and secure; or they will follow a shariah contrary to the Islamic Shariah, and in that case they will find no straight path, and their life will be in danger. Allah says:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 111 (part 3 of 4):

﴿Thus has their associate-gods made fair-seeming to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, to bring them to ruin and to confuse them about their religion.﴾ (6:137)

During this critical campaign it becomes clear that behind every deviation from the Divine Law there is always a satanic plot. Whenever a people abandons the Shariah, whoever they then obey will be God's associates. The essential element of this campaign is that Satan is the open enemy of man, and when his plot succeeds he leads such polytheists towards ruin and a destructive loss.

﴿Eat of what God has provided for you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ (6:142)

This campaign shows that to determine what is lawful and unlawful through any source other than the Islamic Shariah is plain shirk (association of partners with God), and this shirk is equal to manifest shirk. Yet in every age polytheists have claimed that they are compelled to commit shirk, for otherwise how could they oppose God's irresistible power? In fact, God's will was that He made every human being free to a certain degree, and as a consequence of this freedom He made trial inevitable for them. Therefore God has not compelled anyone to commit shirk. In any case, they are under trial, and their trial is taking place within the sphere of God's power.

﴿Those who associate others with God will say: "If God had willed, we would not have associated anyone with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have declared anything unlawful." Likewise did those before them deny the truth, until they tasted Our punishment. Say: "Have you any knowledge that you can bring forth to us? You follow only conjecture, and you merely guess."﴾ (6:148)

Say further: ﴿The final argument belongs to God. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.﴾

Now, after this, we are presented with a scene of demanding proof and testimony. They are asked to produce proof for their claim that God has made certain things unlawful, and to bring witnesses for it. This brings the mind to the fact that at the beginning of this Surah too, proof and testimony were demanded from them on the question of God's sovereignty, because the authority of God's sovereignty and the authority to determine what is lawful and unlawful are inseparably linked. The power to determine lawful and unlawful is one of the most exclusive attributes of God's sovereignty. And this is the real question.

﴿Say: "Bring your witnesses who will testify that God has forbidden this." If they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who have denied Our signs and who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾ (6:150)

Here the word ﴿ya'dilūn﴾ (يعدلون, "they ascribe equals") draws the mind to the use of this same word at the beginning of this Surah, when discussing the doctrine of Tawhid (Divine Oneness). There too the polytheists were told that they ascribe equals to God. (For ﴿ya'dilūn﴾, see Surah al-An'am, verse 1.)

This campaign then concludes with the final decision that the legislation regarding livestock, their young and fruits, which God has determined, is the Straight Path. This same manner of discourse was adopted earlier when the topics of the lawfulness and unlawfulness of slaughtered animals were discussed, and this same manner was adopted at the beginning of this Surah when the subject of Divinity was explained.

﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it. And do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way. This He has enjoined upon you, that you may become righteous.﴾ (6:153)

The matter does not end with the passages we have pointed out. Beyond them it is shown that before this, Moses (peace be upon him) also brought a Book for his people, containing the details of all matters. It was guidance and mercy, and the purpose of that Book was that people should believe in accountability on the Day of Resurrection. The purpose of this Book too is that Muslims obey it and adopt an attitude of God-fearing piety, so that God's mercies descend upon them, and so that they cannot say that God sent detailed books to the Jews and Christians but sent no Book to us containing detailed guidance for us, so that they would know what the commands of the Shariah are, and that the matters told to them as Shariah are not the Shariah but mere fabrication.

After this, a threatening warning is addressed to those who do not believe in the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and who remain upon the jahili (pre-Islamic ignorance) system which they call "from God." Their claim is a plain fabrication. Along with this, they also demand supernatural miracles, by which they would be compelled to accept and follow. They are warned that on the day such miracles come, that day will be their final day, and after that they will be destroyed and annihilated.

﴿Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come? On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before, or that did not earn good through its faith. Say: "Wait, we too are waiting."﴾ (6:158)

After this comes the decision that there can be no unity between the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), the Muslim Ummah, the religion of Islam, and those who disregard the Shariah of God, determine for themselves what is lawful and unlawful, and what is permitted and forbidden, make a Shariah for themselves, and yet claim that this Shariah is from God.

﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, you have no concern with them in anything. Their affair is only with God; then He will inform them of what they used to do.﴾ (6:159)

The decision of God is very clear: ﴿You have nothing to do with them.﴾ Now this Surah reaches its culmination, and the legislation and the sovereignty of God are explained in a very detailed and clear manner. Although on the surface this topic appears to be a partial one, here this doctrinal question is presented in a highly principled manner, and the decision of the whole religion is made: these matters are the aims and doctrines of the religion of Islam. Regarding them, the heart and vision of the people of Islam must be clear and single-minded, and then this doctrine, this belief and this single-mindedness must manifest in the form of a detailed system of life.

﴿Say: "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the creed of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists." Say: "Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner; this I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit." Say: "Shall I seek a lord other than God, while He is the Lord of all things? Every soul earns only for itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to differ about." And He it is who made you successors upon the earth, and raised some of you above others in rank, that He may try you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (6:161–165)

These are the fundamental issues of the Islamic worldview and the religion of Islam: guidance regarding this world and the Hereafter, the issues of life and death, the issues of action and its recompense, the issues of worship and excellence (ihsan). The discourse brings all these matters together in this awe-inspiring concluding passage of the Surah, in a highly majestic and frightening manner. The supreme question of God's sovereignty, dominion and the right of legislation is expressed in the context of ordinary, everyday matters, namely the common matters of eating and drinking. This is because God's sovereignty and lordship make their decision in the greatest and the smallest of affairs. This is Islam, whose explanation is the Qur'an itself, which is the Word of the Lord of the worlds.

Lesson 37: Explanation of the Verses

These are the opening verses of Juz' 8. The first paragraph of it relates to the final verses of Juz' 7. In the final verses of Juz' 7 there was mention of the proposal of the polytheists of Arabia that the Prophet (ﷺ) should present before them the miracles they themselves proposed, and then they would confirm him and believe in him. Because of these oaths of theirs, some Muslims also secretly harboured the wish that it would be better if God fulfilled this desire of theirs, and these people also demanded of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he too should ask God to fulfil their desires. The whole content of these portions of Juz' 7 and Juz' 8 is as follows:

﴿And they swore by God their most emphatic oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say: "Signs are only with God. And what would make you realise that even if they came, they would not believe?" And We turn their hearts and their eyes away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly. And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them all things face to face, they would not have believed unless God willed. But most of them are ignorant.﴾ (6:109–111)

The explanation of these verses we have already given in Juz' 7. Here we will set out the general truths contained in these verses, which were not discussed there.

1. The first truth is that faith and disbelief, and guidance and misguidance, do not depend solely on arguments, such that if an truth was not supported by arguments, people would not accept it. Rather, truth is itself a proof. Truth has within itself such power that it overcomes the human heart; every human heart is satisfied by it and inclines towards it. But there are other internal and external causes which become barriers between a person and the acceptance of truth. It is about such barriers that God says:

If you paste the Urdu text of the commentary itself (the part following the verses), I will translate it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 112–113 (part 1 of 2):

Thus have We decreed for mankind that those polytheists who make their faith contingent upon matters that are extraordinary and beyond the normal course of things, and who do not reflect upon the signs of guidance and the markers of the path present within their own selves and in the vast universe around them, would not believe even if there came to them a thousand such manifest and extraordinary events. This is how We have fashioned the destiny of these people. We have decided that against every Prophet there would arise, from among men and jinn, some devils, and We have decided that some of them would inspire others with attractive words. They deceive the common people and mislead them, and thus, by opposing the Messengers, they deceive people, whereas in reality they are fighting against guidance. This too is Our practice and Our plan: those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who are content with their course and earn the sins in which they are engaged, lend a willing ear to the words of these devils, namely enmity towards the Messengers and the spreading of corruption and misguidance upon this earth.

All these events occur in accordance with the divine decree; they take place according to His will. Had Allah willed, these people would not have adopted such conduct, and the course of events would have been entirely reversed, and the destiny of Allah would have run in a completely different direction. This is because these events do not occur by mere chance, nor do the events of the world come about through the power and strength of man himself.

Once it is established that in this world there is a struggle between truth and falsehood, in which one side is the Messengers and the truth that accompanies them, and the other side is the devils of men and jinn, with whom are falsehood, deception and fraud; and once it is also established that this whole conflict, this struggle between truth and falsehood, proceeds under the will of Allah and the plan of His decree, then it is the duty of a Muslim to reflect upon the wisdom and design that operates beneath this struggle, and, before that, the believing servant should strive to reach the depth of these events.

﴿And thus did We make for every Prophet an enemy, devils of men and jinn, who inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception. Had your Lord willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they fabricate.﴾ (6:112)

That is to say, by Our will and decree We have done this. For every Prophet We have created an enemy. These enemies have been, from among men and jinn, those who were devils. Shaytanah (devilry) means disobedience and defiance of command. The concept of shaytanah is to be an embodiment of evil. It is a quality with which both humans and jinn may be characterised. If someone is an embodiment of evil, then if he is a jinn, that jinn is a devil, and if he is a human, that human is a devil. At times this quality is also found in an animal, when it is disobedient, rebellious and aggressive, for a hadith states that the black dog is a devil.

These jinn and human devils, concerning whom Allah's decree is that they will be enemies of every Prophet, deceive one another with smooth and sweet words, and they inspire these words in one another. Among the meanings of wahy (inspiration) is that a hidden and inward influence is transmitted from one soul to another, or that one person deceives another, and people incite one another to rebellion, disobedience and wickedness.

Among these devils, those who are human, their activities are well known and widely recognised, and upon this earth we see them day and night. Their patterns and models, and their activities in opposition to the Prophets, are known and familiar. People of every age have seen them and still see them.

As for the devils who belong to the jinn, they are among the unseen matters of Allah, and concerning them we know only as much as Allah and His Messenger ﷺ have told us, for the keys of the unseen are with Allah alone, and He alone knows about them. That there exists some creation beyond the known and visible living beings of this earth, Allah has informed us of in His Speech, and within the limits of that information regarding this creation we believe. As for those who, taking science as a shield, deny the existence of such a creation of Allah, we do not know upon what evidence they rely in doing so. For human knowledge has never claimed that man has comprehended all kinds of living beings, especially within this small star, the earth, while regarding the countless other celestial bodies science still has only rudimentary knowledge. One can only suppose whether the kind of creation found upon this earth is possible or not in some other stars. This does not negate the possibility of a different kind of life and some other species and genus of living and animate creatures unknown to science. For no one who speaks in the name of science would deny that there are other worlds beyond this one, and perhaps there are countless such creations.

After this fundamental belief, as to what the nature of this creation is and how its natural life is, we have no knowledge. Concerning this we know only as much as the Truthful Informant, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, has told us.

We know that this creation is a fiery creation. It can live upon the earth, within the earth, and also beyond it. This creation is extremely swift in motion. Among this creation some are righteous and believers, and some are devils and rebellious. They can see human beings, while humans cannot see them in their true form. There are many creations that see humans but whom humans cannot see. Some devils are such that they have been set over human beings, and they mislead people by deceiving them, but they have no power over the special servants of Allah, who remember Allah and possess firm faith. The devil is always attached to the believer; when the believer remembers Allah, he hides and flees, and when he is heedless, he again casts waswasah (whisperings). When the believer is saturated with the remembrance of Allah, the cunning of the devil becomes weak in face of it. The resurrection and gathering of the jinn will be the same as that of human beings; in the same way their reckoning and accounting will be made, and they too will be deserving of the reward of Paradise and the punishment of Hell. When jinn encounter angels, they appear very weak and have no strength. From this verse we learn that Allah has set up, against every Prophet, an opposition from among jinn and men.

Allah, Whose being is capable of doing so, could, had His will required it, have caused the jinn not to adopt this conduct. They would not rebel, and they would never become embodiments of evil. They would not be enemies of the Prophets, would not harm the believers, and would not turn the common people away from the path of Allah. Allah was capable of compelling them and placing them upon the path of guidance, and He would have granted them guidance, provided they turned towards guidance; and thus they would not have engaged in enmity to the Prophets, opposition to truth, and hostility to the believers. But Allah granted them a degree of choice and freedom, and permitted them to go about inflicting harm upon the friends of Allah, in accordance with Allah's will and the scheme of His decree, so that the friends of Allah might be tested, and that this testing should come through the harm inflicted by His enemies. Just as Allah tests His enemies by granting them a limited measure of power, choice and freedom, so too His enemies can inflict harm upon the friends of Allah only to the extent that Allah has determined.

﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾ (6:112). The question is: what consequences follow for us from this guidance?

1. Those who stand against the Prophets and harm the followers of the Prophets are devils. These devils are both from among men and from among jinn. The devils of the jinn and the devils of men are alike, and the nature of their work is also similar. They deceive and mislead one another, while the common quality of all of them is that they are rebellious, astray and enemies of Allah.

2. A second point that becomes apparent is that these devils who are enemies of the Prophets and who harm the followers of the Prophets: the real truth is that through them Allah tests His servants and friends, and this testing is also based upon profound wisdom, so that people may be sifted and examined, their hearts purified, their patience tested, and their endurance and trustworthiness examined. Whenever they succeed in this trial, the trial and test end, and the opposition of the opponents ends. The enemies then no longer have the power to inflict harm, for the decree of Allah's plan comes to an end, and their enemies become weak and unsuccessful. Their condition becomes such that they are returning to Allah bearing the burden of their deeds.

﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾ (6:112).

3. It was a requirement of Allah's wisdom that He grant the devils of jinn and the devils of men the respite to run about committing devilry, for Allah tests them within the respite and power He has given these devils, so that they may continue to harm the friends of Allah for a time. In this way Allah also tests His friends, to see whether they remain patient, whether they stand firm upon the truth they possess while falsehood is pressing upon them and inflicting harm, and whether they sell their selves completely to Allah and remain steadfast in their covenant with Him in both ease and hardship, in straitness and in abundance. Otherwise, it was within the scope of Allah's power not to begin this entire drama at all.

4. The cunning of all the devils of jinn and men has no real substance; they are very weak creatures. They have no self-power, strength or might of their own. They can act only within the limits that Allah has set for them. The believer who knows and is certain that the Absolute Power belongs to Him alone, the One who has granted these people permission, finds these devils weak in his sight, even though outwardly they may appear to be oppressors and tyrants. For this reason the Messenger ﷺ is directed: ﴿So leave them and what they fabricate﴾ (6:112). Leave them and their fabrications. I am the Absolute Power, and their punishment for their crimes is prepared for them.

5. Apart from the trial of the believers and the devils, there is another wisdom as well. This enmity, this spreading of misguidance, and this vast deception by word and deed: Allah has permitted it also for this reason:

﴿And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline toward it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may earn what they are earning.﴾ (6:113)

That is to say, those who do not believe in the Hereafter will not lend an ear to these guidances, and they will give attention to the whispering of these devils. This is because those who do not believe in the Hereafter devote all their capacities to worldly affairs. When such people see that in the world devils are seated at every turn and are opposed to the Prophets, afflicting the followers of the Prophets night and day, and that these devils support one another, embellish one another's words, and affirm one another by word and deed, then these worldly people submit to the devils and are overawed by their false prestige, dignity and splendour, even though their power is in truth extremely weak. Thus they too earn evil and sin, and become partners in spreading wickedness, disobedience and corruption. Because of this attention and listening, these worldly people keep receiving satanic guidance.

This is a matter whose unfolding in this manner was in accordance with the plan of the divine decree, because through this process Allah wished to test His servants and bring forward the genuine from the spurious among them. Moreover, according to this scheme, Allah wished to set every person upon a path with complete freedom, so that on the Day of Resurrection he would become deserving of a reward exactly suited to his deeds.

Furthermore, there was also the purpose that in this struggle, through the contest of truth and falsehood, reformative work in the world might continue; truth might be distinguished from falsehood by separating from it, and goodness might emerge clean and pure through the polishing of patience. The devils will bear on the Day of Resurrection the full burden of what they have done, and this entire scheme continues to operate in accordance with Allah's will; and according to this same scheme, the affair of the friends of Allah is settled, and according to it also the affair of the enemies of Allah is settled. This is the scheme and will of Allah, and Allah does what He wills.

Now consider this scene closely. On this battlefield, on one side stand all the devils of jinn and mankind, with their helpers and friends; on the other side stand the Prophets and all their followers; and in this struggle there is a third, decisive force: the will of Allah, His dominance and His supreme sovereignty. These are the three aspects of this scene, and we should pause and cast a deep gaze upon it.

This is a battle in which all the forces of evil in this universe are gathering. The devils of jinn and the devils of mankind stand shoulder to shoulder. They are gathering all their powers for the completion of their plan, and they work with remarkable cooperation and coordination. The common plan of these people is to be enemies of all the Prophets, their call and their supporters, and their target and plan are fixed. "They inspire one another with embellished words as deception and delusion." They help one another with every means, including all the methods of trickery and deceit, and they also mislead one another; and whenever an assembly gathers in accordance with truth and reality, the distinctive feature of that assembly is that they deceive one another as well. They cooperate and mislead one another, and become helpers of one another in that misguidance. These people do not tell one another any word of truth. Rather, they present their enmity toward truth to one another as a great jihad, and they resolve that they will fight against that truth for a long period.

The cunning of these forces is not completely free and unrestrained either. Around it lies a vast circle of the divine will. Whatever activities these devils display, they display within the bounds of the circle of Allah's will. This circle of will is the circle of Allah's decree. From here, in the eyes of Allah's servants, this gathering of the forces of evil and their backing in the world is not even worth a feather. They are restricted and in chains. This gathering and alliance is not unrestrained and free. Allah does as He wills, and He does not allow everyone to be caught in their snare without any defense or resistance, as all rebellious devils always wish, that they should have unrestricted dominion and that people should obey them unconditionally and act according to their desires and whims. That is absolutely not the case; rather, all the activities of these rebels are confined within Allah's will, His decree and His laws. For this reason these satanic forces cannot cause any harm or injury to the friends of Allah. Yes, they do inflict only as much harm as Allah permits as a test for His friends. In the end, all matters return to Allah.

But this gathering of the forces of evil and their mutual cooperation is also a point for reflection for the people of truth. They should reflect and understand the plan of the forces of evil, and keep in view the means of evil as well. Similarly, this scene, that Allah's will and decree keep watch over all the activities of these people, is also good news for the people of truth. Through it the people of truth gain conviction and tranquility that in the end they will be successful. Therefore their eyes should always remain fixed upon the overpowering might of Allah the Exalted, which is always enforced and effective. In the end, Allah's supreme sovereignty is established, and truth attains dominance. Hence the people of truth should keep their conviction and belief bound to the Being of the Great Lord, whether Satan wishes it or not. They should proceed on their path in such a way that truthfulness is woven into their morals and deeds, and their hearts and minds are imbued with truth. As for the enmity of the devils and their cunning, the people of truth should entrust them to the will and power of Allah, which in every case succeeds and prevails. This is because all these matters proceed according to Allah's will, and "If your Lord had willed, they would not have done it; so leave them and what they invent of falsehood."

Lesson 68: At a Glance

Now begins the subject that is the central theme of this whole surah, and the introductory remarks on this theme appear here and there throughout the surah. The last of these introductory remarks is the doctrinal issue stated in the two preceding verses, as well as the ideological struggle that has continued between truth and falsehood, in which the devils of jinn and the devils of mankind on one side and the Prophets and their followers on the other have been in enmity, and in the end the will of Allah has prevailed. And then the explanation that guidance and misguidance occur in accordance with the Sunnah of Allah and under the will of Allah. In other words, all the discussions that were presented at the end of the previous lesson, and which were treated in detail, come as introduction.

Now the discourse turns to the actual subject for which all these matters were an introduction. This subject is the issue of "mā uhilla bihi li-ghayrillāh" (that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked), that is, the question of the lawfulness and unlawfulness of those things over which, at the time of slaughter, the name of someone other than Allah was taken. The importance of this issue stems from the first principle of Islam, that in Islam the right of sovereignty belongs to Allah alone, and the authority of supreme command belongs to Allah alone. No human being should in any way exercise Allah's right of sovereignty. And when a matter is fundamental and doctrinal, even a small matter becomes as important as a very great matter. It is not important whether this is a matter of slaughtered animals, or whether it is so minor a question that the meat of a particular animal is permissible or impermissible, or whether it is a matter of who holds supreme authority over a state, or who holds supreme authority in a society. In this matter of principles, both are of equal importance, because in both a person acknowledges who holds sovereignty: Allah or someone else; whether the acknowledgment of divine sovereignty is affirmed or denied.

The Islamic system of life and the Qur'an emphasize this principle everywhere, and whether the matter is small or great, this principle is presented again and again and with emphasis, because it is an extremely important doctrinal principle. This principle is Islam, and it is the religion. All other issues apart from this principle are its practical application and its detailed consequences.

In the portion of the surah under discussion, or in all the other verses of the surah, we will find that this reality is repeated in the Qur'an again and again and is brought forward in various forms. When the laws, systems, customs and traditions of the age of ignorance (jahiliyyah) are discussed, this principle is also repeated, and it is said that these laws and customs are shirk and are tantamount to rebellion against Islam. These laws and regulations arose from the belief that there is another deity besides Allah. This is why Islam subjects such laws and such customs to the harshest criticism. And this criticism has been made in various styles and different modes of expression. But the central focus of this criticism is this supreme principle of Islam, that the sovereign authority over this universe belongs to Allah alone. This is the true Islam and the true faith.

We have decided that against every Prophet there would arise, from among men and jinn, some devils, and We have decided that some of them would inspire others with attractive words. They deceive the common people and mislead them, and thus, by opposing the Messengers, they deceive people, whereas in reality they are fighting against guidance. This too is Our practice and Our plan: those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who are content with their course and earn the sins in which they are engaged, lend a willing ear to the words of these devils, namely enmity towards the Messengers and the spreading of corruption and misguidance upon this earth.

All these events occur in accordance with the divine decree; they take place according to His will. Had Allah willed, these people would not have adopted such conduct, and the course of events would have been entirely reversed, and the destiny of Allah would have run in a completely different direction. This is because these events do not occur by mere chance, nor do the events of the world come about through the power and strength of man himself.

Once it is established that in this world there is a struggle between truth and falsehood, in which one side is the Messengers and the truth that accompanies them, and the other side is the devils of men and jinn, with whom are falsehood, deception and fraud; and once it is also established that this whole conflict, this struggle between truth and falsehood, proceeds under the will of Allah and the plan of His decree, then it is the duty of a Muslim to reflect upon the wisdom and design that operates beneath this struggle, and, before that, the believing servant should strive to reach the depth of these events.

﴿And thus did We make for every Prophet an enemy, devils of men and jinn, who inspire one another with ornamented speech as deception. Had your Lord willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they fabricate.﴾ (6:112)

That is to say, by Our will and decree We have done this. For every Prophet We have created an enemy. These enemies have been, from among men and jinn, those who were devils. Shaytanah (devilry) means disobedience and defiance of command. The concept of shaytanah is to be an embodiment of evil. It is a quality with which both humans and jinn may be characterised. If someone is an embodiment of evil, then if he is a jinn, that jinn is a devil, and if he is a human, that human is a devil. At times this quality is also found in an animal, when it is disobedient, rebellious and aggressive, for a hadith states that the black dog is a devil.

These jinn and human devils, concerning whom Allah's decree is that they will be enemies of every Prophet, deceive one another with smooth and sweet words, and they inspire these words in one another. Among the meanings of wahy (inspiration) is that a hidden and inward influence is transmitted from one soul to another, or that one person deceives another, and people incite one another to rebellion, disobedience and wickedness.

Among these devils, those who are human, their activities are well known and widely recognised, and upon this earth we see them day and night. Their patterns and models, and their activities in opposition to the Prophets, are known and familiar. People of every age have seen them and still see them.

As for the devils who belong to the jinn, they are among the unseen matters of Allah, and concerning them we know only as much as Allah and His Messenger ﷺ have told us, for the keys of the unseen are with Allah alone, and He alone knows about them. That there exists some creation beyond the known and visible living beings of this earth, Allah has informed us of in His Speech, and within the limits of that information regarding this creation we believe. As for those who, taking science as a shield, deny the existence of such a creation of Allah, we do not know upon what evidence they rely in doing so. For human knowledge has never claimed that man has comprehended all kinds of living beings, especially within this small star, the earth, while regarding the countless other celestial bodies science still has only rudimentary knowledge. One can only suppose whether the kind of creation found upon this earth is possible or not in some other stars. This does not negate the possibility of a different kind of life and some other species and genus of living and animate creatures unknown to science. For no one who speaks in the name of science would deny that there are other worlds beyond this one, and perhaps there are countless such creations.

After this fundamental belief, as to what the nature of this creation is and how its natural life is, we have no knowledge. Concerning this we know only as much as the Truthful Informant, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, has told us.

We know that this creation is a fiery creation. It can live upon the earth, within the earth, and also beyond it. This creation is extremely swift in motion. Among this creation some are righteous and believers, and some are devils and rebellious. They can see human beings, while humans cannot see them in their true form. There are many creations that see humans but whom humans cannot see. Some devils are such that they have been set over human beings, and they mislead people by deceiving them, but they have no power over the special servants of Allah, who remember Allah and possess firm faith. The devil is always attached to the believer; when the believer remembers Allah, he hides and flees, and when he is heedless, he again casts waswasah (whisperings). When the believer is saturated with the remembrance of Allah, the cunning of the devil becomes weak in face of it. The resurrection and gathering of the jinn will be the same as that of human beings; in the same way their reckoning and accounting will be made, and they too will be deserving of the reward of Paradise and the punishment of Hell. When jinn encounter angels, they appear very weak and have no strength. From this verse we learn that Allah has set up, against every Prophet, an opposition from among jinn and men.

Allah, Whose being is capable of doing so, could, had His will required it, have caused the jinn not to adopt this conduct. They would not rebel, and they would never become embodiments of evil. They would not be enemies of the Prophets, would not harm the believers, and would not turn the common people away from the path of Allah. Allah was capable of compelling them and placing them upon the path of guidance, and He would have granted them guidance, provided they turned towards guidance; and thus they would not have engaged in enmity to the Prophets, opposition to truth, and hostility to the believers. But Allah granted them a degree of choice and freedom, and permitted them to go about inflicting harm upon the friends of Allah, in accordance with Allah's will and the scheme of His decree, so that the friends of Allah might be tested, and that this testing should come through the harm inflicted by His enemies. Just as Allah tests His enemies by granting them a limited measure of power, choice and freedom, so too His enemies can inflict harm upon the friends of Allah only to the extent that Allah has determined.

﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾ (6:112). The question is: what consequences follow for us from this guidance?

1. Those who stand against the Prophets and harm the followers of the Prophets are devils. These devils are both from among men and from among jinn. The devils of the jinn and the devils of men are alike, and the nature of their work is also similar. They deceive and mislead one another, while the common quality of all of them is that they are rebellious, astray and enemies of Allah.

2. A second point that becomes apparent is that these devils who are enemies of the Prophets and who harm the followers of the Prophets: the real truth is that through them Allah tests His servants and friends, and this testing is also based upon profound wisdom, so that people may be sifted and examined, their hearts purified, their patience tested, and their endurance and trustworthiness examined. Whenever they succeed in this trial, the trial and test end, and the opposition of the opponents ends. The enemies then no longer have the power to inflict harm, for the decree of Allah's plan comes to an end, and their enemies become weak and unsuccessful. Their condition becomes such that they are returning to Allah bearing the burden of their deeds.

﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾ (6:112).

3. It was a requirement of Allah's wisdom that He grant the devils of jinn and the devils of men the respite to run about committing devilry, for Allah tests them within the respite and power He has given these devils, so that they may continue to harm the friends of Allah for a time. In this way Allah also tests His friends, to see whether they remain patient, whether they stand firm upon the truth they possess while falsehood is pressing upon them and inflicting harm, and whether they sell their selves completely to Allah and remain steadfast in their covenant with Him in both ease and hardship, in straitness and in abundance. Otherwise, it was within the scope of Allah's power not to begin this entire drama at all.

4. The cunning of all the devils of jinn and men has no real substance; they are very weak creatures. They have no self-power, strength or might of their own. They can act only within the limits that Allah has set for them. The believer who knows and is certain that the Absolute Power belongs to Him alone, the One who has granted these people permission, finds these devils weak in his sight, even though outwardly they may appear to be oppressors and tyrants. For this reason the Messenger ﷺ is directed: ﴿So leave them and what they fabricate﴾ (6:112). Leave them and their fabrications. I am the Absolute Power, and their punishment for their crimes is prepared for them.

5. Apart from the trial of the believers and the devils, there is another wisdom as well. This enmity, this spreading of misguidance, and this vast deception by word and deed: Allah has permitted it also for this reason:

﴿And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline toward it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may earn what they are earning.﴾ (6:113)

That is to say, those who do not believe in the Hereafter will not lend an ear to these guidances, and they will give attention to the whispering of these devils. This is because those who do not believe in the Hereafter devote all their capacities to worldly affairs. When such people see that in the world devils are seated at every turn and are opposed to the Prophets, afflicting the followers of the Prophets night and day, and that these devils support one another, embellish one another's words, and affirm one another by word and deed, then these worldly people submit to the devils and are overawed by their false prestige, dignity and splendour, even though their power is in truth extremely weak. Thus they too earn evil and sin, and become partners in spreading wickedness, disobedience and corruption. Because of this attention and listening, these worldly people keep receiving satanic guidance.

This is a matter whose unfolding in this manner was in accordance with the plan of the divine decree, because through this process Allah wished to test His servants and bring forward the genuine from the spurious among them. Moreover, according to this scheme, Allah wished to set every person upon a path with complete freedom, so that on the Day of Resurrection he would become deserving of a reward exactly suited to his deeds.

Furthermore, there was also the purpose that in this struggle, through the contest of truth and falsehood, reformative work in the world might continue; truth might be distinguished from falsehood by separating from it, and goodness might emerge clean and pure through the polishing of patience. The devils will bear on the Day of Resurrection the full burden of what they have done, and this entire scheme continues to operate in accordance with Allah's will; and according to this same scheme, the affair of the friends of Allah is settled, and according to it also the affair of the enemies of Allah is settled. This is the scheme and will of Allah, and Allah does what He wills.

Now consider this scene closely. On this battlefield, on one side stand all the devils of jinn and mankind, with their helpers and friends; on the other side stand the Prophets and all their followers; and in this struggle there is a third, decisive force: the will of Allah, His dominance and His supreme sovereignty. These are the three aspects of this scene, and we should pause and cast a deep gaze upon it.

This is a battle in which all the forces of evil in this universe are gathering. The devils of jinn and the devils of mankind stand shoulder to shoulder. They are gathering all their powers for the completion of their plan, and they work with remarkable cooperation and coordination. The common plan of these people is to be enemies of all the Prophets, their call and their supporters, and their target and plan are fixed. "They inspire one another with embellished words as deception and delusion." They help one another with every means, including all the methods of trickery and deceit, and they also mislead one another; and whenever an assembly gathers in accordance with truth and reality, the distinctive feature of that assembly is that they deceive one another as well. They cooperate and mislead one another, and become helpers of one another in that misguidance. These people do not tell one another any word of truth. Rather, they present their enmity toward truth to one another as a great jihad, and they resolve that they will fight against that truth for a long period.

The cunning of these forces is not completely free and unrestrained either. Around it lies a vast circle of the divine will. Whatever activities these devils display, they display within the bounds of the circle of Allah's will. This circle of will is the circle of Allah's decree. From here, in the eyes of Allah's servants, this gathering of the forces of evil and their backing in the world is not even worth a feather. They are restricted and in chains. This gathering and alliance is not unrestrained and free. Allah does as He wills, and He does not allow everyone to be caught in their snare without any defense or resistance, as all rebellious devils always wish, that they should have unrestricted dominion and that people should obey them unconditionally and act according to their desires and whims. That is absolutely not the case; rather, all the activities of these rebels are confined within Allah's will, His decree and His laws. For this reason these satanic forces cannot cause any harm or injury to the friends of Allah. Yes, they do inflict only as much harm as Allah permits as a test for His friends. In the end, all matters return to Allah.

But this gathering of the forces of evil and their mutual cooperation is also a point for reflection for the people of truth. They should reflect and understand the plan of the forces of evil, and keep in view the means of evil as well. Similarly, this scene, that Allah's will and decree keep watch over all the activities of these people, is also good news for the people of truth. Through it the people of truth gain conviction and tranquility that in the end they will be successful. Therefore their eyes should always remain fixed upon the overpowering might of Allah the Exalted, which is always enforced and effective. In the end, Allah's supreme sovereignty is established, and truth attains dominance. Hence the people of truth should keep their conviction and belief bound to the Being of the Great Lord, whether Satan wishes it or not. They should proceed on their path in such a way that truthfulness is woven into their morals and deeds, and their hearts and minds are imbued with truth. As for the enmity of the devils and their cunning, the people of truth should entrust them to the will and power of Allah, which in every case succeeds and prevails. This is because all these matters proceed according to Allah's will, and "If your Lord had willed, they would not have done it; so leave them and what they invent of falsehood."

Lesson 68: At a Glance

Now begins the subject that is the central theme of this whole surah, and the introductory remarks on this theme appear here and there throughout the surah. The last of these introductory remarks is the doctrinal issue stated in the two preceding verses, as well as the ideological struggle that has continued between truth and falsehood, in which the devils of jinn and the devils of mankind on one side and the Prophets and their followers on the other have been in enmity, and in the end the will of Allah has prevailed. And then the explanation that guidance and misguidance occur in accordance with the Sunnah of Allah and under the will of Allah. In other words, all the discussions that were presented at the end of the previous lesson, and which were treated in detail, come as introduction.

Now the discourse turns to the actual subject for which all these matters were an introduction. This subject is the issue of "mā uhilla bihi li-ghayrillāh" (that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked), that is, the question of the lawfulness and unlawfulness of those things over which, at the time of slaughter, the name of someone other than Allah was taken. The importance of this issue stems from the first principle of Islam, that in Islam the right of sovereignty belongs to Allah alone, and the authority of supreme command belongs to Allah alone. No human being should in any way exercise Allah's right of sovereignty. And when a matter is fundamental and doctrinal, even a small matter becomes as important as a very great matter. It is not important whether this is a matter of slaughtered animals, or whether it is so minor a question that the meat of a particular animal is permissible or impermissible, or whether it is a matter of who holds supreme authority over a state, or who holds supreme authority in a society. In this matter of principles, both are of equal importance, because in both a person acknowledges who holds sovereignty: Allah or someone else; whether the acknowledgment of divine sovereignty is affirmed or denied.

The Islamic system of life and the Qur'an emphasize this principle everywhere, and whether the matter is small or great, this principle is presented again and again and with emphasis, because it is an extremely important doctrinal principle. This principle is Islam, and it is the religion. All other issues apart from this principle are its practical application and its detailed consequences.

In the portion of the surah under discussion, or in all the other verses of the surah, we will find that this reality is repeated in the Qur'an again and again and is brought forward in various forms. When the laws, systems, customs and traditions of the age of ignorance (jahiliyyah) are discussed, this principle is also repeated, and it is said that these laws and customs are shirk and are tantamount to rebellion against Islam. These laws and regulations arose from the belief that there is another deity besides Allah. This is why Islam subjects such laws and such customs to the harshest criticism. And this criticism has been made in various styles and different modes of expression. But the central focus of this criticism is this supreme principle of Islam, that the sovereign authority over this universe belongs to Allah alone. This is the true Islam and the true faith.
