(Verse) 121 (Number 121).

Once again the discussion returns to the true reality of kufr and iman, and the repetition of the point indicates that in Islam the declaring of things lawful and unlawful is linked to kufr and Islam.

This repeated emphasis and repeated linkage of the matter shows how important legislation and sovereignty are in a person's daily life from the standpoint of Islam.

(Verse) ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than Allah, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book, fully detailed? And those whom We gave the Book know that it has been sent down from your Lord in truth. So do not be among the doubters.﴾ (6:114)

"Then, since this is the situation, should I seek a judge other than Allah, although He has sent down to you the Book in full detail, and those to whom We gave the Book before you know that it has been sent down from your Lord with truth, so do not be among those who doubt."

This is a question put in the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and this interrogation is a negative one. It is a warning that it is not a proper attitude for anyone to accept anyone other than Allah as ruler and decider in any matter of his life. Thus it is decided that in the Islamic system, decision in all matters of life rests with Allah alone; this is an undisputed matter, and it is prohibited that there be anyone other than Allah who is entitled to make decisions in people's lives and to continue doing so according to his own will.

(Verse) ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than Allah?﴾ "Shall I seek another decider other than Allah?"

Then comes the detail of this disagreeable feeling; the circumstances are also explained because of which the sovereignty of others besides Allah becomes a blameworthy act. Allah has given the details of everything and has not left the servants in need of seeking the path of guidance for themselves, or of taking decisions on the problems of their lives from any place other than Allah, and resolving the difficulties of life.

(Verse) ﴿And He it is who has sent down to you the Book fully detailed﴾ "Although He has sent down to you the Book in full detail." This Book has been sent down so that it may decide among people the matters about which they differ, and thus the sovereignty and supreme authority of Allah may be manifested. Moreover, Allah has sent down this Book in a most detailed manner. In it have been fixed all the principles upon which the entire system of life will be founded. In it have also been stated some subsidiary and particular matters, concerning which it was Allah's will that they be permanent rulings for human society, however advanced that society may become and however far it may have progressed in knowledge. For this reason, with this Book present, there is no need at all to take decisions from any other platform. This is the decision that Allah, the Exalted, has made regarding the status of His Book. Now, if someone says: "The world has progressed and there is no need now to return to this Book," then let him say it a thousand times, but he should also plainly state with this statement another point: that he is (God forbid) a disbeliever, a denier of this religion of Islam, and one who denies the words of Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Here, around these people, there is also a particular situation, in which seeking a decision from any source other than Allah in any circumstance of life becomes a most detestable act and appears most strange. It is this: those who were given the scriptures before (the Muslims) know that this Qur'an too is sent down from Allah, because they are people who possess knowledge of the heavenly books.

(Verse) ﴿And those whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth﴾ (6:113 in the source's numbering) "And those to whom We gave the Book (before you) know that it has been sent down from your Lord in truth."

This situation existed in Makkah and the Arabian Peninsula, and therefore Allah directs the polytheists toward it. Whether the People of the Book acknowledge this reality, as some did, whose hearts Allah had opened to Islam, or they conceal it and do not declare it, as most People of the Book did, in both cases this reality remained in place: the People of the Book were aware of the truth. Allah Himself bears witness to their knowledge, and Allah's testimony is true, because Allah clearly says that these people (ya'lamun) know that the Qur'an has been sent down with truth from Allah, and that in it there is nothing but truth, and that this truth is sent down from Allah.

Even today the People of the Book know well that this Book has been sent down from Allah with truth. They understand well that the strength of this religion lies solely in the fact that behind it stands a great truth, and the Holy Qur'an is based on that great truth. For this reason, on account of this knowledge, they fight against this religion with such ferocity, continuously. They fight against this Book, and this struggle has continued from the beginning of this religion until today. It is an extremely severe and painful war. The People of the Book are fighting this war solely for the purpose of ending the rule of this Book over the lives of Muslims, and bringing the lives of Muslims under the rule of some other scriptures and some other man-made laws. They make other persons judges and rulers besides Allah, so that this Book does not remain alive and there is no real existence of Allah's religion. Their effort is to establish, in those Islamic countries where once Allah's sovereignty was established, some other sovereignties and authorities, although in those countries there was once in force the system and law that was in this Book. Only this law was in force, and no other laws shared action with it. Nor were other books current alongside the Book of Allah from which people derived principles of law and other values of life, and which they presented, like the verses and provisions of the Book of Allah, as authority. Behind all such plans stand the designs of the People of the Book, namely the Crusader and Zionist ambitions. All such activities even today are the intrigues of these very People of the Book.

Here it is said that Allah has sent down this Book in a most detailed manner, and that the People of the Book indeed know well that it has been sent down from Allah with truth. Now the address turns toward Muhammad ﷺ, and through him the whole community of believers is told this reality, and consoled that he should not be distressed by the disputation, denial and aversion of the People of the Book. Those who conceal the truth know what the reality is. This matter should not be burdensome to you.

(Verse) ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾ (6:114) "So do not be among those who doubt." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never entertained doubt or suspicion. It is related in a hadith that when this verse of Surah Yunus was revealed upon him:

(Verse) ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who have been reading the Book before you. Indeed, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾ (10:94)

"If you are in doubt about the guidance which We have sent down to you, then ask those who have been reading the Book before you. Indeed, it is the truth that has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters." Upon this, the Messenger ﷺ said: "I do not doubt, and I have no need to ask them."

But what is understood from these instructions and other similar examples is that in that period the Messenger ﷺ and the Muslim community were facing very deep intrigues and conspiracies. The opponents were displaying harsh enmity and denial, and the mercy of Allah required that by giving such firm instructions to you, both you and the Muslim community be urged to adopt a firm stance.

It is further said that the decisive word of Allah has now concluded and been completed. Above the authority of Allah there is no other authority that could change this decisive matter, because it is true, and this truth reaches all their plots.

(Verse) ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can alter His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (6:115)

"The word of your Lord is complete in truth and justice; no one can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." Allah has, with truth, made whatever He was to say and whatever decisions He was to make, and with justice has made whatever legislation He was to make. After the word of Allah, there is now no word of anyone else, no belief or ideology, no principle or law, and no standard of value. Now no one can speak against the law and the Shariah, nor can any custom or tradition stand against it. Nor is there any authority above the authority of Allah that would be entitled to change the word of Allah.

(Verse) ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (6:115) He hears everything. He hears what His servants say, He knows the context of their statements, and He knows well their interests and benefits.

After deciding that the truth is what is in the Book of Allah and what Allah has sent down, it is also decided that the thinking which man presents against the thinking of the Book of Allah rests merely upon the four legs of conjecture and estimation. Those who follow human thinking merely follow conjecture and estimation, and their end will be nothing but that they will stray from the straight path. Human thinking can be correct and rightly guided only when it is derived from the Book of Allah, which is a certain source of guidance. At this point Allah also warns the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not to heed what people say on the basis of mere human thinking, even if a large number of people adhere to that thinking, because jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah in any case, whether its adherents are many or few; in any case they go astray.

(Verse) ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but guessing.﴾ (6:116)

"O Prophet, if you follow the majority of those who dwell on earth, they will mislead you from the path of Allah. They only follow conjecture and make conjectures."

The majority of the people living on earth, at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, consisted of the people of jahiliyyah, just as today the majority of people have adopted jahiliyyah. At that time the majority of people did not make their decisions according to the divine law, nor did they regard the Shariah contained in the books of Allah as the law of the land. They did not derive their concepts and thoughts, their way of thinking and their way of life, from the guidance and direction of Allah. For this reason the majority of them at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an were afflicted with jahiliyyah, just as today the majority of people are afflicted with jahiliyyah. Those people did not derive any thought, opinion or decision from this "truth," nor was it based upon that reality. Moreover, the leaders of that age led their followers not to guidance but to misguidance. Just as today's situation is that people, having abandoned certain knowledge of the Book and Sunnah, pursue conjecture and estimation. It is clear that conjecture and estimation can only result in misguidance. For this reason the Messenger ﷺ was warned that if he began to obey the people, they would lead him astray. Although Allah has given these general instructions to the Messenger ﷺ in terms of the occasion of revelation, this guidance came in connection with a particular matter, namely the slaughtered animals, as the details that follow make clear.

After this comes the resolution that the determination of whether servants are guided or misguided also rests with Allah alone, because it is Allah who knows the reality of His servants. Only He can decide whether someone is on the right path or has gone astray.

(Verse) ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided.﴾ (6:117)

"Indeed, your Lord knows best who has strayed from His path, and He knows best who is upon the right way."

For judging the thoughts and concepts of people, their values and standards, and their conduct and activities as good or bad, there must necessarily be a criterion by which it can be decided what is truth and what is falsehood. This criterion should not be people's base desires, their changing terminologies and customs, because both of these are variable. Therefore there must be fixed a source and origin from which people can make decisions about their standards and about people themselves.

Here Allah, the Exalted, declares that it is Allah who decides what is good here and what is bad, and this right belongs to Allah alone. He alone can decide, and He alone knows what guidance is and what misguidance is, who is the guide and who is the one who goes astray.

We cannot grant any society the authority to determine good and evil according to its changing circumstances and conventions, because the constituent elements of every society, its form and appearance, and its material needs keep changing. If this right were given to society, the standards of good and evil would also cease to be fixed. Then the moral values of an agricultural society would be different, the values of an industrial society would be different, the values of a capitalist bourgeois society would be different, the values of a socialist and communist society would be different, and then people's principles of good and evil would differ according to the values of those societies.

Islam knows this well, and therefore it establishes permanent, fixed values which have been given permanently by Allah. Whatever societies and communities change into, whether advanced or backward, those societies which abandon these principles are described in the Islamic system by a specific term. Islam calls them jahili (ignorant of divine guidance) societies. Such a society is a polytheistic (mushrik) society, because it gives gods other than Allah the authority to set the standards of good and evil for it, to provide it with its conception of life, its principles of morality and its system of living. The Islamic system maintains only one division: in its view, a society is either an Islamic society or a jahili society. No third category exists in its view. Thereafter, the forms and shapes of jahili society may vary.

After this lengthy preface, we now take up the fundamental issue of slaughtered animals in the Islamic system. This issue is addressed in accordance with the same basic principle, that in Islam the authority to determine good and evil and lawful and unlawful rests solely with Allah. For this reason, a detailed discussion of this principle took place in the preceding verses:

(Verse) "So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs (118). And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to? And indeed, many lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors (119). And leave the outward and inward of sin. Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit (120). And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, and indeed it is defiance. And indeed, the devils inspire to their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you would be associates [of Allah] (121)."

(Translation of the verses) "So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs." "And what is the matter with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to? And indeed, many lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors." "Leave the outward and inward of sin. Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit." "And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiance. And indeed, the devils inspire to their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you would be associates [of Allah]." (6:118–121)

The command is: eat that slaughtered animal over which the name of Allah has been mentioned. The mention of Allah's name is made obligatory so that the direction of people's outlook and belief is determined, and so that their faith and obedience are specific to those commands which proceed from Allah.

(Verse) "So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs (118)"

"So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs." After this, they are asked: what is it that prevents you from eating the meat of such animals over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, and which Allah has made lawful? Whereas Allah has given the details of what is forbidden, leaving room for exception in a state of necessity. Thus, in matters of lawfulness and unlawfulness, Allah has given no one the right to speak. Therefore, no person may, according to his own will, eat some things considering them lawful and abandon others considering them unlawful.

(Verse) "And what is the matter with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to (6:119)"

"And what is the matter with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to." The details of these have already been given to you.

This issue is related to a matter existing in the society of that time. The polytheists of Makkah used to eat the meat of some animals which Allah had declared unlawful, and they would refrain from eating the meat of some animals which were lawful in the sight of Allah, and they believed that this was the law of Allah. Thus the Qur'an, deciding this affair, declares that these people legislate under the influence of their desires and without knowledge, and thereby encroach upon the sovereign right of Allah. In this way, they enter into the bounds which are specific to Allah, although they are the servants and slaves of Allah.

(Verse) "And indeed, many lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors (6:119)"

"And indeed, many lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors." Therefore Allah commands you to abandon every kind of sin, whether outward or inward. This matter too is among those sins: that someone should, without knowledge, become a cause of misguiding people. And he does this merely to satisfy his desires, and then gives this activity a religious and legal colour, even though it has no connection with the Shariah; rather, it is mere fabrication upon the Islamic Shariah. Therefore Allah warns them of the evil end of such fabrication.

(Verse) "Leave the outward and inward of sin. Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit (6:120)"

"Leave the outward and inward of sin. Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit." After this, it is commanded that you refrain from eating the flesh of those animals over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned. These people, when slaughtering some animals, would mention the names of other gods besides Allah over them. Or they would slaughter them for gambling, and then divide them by means of arrows. In respect of eating the flesh of dead animals, they would dispute with the Muslims. They would say: although such dead animals have not had Allah's name mentioned over them, Allah Himself has slaughtered them. Their argument was that Muslims eat the flesh of animals slaughtered by their own hands, but they do not eat the flesh of animals slaughtered by Allah. This is the conception and argument whose weakness is entirely clear, and this conception has persisted within all jahiliyyahs. This conception was given to the polytheists by their devils, who were attached to them from among jinn and men, so that they might dispute with the Muslims through their feeble notions and arguments. The details of these matters are given in these verses.

(Verse) "And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiance. And indeed, the devils inspire to their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you would be associates [of Allah] (6:121)"

"And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiance. And indeed, the devils inspire to their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you would be associates [of Allah]." Consider deeply this final judgement. How clear and categorical this decision is. It states that the sovereign is Allah alone, so the one obeyed is also He, and this is the fundamental principle of this religion. This verse makes clear that obeying anyone other than Allah in even a single detail of life's matters, when that obedience is not attributed to the Shariah of Allah and its principles, is manifest shirk, and because of it a Muslim leaves the fold of Islam and enters the fold of disbelief. Ibn Kathir says: Allah's saying "And if you obey them, indeed you would be associates [of Allah]" means: where you abandon the command of Allah and the divine Shariah and prefer the commands and orders of others over them, this is manifest shirk. Allah says elsewhere: "They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah." (Tirmidhi narrated a report in explanation of this verse, from Adi ibn Hatim (may Allah be pleased with him), who asked: O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they did not worship them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes, indeed they did. They made unlawful things lawful for them and lawful things unlawful, and they obeyed them; this is their worship of the rabbis and monks.") Similarly, Ibn Kathir narrated from Adi that the meaning of the verse "They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah" is that they sought guidance and admonition from people and cast the Book of Allah behind their backs. For this reason Allah said: "And they were commanded only to worship one God" — that is, to worship the One who, if He declares something unlawful, it becomes unlawful, and if He declares something lawful, it becomes lawful. Whatever law He makes is binding to follow, and whatever judgement He gives is enforced.

These are the statements of Ibn Kathir and Suddi. Both of them decide in extremely plain words and explain the matter fully, and this is because the Qur'an's statement on this issue is also extremely clear and categorical. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself explained it clearly, that whoever follows the law made by people in opposition to the Shariah of Allah in any detail of the affairs of life is a mushrik, even if such a person is a Muslim in his origin, because by this act he leaves Islam and stands in the ranks of the polytheists, even though he may repeatedly recite "Ashhadu" with his tongue while in practice he is the obedient follower and disciple of other than Allah.

Today, when we look at this globe from this angle, and then view it in the light of these clarifications of these verses, it appears that shirk and jahiliyyah have complete control over it. Except for those whom Allah wills, we turn away from the conduct of the holders of power on this globe who have claimed divine attributes, such that their law and command are deemed unacceptable. Unless someone is utterly compelled.

Regarding the detailed legal rulings on lawful and unlawful slaughtered animals among the guidance given in the verse under discussion ("wa la ta'kulu"), Ibn Kathir gives them as follows. He says that on this issue the jurists have three opinions.

Some jurists say that eating the meat of such a slaughtered animal is unlawful, whether or not the name of Allah was deliberately omitted over the animal or omitted by mistake.

This is also reported from Ibn Umar, Nafi, Amir al-Sha'bi and Muhammad ibn Sirin. Imam Malik also has a report to this effect. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal also has a report like this, and a group among the earlier and later scholars has supported it.

Abu Thawr, Dawud al-Zahiri, and Abu al-Futuh Muhammad ibn Ali al-Ta'i, who are among the later Shafi'is, adopted this same opinion in their book Arba'in, and they argued for their position from this very verse. Moreover, this group also argued from the other verse concerning hunting.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 6, verse 121 (part 3 of 3):

(Verse) "Wa la ta'kulu mimma lam yudhkar-smullahi 'alayh" — So eat of that over which the Name of Allah has been mentioned, which (the hunting dogs) have caught and held for you, and mention the Name of Allah over it.

Their argument is also that in this verse the emphatic particle "innahu lafisq" has come. The pronoun in "innahu" refers to the act of eating. Some exegetes have related it to slaughter performed in the name of other than Allah. Moreover, those holding this view also draw evidence from the hadiths that concern mentioning Allah's Name over game and slaughtered animals, such as the hadiths of 'Adi ibn Hatim and Abu Tha'labah. "When you release your trained dog and mention the Name of Allah over it, then eat what it holds back for you." Both of these hadiths have been narrated by the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim). Also, this group draws evidence from the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij: "Whatever draws blood and over which the Name of Allah has been mentioned, eat it." This hadith too has been narrated by the two Sahihs.

On this matter, the second view is that mentioning Allah's Name over slaughtered animals is not a condition and not obligatory, but rather recommended (mustahabb). If someone does not mention Allah's Name at the time of slaughter, whether deliberately or through forgetfulness, it makes no difference. This is the view of Imam al-Shafi'i, and all his companions have also gone this way. A narration to the same effect is also reported from Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. A narration in accordance with this is also reported from Imam Malik. Among his companions, Ashhab ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz has explicitly stated it, and he has also transmitted similar reports from Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurairah and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, may Allah be pleased with them, Wallahu a'lam.

As for the verses and hadiths, Imam al-Shafi'i has interpreted them thus: the verse "Wa la ta'kulu mimma lam yudhkar-smullahi 'alayh" refers to slaughtered animals over which idols' names were mentioned, as is made explicit in "wa fisqan uhilla lighayrillah bih" (what has been dedicated to other than Allah). Similarly, Ibn Juraij says that the prohibition in the verse "Wa la ta'kulu..." concerns the slaughtered animals that the Quraysh used to sacrifice on idols. Also, regarding the slaughtered animals of the Magians (Majus), the position adopted by Imam al-Shafi'i is stronger.

Ibn Abi Hatim, with his chain of narration, reports from Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas that "Wa la ta'kulu mimma lam yudhkar-smullahi 'alayh" is about carrion (maytah). In support of this, Imam Abu Dawud, in his mursal hadiths, cites the hadith of Thawr ibn Yazid: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The slaughter of a Muslim is lawful, whether or not the Name of Allah has been mentioned over it, because if he mentioned a name, he would mention only Allah's." And this mursal narration is supported by the narration of Daraqutni, that when a Muslim slaughters and does not mention Allah's Name at the time of slaughter, its meat should be eaten, because within a Muslim there is certainly one of the Names of Allah.

The third view is that if someone forgets to mention Allah's Name, there is no blame, but if he does so deliberately, eating it is not permissible. This is the well-known view of Imam Malik and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Imam Abu Hanifah and his companions have also gone this way.

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh also holds this view. Similarly, it is reported from Hadrat 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata', Tawus, Hasan al-Basri, Abu Malik, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, Ja'far ibn Muhammad and Rabi'ah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman.

Ibn Jarir says that scholars have differed about whether any ruling of this verse has been abrogated. Some have said that it is a muhkam (clear, non-abrogated) verse in its meaning and no part of it is abrogated. Mujahid holds this view. Hasan al-Basri and Ikrimah's statement is that the verse "Fakulu mimma dhukiresmullahi 'alayhi in kuntum bi-ayatihi mu'minin" (118) ... and in another place Allah says: "Wa la ta'kulu mimma lam yudhkar-smullahi 'alayhi wa innahu lafisq" — thus this verse abrogated the earlier one. Then the food of the People of the Book was exempted: "Wa ta'am alladhina utul-kitaba hillun lakum wa ta'amukum hillun lahum."

Ibn Abi Hatim says that in the presence of 'Abbas ibn al-Walid, the narration of Makhul was read, that Allah first revealed the verse "Wa la ta'kulu mimma lam yudhkar-smullahi 'alayh," and afterwards Allah abrogated it, thus showing mercy to the people of Islam, and this verse was revealed: "Al-yawma uhilla lakumu't-tayyibat, wa ta'amu alladhina utul-kitaba hillun lakum" (the People of the Book's food is lawful for you). Thus this second verse abrogated the first and declared the slaughter of the People of the Book lawful.

After this, Ibn Jarir said: "The reality is that there is no difference between the ruling on things over which Allah's Name has not been mentioned being forbidden and the ruling on the slaughter of the People of the Book being lawful." I consider Ibn Jarir's statement correct. Among the early scholars, those who used the term abrogation (naskh) meant specification (takhsis), Wallahu a'lam.

After this, a complete battle between Islam and disbelief is presented, and it is explained that Allah has placed great criminals in every town, and a large measure of arrogance and pride is found in their hearts. They are the great sinners of that town. These people prevent others throughout the region from coming onto the right path. In this narrative, it is clearly shown how the circumstances are of those whose hearts open to faith, and what circumstances those are in which people's hearts become constricted toward Islam and the acceptance of truth, so that upon conceiving of Islam they feel constriction, and it seems as though their breath has been cut off. Thus this narrative is connected in principle with the subject under discussion, namely lawfulness and unlawfulness in Islam. That is, a relationship between principle and branch is established, and it is indicated that the question of the lawfulness and unlawfulness of slaughtered animals is not a minor matter, but a most fundamental one.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 122:

Verses 122 to 125.

These verses portray the nature of guidance and misguidance, and describe the reality of misguidance in a highly realistic manner in contrast with the reality of guidance. The similes and figurative language employed here are used so that this picture becomes impactful. The similes and metaphors are themselves extremely realistic.

The realities of guidance and misguidance, by their very nature, are such that to explain them this kind of vivid depiction and effective mode of expression is extremely necessary. Although guidance and misguidance are undoubtedly realities, they are spiritual and ideological realities, and they are realities that can be tasted through experience and practice. As for the expression of a spiritual reality, or the beauty of its expression, only the person who has practically experienced these realities can enjoy it.

These are realities which give life to dead hearts and which illuminate dark heart and sight. These realities give a person a life through which he savours everything, adopts the right viewpoint about everything, and determines the correct value of everything. A person's perception about all sensory things changes completely, and such a light is produced in his heart and mind that through it he discovers a new world, of which previously he had no awareness at all.

It is an experience which cannot enter the perception and understanding of the ordinary person, nor can a person clothe it in words. Only the person who has tasted this reality can comprehend it. The expressive style of the Holy Qur'an is so powerful that only it can bring this close to our understanding, because it is the perfection of the Qur'an that it brings for every reality words suited to its circumstances, which harmonise with the reality of the meaning.

The reality is that disbelief removes a person from the eternal and everlasting reality. That eternal and everlasting reality is such that it has no extinction, it is not hidden, and it does not descend to a depth. Severing relations with the eternal and everlasting reality is, in truth, death for a human being. Such a person can never become active, can never become effective, and cannot gain control over this universe. Therefore such a person is a dead person. His powers and capacities die, and he is by nature a dead human being. This is the reality of death.

In contrast, faith is the name of union and connection with that everlasting power. Faith draws help from that power, and that power accepts its supplication. Therefore faith is life and disbelief is death.

Then, in the state of disbelief, the human soul is deprived of honour and knowledge. It is enveloped in darkness. The limbs of a person and his consciousness are locked. A person is lost in darkness and goes astray. It is faith that truly opens the eyes. It is the best means of perception. Through it steadfastness is granted. It is a light, in every sense of the word light.

Through disbelief a person contracts, and eventually becomes like stone; his thinking becomes narrow, and because of it he is led astray from the natural path. Therefore disbelief is a kind of constriction in which every person is deprived of tranquility, and his heart is always troubled. Whereas faith brings expansion of the breast, joy and ease, and under its pleasant shade tranquility is attained.

The disbeliever's position is like that of a self-grown grass or plant which has no firm existence on this earth and no deep roots. He is an individual who is severed from his Creator and appears alone and isolated. Nor is he connected with this universe; he has no spiritual bond with this universe. He has only a material bond, which is an extremely limited relationship, and this is just as any animal has a natural bond with this universe: merely a sensory bond and sphere.

In contrast, the relationship that exists purely for the sake of Allah connects the mortal human being with the eternal reality and the everlasting reality, and at the same time connects him and makes him in touch with this apparent universe too.

After this, a believer has a deep connection with the caravan of faith and with a community whose roots spread far and wide through human history. Therefore the believer is the owner of a great treasure of relationships. He possesses a vast and great wealth of connections. He has an extremely full and expansive personality. His existence and his personality do not end with the end of his lifespan.

When a person believes, he finds a light in his heart, and through this light he then comes to know the realities of the religion, and he also learns the method of action and the manner of movement of this religion. Extraordinary disclosures take place upon his heart. When a believer finds this light in his heart, he sees wondrous scenes and stations. He sees that there is a profound connection among all the parts of this religion. The realities become clearly visible to him. He sees that the method of action of this religion is extremely deep and extremely beautiful. This religion is not an incoherent collection of scattered beliefs and scattered worship, containing some laws and some directives; rather, this religion is a complete plan. All its parts penetrate one another and are joined to one another, are in harmony with one another, and hold an extremely deep love for one another. All these parts are alive like a single body, and travel together with the nature of this universe, and this journey proceeds with the utmost friendliness, mutual love and deep affection, with the greatest enthusiasm and love.

A person finds this light in his heart, and through it there are disclosed to him the realities of his own self, the realities of his life, the realities that occur on the earth, the realities of people and the realities of the conditions of people. Before their eyes appear extremely bright and dazzling scenes. He also comes to know the divine law (sunnat Allah) operating throughout this universe and its regulations, which operate in an extremely firm, natural and pleasant manner. Then he also understands that behind these laws and regulations the will of Allah is also at work, and it is the will of Allah that has set the divine laws in motion in this universe freely and has provided opportunities for action. Such a person then observes the people of this universe, how they move and act in accordance with the divine laws, but within the limits of the divine laws.

When this light of faith is born in a person's heart, he clearly finds the path of truth in every matter, every event and every problem. Now he can clearly see the divine laws and events operating around him, whether they relate to his own self, relate to his thoughts, or relate to the plans being pursued by various people around him. He also discerns the intentions of his environment, whether these intentions are apparent or hidden. He finds the interpretation and explanation of events clearly within his own intellect and his own self. He can properly interpret all the events that take place, as if he is taking the answer to every matter from the Book of Allah.

The one who possesses this light finds his thoughts, his consciousness and his features also illuminated. He is joyful in his heart, content with his circumstances, and satisfied with his end. He adopts a gentle and pleasant manner when giving instructions. He also confronts events and circumstances with extreme seriousness, and in every condition he is content, hopeful and firm in conviction. This is the reality which the Holy Qur'an depicts in these words, and how beautifully and in what endearing manner.

﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness and cannot emerge from it?﴾ (6:122)

Before this religion, the Muslims were just like this: they were dead. It is Islam that gave their souls expansion and gave them life. It granted them progress, striving, movement and everlasting life, whereas before this their hearts had been dim. Their souls were dark, but when the rain of faith fell upon their hearts, they became like green and flourishing fields. Springs of light began to flow from their souls, and waves of light and illumination began to rise. They began to guide the misguided. They showed the way to bewildered and distressed people, gave tranquility to frightened humanity, freed slaves, and began to determine the direction of the journey of life for people, and to proclaim that the human being had been granted new life. Now he is only a servant of Allah, and he has been freed from every servitude to the world.

The question is: can one in whose soul Allah has infused life be like the person who is surrounded by darkness and for whom there is no way out of it? Certainly the circumstances of these two individuals are very different from one another, and there is a great difference between them. Therefore, who is there who would sit down and settle in this abode of darkness when light is being bestowed all around him?

﴿Thus has it been made attractive to the disbelievers, what they used to do.﴾ (6:122)

This is the real secret. Here the expression for disbelief is darkness and death, and these qualities have been deposited in disbelief by the will of Allah. Then Allah has created among human beings such varieties that some of them love light and some of them love darkness. When someone begins to love darkness, darkness is made beloved to him, and he goes far out into misguidance, to the point that no path of return remains for him. After this, a host of devils from among jinn and humans comes forward, who present to one another evil and misleading things as good. And then they make the deeds of the disbelievers even more attractive. The heart in which there is no light of faith gives careful ear to the words of these devils. It is trapped in the snares of their whisperings. Now it cannot even distinguish between guidance and misguidance, because it is enveloped in darkness. Thus Allah makes the deeds of the disbelievers attractive to them.

In accordance with this principle, Allah has made some criminals in every village into leaders, and they spread the nets of their deceit in those settlements. Thus this scheme of Allah for the trial of human beings is completed, and the decree of Allah accomplishes its work. The requirements of His wisdom are fulfilled, and every person in this world adopts the path which has been made favourable for him, and eventually every person reaches his appointed end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 123:

"And thus have We placed in every town its greatest criminals, that they may plot therein. But they plot only against themselves, and they perceive it not."

"And thus have We placed in every town its greatest criminals so that they may spread their web of deception there. In truth they are themselves caught in the net of their own deceit, but they are not aware of it."

This is the sunnah (established way) of Allah that in every town, city or seat of government He raises up some of its great criminals to positions of authority. These criminal people are such that they are enemies of the religion, and these enemies of the religion are so because they gain power over the towns and use it for their own aims. Religion takes this power away from them and uses it for its own aims. Thus religion strips them of the status of lordship and sovereignty, and people attain freedom. In this way religion places all people in the servitude of Allah, and Allah alone becomes Lord of mankind (Rabb al-Nas) and King of mankind (Malik al-Nas).

It is the sunnah of Allah that He sends the messengers with truth, and that this truth strips all claimants of lordship of their lordship and all claimants of sovereignty of their right to authority. Therefore, despite the truth, these great criminals become enemies of the messengers and of the truth, and they spread the web of their cunning in towns and capitals. All people, from their respective seats of government, give guidance and reports to one another that are based on deception, and these people become helpers of the satans in the battle between truth and falsehood. They keep striving to spread falsehood and misguidance, and because of this outward and secret conspiracy they regard people with contempt.

This is a continuing and all-encompassing battle (sunnah jariyah). This is because the contradiction between the two forces has arisen on the basis of the first principle. The first principle is that judgment and supreme sovereignty belong exclusively to Allah, the Exalted, while the desire of the criminals of any town is that their word should prevail in that town. Besides this, there is also a personal contradiction between the people of truth and these great criminals.

Every prophet has had to face this battle. No prophet can escape it. It is necessary for the prophets and the believers to plunge into this battle, and in the end they emerge from it with success. Allah assures His friends that no matter how great the deception of these criminals may be, and no matter how long their period of power may be, in the end their plotting will fall back upon themselves. This is because the believers do not plunge into this battle alone; Allah is with them, and He is sufficient as a helper for them. He returns the plot of the disbelievers upon themselves. "In truth they are themselves caught in the net of their own deceit, but they are not aware of it."

"And they plot only against themselves, and they perceive it not."

Therefore the believers should remain fully content.

Now the Qur'an explains that the enemies of Allah's messengers and of Allah's religion have a disposition filled with pride and arrogance. And this very pride is the cause that they keep away from Islam, and they flee from this doctrine because in it, just as these great ones are servants of Allah, so too all the common people are servants of Allah; no class distinction remains. Since these people wish to maintain this class distinction and privilege, it is a very bitter draught for such people to believe and to obey the Prophet, although they are accustomed to being obeyed themselves and to occupying the station of divinity and lordship, legislating, and having their laws accepted. They issue commands and people obey their commands. That is why they make statements that are not to be made; they speak with utterly baseless claims, saying: "We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of Allah":

"And when a sign comes to them, they say: 'We will never believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah.'" (6:124)

"When a sign comes to them, they say: 'We will not believe unless we are given the same as what was given to the messengers of Allah.'"

Walid ibn al-Mughirah once said: "If prophethood were a true matter, I would have been more deserving that I be the prophet, for I am older than you, O Muhammad, and I have more wealth than you." And Abu Jahl said: "By God, we will not be pleased with this movement, nor will we obey it, unless Gabriel brings revelation to us in the same way that he brings it to him."

It is not hidden from anyone that pride of the self and the kind of people who are accustomed to issuing orders while others obey are matters through which error is made attractive to people, and thus these people become hostile to the religion and to the callers to the religion (the messengers).

Accordingly, Allah refutes the statements of such people. First, that appointing someone as a messenger depends upon Allah's all-encompassing knowledge of who is worthy of it, since prophethood is an extremely important cosmic office. And second, here Allah refutes them with severity, contempt and warning, that the end awaiting you is very evil indeed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 124:

﴿Allah knows best where to place His message.﴾ ﴿Those who committed crime will soon be struck with humiliation before Allah and severe punishment for the schemes they used to devise.﴾

Prophethood is an extremely great and momentous office. It is a cosmic matter in which the eternal and everlasting Divine will becomes attached to a human being. A connection is established between the higher world and the limited world of man. Heaven and earth come together; this world and the Hereafter become one. In it, the universal principles of truth are applied to human hearts, human events, human history and the practical world. In it, a person separates himself from his own self and becomes wholly and completely Allah's. It is not merely sincerity of intention and action, but the very capacity of that particular person is emptied to receive this great task. The person of the Messenger becomes bound to the Lord; a direct link is established between the Messenger and God. And this connection is possible only when the very nature of the Messenger's being becomes fit and capable for this link. Such capacity is created within him that he is able to receive this message.

Therefore, it is Allah alone who knows and decides where to place the trust of prophethood, and upon which person to place it. For Allah's billions of servants come and go and remain upon this earth; it is Allah who selects one from among these billions.

Those who wish to reach the station of prophethood, or who demand that they be given the religious teachings that were given to the Messengers, yet hold a disposition that is not suitable for a Muslim, because they regard their own selves as the axis of the universe, whereas the disposition of the Messengers is entirely different. The disposition of a Messenger is that he accepts prophethood with great humility and then devotes himself to it. He nurtures his own self within this message, and the office is given to him in circumstances where he has no knowledge of it and is not even a hopeful candidate for it.

﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, but it was a mercy from your Lord.﴾ Secondly, these great men are ignorant and are not even aware of the importance of this office. They are not able to grasp the reality that bestowing this office upon anyone rests solely in the authority of Allah.

It is for these reasons that the Qur'an answers their claim in decisive words:

﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ (6:124)

Since Allah knew, He gave this office to a suitable person. It was entrusted to a most honoured and sincere person. Throughout history He continued the honoured line of Messengers and concluded it with the Seal of the Prophets ﷺ.

After this, Allah threatens these criminals that their end will be humiliating and they will be afflicted with severe punishment.

﴿Those who committed crime will soon be struck with humiliation before Allah and severe punishment for the schemes they used to devise.﴾

They will receive humiliation before Allah because they had elevated themselves among their followers, and because of their arrogance and pride they rejected acceptance of the truth. Along with these evils, they also desired the station of prophethood. And since they spread a web of conspiracy against the Islamic movement, took up enmity against the Messengers and inflicted torment upon the believers, they will be given severe punishment.

Now this passage concludes with a description of the state of affairs when faith is present in the hearts and minds of people, and how, through guidance, the days and nights of a human being are transformed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 125:

"So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whoever He intends to leave astray, He makes his chest tight and constricted, as if he were climbing up into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe." (125)

Allah Almighty has given every person in this world the power of discernment and freedom to choose either misguidance or guidance. Now, whoever, in accordance with this constant Sunnah of Allah which He has established in this universe regarding guidance, is interested in attaining the path and uses the freedom given to him for the purpose of testing, and strives for guidance, then Allah opens his chest to Islam. The doors of his heart are opened, and he accepts Islam with ease, takes interest in it, becomes satisfied with it, and becomes intimately united with Islam.

On the other hand, for the one for whom Allah has decreed misguidance, and this too, in accordance with the same constant Sunnah of Allah, is decreed for the very person who no longer has any interest in Islam and guidance. The doors of his heart are closed, and his chest becomes tight for Islam. His condition becomes such that it is as if his soul is about to ascend into the sky. Thus his heart and mind are closed to him, and he finds it extremely difficult to adopt the path of guidance.

In the words "kaannama yasṣaʿʿadu fi as-samaa'" (as if he were climbing up into the sky), a psychological state is depicted in a sensory manner of expression. Such is the situation in which a person's breath becomes short and he feels constriction in his chest, just as a person feels when climbing to a height. Along with the meaning, according to the recitation of Hafs, the word (yaṣṣaʿʿadu) itself contains a kind of hardship and difficulty, and this word is pronounced with great effort. From the sound of this word itself, one can gauge the difficulties of its meaning. Thus the psychological state of the person, his sensory state, and the manner of expression all become united and of one hue here. (For details see my book At-Tasweer al-Fanni, the discussion on sensory imagination.)

This scene concludes with this closing statement:

"Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe." (125)

The meaning of "thus" is that just as Allah has established His system of destiny and decree in this world, in accordance with it and with the continuous Sunnah of Allah, whoever seeks the path of guidance, Allah opens his chest, and whoever does not like guidance, Allah puts him on the path of misguidance. Thus Allah casts into filth those who do not believe. One of the meanings of "ar-rijs" is punishment, and its meaning also includes filth, impurity, and degradation. That is, whoever becomes trapped in the swamp of this impurity and filth remains in it, and the use of the word rijs is intended to give this indication.

Now we reflect twice on this verse:

"So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his chest for Islam; and whoever He intends to leave astray, He makes his chest tight and constricted, as if he were climbing up into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe." (125)

To properly understand the great truth stated in this verse, namely the Divine will, and all the other verses and texts connected with Allah's will and human deeds and inclinations, in which reward and punishment for human actions are established, or in which the rulings of human guidance and misguidance are established, a logic other than rational and philosophical logic, and a different faculty of perception, is required. This logic and faculty of perception lie beyond our outward reason and logic. The debates that took place in the history of Islamic thought between the Mu'tazila and the Ahl as-Sunnah, between the Ahl as-Sunnah and the Murji'a, and earlier the disputes and controversies within the theology of the Christians, and the logical premises and conclusions established in them, are all beyond that perceptive capacity.

To understand this delicate discussion, we must go a little beyond the rational and logical world of man, and to grasp this truth we must step a little outside the rational and philosophical world and come into the practical life of man. The situation that the Qur'an depicts relates to the practical circumstances of man. It is not related merely to rational and philosophical discussions. The actual conditions of man and his daily intellectual life, and the way they operate practically in this universe, are depicted in these verses. When we look at the practical world of man, we see Allah's power, His will, and man's will, effort and action moving side by side, and their practical field is so intertwined that purely philosophical logic cannot untangle this knot.

If someone says that Allah's will and decree push a person toward guidance or misguidance, this too is not a practical picture; and if it is said that only a person's will and action determine his end, then in practice this is also not so. The reality is connected with both these matters, and it is so subtle and hidden from sight, and so in-between, that on one side there is Allah's absolute will, and on the other side there is man's will and inclination; both move together, and no practical clash occurs between them.

However, the true nature of this beautiful blend of compulsion, free choice and capacity cannot be determined by us through argument or rational thought alone. Nor can we express it clearly in human words and phrases, because human expressions are the form of the real nature of a reality, and when the very reality lies outside the range of logical argument and rational thought, what can expression and style accomplish?

For a correct conception of this great practical reality, it is necessary for a person to experience both the rational and the spiritual world at once. In practice, what happens is that for the one whose natural inclination is toward Islam, Allah opens his heart to Islam. This is definitely an act of Allah, because this expansion of the chest is an event, and no event can occur without Allah's creation. And for the one whose nature is turned toward misguidance, he feels constriction and suffocation in his heart, and upon imagining Islam and guidance he feels difficulty. This too is Allah's doing, because this too is an event, and its occurrence also cannot take place without Allah's creation and, in practice, His will. Both these matters are subject to the will which Allah's Being decrees concerning human beings. But this will of Allah cannot be called coercive will. This will is in accordance with Allah's continuous Sunnah. That Sunnah is that Allah, by granting the human being a specific measure of freedom, has placed him in a trial, and this Sunnah and this decree of Allah carries out its function as a result of the use of that freedom by man. As for guidance and misguidance, these are based on man's own inclination and capacity.

If we bring a rational minor premise against a rational major premise, and do not join with these premises and their disputes the spiritual and inner knowledge, nor include with them the practical and psychological experiences of man, then we cannot bring this great truth within the sphere of our perception. The result of all the debate and controversy on this issue throughout Islamic history has been just this.

Similarly, the outcome of philosophies other than Islam has also been of this kind. Therefore, to understand this issue we must also make use of practical and spiritual taste, a taste which can directly grasp this truth beyond rational minor and major premises.

Now we return again to the context of the Qur'an. This wave of this lesson came as a commentary upon the previous statement. The previous statement was about the lawfulness and unlawfulness of slaughtered animals, but all these matters are in fact different parts of one single package: building religious consciousness within man, proposing law and authority for man, the concept of Allah's sovereignty over man, and bringing all of these within the circle of faith to make them one single package. This is why the subject of faith, disbelief, guidance and misguidance has also been stated in between here. Now, at the end, another comment comes, as a result of which all these matters become interconnected. The totality of these matters is called the Straight Path. If any one of these matters is abandoned, it is as if the person has abandoned the Straight Path. That is, the belief in Tawhid and consciousness is also a part of it, and by walking on this path a person reaches the Abode of Peace (Dar as-Salam). And in the Abode of Peace, Allah is the friend and protector of the believers.

This is the way of your Lord, a straight path. The phrase "your Lord" is extremely reassuring and comforting. It fills the believer's heart with confidence and certainty, and it is good news of a good end. That is, this is the divine sunnah concerning guidance and misguidance, and this is the law of Islam on the lawful and the unlawful. Both are part of the religion of Islam, and this is why, in the context of the Quran, they have been placed together as one unit.

We have indeed explained these verses of Allah most clearly, but only those who will benefit from them will be those who do not forget them but remember them. This is because the heart of the believer is one that remembers, not one that forgets. Moreover, the believer's heart always remains open to guidance. It is alive and listens to speech; it is not like the dead.

Then, for those who remember and take admonition, there is the abode of peace (Dar al-Salam) with their Lord, where they will live in contentment and tranquility. Allah gives the guarantee of this peace and tranquility, and He does not waste the deeds of anyone. He is their Protector and Helper, because they act upon the right path, and their success in the trial of this world is a reward for them.

Here we once again find ourselves standing before a great truth. This truth relates to the ideological aspect of this religion, and it consists of the beliefs of Islam and Allah's right of sovereignty, upon which Allah's straight path is established. This is the true nature of this religion, and upon it Allah, the Lord of the worlds, has established it.
