Lesson No. 69: Explanation of the Verses

128 to 135

Earlier in the lesson it was mentioned that Allah opens the hearts of some people to Islam. Such people have awakened hearts, and they keep remembering Allah. These people enter the Abode of Peace (Dar al-Salam) and live under the guardianship and protection of their Lord. Now the mention is of those who are their opposites. In describing the scenes of the Resurrection, this is the way of the Holy Quran: it presents both sides of the picture before a person. Now the mention is of the daily life of those among humans and jinn who carry out satanic deeds. These are the people who, in the world, lived such a life that they kept telling one another deceptive things, kept deceiving one another, and did this so that people would be led astray. Their conduct has always been that they support one another against the prophets, and they keep giving counsel to one another so that they may dispute with the Muslims concerning matters in which Allah has determined what is lawful and unlawful. The Holy Quran has presented these people in the manner in which someone is seen walking about in a living and moving scene. In this scene, they are seen blaming one another and being extremely hypocritical. In short, in this verse those scenes have come forth in full, in the manner that the Holy Quran everywhere generally adopts when describing the scenes of the Resurrection.

(Verses) 128 to 130.

This scene begins directly with future events, when Allah will gather everyone together around them in the place of assembly. But a provision is made for the listener so that he can see this scene with his own eyes, and it is before him. This imagery and conception come forth through the omission of a single word, "(and He will say)". That is: "And on the day when He gathers them all together (and says): O assembly of jinn..." With the omission of the word "He will say," the meaning stands before the eyes in the form of a scene, and the scene that was to occur in the future actually comes before one. This style of expression is peculiar to the Holy Quran. Now, let us observe the details of this scene.

(Verse) "O assembly of jinn! You have taken a great portion of mankind." (6:128)

"O assembly of jinn! You have thoroughly exploited humankind." That is, you have made a majority of mankind your followers. They walked according to your guidance and signals, believed greatly in your whisperings, and walked upon your plans. This statement of the situation is not merely for the purpose of narrating an event, since the jinn knew well that they had misled a large majority of humans. Rather, the purpose of stating this actual situation is that it is your very great crime that you have misled such a large majority of mankind. The purpose is that, seeing their crime, they should become remorseful. This is why no reply is given here from the side of the jinn. However, those who answer are those who were deceived and who easily fell prey to the whisperings of those devils. They answer thus:

(Verse) "And their friends from among mankind will say: Our Lord! Some of us benefited from others, and we have reached the term which You appointed for us." (6:128)

"And their friends among mankind will say: Our Lord! Some of us have enjoyed the others, and we have reached our appointed term which You have fixed for us." This answer indicates the heedlessness and frivolousness of those negligent ones, and it also clearly shows the path on which Satan misleads humans in this world. That is, while the jinn were deceiving these people, those who were deceived also used them for their own purposes. Thus the jinn made these ideas and conceptions appealing to these people. In this way, these people became entangled in outward and inward immoralities. It means that Satan misleads a person through the path of pleasures. In this way, through this deception and misleading, these devils also enjoyed themselves greatly. Thus Satan made them the prey of his lust, toyed with them, and used them in this world for satanic purposes. Meanwhile, those who were deceived thought that they had misled Satan. Thus they themselves were also engaged in this game, took interest in it, and enjoyed it. This is why they used to say:

(Verse) "Some of us enjoyed the others." (We enjoyed one another greatly.) Thus our this indulgence continued until death, and then sudden death came. And now they realize that this respite was granted by Allah, and that those indulgences they practised were, in fact, fully within Allah's power at that time as well. (And now we have reached the time which You have appointed for us.) At this point, the decisive reply comes from Allah:

(Verse) "He will say: The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide forever, except what Allah wills. Surely your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing." (6:128)

"He will say: Now the Fire is your place of residence; you will remain in it forever, except as Allah wills. Surely your Lord is Wise and Knowing." That is, your place is Hell; here will be your dwelling, and this dwelling will be eternal (except what Allah wills, 6:128). The word "except what Allah wills" (6:128) is used here because Allah's will is absolute and unrestricted. In Islamic concepts and beliefs, the unrestrictedness of Allah's will is a fundamental principle. There is neither any check upon it nor any defect in it, because Allah is All-Wise and All-Knowing, and He directs His will and decree with complete knowledge. Along with His knowledge, wisdom is also present. Before the end of this scene, a comment on this scene appears, and thus a wisdom is placed in our hands.

"Surah al-An'am, verse 129:

"And thus do We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn."

"Behold, in this way (in the Hereafter) We shall make the wrongdoers companions of one another, because of the earnings they used to accumulate (in the world, by joining together with one another)."

That is, it is a matter worthy of admonition that such friendships are established between jinn and humans, and this is the end of such friendship. In this way Allah makes them agreeable to one another. Because of their own earnings they become friends of one another, since their temperaments and desires coincide. Their inclinations and aims are one, and then their end too is alike.

This sequence and the truth it states have far-reaching consequences compared with the present circumstances. It unveils the real nature of the connection and friendship between the human and jinn satans, for those who are wrongdoers and in some form associate partners with Allah unite against truth and guidance, and it is their practice always to confront the Prophet and his companions. Just as the nature and temperament of these people is one, although their forms differ, so too their aims and objectives are one. Their aims and objectives are that they exercise their sovereignty in opposition to Allah, and accept no limit or restraint in matters of carnal desire and debauchery, that is, the limits and restrictions set by Allah.

These people are, in every age, a single group and a single bloc, and they help one another, although among themselves their aims are the same, and because of this they love one another. Therefore, just as was described in the previous scene, their end is also one and the same.

In today's age, for a long time we have been witnessing that human satans, such as the Crusaders, Zionists, idolaters and communists, despite being members of different interests and different blocs, are friends with one another and mutually supportive and helpful. This unity and agreement is against Islam and Islamic movements' ranks, and it exists across the whole world.

In practice this is a frightening alliance. The people forming this alliance are those who have experience of enmity against Islam for centuries. These people, with material and intellectual social forces and all other equipment, are engaged in battle against Islam and are busy with their deceitful satanic schemes. Allah's saying about this alliance applies well today: "And thus We make the wrongdoers allies of one another because of what they used to earn together." This verse, which came to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), also applies to this alliance:

"And had Allah willed, they would not have done it. So leave them and what they invent." 

But the demands of this consolation will be fulfilled only if there exists in the world a group that follows the footsteps of the Messenger (ﷺ), and it is known that this group is the stand-in for the companions of the Messenger (ﷺ), standing in the path of enemies' attacks upon the religion. Now let us return once more to the Qur'anic verses.

(Verse 130) "O assembly of jinn and men! Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves, who recounted My signs to you and warned you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "We bear witness against ourselves." It was the life of this world that deceived them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.

This interrogation is rhetorical (taqriri). It is not asked because Allah wanted to obtain information from these people as to whether messengers had come or not. Allah knew well what had taken place. Their acknowledgment and their testimony are in reality the justification for their punishment. The purpose is to show that this punishment is a just punishment for them, and that they deserve it.

The address is directed to jinn as it is to humans. The question arises: were messengers from among their own kind also sent to the jinn, just as messengers from among humans were sent to humans? The jinn are a hidden creation, and only Allah has knowledge of their true condition. As for this verse, in its interpretation it may be said that the jinn too would listen to the speech revealed upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and would then go and warn their people, and also give glad tidings. The details of this are given by the Qur'an in Surah al-Ahqaf:

"And mention when We turned to you a company of jinn listening to the Qur'an. When they were present, they said, 'Be silent.' And when it was finished, they went back to their people as warners. They said, 'O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path. O our people, respond to the caller to Allah and believe in him; He will forgive you of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment. And whoever does not respond to the caller to Allah will not escape within the earth, and he will not have besides Him any protectors. Those are in manifest error.'" (46:29–32)

It is possible that this question and answer is directed to those humans and jinn who were standing in such a manner. In any case, true knowledge belongs to Allah alone. We cannot say more here, and there is no benefit in debating this matter further.

In any case, those among the jinn and men who were questioned knew that this was not mere inquiry, but rather the formal reading of an indictment. Their record of crimes was being prepared, and this question and answer were solely for rebuke and reproach. Accordingly, they fully confessed and acknowledged what they deserved.

(Verse 130, continued) "They said, 'We bear witness against ourselves.'" Now a commentator appears in this scene and says:

"It was the life of this world that deceived them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers."

This comment fits very well the condition of these people in the world. Indeed, the varied allurements of this worldly life deceived them, and because of this deception they are afflicted with disbelief. Now, on the Day of Resurrection, after seeing everything, they are compelled to bear witness against themselves, because there is no hope of gaining anything by denial and obstinacy here. What more despairing state could there be than for a person to find himself in circumstances where he cannot even defend himself, has no capacity to deny, and has no excuse or pleading to offer?

Now observe the manner of expression of the Holy Qur'an. The pictorial depiction of the Resurrection that the Qur'an presents has no equal. Events to occur in the future are drawn in such a way that a person feels the scene running on a screen. Instead of the future, the Qur'an uses the past tense for these scenes, as if these scenes have already been shown.

We are reading this Qur'an in this world, indeed today we are reading it, and the Resurrection has not yet occurred. We are still on this earth, yet it appears as though this scene is before our eyes, indeed as though we have already seen this scene. A story of a seen scene is being related, and we refresh it through our memory. A person forgets that this scene is yet to come. Yet the matter is spoken of as though some historical event is being repeated.

(Verse 130, repeated) "It was the life of this world that deceived them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers."

This is one of the wonders of the expression of imagination.

Now this scene ends, and the direction of speech turns back to the Holy Prophet ﷺ. Addressing him, the believers are made to understand, and after the believers, the believers who will come until the Day of Resurrection are told that in this end of jinn and men there is a lesson for you. This great creation that is heading toward Hell, and whom you see in this scene confessing their crime against themselves, admit that indeed messengers came and recited to us Allah's complete guidance. We were warned in advance of this evil end. The believers are warned that Allah does not do injustice to anyone; rather He establishes proof against them, and through the messengers He tries to awaken them from the sleep of heedlessness. He gives glad tidings and also warns of the evil end.

(Verse) No. 131.

It is part of the mercy of God that He does not punish people for polytheism (shirk), disbelief (kufr) and disobedience until He has conveyed His message to them through the messengers, although God had placed within the nature (fitrah) of people the capacity to turn towards their Lord and seek Him of their own accord. This arrangement was made because human nature sometimes loses the right path. Beyond human natural inclinations, God also granted man a distinction by giving him the faculty of reason; yet God sent messengers despite this faculty of reason, because reason too is at times suppressed as a result of carnal desires. Moreover, within the observation and contemplation of this universe there were countless proofs that invited man to reflection, but the rational and perceptive faculties of man are at times rendered inactive.

For these reasons, God linked human nature, human reason and human observation with the call of the messengers so that these faculties of man could be protected from corruption. This is why God punishes people only when the call of the messengers has reached them and the proof (hujjah) has been established against them.

From this reality it becomes clear how merciful and generous a treatment God accords to man. It also becomes clear that man cannot find the path of guidance by relying solely on his power of perception and his rational faculties. Nor can he attain certainty, nor can he, through reason and perception, bring his carnal faculties under the discipline of a rule. These faculties can function only when they are backed by the strength of religion and faith.

After this, God mentions another important principle regarding reward and punishment, and this principle applies to the believers as well as to jinn and devils alike.

(Verse) "No. 132.

Believers too have ranks, one above another. Satans too have ranks, one above another. And the deeds of all people are recorded, and Allah is not unaware of them.

﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾ (132)

Allah sent Messengers to His servants. This is purely out of His bounty that He did so, because He is the Self-Sufficient King. He has no need of their faith, nor any need of their worship and servitude. If they become righteous, they will become so for their own good, in this world and in the Hereafter. Similarly, the manifestation of Allah's mercy is also, in this world, in the form of respite: Allah gives the disobedient a respite in this world, whereas He has full power to destroy them all and bring in another people and generation in their place."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 133:

(Verse) "No. 133."

People should bear in mind that they live in this world solely by the mercy of Allah. Their remaining here depends upon the will of Allah. The power and wisdom they possess has been bestowed upon them by Allah. This is not true power of their own; it is a granted power. They are not self-sufficient, because no person has any control over his own creation, his own existence, or his survival in this universe. Whatever power has been given to a human being, he has no authority over it. It is very easy for Allah to remove them from here and bring other peoples in their place. Do they not see that Allah Himself brought them into existence here in place of other peoples, and by His power gave them authority and strength here in place of those other peoples?

These are extremely severe warnings, and they shake the minds and hearts of human beings with great force. Especially [addressed are] those who are unjust and associate partners with Allah, and those jinn who spread a net of deceit, who lay hands upon people, who spread the throne of power, who declare things lawful and unlawful by themselves, who transgress against the Shari'ah of Allah and make laws on their own. All these people are within the power of Allah; as long as He wills, they will remain, and when He wills, He will remove them from this world and bring other peoples in their place. Through these warnings, Allah also gives consolation to the believers: although injustices are inflicted upon them, plots are hatched against them, and they are persecuted, their enemies do not prevail over Allah. This is a trial, and Allah can at any time wipe out them and their cunning from the face of the earth, and this is the final blow.

(Verse 134)

You are in the power of Allah, and you are dependent on His will. You cannot step outside the sphere of His will, nor can you be defiant against Allah. The scenes of the Resurrection, a glimpse of which you have already seen, are awaiting you. These scenes are going to come before you in practice. You will not be able to escape from them, because the system of Allah is extremely powerful and firm.

Now these remarks and conclusions end with a very severe warning, whose profound effects are felt.

(Verse) 135.

This is an extremely firm warning, based on truth and backed by the strength of truth. It is a warning spoken through the Prophet ﷺ, who is washing his hands of their affairs. He is certain that he is upon the truth, certain that his method and system are based on truth, and firmly certain that his opponents are upon misguidance and that their end will be evil. And it is this: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾

This is because it is an unchanging principle that the polytheists, who associate partners with Allah and take them as their protectors, will not prosper, since no one other than Allah can be a helper of anyone, nor can anyone other than Him grant victory. Those who turn away from the guidance of Allah have gone very far into the highest degree of misguidance, and they are in utter loss.

Now, before speaking in the second part of this surah, it is appropriate to reflect a little upon this lesson. The discussion before this lesson concerned slaughtered animals over which Allah's name had not been mentioned, and after this lesson there is a discussion about the vows and offerings concerning fruits, livestock and offspring. Between these two partial matters, this lesson consists of purely theoretical and doctrinal discussions, and in it the issues and scenes of faith and disbelief are described. In this middle lesson, the struggle between humans and jinn, and between the prophets and their enemies, is mentioned, and all the great doctrinal issues that are generally described in this surah are raised.

What we must see is how the Qur'an applies these partial matters of life to the doctrinal foundation of Islam in accordance with the Shariah, and how it gives importance to ensuring that the doctrinal background of every issue does not slip from view. That doctrinal foundation is that the Lord and Sovereign of this universe is Allah alone, and it is He who determines the limits of the lawful and the unlawful. The question is why the Qur'an repeatedly restates its foundational doctrine again and again. The reason is that the Qur'an, in principle, declares this to be the basic doctrine of Islam. The basic doctrine of Islam rests upon the testimony of faith (La ilaha illa Allah). Through this testimony, Islam removes all other divinities from the hearts of Muslims and establishes in their hearts only the belief in the divinity and sovereignty of Allah. Thus Islam takes away the right of sovereignty from all people and establishes the sovereignty of Allah alone. Legislation is a matter in which, whether a law is small or large, the sovereign right of Allah is exercised. This is the right which a Muslim exclusively assigns to Allah, and for all other people he negates this right. In Islam, the meaning of religion is that in all matters of life, whether they relate to beliefs and ideologies, such as divinity and sovereignty, or practical affairs, obedience and servitude are to be rendered to Allah alone, and the right of legislation belongs to Allah alone. In this way, the right of law also belongs only to the law of Allah. Thus the religion of a Muslim is that he rejects all obediences and leaderships and accepts only the obedience and leadership of Allah.

This is why the Qur'an repeats these doctrinal matters again and again and gives them great importance, and arranges all matters upon these principles, as is clearly visible throughout this complete surah. As we said at the beginning of the surah, this surah is entirely Meccan, and in the Meccan surahs the Muslim community did not face any problem of legislation. Yet in this surah, on the doctrinal and theological level, it is clearly indicated that the right of legislation belongs to Allah alone, and this is a great and foundational doctrinal principle of Islam and of the Islamic religion, upon which this religion stands. (1) (See Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami, the chapter on Divinity and Servitude.)

Lesson No. 70, Part One:
This lesson, which is rather long, and the lesson before it and the commentary that follows it, relate to the Islamic doctrine of sovereignty. These are in a surah that was revealed in Mecca, while it is known that the subject of Meccan surahs is generally related to beliefs and doctrines. In the Meccan surahs, legislation was not touched upon; the only things said about legislation in those surahs were matters related to the principles of law. In Mecca there was no Islamic government in existence that would need legislation, and Allah did not wish to mention the Shariah merely as a story or history. Nor at that time was the Islamic Shariah merely a subject of academic discussion and research. Islam wanted a society that could practically enter fully into Islam, in which people were ready to give themselves, their whole lives, to the servitude of Allah and to the leadership of the Shariah. Therefore legislation in Islam could not take place until an Islamic government was established and began to make decisions among people according to the law of Allah. The situation should not be one in which orders come from one side while they are being enforced upon people on the other, because the very nature of Islam is that it is a practical system, and it implements its legal system with seriousness, dignity and gravity.

But I say that although this lesson is in a Meccan surah, it is connected with the issue of legislation. From this it is known that Islam gives very great importance to legislation and regards legislation as one of the foundational matters of this religion.

Before we go into the details of this lesson, it will be appropriate, in the manner of Zilal al-Quran, to cast a general glance over this whole lesson and see what its meaning is and what guidance it gives.

It begins with the fact that the polytheists of Mecca held certain notions and superstitions concerning fruits, livestock and offspring. They had some financial and some social notions which, in the age of ignorance, had the status of belief and law. These notions and superstitions consisted of the following matters:

1. The provision Allah had given them in the form of crops and livestock, they divided into two portions. One portion was for Allah, and they claimed that Allah had reserved this portion for Himself. Another portion they assigned to their partners. These partners were the deities they invoked, whom they associated with Allah in matters of their own persons, their wealth and their children.

﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of crops and cattle, and they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, and "this is for our partners."﴾ (6:136)

2. Then they would encroach upon the portion they had assigned to Allah by their own claim: they would take something from it and add it to the portion of their partners, but they did not treat the portion of their partners in the same way.

﴿So what was for their partners does not reach Allah, but what was for Allah reaches their partners.﴾ (6:136)

3. Their partners had made the killing of their children attractive to them. This was the work of the soothsayers present in their society, who made their laws and invented rituals for them so that people were compelled to act upon them. On the one hand there was social pressure upon them, and on the other they themselves wished to do such things under the aspect of religious rites. For example, they killed girls out of poverty and shame, and sometimes they also killed children as a vow, just as Abd al-Muttalib had vowed that if he had ten sons who reached maturity, he would sacrifice one of them to the gods.

﴿And thus their partners have made the killing of their children seem fair to many of the polytheists, in order to ruin them and to confuse their religion for them.﴾ (6:137)

4. These people placed prohibitions upon certain animals and certain crops. They said that their eating depended solely upon the permission of Allah, and this was their claim. Some riding animals' backs they did not regard as lawful to ride. Over some they did not consider it lawful to mention Allah's name at slaughter, or, if they rode them during the season of pilgrimage, they did not mention Allah's name, because they said these were pilgrimage mounts and Allah's remembrance was in them. They would say that this was Allah's command.

﴿And they say, "These are cattle and crops set apart; none may eat of them except whom we wish," by their claim; and there are cattle whose backs are forbidden, and cattle over which they do not mention Allah's name, fabricating against Him.﴾ (6:138)

5. They said that the unborn young of certain animals was only for males and was forbidden to their women, but if it was born dead, then men and women would share equally in it. They also regarded this ridiculous law as coming from Allah.

﴿And they say, "What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives, but if it is dead, then they may share in it." He will surely requite them for their attribution; indeed He is Wise and Knowing.﴾ (6:139)

The aforementioned notions, claims and customs give a clear idea of the state of Arab society before Islam, and through the reforms of this surah in Mecca the Qur'an seeks to eradicate them.

It is purifying the minds and hearts of the Arabs from these false claims and erasing them from the ignorant society of Arabia. The Qur'an, with its own method of reform, is clearing this jungle of false notions very gently and gradually.

• First, it told people that those who were killing their children for various reasons were foolish. They were devoid of knowledge and understanding, and they were depriving themselves of the blessing of offspring. Moreover, by doing this in the name of Allah, they also committed the crime of fabricating against Allah's flawless essence. The Qur'an declared that this is sheer misguidance and that all these claims are entirely false.

• After that, the Qur'an explained to them that all these possessions in which they dispose are in reality created by Allah. It is Allah who created for you various gardens, vineyards and palm groves. It is He who created all your livestock, and He who provides sustenance to all. In short, He is the Owner, and He alone has the right to legislate for people concerning all the things He created in this world as provision. In the course of this explanation, the Qur'an employs scenes that affect humans: fruit gardens, flourishing fields, palm groves and vineyards, and animals which serve as excellent and beautiful mounts, whose wool and hair are used for carpets, whose flesh is eaten, whose hides serve many benefits. At this point it also clearly conveys the impression that there has been enmity between humans and Satan from the very first day, so they should never follow the footsteps of their enemy, since he is an open enemy.

• Then it is explained that their foolish notions about certain animals are devoid even of basic logic. These notions and beliefs are presented in such a way that at first sight they appear contemptible, weak and worthless. After this clarification, they are asked why they follow these baseless laws and customs. By what proof do they say that these animals and these crops are protected, that only those whom we wish may eat them, when this restriction is their own invention? Then there are animals on which riding and carrying loads are forbidden, and animals over which they do not mention Allah's name, and all this they have fabricated against Allah. Allah asks: were you present when Allah made these laws? Or was it a secret matter which Allah told only you, or was this command only for you? He says that all this is fabrication and unjust misleading of people, and that for this fabrication and misguidance Allah will hold them accountable.

• At this point Allah makes clear what is forbidden and what is lawful, and why certain things were forbidden to the Jews, and what is forbidden to Muslims, and what things, although previously forbidden to the Jews, have now been made lawful.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 135 (part 2 of 2):

٭ After this, their argument is refuted, the argument that they make: that if Allah had willed, they would not have fallen into this jahiliyyah, and thus would not have set for themselves the principles of lawful and unlawful and committed shirk.

﴿Had Allah willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have made anything unlawful﴾ (6:148)

Thus Allah says:

That this statement and this argument have always been presented by all the disbelievers, but among the nations in history who have made this argument, they could not escape Our punishment.

﴿Thus did those before them deny until they tasted Our punishment﴾ (6:148)

From these verses it is established that to consider anything unlawful on one's own, without any shariah, is equivalent to associating partners with Allah. Those who have always denied the signs of Allah have done exactly this. Allah then asks them by what logic they make such decisions and arguments.

﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow nothing but assumption, and you only conjecture"﴾ (6:148)

٭ After this, they are invited to present a scholarly proof for their position, but if they give false arguments, they are to be completely rejected. At the beginning of this surah too, in the discussion of the fundamental beliefs, this same command was given: that the connection with these people should be severed. In both places the wording of the subject shows very little variation, which indicates that shirk in Allah's essence and shirk in Allah's sovereignty hold the same rank. Whoever legislates apart from Allah, or accepts someone as a legislator, also commits shirk.

﴿Say: "Bring forth your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this." Then if they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who have denied Our signs, and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who set up equals to their Lord﴾ (6:150)

The scenes, expressions and words of these verses and the previous verses are the same. Those who legislate on their own are followers of their own desires, and these are the same people who deny the signs of Allah, and these are the same people who do not have faith and certainty in the Hereafter. If they had truly accepted the signs of Allah, believed in the Hereafter, and acknowledged the guidance of Allah, they would not have made laws for themselves and for others on their own, nor would they have declared anything unlawful apart from the commands of Allah.

٭ And at the end, Allah tells about the things that He has actually made unlawful. In it all the principles of social life are explained, namely the Oneness of Allah, the commands and limits and obligations of Allah, but mostly the things that are forbidden are enumerated... Thus Allah prohibited shirk, commanded kindness to parents, and prohibited killing children out of fear of poverty and [stated] that Allah is the Provider, and the prohibition of approaching the property of an orphan except in a lawful manner, and the command to keep weights and measures accurate, and to act with justice in speech and in dealings even if the matter concerns relatives, and to fulfil the covenant of Allah. All these matters have been declared a command from Allah, and the commandment regarding these matters has been repeated again and again.

All these matters are the fundamental principles of the Islamic vision of life and the basic foundations of the shariah. They have been gathered in a single discourse and presented in a closely linked and organized manner. All these commands have been brought in one sentence, one group and one social form. From this, the social outlook of the Qur'an becomes well understood and the methodology of Islam also becomes clear, so at the end of this lesson it is said:

﴿And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other paths, for they will scatter you away from His way. This He has enjoined upon you, that you may become righteous﴾ (6:153)

This last sentence was said so that the real purpose of the whole lesson becomes fully visible, and the matter is gathered into a single phrase, becoming clear and decisive. In the religion of Islam, both belief and law are connected to tawhid and shirk. Indeed, shirk can be committed in Islamic legislation just as it can occur in belief, because in Islam legislation is itself belief, since Islamic law is in fact the detailed explanation and elaboration of the belief in tawhid. This reality is clear from many texts of the Qur'an, and it is stated in many places in accordance with the style of Islamic expression.

This is the true position from which the meaning of religion has moved away due to long historical processes, and this process was completed over a long period. To achieve this goal, vile and mean methods were employed. Today the situation is that the enemies of religion are indeed enemies, but even among those who work for religion and its fervent workers, this reality has become hidden from their minds. Even the supporters of religion consider the belief in the sovereignty of Allah separate from Islamic beliefs, and the supporters of religion are no longer as fervent about the issue of the sovereignty of Allah as they are for the well-known religious beliefs. They do not regard the denial of the belief in the sovereignty of Allah as a denial of religion, in the way that they regard the denial of the belief in the Oneness of Allah and the denial of the worship of Allah as a denial of religion, although the religion of Islam has nowhere separated the belief in servitude and the shariah from one another. The concept of the Islamic vision of life has been extracted through long historical and gradual conspiracies, and this work has been carried out with great cunning and experience, until the belief in the sovereignty of Allah has taken its present form. Even the fervent supporters of Islam have ceased to be its supporters, although this reality is clearly stated in this surah, despite the fact that this surah is a Meccan surah and its subject is not constitution and law but rather the belief in Tawhid and the Islamic vision of life. Nevertheless, all aspects of this point have been taken up and all details have been given, and this too in the context that the discussion was about a partial issue of social life, but since this partial issue was connected to a principle, to a theoretical and constitutional matter, and this principle is the foundation of the religion, therefore emphasis is laid upon it here.

People pronounce the charge of shirk upon the worshipper of idols, but they do not pronounce the charge of shirk upon those who get their decisions made through tyrannical courts. They abstain from idol worship, but they do not abstain from obedience to tyrannical rulers. These people recite the Qur'an, but they do not understand the temperament of this religion. They should read the Qur'an in the manner in which it was revealed. They should reflect upon this verse:

﴿And if you obey them, indeed you are associators﴾ (6:121)

These fervent supporters of Islam try to satisfy themselves and others by raising only some partial matters for discussion, saying that such and such law is against Islam, or such and such part of such and such law is against Islam. Their zeal is confined to some partial matters, or they restrict themselves to correcting some bad practices, and from their conduct it appears that although Islam is standing in its entirety, some partial matters have remained deficient, and only the correction of these matters will complete it.

Those who have zeal for the religion of Islam and are its fervent supporters are in reality a source of distress for this religion, but they do not realize it. Rather, by giving importance to these kinds of partial and unimportant matters, these people stab religion in the back.

The theoretical strength and fervour that exists in the Muslim ummah at present, these people spend upon such unimportant matters, and incidentally they lend support to the present-day jahili social system and jahili society. They practically testify that the religion is established, and that if there is any deficiency, it is only these partial faults which they wish to remove, whereas the real situation is that the religion is completely suspended, and at present the existing society is wholly a jahili society. In it the sovereignty of Allah is not in operation, that sovereignty in which no one is a partner with Allah.

The religion of Islam will be established when the sovereignty of Allah is enforced on earth. As long as the sovereignty of Allah is not established, the religion cannot be fully established. Today the problem on this earth is simply that tyrannical systems have been established here, who by aggression have seized the sovereignty of Allah. They have taken this authority into their own hands and have begun to determine what is lawful and unlawful for people, and they make laws concerning people's property and children.

In the verses under discussion and the statements, this very difficult matter has been taken up in an extremely effective manner and in extreme detail. All matters have been linked with the concepts of the sovereignty of Allah and servitude, and they have been declared to be the issue of kufr and Islam and the issue of Islam and jahiliyyah.

The great struggle after which Islam established its existence in this world was not merely a struggle against atheism, such that a person accepts God and becomes bound by some religious rituals and becomes a supporter of religion. Nor was this struggle merely a reformist movement against social corruption and moral corruption. Although these matters were also included in that struggle, these movements continued even after the establishment of religion. The struggle which Islam undertook for its own existence was the struggle for the establishment of the sovereignty of Allah on this earth. In Mecca, people understood that the meaning of "La ilaha illallah" is that there is no sovereign except Allah. At that time in Mecca, the Qur'an firmly established this concept in the minds of the Muslims. The Qur'an had thoroughly impressed upon the conscience of the Muslims and within their hearts and minds this concept, that the sovereign is Allah alone, although in Mecca there was no opportunity for a system of the sovereignty of Allah and a system of Islamic law. It did not occur to any Muslim that anyone other than Allah could be a sovereign, and if anyone conceived of it, he could not be a believer. When this concept settled firmly in the hearts and minds of the Muslims in Mecca, then in Medina the sovereignty of Allah was established on the basis of this concept. If this thought takes root in the minds of the fervent supporters of religion of our age, they should reflect upon their conduct: what are they doing, and what ought they to be doing? ...... I think this commentary on the lesson is sufficient. Now observe the explanation of the verses.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 136:

Verse No. 136.

After describing the customs of the Jahili (pre-Islamic ignorant) society regarding crops and cattle, it is here stated that the Creator of these crops and cattle is Allah, and it is He who provides the means of sustenance for people from the heavens and the earth. But after understanding and accepting these realities, consider for a moment how you people treat the sustenance that Allah has bestowed: that they set aside one portion of it for Allah and assign the other portion to their idols. (It is obvious that it is the custodians of the idols who are entitled to take the portion meant for the idols.) Now, with the portion of Allah they engage in the insulting treatment whose details are given within the verse.

It is narrated from Hadrat Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) that when they brought the grain, they would make it into a heap. From it they would set aside one part for Allah and one for the idols. Now, when a strong wind blew and the grains from the idols' portion were blown and mixed into the portion of Allah, they would separate them from that portion and return them to the portion of the idols. And if the wind came from the side of Allah's portion and grains from Allah's portion mixed into the portion of the idols, they would leave them as they were. Concerning this, the following verse was revealed:

﴿Evil is that which they decide.﴾ (6:136)

It is narrated from Mujahid that they would dedicate one part of the field to Allah and one part they would specifically reserve for their idols. Now, if the wind carried something from Allah's part into the idols' part, they would leave it as it was; but if something from the idols' part went into Allah's part, they would return it. And they would say: "Allah is free of this need." And among the cattle they had designated the Saibah and the Bahirah.

It is narrated from Hadrat Qatadah: The people of misguidance decided to make one part of their cattle and crops the right of Allah and one part the right of the idols. Now, if something from Allah's portion got mixed into the idols' portion, they would leave it; and if something from the idols' portion fell into Allah's portion, they would return it. And if at any time there was drought, they would withhold Allah's portion and use it themselves, but they would keep the idols' portion intact in every circumstance. About this Allah said:

﴿Evil is the decision that they make.﴾ (6:136)

Hadrat Suddi says that they would make shares of their wealth, and from the crops too they would fix a portion for Allah; similarly, a portion was fixed for the idols. The portion of the idols they would spend on the idols, and the portion of Allah they would give in charity. Now, if an animal that was part of the idols' portion died by chance, and Allah's portion became larger, they would say: "Our gods also need expenses," and so they would take from Allah's portion and spend it on the partners they had set up with Allah. And if the crop of Allah's portion was ruined and the crop of the idols' portion became greater, they would say: "If Allah had willed, He would have made His portion good." Thus they would not make up the shortfall of Allah's portion from the idols' portion. Allah the Exalted says: "If these people were truthful, they would certainly not have done this, for these people take from My portion but do not include it in My portion." And this is the meaning of: ﴿Evil is that which they decide.﴾ (6:136)

Ibn Jarir, in his commentary on ﴿Evil is that which they decide﴾ (6:136), writes: This is information from Allah about these people, that they make evil decisions. Allah says that the decision they made was extremely wrong: they gave My portion to those whom they had, in their own opinion, made My partners, and moreover, from the portion of these supposed partners they give Me nothing. This alone is sufficient proof that these people are both misguided and ignorant. They have left the path of truth aside, for when they do not deal justly with their Creator and Provider, with whom will they deal justly, especially when He has bestowed countless favours upon them? They make Allah equal to idols that cannot benefit or harm. Rather, they have given the idols precedence over Allah, by declaring their portion greater than Allah's portion.

This was the very thing that the devils among men and jinn would whisper to their friends, so that they would keep disputing with the believers about cattle and crops. It is obvious that the outlook which these devils give to people always contains some interest of those devils. The interest of the human devils (who are from among the soothsayers, custodians, and chiefs) is that first they overpower the hearts and minds of these people, and after establishing this influence, they move them in their desired direction, in exact accordance with the outlook they have given, which is composed of false notions and corrupt beliefs. Thus, by misguiding these common people, they also obtain their own material gain; for example, the portions these self-deceived common people set aside for the idols actually go to those very people who give them this notion. The interest of the devils among the jinn is that they cast whisperings into the hearts of people to misguide them, and by leading them they ruin both their worldly life and their Hereafter.

The concepts that existed in the Arab Jahiliyyah are also found in the other Jahiliyyahs present in the world, for example among the Greeks, Persians, Romans, and the other Jahiliyyahs of Africa and Asia. These concepts exercise financial disposals in all Jahiliyyahs, and they are present in every Jahiliyyah. For example, the Jahiliyyah of the modern age also permits such financial dispositions as Allah has not permitted. Therefore, in this shirk the Jahiliyyah of the modern age is exactly equal to the Jahiliyyahs of earlier times; both rest upon the same principle. For example, the definition of Jahiliyyah is: any disposition carried out in the lives of common people while Allah has not permitted it. Now, it is another matter that in earlier times the form and nature of such dispositions were different, and today they are somewhat different. The principle is one, and the forms are different.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 137:

Verse 137.

Just as their partners (shuraka') and their satans have made attractive to these people the killing of their children, so too have they made these practices attractive to them regarding their wealth and their crops. They used to bury their daughters alive out of fear of poverty, or because they would become captives in war and be a source of shame for them. Sometimes they also killed their children as a vow (nadhr). It is narrated from Hadrat Abdul Muttalib that he vowed that if Allah granted him ten sons who would become his strength and support, he would sacrifice one of them.

All these matters had been firmly established in their hearts and minds by their jahili customs. These customs of the Jahiliyyah were those which people had devised for themselves. The partners mentioned in this verse refer to the satans of jinn and mankind. Among humans, the satans were the soothsayers (kuhhan), custodians (mujawirin) and chiefs. Among the jinn were those who became friends of certain humans and helped them. The clear aim of these satans mentioned in this verse is as follows:

﴿to lead them to ruin and to confuse their religion for them﴾ (6:137)

That is, they destroy them and make their religion ambiguous and confused for them, in such a way that they cannot understand it clearly. One instance of ruin is that they kill their children. Another instance is that their collective life becomes opposed to Islam, and they become like cattle in their society, which those satans drive wherever they wish, according to their own aims and interests, to the extent that these satans even acquire the authority to kill and destroy the wealth, children and even the lives of those cattle. For these cattle there is no option but to obey completely. This is because the excessive notions attached to religion and belief, which in reality are not part of religion, have become very deep-rooted, and now religious people are under their heavy pressure. Since these notions have become attached to religion through the customs existing in society, this custom also stands behind them, and the pressure of these customs on society becomes so great that the common people (awam al-nas, kal-an'am) cannot resist it, unless one of them firmly holds on to the foundations of true religion and his grip on the Qur'an and Sunnah is firm.

These ambiguous and complicated notions of a religious hue, which people regard as religion, and these collective customs through which these notions are nurtured and which have become a crushing burden upon the common people, are not confined to the forms that existed in the jahiliyyahs of ancient times. In the most recent jahiliyyah of the modern age, these notions are also clearly present. These customs, which in the modern age too are a heavy burden on the common people and because of which the life of the masses has become miserable, have become necessities for people, and now there is no way left for people to escape from their grip. People have made special dress obligatory upon themselves, and sometimes they spend on it money they do not have. These customs devour people's lives. All their desires are reduced to dust, their morals are destroyed, yet they observe them in every circumstance. Morning dress, afternoon dress, evening dress, mini skirts, teddy outfits and ridiculous clothing, all kinds of make-up and adornment. Some people do these things, and some get others to do them. Among those who cause them to be done are the great clothing merchants, large companies, and the usurious agents of banks and financial institutions, and those merchants who make people do these things so that they may enjoy the profit that results. Behind this entire situation lies a Jewish conspiracy, and the Jews have set up this situation so that through it they may rule over people economically and politically. But the Jews do not do this work through weapons and armies; rather they do it through the weapons of ideas, notions and theories, and they achieve this rule through the pressure of common custom. It is well known that ideas have no effect until they take the form of a system of government and assume a collective shape, and penetrate the structure of society. Thus, these Jews spread and propagate these jahili ideas and notions within society with a grand scheme.

All the satans of society do this work, those satans who are among the jinn and also among mankind. All this work in jahiliyyah, whose forms and shapes differ, but whose principles, roots and foundations are one and the same. If we think that the Qur'an has discussed and criticised only the jahiliyyahs of ancient times and has no connection with the jahiliyyahs of the modern age, then we would be diminishing the dignity of the Holy Qur'an. The truth is that the Holy Qur'an discusses all ancient and modern jahiliyyahs. It confronts the society that deviates in every age and brings it back to set it on the straight path.

Despite the fact that this is a great social burden and conspiracy, the Qur'an, in order to ease the resolution of the problem of jahiliyyah, reveals the truth that all these satans and their friends are in Allah's hand, and that what they are doing they are not doing by their own power and ability. They are doing this work because Allah has granted them respite for the short life of this world. What these people are doing here, they are doing within the sphere of Allah's power and with Allah's will; if Allah's will were not there, they would certainly not do it. Therefore, there is no cause for concern. Let them be left to their course.

﴿And had Allah willed, they would not have done it; so leave them and what they fabricate﴾ (6:137)

﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have done it; so leave them to their fabrications.﴾

They are not saying this on their own; indeed, they claimed that all these notions and practices were from Allah and that they were a sharia for them. According to their assumption, they said that these notions and practices were the sharia of Hadrat Isma'il (peace be upon him) and Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

Today, in the age of modern jahiliyyah too, the attitude of the satans is the same. Most of them do not have the audacity to outright deny the existence of the Creator as the communists did. But they treat religion in the same way as the people of the ancient jahiliyyah did. These people say that we deeply respect religion and faith, and that the foundation of the laws they prescribe also lies in the religion of Islam. But the method and conduct of these people is more cunning and more painful than that of outright deniers of God and communists. These people greatly fear the dormant sentiment of religion among Muslims, which flows through their veins and souls, even though that sentiment may not be the true sentiment of Islam, because complete Islam is a whole system of life. It is not merely a hidden sentiment, nor an extinguished spark. Thus these people wish to escape the anger and wrath of Muslims. This is an extremely cunning ploy and a most painful situation for Islam.

Now look at the condition of these ignorant supporters of religion. They spend their energies on peripheral matters, abandoning the fundamental aims of the Islamic system of life. Within this jahili situation they do not see that by encroaching upon the sovereignty of Allah, shirk is being committed, and through unthinking zeal they make the present polytheistic system into an Islamic situation. Through this approach they give the impression that the present circumstances are in effect Islamic circumstances, and that there is only a difference of minor details between these circumstances and the condition of the Islamic world.

Because of this attitude, these ignorant friends of Islam, the religious classes and those apparently passionate supporters of Islam, prolong this non-Islamic situation, which is entirely non-Islamic and which has enveloped the Islamic world, although through such conduct the aims of the enemies of Islam are being fulfilled. These services are performed by those who have put on the special religious dress of Islam, although the Islamic system has never had any special religious class such that only they could speak about Islam. Islam has no priest (kahin), nor is there any room in it for a clergyman such that no one but they could speak about Islam.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 138:

Verse No. 138.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari says: Concerning these ignorant people, Allah informs us that they used to declare certain things lawful and certain things unlawful on their own, although Allah had not given these people any legislative authority.

In the verse, the word ḥijr (حجر) means "forbidden." These people, who encroached upon Allah's right of legislation and His right of sovereignty, claimed that this was the Shariah of Allah, which is a crime. They had set aside a portion of their crops and certain kinds of livestock for their gods, as we have already said before. They used to say that these fruits and livestock were forbidden for them, and that only the person whom Allah permitted could eat them. All these statements were merely their own assumption, and it is evident that, in their religion, permission was then granted only to soothsayers, custodians of shrines and certain chieftains. Then they also made some of the livestock forbidden to themselves in the same manner, which has been mentioned in Surah al-Ma'idah: "Allah has not appointed any animal as baḥīrah, sā'ibah, waṣīlah or ḥām" (cf. 5:103). They decided on their own that riding these animals was forbidden. Similarly, they decreed that Allah's name should not be taken over certain animals, that is, at the time of riding, at the time of milking and at the time of slaughtering them; rather, the names of the gods for whom they had been set aside were to be taken over them.

Ibn Jarir, in his explanation of the phrase "fabricating lies against Allah," says that these people, by declaring certain things forbidden and then saying that this is the law revealed by Allah, have fabricated a lie against Allah and told a falsehood about Him, because by declaring certain things forbidden on their own, they attributed that to Allah. In this verse, Allah refuted this claim, that He had not done so. Thus Allah declared them liars, and informed the Prophet ﷺ and the believers that these people are liars.

Here we come to know what the features of jahiliyyah are. Most jahiliyyahs share the characteristic that some people, with audacity, declare this world to be mere matter, and others, although they do not go so far in shamelessness and do not deny God altogether, say that religion is merely the name of belief. It is not a system of life, a social structure, or a political or economic system that can take the whole of life within its jurisdiction.

The second characteristic of jahiliyyah is that every jahiliyyah establishes a particular worldly system in which sovereignty and supreme authority belong to someone other than Allah. However, every jahiliyyah claims that it respects religion and that it takes its features from religion itself. The truth is that the approach of any jahiliyyah is extremely dangerous and based on deep cunning and trickery. World Christianity and world Zionism have adopted this very policy in that region which was once Dar al-Islam, and where the divine Shariah had the status of law. They adopted this policy after the failure of the experiment of the great leader in Turkey. It should be remembered that this great leader of Turkey was artificially created by them themselves, and on their direction he abolished the Islamic caliphate from Turkey, because the Islamic caliphate of Turkey was the last sign of the glory of Islam on this earth. But their openly atheistic policy in Turkey failed miserably and played no important role in that region. This atheistic policy openly separated itself from religion. Consequently, this policy remained completely alien to the social system there, because the fire of love for Islam was still burning in the hearts of the people of Turkey. Therefore, after this experiment, world crusaderism and Zionism began new experiments, whose aims are the same, but in these new experiments the mistakes of Kemal are not repeated. So now the conspiracies they plan are carried out behind the veil of religion. They establish religious organizations which either openly work for these aims or whose aim is this. They take up some partial issues of these organizations and give the impression that apart from these partial defects, everything else is correct. I consider this to be an extremely deep conspiracy against Islam, which the devils of jinn and mankind have devised against the religion of Islam.

The crusaders and Zionists have continued to work fully for their aims in this field. Despite religious differences, they remained united and agreed with one another, and continued to exchange experiences and skills. Outwardly they were also opposed to this Turkish experiment, and they kept giving the impression that the Turkish movement was in fact a movement for the revival of Islam, and that the Turkish government was merely verbally presenting itself as a secular government.

Orientalists supply intellectual food to crusader and Zionist imperialism. They have worked hard to establish that the Turkish experiment was not in reality an atheistic experiment, and they do this because, owing to the atheistic features of the Turkish experiment, its influence and effectiveness had decreased. This was a destructive attack by the orientalists against the Islamic movement, but the atheist movement of Turkey was no longer capable of becoming active again. In the modern age, the orientalists' action against Islam is being carried out in the name of Islam itself. These people are changing the meanings of Islamic concepts, reducing the enthusiasm and fervour of people for Islam, and giving it a jahili colour. In the name of religion they strive to change religious ideas. They are leading Islamic morality and the most natural human habits astray in the name of religion. Then they prove every mark of jahiliyyah to be exactly Islam, and promote it in those countries where people's feelings about Islam are not sensitive. Thus they ensnare the Muslim world in the snares of crusaderism and Zionism, and this movement of theirs is more successful than the crusading and Zionist wars which they have been fighting against Islam for the last thirteen hundred years. But the truth is:

﴿Surely Allah will recompense them for what they used to fabricate.﴾ (6:138)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 139:

Verse 139.

Through the superstitions born of this polytheism and idol-worship, these people went so far that they handed over the determination of what is lawful and unlawful to human beings rather than to Allah, and they claimed that the laws which human beings were making were the Shariah of Allah. Thus, in the world of superstition, they reached the point of saying that what is in the bellies of these animals is for men alone, or perhaps they said, regarding the above-mentioned baheerah, saa'ibah and waseelah and the like, that its eating is forbidden for women. Yes, there is one condition: if such an animal is born dead, then women may also eat from it. And why? They had no logical justification for this. The only justification was that the people to whom they had entrusted the task of lawmaking would have such a wish, or that their own interest lay in it. This was purely meaningless lawmaking. For this reason, at the end of this verse the Noble Qur'an says that this is a most detestable law. Those who made it have fabricated lies against Allah, especially in that they claim that this too is a Shariah from Allah.

﴿Surely He will requite them for their attributes; surely He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.﴾ (6:139)

"Allah will certainly repay them for their description. Indeed, He is Wise and All-Knowing." He conducts all affairs with great wisdom, and His decisions and laws are not like those of these ignorant people.

When a person, while reading the Word of Allah, casts a glance over these deviations and reflects upon the losses, harms and difficulties in which the bearers of these deviations are entangled, he is greatly astonished to see how much loss people incur by deviating from the Islamic Shariah and the Islamic system, and into what unbearable responsibilities they have fallen. Taking up these responsibilities, they have become entangled in futile and obscure matters that are incomprehensible. Their beliefs are wrong, and obligations have been imposed upon them that are unbearable. Their life is complicated and agitated; there is no principle of life. Everywhere there is illusion, superstition, imitation and mere copying. In contrast to all these conditions stands the Islamic doctrine of Tawhid, which is perfectly pure, clean and clear. This belief scrapes illusion and superstition from the human mind and frees human reason from blind imitation and rigid bondage. This belief delivers humanity from jahiliyyah (ignorance, the age of pre-Islamic darkness) and its rituals. Then this belief frees slaves from the servitude of other slaves, whether this servitude is in the matter of lawmaking, or in customs and patterns of conduct, or in the arenas of the standards of good and evil. Taking man out of this jungle, the doctrine of Tawhid gives him a clear outlook and a clear meaning. Its concepts are clear and easy. In the light of these concepts, man attains all-embracing freedom, and he reaches the lofty and exalted station of servitude and worship of Allah alone. People can reach there by following the Prophet.

Alas! This is a great loss, and this loss is both in this world and in the Hereafter, rather the loss of the Hereafter is far greater. This is because humanity has deviated from the straight path of Allah and has sunk into the filth of jahiliyyah. It has surrendered itself into the slavery of human beings.

Verse 140.

This is a general and absolute loss. It is a loss in both this world and the Hereafter. It is a loss for themselves and also a loss for the generations to come. It is a loss of intellect, a loss of spirituality, and a loss of their freedom: Allah had freed them from servitude to human beings and brought them into the servitude of their Lord, but they re-enrolled themselves in the servitude of their fellow servants and made those humans their rulers. Setting aside all these matters, they have adopted misguidance and abandoned the path of guidance.

﴿They have indeed gone astray, and they were not among those rightly guided.﴾ (6:140)

After this, the Qur'an brings them to the first reality of this universe, which they had forgotten, and which was pointed to at the beginning of the discourse in the verse ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of the produce and cattle which He has created﴾ (6:136). They are brought to the reality that the crops and cattle concerning which they lay down such unreasonable rules, what is their true nature and what is their origin and source? They take guidance about them from the jinn and the human satans, whereas it is not those jinn and satans who created them. Allah is the Being who created these crops and cattle. These things were created as provisions for you, and you are using them. Your duty is to render thanks to God and worship Allah alone, although Allah has no need of your gratitude or your servitude, for He is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy.

The truth is that these realities and beliefs are set forth for the sake of setting right the worldly and otherworldly affairs of human beings themselves, who are not the owners or creators of any one of these things. These crops and cattle are the creation of Allah, yet human beings divide the creation of Allah, assigning some to idols and setting aside some for Allah. Then they treat Allah's share with contempt, and thus they please the satans.

Whereas Allah alone is the Creator, Owner, Provider and Lord, and no disposal of these possessions can take place without His permission. His permission exists in the form of the Islamic Shari'ah, and this Shari'ah has been brought from Allah by the Messenger of Allah. The laws enacted by those usurpers, who have seized the right of Allah to sovereignty, do not possess Allah's permission.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 141–142:

Verse 141–142.

Allah is the One who brought into being these gardens, both the trellised and the untrellised, the date-palms and the crops of varied produce, the olives and pomegranates, and fruits that are alike and yet different. He is the One who brings the living out of the dead. Some of these gardens are of the kind that resemble trellised vines, which man cultivates and around which he erects fences, while others are of the kind of date-palm groves that grow on their own and need no assistance from man. He also produced other crops. He created the olive and the pomegranate, and fruits of every kind, some resembling one another and some differing. Then He created livestock as well, some of them tall in stature and some small in body, and they are for your food and for your clothing, and from their hair you make carpets and rugs.

It is Allah alone who spread across this earth living creatures of every colour and variety, and the diversity of this creation is astonishing. Then He provided this creation with an environment most suited to the duties that man performs on this earth, and He also made them suitable for those needs which are indispensable to human life. Seeing these signs and proofs and these creatures of many hues, how can a human being pass by without being affected? Yet even so, he acknowledges the authority and powers of someone other than Allah over this creation and these agricultural produce.

The Qur'an repeatedly mentions the provision that Allah has scattered upon this earth for man, and presents this varied sustenance as evidence that if He is the Provider, then He is also the Ruler. His sovereignty must be operative over humanity, because the One who is the Creator, the Provider, the Lord, and the Sustainer throughout life is the only one deserving that people regard Him as their Ruler, Authority and Legislator in matters of agricultural produce, livestock, and all the affairs of life. And none shares with Him in this.

Here Allah has alluded to several scenes of gardens and fruits, has mentioned various kinds of animals, and has shown that these are His bounties upon you. Previously, from these scenes, the divinity and lordship of Allah was argued. Here, by mentioning these things, Allah argues for His right to sovereignty. The intention is to show that divinity and sovereignty are in reality one and the same reality. He alone is the Ruler, and this is the fundamental belief of Islam.

(There is no god but Allah; there is no ruler but Allah.) Now, after the mention of crops and fruits, comes this command, an indication of a law:

"Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest, and do not be extravagant; indeed He does not love the extravagant." (141)

Here it is said that when you harvest its produce, give Allah's due. Because of this phrase, some narrations state that this verse is Madani. But we have clearly explained in the introduction to this surah that this verse is Meccan. If this verse is separated from this surah, the matter is not complete; the speech before this verse and after it becomes disconnected from one another unless this verse is revealed in Medina, so this view is not correct. Moreover, it is not necessary that the "due of Allah" mentioned in this surah must be zakat. Some narrations also state that it refers to the due on the day of harvest in general. As for zakat, with its fixed rate, it became obligatory in the second year after the Hijrah.

"And do not be extravagant; indeed He does not love the extravagant." (141)

This verse sets a proper limit both on eating and on giving. Narrations state that when the Muslims began to give, they went to excess, and this verse was revealed: "And do not be extravagant; indeed He does not love the extravagant." Islam loves moderation in everything.

"And of the livestock are those for carrying loads and for bedding. Eat of what Allah has provided you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan; indeed he is to you a clear enemy." (142)

Here He is the One who created from among the livestock those animals used for transport and burden-bearing, and also those used for food and for spreading. The mention of livestock is made because it is intended to remind man that all this creation is created by Allah. Satan is not the creator of anything. The question is: when Satan has nothing at all, then what is this, that the blessings are from Allah and the following is of Satan? Especially when it is known that Satan is a clear enemy. Do you not reflect? You use the things Allah has given and follow Satan, while he is a clear enemy.

Now the Qur'an goes into great depth, seeking out the delusions of jahiliyyah. It sheds light on the most hidden corners, and brings to light each and every hidden recess. It makes clear corners that are, at first glance, absurd, for which no justification can be offered, and at times people caught up in these delusions suffer great embarrassment, especially when their conduct is exposed in the open field, and when they see that behind these delusions there is neither any authority, nor any illuminating book, nor any rational proof.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 143–144:

Verses 142 to 144.

These cattle, about which there is dispute, and which the preceding verse said are merely God's creation, come in eight pairs. The word "azwaj" (pairs) is used when both male and female are present; zawj means a pair: one pair of sheep and one pair of goats. The question is: on which people has God forbidden them? Or where is the ruling on the foetuses (janin) in their wombs? If you are truthful, then produce it.

﴿Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful.﴾ (143)

For decisions on what is lawful and unlawful cannot be made by mere conjecture and estimation, nor can a fatwa be given on this matter by guesswork. Nor can any law be made in this regard without a known and sound authority.

The remaining pairs are the male and female camel, and the bull and the cow. The question is: where is the ruling on their lawfulness and unlawfulness? Or where is the ruling on their foetuses, and who gave it?

﴿Or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you?﴾ (6:144)

That is, were you present, and are you witnesses that God has commanded you this? For only God's command can make something lawful or unlawful, and the command must also be certain. Mere conjecture and estimation cannot speak in this matter.

From this verse it becomes clear that the sole legislator is God. They believed that the laws they made were the law of God, and this is why God immediately warns them.

﴿So who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God to mislead people without knowledge? Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (6:144)

No one is more unjust than the person who, by making law himself, presents it as the law of God and claims that it is sharia. The aim is to mislead the common people, the herd. Such a person calls people only to conjecture, while the path of guidance is closed to such people. They have adopted a wrong path and, by committing shirk with God, have committed injustice, and God does not guide any wrongdoer.

Now that the flimsiness of their beliefs, conceptions and practical rites has been exposed, and it has been demonstrated that all of this is merely imaginary and baseless, and it has also been explained that their conceptions and beliefs are not based on any knowledge or proof, and that the conceptions and rites they hold regarding cattle and crops are either fabricated by themselves or have been inspired into them by their devils, although these cattle, crops, fruits and produce are not of their creation, but are the marvels of God's creation, therefore sovereignty and worship must all be exclusively for God. Because the creation is His, the provision is His, and He has given people all kinds of wealth.

After this preface, God now tells what are the things He has made unlawful. He has made those things unlawful on the basis of truth and proof, not merely on the basis of illusion and conjecture. For God is the One who holds the right of sovereignty and the right of legislation. It is the station and position of God alone that whatever He makes lawful is lawful, and whatever He makes unlawful is unlawful. No human being shares in this, and no one can interfere in it in any way. God's sovereignty and His legislation are not subject to review by anyone. In keeping with the occasion, God has also enumerated here the things which were unlawful for the Jews and were made lawful for the Muslims, because they were made unlawful for the Jews as a punishment, since they had fallen into injustice and shirk and had turned away from the sharia of God.
