Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 145–146:

Verses 145–146

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari writes: Allah addresses His Prophet, saying: "O Muhammad! Say to those who have set aside for Allah a portion of the crops and cattle that He created, and a portion for their gods whom they themselves have made partners with Allah, who say that these cattle and this crop are forbidden and may be used only by those whom we wish, a law which they make according to their own assumption: they forbid the carrying of loads upon some animals, and there are animals over which they do not consider it permissible to pronounce Allah's name at slaughter. They declare the embryo in the bellies of some animals forbidden to their women and wives and lawful for the men. They declare some other provisions created by Allah to be forbidden, and beyond that they further claim that these laws and regulations are made by Allah. Their acts fall within the category of shirk. Ask them: Did a messenger come from Allah who forbade these things? Then tell us which messenger that was. Or when Allah forbade these things, were you present in that assembly? You yourselves heard from Allah that these things are forbidden. If you make such a claim, then on the face of it, it would be a lie, and you could not rationally make such a claim at all. If you make such a claim, the whole world will refute you. As for my own matter, in the Book that is being revealed to me, there is nothing forbidden to any person of what you forbid, and what you forbid by your own assumption. What Allah has forbidden to me is this: an animal that has died, or died without slaughter, or flowing blood, or the flesh of swine, which is forbidden because it is impure, or the flesh that is of transgression (fisq), such as the sacrifice which the polytheists slaughter for their idols and shrines, and over which the names of idols have been pronounced. In Islam, such a slaughter is considered fisq; Allah has forbidden it and prohibited doing so. It is considered carrion, and eating it is forbidden."

This is a declaration from Allah to those polytheists who disputed with the Messenger ﷺ and his companions about the lawfulness and unlawfulness of carrion, saying that among the things they dispute, some are forbidden, which Allah has forbidden, and some are lawful, which Allah has made lawful. Their claim that the prohibition of these lawful things is from Allah is false. Ibn Jarir, in his commentary on the verse (Famani idturra...), says: "Its meaning is that Allah forbade carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, or animals slaughtered in the name of idols. But if someone is compelled to eat them, not in disobedience and not while not in a state of necessity, and similarly does not exceed the limits deliberately, and eats within the bounds of need, for example eating only enough to save his life and no more, then there is no harm in eating that much. Indeed Allah is Ghafur and Rahim, and He is the Concealer of such a person. No punishment will be imposed on him for it, and his sin will be forgiven; this is the meaning of Ghafur. And He is Rahim because, out of mercy on people, He commanded permission at the time of compulsion. Otherwise, if He had willed, He would have made the use of these things forbidden in every circumstance."

As for the amount that may be eaten of these things, there are differences among the jurists. One opinion is that he will eat only as much as will save his life. Another opinion is that he may eat to the extent of sufficiency and until he is satisfied. One opinion is that, apart from eating once, he may also store some for the compelled person at other times, if he fears that lawful sustenance will not be available to him again. I do not go into the details of these differences; enough has been said on this subject.

As for the Jews, all animals with claws were forbidden to them, that is, all creatures whose feet are not cloven, such as the camel, the ostrich, the goose and the duck. Upon them, the fat of cows and goats was also forbidden, except the fat of the back, or the fat that clung to the intestines, or that which was mixed with bones. These things were forbidden to them as a punishment, and this punishment was given to them as a consequence of the rebellion they committed against Allah's commands and laws.

Verse 146

"And to those who followed Judaism We forbade every animal with claws, and of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except that which is on their backs or the entrails, or that which is mixed with bone. That was Our recompense for their rebellion, and surely We are truthful in what We say."

The Qur'an clearly stated the cause for which these things were forbidden to them, and this prohibition was specific to the Jews, and this was the true cause. It was not the cause that they claim: that Israel, that is Prophet Ya'qub (peace be upon him), himself forbade these things to himself, and in obedience to Israel these people too continue to keep these things forbidden to themselves. The truth is that these things were permissible and lawful for Prophet Ya'qub (peace be upon him); rather, after them, when they adopted rebellion, Allah forbade these things to them, and so that He might punish them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 147:

Verse No. 147.

Its skirt of mercy is very wide, and this mercy is wide for us, and it was wide for the believers before us, and apart from the believers, its breadth extends to all creatures, for He is the Benefactor. He is merciful to the friend and merciful to the enemy. Even if the criminals deserve punishment, He does not hasten to carry out the punishment, and this is the glory of His generosity. During this respite, many people repent and turn back to Allah, but their punishment is extremely severe. Only His forbearance can hold it back from the people of faith. Within the system of Allah's destiny and decree, it can be postponed only until the time that has been fixed.

Although this verse keeps the lamp of hope burning and does not leave a person in despair, alongside this it also contains a warning that a person should not exceed the limits. Allah is the One who created the hearts and minds of people, and He knows that both of these things are necessary for them, so that they may be frightened, reflect upon their conduct, and accept the call of Islam.

When the matter reaches this point and there is no escape left for the people of misguidance, when they have no argument left and all paths of flight are closed, the Qur'an closes off even their final avenue of escape. For their misguided notions, their polytheistic beliefs, and their meaningless deeds, there was one path remaining. They used to say that they have no power of their own and that they are compelled. If Allah had willed, they would neither have held such notions, nor would they have had false beliefs, nor would they have been engaged in wrongful deeds. If Allah had willed, He would have stopped us from these things. He is the Absolute Power, and His power is subject to no restriction.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 148–149:

Verses 148–149

In the history of Islamic thought, the question of predestination and free will (jabr and qadr) has given rise to lengthy debates. Ahl al-Sunnah, the Mu'tazilah and the Murji'ah have been locked in dispute over it. When Greek philosophy and Greek logic entered the Muslim world, they too influenced these discussions. Then the theology of the Christians (lahut) also left its effects. This made the matter so complicated that it became incomprehensible to the clear and realistic concept of Islam. If this issue had been considered seriously, realistically and directly in the light of the Qur'an, there would have been no such contention and argument, and the discussion would not have taken the course it took.

When we read the saying of the polytheists and see the simple and clear manner in which the Qur'an refutes it, it appears very simple and comprehensible.

﴿The polytheists will surely say: "Had Allah willed, neither we nor our fathers would have associated anything with Him, nor would we have declared anything unlawful."﴾ (6:148)

Their purpose was that the shirk they committed, and the shirk their forefathers committed, or the things they declared unlawful on their own, Allah had made unlawful; and their claim that this is the Sharia prescribed by Allah, and their baseless claim that all these matters are proceeding according to Allah's will. "If Allah had not willed, we would not have committed shirk, nor would we have declared these things unlawful." All these are idle words.

Now see how the Qur'an refutes this philosophy of theirs. The Qur'an merely says that these people are lying in exactly the same way as those before them lied. And those who lied before them have already tasted the result of their lies, and now these new deniers have come, and the punishment of Allah awaits them and is ready to receive them.

﴿Likewise did those before them deny, until they tasted Our might.﴾ (6:148)

﴿Thus did those before them make such claims and deny the truth, until at last they tasted Our punishment.﴾

This is the warning that shakes the thinking person to the core. Even the most heedless person comes to his senses and is compelled to consider the outcome.

Now there is a second warning, through which their intellectual reform is intended: that Allah has given commands and orders, has forbidden certain things and has declared them unlawful. Regarding these things, they can acquire certain and indubitable knowledge. As for Allah's will and His system, it is a hidden system, and reaching its true reality is no easy task for the human power of perception. How can they know what Allah's will is? And when a human being cannot even comprehend Allah's system of qadar and qada, how can he attribute someone's act to the system of qada and qadar?

﴿Say: "Have you any knowledge that you can bring forth for us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess."﴾ (6:148)

The commands that Allah has given, and the prohibitions from Him, are known, and we have certain knowledge of them in the Qur'an. The question is: why do these people abandon these certain matters and run after the mirage of mere conjecture and speculation, and why do they set foot in that valley whose rises and falls they do not know?

I consider this a decisive point in the matter of jabr and qadr. Allah does not make people responsible for acquiring knowledge of the system of His qada and qadar and shaping their lives accordingly. The only obligation Allah has placed upon people is that they acquire knowledge of Allah's commands and prohibitions and shape their lives accordingly. When they begin to strive in this matter, Allah has promised that He will set them on the path of guidance and their hearts will open to Islam. In the matter of qada and qadar, this is a realistic and practical outlook, and it is sufficient for the solution of human problems. It is easy, it is clear, and there is in it no debate, no argument and no contention, nor any dictation or arrogance.

If Allah had willed, from the very beginning He could have created man in such a way that he could not have walked on any path other than the path of guidance; or Allah could have compelled them to adopt guidance; or Allah could have placed guidance in their hearts by Himself, and there would have been no need to adopt coercive means for guidance upon them. But Allah, glorified is He, did not want this. The will of Allah was that He would give Adam power and free choice and test him, and that this choice would be such that he could choose whichever path he wished, of guidance or of misguidance. When a person freely determines upon a path, then Allah helps him further, towards guidance or towards misguidance; that is, whoever points towards misguidance, the path to it also becomes easy for him. This is the method according to which His sunnah continues to operate.

﴿Say: "With Allah is the conclusive proof; had He willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ (6:149)

Now this matter becomes clear, and the Qur'an presents it in a manner that every person can easily understand. As for those scholarly battles that took place over this issue, and the lengthy contention and argument which form part of our history, they do not fit with the Islamic sensibility and the Islamic method. Not only does Islamic thought not accept them, but even the Greek philosophy and the theological discussions of the Christians have not reached any conclusion to this day. This is because these discussions proceeded in a manner contrary to the nature of this matter.

Every reality is taken according to its nature, and its method of discussion is adopted in accordance with its condition. As far as material realities are concerned, they can be known through experiment, and mathematical realities are known through rational premises; but realities that lie beyond the material world have their own method of discussion. As we said above, these realities are of a practical nature, and they should be taken in a practical manner and with a realistic method of discussion. They should not be taken in the manner of mere religious assumptions, as they were taken previously and are being taken even today.

The truth is that the religion of Islam came into this world so that it might bring about a practical state of affairs here. It consists of commands and prohibitions, and these commands and prohibitions are clear. To bring the unknown will of God into discussion regarding them would mean that we fall into a boundless desert without any proof and waste our energies in fruitless contention and wandering in the wilderness.

Now Allah instructs the Prophet ﷺ: that he should present Allah as the witness in this legislation. In the same way as he was earlier instructed that he should present the Being of Allah as witness in the matter of Allah's supreme authority and sovereignty. At the beginning of this surah it was said:

﴿Say: "What thing is greatest as a testimony?" Say: "Allah is witness between me and you. This Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it and whomever it reaches. Do you really bear witness that there are other gods with Allah?" Say: "I do not bear witness." Say: "He is only one God, and I am free from what you associate."﴾ (6:19)

And here Allah, the Exalted, says thus:

This is a great contest, and it is decisive too, and from it we learn what the temperament of the religion of Islam is. In the religion of Islam, to associate another with Allah in His Being is shirk. Likewise, to associate another with Allah in His right of sovereignty (hakimiyyah) and in legislation, in practice, is also shirk, which is practical shirk (shirk 'amali). Except where someone makes a law that the Qur'an and Sunnah have permitted. If someone in legislation verbally declares that this law is from Allah, his claim will be rejected, unless in reality it is from Allah. Here Allah declares liars those kinds of people who make laws themselves or who make some law and attribute it to Allah, and it is also announced that such people have neither fear of the Hereafter nor faith in the Hereafter in their hearts, because if these people were not deniers of the Hereafter, they would not have dared to make others equal with Allah. They would not associate anyone with Allah. A similar expression also came at the beginning of this surah:

﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve equate others with their Lord.﴾ (6:1)

This is the ruling concerning those who snatch from Allah His right of sovereignty and hand it over to those who are themselves human beings like them. Here, too, their claim that such legislation could be Islamic legislation is rejected. Now, after this ruling of Allah, what worth could any other human opinion have?

If we wish to understand why Allah decided this matter in this manner, and why He called such people deniers of the signs of Allah, and why He passed the judgment about them that they do not believe in the Hereafter, and that they are polytheists who make others equal with their Lord, then it is our duty to strive to understand, because to reflect upon the Shariah of Allah, His commands and decisions, and to discover their wisdom, is a desired matter.

Allah, concerning those who make laws on their own behalf for the people, has ruled here that they deny the signs of Allah, even though they give it the title of the Shariah of Allah, because from the signs of Allah two meanings can be taken here. One is that by them are meant the cosmic signs (ayat kawniyyah); these signs also bear witness that the Creator and Provider is Allah alone, and whoever is the Creator and Provider will be the Owner, and therefore He alone will be the one who disposes and rules. So a person who does not regard Allah alone as the Ruler is, in effect, denying the cosmic signs of Allah. And if by these signs the Qur'anic verses are meant, then countless verses of the Qur'an declare clearly and emphatically that in the matter of sovereignty and legislation Allah is alone, without partner. Only the Shariah of Allah has legal standing, and people should only observe and enforce the Shariah of Allah.

Concerning such people, Allah has also declared that they do not believe in the Hereafter, because a person who has faith and conviction in the Hereafter, that he is to meet his Lord on the Day of Resurrection, will certainly never encroach upon the right of sovereignty of Allah, nor will he demand for himself any such right. Allah is the absolute Ruler of mankind; His system of decree and destiny also operates upon human beings, and in the same way His Shariah should also be enforced upon them.

Allah's third resolution about these people is that they make others equal with their Lord. That is, they are polytheists in the same way as idol-worshippers are polytheists. If they were among the people of tawhid, they would not make others equal with Allah, neither in His right of sovereignty nor in His right of divinity, because He is unique in these. And if someone else were exercising these rights, they would oppose him and would never be pleased with it.

As appears, this matter is the cause (illah) of all these rulings: that those who legislate against the Qur'an and Sunnah, because of this act of theirs, Allah has issued these rulings upon them, that they are polytheists, deniers of the signs of Allah, and that in reality they do not believe in accountability in the Hereafter, that they have to appear before Allah. This is the cause, and as its consequence this is the ruling. As for why Allah's ruling about such people is as it is, this is a definitive text (nass qat'i), and it cannot be changed, and according to it such people will be regarded as polytheists. So now it is for every Muslim to think about what conduct he adopts in this regard.

After this testimony and witness, and after rejecting the prohibitions they have set, now the list is given of what Allah has in fact made unlawful. Here, along with the mention of prohibitions, some positive commands are also recalled, the opposite conduct of which has been declared unlawful. These prohibitions begin with committing shirk, because it is the first principle of Islam, and it is necessary to fix it in the mind first. By shirk is meant generally: shirk in belief (shirk fi al-i'tiqad) and shirk in judgment (shirk fi al-hukm). Here by shirk both kinds of shirk are meant. After this basic principle, all commands and prohibitions are built upon it, that is, one accepts Islam and then submits completely.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 151–152 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 151 to 153.

The instructions and laws that Allah has set out in this section of the verses, such as those concerning livestock and produce, and the refutation of the superstitions and customs of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam), show that these laws and guidance rest on the foundational principles of this religion. Through them the human conscience receives the light and life of tawhid (the oneness of Allah), and over the course of centuries the human family is strengthened. Through mutual solidarity (takaful) and mutual support, social bonds are made firm, and a society comes into being in which rights are guaranteed and duties are fulfilled. All these affairs proceed in accordance with Allah's guidance, but they begin with the creed of tawhid.

And when these instructions conclude, Allah says that this is the Straight Path of Allah, and that every other path, however many crooked paths there are, is a deviation from the way of tawhid.

In short, the matters stated in these three verses are of the utmost importance. These matters are mentioned after a question which apparently seems to be a partial issue of the Jahiliyyah, but this question is in fact a most fundamental issue of this religion, because it is linked to these important instructions.

Verse: "Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you" (6:151)

"O Prophet (ﷺ), say to them: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has imposed upon you as prohibitions. Come, I will tell you what Allah has forbidden. The things which you yourselves have declared to be forbidden are in fact not forbidden. He has made certain things forbidden to you because He has the right to do so, for He is your Lord. The meaning of Rabb (Lord) is: sustainer, nurturer, guide and ruler. Therefore, the determining of what is lawful and unlawful is His task. This is His station and rank, that He should do so. If anyone other than Allah determines what is lawful and unlawful, he would be called a lord. In reality, a lord is only the one who determines what is lawful and unlawful."

Verse: "That you associate nothing with Him" (6:151)

This is the basic principle upon which the entire structure of the Islamic conception of life is raised. All obligations and duties return to it, and rights and responsibilities are determined by it. This is the principle which, once accepted, makes other commands and prohibitions binding upon a person. The obligations, duties, the details of the Islamic system and the following of Islamic constitution and laws become binding only when a human being or a society accepts the creed of tawhid and affirms that Allah alone is their Lord, and that He is the God and the sovereign. In His divinity, His supreme authority and His lordship, they associate no one with Him. They acknowledge that Allah alone exercises control over all the natural affairs of this entire universe. The world of causes and the system of destiny and decree run by His will. They also accept the belief that in the Hereafter they will have to answer for the whole of their life's conduct. They further acknowledge that in the system of government too they are bound by the commands of Allah. In short, for the human heart and mind this creed is a complete purification, and human thought and rationality are completely cleansed of the diseases of illusion and conjecture. Through it alone a society can be purified from the pollutions of Jahiliyyah, and a human being can be freed from the slavery and servitude of other human beings.

Shirk (associating partners with Allah), in every form and appearance, is forbidden, because through it a person can fall into every forbidden thing. This is the first evil against which the struggle (jihad) begins, and every aspect of it must be denied, until people acknowledge that there is no god but Allah, that there is no lord but Allah, that there is no ruler but Allah, that there is no legislator but Allah, and then people also acknowledge that in these matters they will not turn to anyone except Allah.

This is the path in comparison with which all other paths are wrong and difficult; this is the straight path.

﴿And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may be mindful of Allah.﴾ (6:153)

Allah has guided you to walk on this very path so that you may become righteous. Thus it is known that the basis of taqwa rests upon correct belief and correct action. It is taqwa that leads a person to the path of Allah.

Then He said: ﴿And this is My straight path, so follow it﴾ (6:153), meaning this is My straight way and religion. This sentence was joined to the earlier one, that is, to ﴿that you associate nothing with Him﴾. After that came this verse: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book﴾ (6:154), which is joined to both of the above sentences. In this way, the whole discourse is continuously connected with one another.

The meaning of ﴿perfectly, upon him who did good﴾ (6:154), as Ibn Jarir has written, is: then We gave Moses the Torah, and this was a completion of Our favour upon him. It was an honour and distinction from Us for him, because he adopted the attitude of doing good and obeyed his Lord. Whatever obligations were imposed upon him by his Lord, he acted upon them, and in that Book were recorded all the matters that the people of Moses (peace be upon him) needed.

﴿Detailing everything﴾ (6:154): Qatadah says that this refers to the lawful and the unlawful.

﴿And as guidance and mercy﴾ (6:154): its meaning is that his people would be guided, would believe in accountability in the Hereafter, and thereby, becoming deserving of Allah's mercy, would be saved from Allah's punishment.

These were the purposes for which We gave the Book to Moses, and for these same purposes God has sent down this Book to you as well, so that you too may be guided and then become deserving of mercy.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 155:

Verse 155.

Indeed, this is a blessed Book, and we have explained it in great detail in the commentary on the verse where this word first appeared:

﴿And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed, confirming that which was before it, and that you may warn the Mother of Cities (Makkah) and those around it. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are over their prayers, guarding them.﴾ (6:92)

"This is a Book that We have sent down. It is full of goodness and blessing. It confirms what came before it. It was sent down so that through it you may warn the central city of the settlements (that is, Makkah) and those who live around it. Those who affirm the Hereafter believe in this Book, and they are punctilious in observing their prayers."

Here the word "mubarak" (blessed) has come in the context of the discussion of the Islamic way of life, its comprehensiveness and its all-encompassing nature; that is, this Book contains a system of Shari'ah. The command being given is that you should obey this Shari'ah system, and that the mercy of Allah upon you can only come about if you follow this Book, since the discourse here concerns the Shari'ah system, whereas at the beginning of the surah the subject was Islamic beliefs and ideologies.

That is, now you have no excuse left and no argument remains. This Book has been revealed and it has nullified and rendered void all proofs and arguments. In this Book are the details of all matters of life; there is no aspect of life about which it does not contain guidance, so that you would have no need to make laws for yourselves.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 6, verse 156–157:

Verses 156 to 157.

It was Allah's plan that a messenger was sent to every people with a message in the language of his nation, and when the final message came into the world, Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent to all the nations of the world. Therefore, the Messenger (ﷺ) is the final Messenger for mankind, because he has been sent as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner for all mankind.

Allah established His proof against the Arabs in this manner: Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) and Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) were sent to their respective peoples, and the Arabs used to say that they could not read their books; they were not scholars, and no arrangement had been made to convey this call to them. If a book had come to us in our own language, we would certainly have believed and would have been more rightly guided than those people. So the book came to them, and the Messenger also came, indeed this Messenger came for all the worlds. This Messenger was given a book which is itself a proof of its own truth. (Aftab aamad dalil aftab: when the sun rises, it is its own proof.) Then, the truths that are stated in this book contain no confusion or complexity. For those who are drowned in the misguidance in which they are, it is a lamp that is lit, and against the calamities in which they are afflicted, it is a mercy, both for the world and for the Hereafter.

If the situation is so, then who could be a greater wrongdoer than the one who denies the verses of such a book or turns away from them, although this book calls to the right path, to the reform of one's condition, and to the success of this world and the Hereafter? Who could be a greater wrongdoer than the one who deprives himself and the common people of the blessings of this book? The one who is a wrongdoer is the one who spreads corruption on this earth by framing jahili notions and laws contrary to Islam. Those who turn away from this book, in reality corruption is hidden in their temperament, which keeps them far from this fountain of good. For example, when a camel has a defect or disease in its feet, it leans to one side and does not walk straight. (This is the meaning of sadf.) That is, these people go away from the truth to one side, just as a sick camel is leaning to one side and cannot walk straight. Because of this inclination, they will deserve a terrible punishment.

Verse 157:

"Those who turn away from Our verses, We shall surely make them taste a severe punishment for their turning away."

It is a feature of the Qur'anic style of expression that it takes each word of the Arabic language from its sensory meaning and uses it for a figurative meaning, but this usage fits the figurative meaning in such a way that the original sensory meaning also appears correct in its place. In this way, the usage of (yasdifun) has come. (Sadf) means that a camel, because of a disease in its feet, leans over to one side and walks. Another example of this is (al-sa'r). In Arabic, sa'r is the name of a disease in which a camel's face becomes crooked to one side and its neck cannot be straightened. This disease also afflicts humans. The Holy Qur'an has used it to mean turning the face crooked out of arrogance: "And do not turn your cheek away (from people) [in arrogance]" (31:18), i.e., do not make your face crooked, do not be arrogant. A third example is khabt. Khabt means that an animal swells up after eating poisonous grass. It is said khabatat al-naqah when a she-camel swells after grazing on poisonous grass. The Qur'an has used this word for deeds that are without purpose and without faith, in which the deeds apparently appear great. There are countless instances of this kind of usage in the Qur'an.

Now the matter moves a little further: after this Book has come, these people now demand further extraordinary events and miracles so that they may accept it. A similar warning was also in the beginning of the surah, where a warning was given for not accepting the Islamic doctrine of tawhid and beliefs, and here this warning is repeated in connection with not accepting the Islamic system of life and the Islamic Shari'ah. At the beginning it had been said:

"And they say, 'Why has no angel been sent down upon him?' Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved." (6:8)

Here the same theme is repeated:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 6, verse 158:

Verse No. 158.

This is a clear and unambiguous warning, for it is the unchangeable Sunnah (established way) of Allah that when a miracle comes and people still deny, they are destroyed. Allah the Exalted says that if any of the extraordinary events which these people demand were brought, their judgement would have been decided long ago, because when a miracle of this kind comes, the period of action and the respite come to an end, and then faith and deeds are no longer beneficial. For those who were not already believers and not acting upon the Islamic system, there is then no further time. In the Qur'an, action is always mentioned along with faith, because according to the Islamic standard, only that faith is accepted which is accompanied by action. Many narrations report that by the verse ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾ (6:158) are meant the signs of the Hour, because after the signs of the Hour appear, faith and deeds are no longer beneficial, and some narrations even enumerate the portents of the Hour (ashrat al-Sa'ah). However, the interpretation of this verse in the sense that it refers to the continuing Sunnah of Allah in this world is much more appropriate. Its example is present at the beginning of this same surah.

﴿They say, "Why has an angel not been sent down upon him?" Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved.﴾ (6:8)

It should be kept in mind that at the beginning of the surah these same matters were stated on the subject of accepting faith and adopting Islamic beliefs, and here matters are being stated on the subject of the establishment of the Islamic system and the enforcement of the Shari'ah. This is extremely important and worth remembering, so that the reality of the Islamic Shari'ah and the establishment of Allah's sovereignty remains in mind. Just as the statement at the beginning of the surah is applied to the continuing Sunnah, similarly here its interpretation as the continuing Sunnah is appropriate in contrast to the signs of the Hour. This would be an appropriate interpretation and explanation, and there would be no need to apply it here to the Resurrection, the timing of whose occurrence was known to the Knower of the Unseen.

Now the discussion turns towards the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that his Shari'ah and his community are distinct in the world from all the other established communities. All sects and religions, including the religion of the polytheists of Makkah, are false and contrary to his religion and Shari'ah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verse 159:

Verse 159.

Here it is decided concerning the religion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his Sharia and his system of life, that none of the religions and legal systems established in the world has any connection with his religion. He has no connection with the polytheists of Arabia, who have been broken into pieces by the superstitions of Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), Jahili beliefs, customs and rituals, who are engaged in mutual war and strife, and who are divided into groups, sects and branches upon branches. Nor does his religion and system have any connection with the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, who have been broken into pieces by religious differences and within whom many sects and groups have arisen. And he has no connection with the sects and schools that will come into being after him until the Day of Resurrection.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has no connection with these sects and religions. His religion is the religion of Islam, and his Sharia is that which is in this Book. The system he brought is a unique system, distinct from all others. The concepts and beliefs of this religion cannot be mixed with other religions. Nor can his Sharia be mixed with other legal systems and customs. In no circumstance and under no legal system can the Islamic and the non-Islamic be applied at the same time. Islam is simply Islam, and the Sharia of Islam is the original Sharia. The political, social and economic system of Islam alone is the Islamic system. And until the Day of Resurrection, the Messenger of God and the system of life he brought have no connection with other people and systems.

When a Muslim encounters all these religions and concepts, his first reaction should be complete rejection, separation and severance. Likewise, all those social and political systems in which sovereignty and authority, in other words the divinity and lordship (uluhiyyah and rububiyyah) of Allah, is not present, a Muslim's first duty is to reject them as soon as he encounters them and to declare his disassociation from them. He should neither seek a common ground between those systems and Islam, nor take part in debates about their acceptance or rejection.

According to Allah, the religion is Islam alone, and those who have not accepted the religion of Islam and have not enforced it upon their lives, the Messenger of Allah has no connection with them.

According to Allah, the religion is Islam alone, and those who have not accepted the religion of Islam and have not enforced it upon their lives, the Messenger of Allah has no connection with them.

According to Allah, the religion of Islam is a political and legal system, and those who do not adopt it, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has no connection with them. This is the reality, and there is no room for discussion or debate about it, nor any need for argument.

Those who have practically adopted other systems of life also have no connection with the Messenger of God. Allah has decided their matter, and on the Day of Resurrection too Allah will decide concerning them, and Allah is the One who will call them to account for all that they do.

﴿Indeed, their affair is with Allah; then He will inform them of what they used to do.﴾

Concerning the reckoning of such people, Allah the Exalted has made clear that He has bound Himself, in reckoning, to be merciful and generous toward His servants. Therefore whoever is a believer and does a good deed will receive ten times its reward. Let it be remembered that faith is a condition for a good deed, since without faith no deed can be good. Yes, if one has faith, the reward for a good deed is multiplied tenfold, and if one does evil, the recompense is only equal to it. Allah does not wrong anyone.

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged.﴾ (160)

At the conclusion of this surah, and at the end of this lengthy discussion on the Islamic doctrine of sovereignty and legislation, there comes a passage that is extremely fresh, in very gentle and beautiful words, in a most pleasant tone, yet in an extremely firm and decisive manner. The matter is concluded in such a way that this theme reaches the depths of the heart. Every point is repeated with the words "Qul, qul" (Say) and "Qul" (Say), and the all-encompassing doctrine of Tawhid (Divine Oneness) stands before us: the unity of the path and the community, the unity of direction and movement, the unity of the Deity and the Lord, the unity of worship and obedience, and the unity of the whole cosmos and of the cosmic laws operating within it and of the constituent elements found within them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 160–165:

Verses 160 to 165

This concluding passage, bearing in mind the themes at the beginning of this surah, is a most beautiful melody, most fitting and dazzling. With this melody the subject of sacrifices and vows, of offerings from fruits and crops, and in this connection the superstitions and customs of the age of ignorance, and then the claims that this law is from Allah, comes to its conclusion here. What does this concluding melody add to the theme? I think that after what we have said on these subjects, there is no need to say anything further on them.

﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the creed of Ibrahim, a man of pure faith, and he was not one of the polytheists.﴾ (161)

Say, O Muhammad (ﷺ): My Lord has surely shown me the straight path, a perfectly right religion in which there is no crookedness, the way of Ibrahim, which he adopted with single-minded devotion, and he was not one of the polytheists.

This is a declaration full of gratitude, which expresses firm conviction and complete trust. In it the literal structure of the words and their true meaning are combined. It expresses the connection of guidance with the Lord, the relationship of lordship, and His continuous protection. In it thanks are rendered that He has guided us to the straight path, in which there is no crookedness. That religion is the upright religion (din qayyim), and this religion is also our ancient heritage. From the time of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), this same religion is Islam; Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is the father of the fathers of this ummah, and from that time the Muslim ummah is a blessed ummah. In it there is a clear declaration that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was not among the polytheists.

﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. This I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit.﴾ (162–163)

Say: my prayer, my acts of worship, my life and my death all belong to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, who has no partner; this is what I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit.

This is the melody of Tawhid: an expression of absolute monotheism and all-encompassing servitude, in which prayer, retreat, life and death are all dedicated to Allah, who is the Lord of the worlds, the One who sustains, the sole controller and guardian, the Nurturer and Lord and ruler of the worlds. In it is the declaration of complete Islam, in every aspect of life, even up to death, in the conscience and in action, complete Islam. In the words (wa bidhalika umirtu) it is said that this complete Islam is a command of Allah, not merely a voluntary act. Therefore, the first of them is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns only for itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.﴾ (164)

Say: Should I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of everything? Every soul earns only for itself, no one bearing burdens bears the burden of another; then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of that about which you differed.

This is a single word which encompasses the whole universe: the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. All creatures that are known or unknown are included in it; every event and occurrence, whether apparent or hidden, is included in it. All of these are under the shade of Allah's lordship, and this great universe is within the sphere of Allah's lordship. Over it Allah's sovereignty prevails, and it is obedient to Him in beliefs, in worship and in the legal system. In "wa Huwa Rabbu kulli shay'" (He is the Lord of all things), observe the manner of speech: it is a rhetorical question of denial: Should I seek a lord other than Allah? How can I accept a non-Allah as lord, one who would be my ruler, who would have authority over my affairs, who would watch over me, who would be my reformer and guide, when only Allah will call me to account for my intention and my deeds, and only He is the one who will reckon for obedience and disobedience? So how can I accept a non-Allah as lord when this entire universe is in the power of Allah, and I and you all are part of His system of lordship?

How can I make a non-Allah a lord, since on the Day of Judgment, when every person will be requited for the crimes they committed, that other would be unable to do anything; there each person alone will be responsible for what they did, and no one will be able to bear another's burden?

How can I make a non-Allah a lord? It is among these very people that Allah has settled humankind and arranged them, raising some to high ranks and making others subordinate; some intelligent and some ignorant, some strong and some weak, some wealthy and some poor, so that all may be tested. How should I make some other a lord, when the Forgiving and the Merciful is Allah alone, the Lord of the worlds?

﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees, to test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (165)

And He it is who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in ranks, that He may test you in what He has given you. Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Shall I make a non-Allah a lord, and make His law my law, and understand His command and accept His order as a command? All these proofs are before me, all evidence is present, and all these proofs show that we should make Allah alone our Lord.

This is the melody of Tawhid, very gentle and pleasant. Within this melody the reality of faith and its manifestations and witnessings are clearly seen on the screen of the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is expressed in a manner and with words that are a clear miracle of the Qur'an and a unique style of expression.

It is the final strike on the strings of consciousness, whose purpose is the declaration of Allah's sovereignty and obedience to His system of law, exactly as was done at the beginning of the surah when the theory of Allah's sovereignty was expressed. Look again at this verse and similar ones from the beginning of the surah:

﴿Say: Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds and is not fed? Say: I have been commanded to be the first to submit, and do not be among the polytheists. Say: Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day. Whoever is spared it on that Day, He has had mercy on him, and that is the clear success.﴾ (14–16)

There is no need to say more on this: the matters mentioned at the beginning of this surah have been repeated at its end. The meanings of the beginning and the meanings of the end are alike; at the beginning these meanings and realities were taken in their theoretical aspect, and at the end they are taken in their practical form as a system of life. In both places two aspects of the one reality of this religion have been taken.

Now this surah has ended. Look back: we have made a long mental journey, crossed the vast deserts and rivers of meanings, and traveled through long and deep valleys. Part of this surah was in the previous juz and part came in the present juz. What a great journey of meanings and realities it was. If one looks at the size of this surah, it is only a few pages, limited verses and phrases. Were it human speech, it could not have conveyed these unlimited realities in so short a surah. It is a vast store of realities, observations, guidance and signs compressed into these verses; the style of speech is most miraculous and melodious, and the expression is extremely concise and unparalleled.

The journey we made through the world of this surah was very long, wide, and full of ups and downs. In it we encountered the realities of this universe, and we also measured the bounds of the Islamic conception of life. In this journey we became aware of the reality of divinity, its beauty, and its majesty and grace. In this journey we also observed this universe and the realities within it, life within it and its varieties, and we saw the scenes of the unseen realities behind it, whether present or to come. We also learned about the system of Allah's will: how He grants stability and how He erases, how He creates and how He brings to nothing, how He gives life and how He brings death. How He has set this whole universe in motion, and how all living and dead creation moves and flows.

In this journey we went down into the depths of the human soul, traveled through its heights and depths, came to know its outward appearance and inner reality, encountered its desires and inclinations, observed its guidance and its misguidance, saw the mischiefs of the devils of jinn and mankind within the human soul and their plans and schemes, and saw guiders and misleaders grappling with one another.

In this long journey we witnessed the scenes of the Resurrection, the gathering and dispersal, moments of anguish and trial, moments of joy and success, the settling of humanity on this earth, some chapters of its history, and some glimpses of the history of this universe. In short, in this surah we saw what cannot be fully summarized here. The complete reality can only be derived from studying this surah and from its beloved style. The truth is that the Qur'an is indeed a blessed book, and this surah is one part of its blessings.

The journey we made through the world of this surah was very long, wide, and full of ups and downs. In it we encountered the realities of this universe, and we also measured the bounds of the Islamic conception of life. In this journey we became aware of the reality of divinity, its beauty, and its majesty and grace. In this journey we also observed this universe and the realities within it, life within it and its varieties, and we saw the scenes of the unseen realities behind it, whether present or to come. We also learned about the system of Allah's will: how He grants stability and how He erases, how He creates and how He brings to nothing, how He gives life and how He brings death. How He has set this whole universe in motion, and how all living and dead creation moves and flows.

In this journey we went down into the depths of the human soul, traveled through its heights and depths, came to know its outward appearance and inner reality, encountered its desires and inclinations, observed its guidance and its misguidance, saw the mischiefs of the devils of jinn and mankind within the human soul and their plans and schemes, and saw guiders and misleaders grappling with one another.

In this long journey we witnessed the scenes of the Resurrection, the gathering and dispersal, moments of anguish and trial, moments of joy and success, the settling of humanity on this earth, some chapters of its history, and some glimpses of the history of this universe. In short, in this surah we saw what cannot be fully summarized here. The complete reality can only be derived from studying this surah and from its beloved style. The truth is that the Qur'an is indeed a blessed book, and this surah is one part of its blessings.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 6, verses 160–165:

Verses 160 to 165

This concluding passage, bearing in mind the themes at the beginning of this surah, is a most beautiful melody, most fitting and dazzling. With this melody the subject of sacrifices and vows, of offerings from fruits and crops, and in this connection the superstitions and customs of the age of ignorance, and then the claims that this law is from Allah, comes to its conclusion here. What does this concluding melody add to the theme? I think that after what we have said on these subjects, there is no need to say anything further on them.

﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the creed of Ibrahim, a man of pure faith, and he was not one of the polytheists.﴾ (161)

Say, O Muhammad (ﷺ): My Lord has surely shown me the straight path, a perfectly right religion in which there is no crookedness, the way of Ibrahim, which he adopted with single-minded devotion, and he was not one of the polytheists.

This is a declaration full of gratitude, which expresses firm conviction and complete trust. In it the literal structure of the words and their true meaning are combined. It expresses the connection of guidance with the Lord, the relationship of lordship, and His continuous protection. In it thanks are rendered that He has guided us to the straight path, in which there is no crookedness. That religion is the upright religion (din qayyim), and this religion is also our ancient heritage. From the time of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), this same religion is Islam; Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is the father of the fathers of this ummah, and from that time the Muslim ummah is a blessed ummah. In it there is a clear declaration that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was not among the polytheists.

﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. This I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit.﴾ (162–163)

Say: my prayer, my acts of worship, my life and my death all belong to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, who has no partner; this is what I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit.

This is the melody of Tawhid: an expression of absolute monotheism and all-encompassing servitude, in which prayer, retreat, life and death are all dedicated to Allah, who is the Lord of the worlds, the One who sustains, the sole controller and guardian, the Nurturer and Lord and ruler of the worlds. In it is the declaration of complete Islam, in every aspect of life, even up to death, in the conscience and in action, complete Islam. In the words (wa bidhalika umirtu) it is said that this complete Islam is a command of Allah, not merely a voluntary act. Therefore, the first of them is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns only for itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.﴾ (164)

Say: Should I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of everything? Every soul earns only for itself, no one bearing burdens bears the burden of another; then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of that about which you differed.

This is a single word which encompasses the whole universe: the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. All creatures that are known or unknown are included in it; every event and occurrence, whether apparent or hidden, is included in it. All of these are under the shade of Allah's lordship, and this great universe is within the sphere of Allah's lordship. Over it Allah's sovereignty prevails, and it is obedient to Him in beliefs, in worship and in the legal system. In "wa Huwa Rabbu kulli shay'" (He is the Lord of all things), observe the manner of speech: it is a rhetorical question of denial: Should I seek a lord other than Allah? How can I accept a non-Allah as lord, one who would be my ruler, who would have authority over my affairs, who would watch over me, who would be my reformer and guide, when only Allah will call me to account for my intention and my deeds, and only He is the one who will reckon for obedience and disobedience? So how can I accept a non-Allah as lord when this entire universe is in the power of Allah, and I and you all are part of His system of lordship?

How can I make a non-Allah a lord, since on the Day of Judgment, when every person will be requited for the crimes they committed, that other would be unable to do anything; there each person alone will be responsible for what they did, and no one will be able to bear another's burden?

How can I make a non-Allah a lord? It is among these very people that Allah has settled humankind and arranged them, raising some to high ranks and making others subordinate; some intelligent and some ignorant, some strong and some weak, some wealthy and some poor, so that all may be tested. How should I make some other a lord, when the Forgiving and the Merciful is Allah alone, the Lord of the worlds?

﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees, to test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (165)

And He it is who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in ranks, that He may test you in what He has given you. Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Shall I make a non-Allah a lord, and make His law my law, and understand His command and accept His order as a command? All these proofs are before me, all evidence is present, and all these proofs show that we should make Allah alone our Lord.

This is the melody of Tawhid, very gentle and pleasant. Within this melody the reality of faith and its manifestations and witnessings are clearly seen on the screen of the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is expressed in a manner and with words that are a clear miracle of the Qur'an and a unique style of expression.

It is the final strike on the strings of consciousness, whose purpose is the declaration of Allah's sovereignty and obedience to His system of law, exactly as was done at the beginning of the surah when the theory of Allah's sovereignty was expressed. Look again at this verse and similar ones from the beginning of the surah:

﴿Say: Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds and is not fed? Say: I have been commanded to be the first to submit, and do not be among the polytheists. Say: Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day. Whoever is spared it on that Day, He has had mercy on him, and that is the clear success.﴾ (14–16)

There is no need to say more on this: the matters mentioned at the beginning of this surah have been repeated at its end. The meanings of the beginning and the meanings of the end are alike; at the beginning these meanings and realities were taken in their theoretical aspect, and at the end they are taken in their practical form as a system of life. In both places two aspects of the one reality of this religion have been taken.

Now this surah has ended. Look back: we have made a long mental journey, crossed the vast deserts and rivers of meanings, and traveled through long and deep valleys.
